description: Optional; evaluate after K1b. Queue-mode parity with Kiro's Ctrl+S toggle: a client-side buffer that flushes to session/prompt on TurnCompleted instead of steering mid-turn (pure cyril-side, no new wire). Subagent steering: probe _session/steer against subagent session ids, then wire /steer @<name> <msg> through SubagentTracker::find_by_name if it works.

notes.content: Reconstructed 2026-06-17.

title: KAS hooks host: registry hot-reload (file-watch .kiro/hooks + serve updated list without bridge restart)
description: DEFERRED FROM cyril-jiyn v1 (load-once per bridge). KAS's own v2 loader file-watches .kiro/hooks (ConfigFileWatcher); cyril's host-mode registry should eventually match: watch workspace+global hook dirs, reload on change. The agent re-queries _kiro/hooks/list per trigger, so a reloaded registry takes effect next trigger without any notification (didChange is agent->client, not client->agent — covenant §1c).

title: W1 follow-up: extend /workflow with the remaining mutating verbs (pause, retry, delete, update, resumeAll)
description: cyril-0qe6 ships the v1 surface (recipes, list, run, attach, status, cancel, resume). The engine's remaining verbs — pause {workflowId}, retry (terminal runs only), delete, update {action: replace_remaining} (valid on paused runs), resumeAll — are deliberately out of v1. All 14 request verbs exist on 2.16.2 (carved from the bundle; see .cyril-0qe6/findings.md F4). Per ADR-0011, treat a -32601/-32603 from these as 're-probe the gate', and note cancel's reply shape {ok, previousStatus} differs from invoke/resume's {workflowId, status} — probe each verb's reply shape before modeling. ALSO in scope here: richer /workflow run input values — v1 parses k=v tails as JSON strings only; extend to typed values (numbers, booleans, JSON literals) if a recipe's inputs schema demands them.

title: @-file completion is silently empty outside a git repo (git ls-files only, no UI feedback)
description: FileCompleter::load shells out to git ls-files and returns an empty completer on failure with only a tracing::warn. In a non-git cwd (or for untracked files) typing @query silently produces no suggestions and the user gets no indication why. Discovered by the cyril-a14l pty oracle: the probe scratch dir was not a git repo and the completer came up empty. Options: fall back to a bounded filesystem walk, or surface a one-time system message ('@-completion unavailable: not a git repository').

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #87 (8604c60d8). Repro: completion_unavailable_notice_shown_once (red pre-fix). First-@-trigger one-time system message; loaded-empty vs load-failed modeled via Option reason, no sentinel.

title: KAS live shell-output streaming: advertise streamingShellContent + render _kiro/tools/content_chunk
description: kiro-cli 2.19.1 / KAS 0.48.0 adds the first new _kiro/* wire method since 2.16.0: _kiro/tools/content_chunk {sessionId, toolCallId, content:{type:"content", content:{type:"text", text}}} — incremental mid-run shell output for execute tool calls, replacing content-bearing tool_call_updates while the tool runs (terminal update unchanged). Emission is CLIENT-GATED on initialize.clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.streamingShellContent:true (same family as textSearch/findFiles); output is sanitized + redacted + coalesced server-side (flush interval + max-bytes cap). NO shipped client consumes it yet — tui.js 2.19.1 neither advertises the capability nor subscribes (0 hits), so cyril would be the first client with live shell streaming. Default-off = zero risk today; cyril warn-drops the unknown method only if some future kiro flips it server-side. Work: advertise the capability on KAS spawns, route content_chunk by toolCallId into the tracked tool call as streaming content (append semantics, like agent text streaming but scoped to the tool call widget), and reconcile with the terminal tool_call_update (which carries the full final output — replace accumulated stream on terminal to avoid duplication). See docs/kiro-2.19.1-wire-audit.md.
acceptance_criteria: capability advertised only on KAS engine; content_chunk appends to the owning tool call display live; terminal update replaces (not duplicates) streamed content; unknown-method warn+drop path untouched for other clients; state + render tests with captured payload shape.

notes.content: LIVE CAPTURE landed (docs/kiro-2.19.1-wire-audit.md § 1, experiments/conductor-spike/kas-content-chunk-2.19.1.jsonl + probe): chunks are real-time (one per output line, ~1s coalescer flush, <100ms latency), toolCallId matches the tool_call lifecycle id, mid-run tool_call_updates carry NO content while chunks flow. RENDERING CONTRACT: chunks are raw text; the terminal completed update carries the FULL output as a JSON-object STRING ({"output":"..."}) inside the text block — replace accumulated stream on terminal, and parse/unwrap the JSON shape difference. Redactor is value-based (4 sandbox env vars) — inert on workstations; do not assume pattern-based secret masking.

title: Intermittent empty tracing-capture in warning-assertion tests (EOF while parsing)
description: PR 92 oracle-hardening round (2026-08-10): malformed_workflow_field_matrix_isolated (and once workflow_run_complete_status_mismatch_rejected) fail ~1-2 in 8 full-suite runs with 'workflow warning must be one JSON event: EOF while parsing a value' — an empty capture buffer from test_support::CaptureWriter. A/B-verified pre-existing (reproduces with fixtures reverted to HEAD). Suspected mechanism: unlocked warning-emitting tests racing tracing's global callsite-interest rebuild when a locked capture test installs its thread-scoped subscriber. Candidate fixes: take tracing_capture_lock in every warning-EMITTING test (not just capture consumers), or retry-once in capture_rejection when the buffer is empty, or a dedicated tracing dispatcher per capture. Repro: loop 'cargo test -p cyril-core --features kas malformed_workflow' ~10x.

title: Enter-while-busy silently drops the user's message (regression from cyril-84ca off-loop guard)
description:
Regression introduced by cyril-84ca (PR #22): pressing Enter (non-slash text) while session.status()==Busy silently drops the user's message.

ROOT CAUSE: app.rs submit_input() (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:640) has NO busy guard. On Enter it take_input()s (clears the box), add_user_message()s (commits the text to the visible chat), set_status(Busy)+set_activity(Sending), then sends BridgeCommand::SendPrompt. After cyril-84ca the bridge's one-turn guard rejects a second SendPrompt mid-turn with BridgeError{operation:'prompt', message:'a turn is already in progress'} (bridge.rs SendPrompt guard). So the message is committed to chat and the input cleared, but it is NEVER sent to the agent — only an error system message appears.

BEHAVIOR CHANGE: pre-cyril-84ca the blocked command loop QUEUED the second SendPrompt and ran it as a sequential second turn after the first completed (message eventually sent). Post-cyril-84ca it is rejected (message lost). Live on main in the window between cyril-84ca merging and cyril-bm1j (K1b) landing — cyril-84ca blocks cyril-bm1j, so this PR merges first.

SECOND AFFECTED PATH: dispatch_code_command's Prompt branch (app.rs:1043) programmatically emits SendPrompt with no busy check; a /code-triggered prompt arriving mid-turn is rejected the same way, and its already-committed user text is never sent.

UI INCOHERENCE: UiState's BridgeError handler (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs:638) only add_system_message()s — it does NOT clear activity. So set_activity(Sending) from the rejected submit regresses the spinner from Streaming/ToolRunning back to 'Sending', the user sees 'prompt failed: a turn is already in progress', and then turn 1 keeps streaming — a sequence that did not occur pre-cyril-84ca.

PROPER FIX: this IS 'the latent second-prompt-mid-turn bug' that cyril-bm1j (K1b) is designed to fix by routing Enter-while-busy to SteerSession when status==Busy and input is non-slash. If the pre-K1b window matters, a minimal interim guard in submit_input (don't commit/clear + show a 'turn in progress' hint, or drop the second send before mutating UI) closes it without the full K1b UX.

Found by /code-review of PR #22.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting non-slash text while session.status()==Busy must not silently drop the message: either route it to SteerSession (K1b) or, at minimum, leave the input uncleared/uncommitted and surface a clear 'turn in progress' affordance, with no orphaned activity state (no spinner regression to Sending, no BridgeError-only dead end). The /code Prompt path (app.rs:1043) must likewise not lose its injected prompt mid-turn. Regression test: with a Busy session, submit Enter and assert the message is not lost and activity/status stay consistent.

title: Parse _meta.kiro.toolName / mcpServerName in convert/kiro.rs — trusted tool identity instead of LLM-authored titles
description: v2 tool_call / tool_call_update notifications carry a canonical, NON-model-authored tool identity in _meta.kiro: toolName (the real tool name) and mcpServerName (set ONLY for MCP-served tools, so a non-empty value is the trusted discriminator for a genuine MCP tool call vs a shell command whose output the model authored). The visible title is LLM prose — for the todo_list tool it reads like "Creating task list: ..." — so title can never identify a tool reliably. Kiro Crew keys its dashboard and security gating on this channel; cyril convert layer currently never reads _meta.kiro and docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md does not document it. Bonus unlocked by this channel: v2 never emits the ACP plan update (confirmed through 2.14.0) — the agent task list is the todo_list tool call, identified only via _meta.kiro.toolName, with the FULL list (never a delta) in rawOutput. Also note the related echo quirk: kiro camelCases snake_case rawInput keys on echo, so any key matching must read both spellings.
acceptance_criteria: convert/kiro.rs parses _meta.kiro.toolName and _meta.kiro.mcpServerName from tool_call and tool_call_update into ToolCall as Option<String> fields (Option for absent values, no sentinels; Kiro deviations stay in convert/kiro.rs, never mod.rs); merge_update preserves both fields when an update omits them; any tool-identification logic (e.g. todo_list detection) keys on toolName, never title; tests cover a fixture with _meta.kiro populated and one without (fields None); docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md documents the _meta.kiro identity channel and the rawInput camelCase echo quirk.

notes.content: Source: github.com/kirodotdev/kirocrew @ e44259ce, src/kiro_crew/acp/_dispatch.py (_kiro_tool_name, _kiro_mcp_server_name) + acp/types.py (KIRO_TOOL_TODO_LIST). Engine-side symbol cited by Crew: kiro_tool_identity_meta. Diffed against docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md 2026-08-04; see memory reference_kirocrew_platform.

Deep-dive addendum (docs/kirocrew-deep-dive.md): session/request_permission is identity-POOR — no kind, no _meta, truncated title. KiroCrew caches rawInput + trusted identity per toolCallId at the ToolCall notification and joins at permission time; the approval overlay must show the recovered real command (never the LLM-authored title), and gate fail-closed when _meta identity is absent. Permission response must echo the agent-provided optionIds exactly (allow_once/allow_always on kiro; differs per vendor; legacy options may omit kind). Cache needs a size cap (KiroCrew: 256, cleared per prompt).

title: KAS shell pipelines survive terminal cancellation
description: While implementing cyril-6bol, the selected-shell lifecycle fence proved that terminal/release killed only the outer shell process. Once a pipeline child had started, it survived release long enough to perform a delayed side effect; CancelRequest inherited the same process-only kill path. The terminal owner must isolate each Unix command in a process group and terminate the tree on kill/release/cancel/drop; native Windows explicit lifecycle paths must use taskkill /T /F with direct-child kill as a fallback.
acceptance_criteria: release_kills_child_and_frees_id starts an operator pipeline, waits until its child is live, releases it, and proves no delayed marker appears. cancel_reaps_sessions_running_terminals does the same through BridgeCommand::CancelRequest. Existing kill/output/status and dropped-owner lifecycle fences remain green.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed in PR #80 (ce0ea4f): process-tree fences — process_group(0)+killpg on unix, taskkill /T /F helper on windows — on kill/release/cancel

title: Probe FeatureConfigRegistry client/session providers — can an ACP client set KAS feature flags?
description:
KAS 0.54.3's feature flags resolve through a FeatureConfigRegistry whose provider precedence is:

  ['governance','env','client','session','experiment']

'client' and 'session' as provider SOURCES suggests an ACP client may be able to set flags over the wire — including stream_idle_watchdog and the retry family (empty_response_retry, truncated_response_retry, stream_error_retry, auth_expiry_retry), all default-true.

If reachable, this is a real cyril lever: tune or disable the stall watchdog per session rather than depending on KIRO_STREAM_IDLE_* env vars set at spawn time. Consistent with the known KAS pattern that initialize._meta.kiro.settings OVERRIDES backend flags.

Not probed in the 2.20.1 audit (docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 4). Scope: find the client/session provider read path, then live-probe whether initialize/session-meta can carry these keys and whether they take effect (control: an unset session in the same process).

notes.content: Closed: ANSWERED — NO, not wired. Static: exactly one buildFeatureConfigRegistry() and it passes only [env, experiment]; only two provider classes exist (bhe source='env', QNe source='experiment'). Nothing declares client/session/governance — the precedence array is a sort key over a forward-looking vocabulary with 3 of 5 sources unimplemented. Live (clientmeta leg): five plausible shapes on BOTH initialize._meta and session/new._meta produced 4 notifies + the -32000 terminal, identical to baseline; meta accepted silently with no error or echo. The env provider is the only client-reachable lever: KIRO_FEATURE_STREAM_IDLE_WATCHDOG_ENABLED (9 of 15 flags have env vars; the retry family and memory_internal are experiment-only). Caveat spun out to cyril-0w3u: =false kills the hard timeout/retry/-32000 but an intermittent single soft warning still escapes (unregistered model instance hits 'undefined ?? default(true)'), so cyril must handle _kiro/system/notify regardless. See docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 5.

title: M3: Add and search one cited knowledge document
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Deliver Cyril's first cited knowledge path. A user or bound agent submits one document's text with a title and opaque source label. Cyril redacts, chunks, hashes, and indexes it in the separate knowledge store. The agent can list sources and search through namespaced MCP tools; results are bounded and carry canonical source, document, section, and locator metadata. `/library` shows the source and lets the user run the same search without relying on an agent-native `/knowledge` command.

The demo is exact-recall oriented: add a distinctive design document, search for a detail, receive the supporting chunk with a verifiable citation, add the same content again, and observe an idempotent duplicate result. The source label is displayed and stored as identity only; Cyril never resolves, opens, stats, or fetches it.

## Placement / boundaries

The knowledge module owns source/document/chunk identities, redaction, chunking, hashes, FTS5 indexing, lexical ranking, deduplication, citations, result budgeting, and source-scoped search. Define a first-class citation/source-location domain type; do not overload generic tool text or file-diff location types. The MCP adapter exposes namespaced add-document, list-sources, and search tools by translating the knowledge interface. The TUI owns `/library` source/search projection and rendering only. The memory prompt adapter does not auto-inject knowledge.

Keep knowledge in its separate versioned SQLite store. The ingestion tool accepts text already read by the caller plus an opaque source label; it must not touch the filesystem or network. Search input is parameterized and treated literally by FTS5. Stored and returned content is credential/exfiltration-redacted and framed as untrusted evidence, not instruction. Do not add folder scanning, automatic project ingestion, URL fetching, embeddings, graph extraction, or native-Kiro federation in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user and a bound agent can add document text with title and opaque source label through one validated knowledge interface.
- [ ] The source label is stored/displayed as identity and is never opened, resolved, statted, or fetched.
- [ ] Documents are redacted, deterministically chunked, content-hashed, and indexed in the separate knowledge FTS5 store.
- [ ] Re-adding identical content is idempotent and does not create duplicate searchable chunks.
- [ ] Namespaced MCP tools list valid sources and return bounded source-scoped search results.
- [ ] Every result carries a canonical citation with source, document, section, and available locator metadata.
- [ ] `/library` shows sources and search results without shadowing the agent-provided `/knowledge` command.
- [ ] Knowledge is never automatically added to the first-prompt memory block.
- [ ] FTS queries are parameterized/literal; stored and returned content is redacted and framed as untrusted evidence.
- [ ] MCP and TUI behavioral tests prove add, duplicate, list, search, scope, citation fidelity, and no path/network access.

## Blocked by

- cyril-3dqf
design:
### Knowledge MCP tool schemas

`cyril_knowledge_add_document` accepts exactly `title` (1-200 characters), `content` (1 byte to 1 MiB UTF-8 after transport decoding), `source_uri` (1-2,048 characters), and optional `reason` (maximum 500 characters). `source_uri` is an opaque identity label: the raw value is hashed for identity, a redacted bounded form is stored/displayed, and no code in this operation resolves, opens, stats, or fetches it. Re-adding the same source identity with unchanged content returns `unchanged`; changed content atomically replaces that document's chunks; corpus-identical content returns `duplicate` without duplicate chunks.

`cyril_knowledge_list_sources` accepts an empty object only. Success returns ordered sources with opaque source ID, redacted name/label, source kind, active document/chunk counts, and indexing state. Counts include only active searchable chunks.

`cyril_knowledge_search` accepts required `query` (1-4,096 characters), optional `limit` (1-10, default 5), and optional opaque `source_id` (1-128 characters). Unknown fields and unknown source IDs are rejected; an unknown source response points to list-sources without revealing filesystem details. Search has no path, namespace, SQL, ranking-weight, or trust argument.

Each successful search result contains opaque chunk/document/source IDs, title, bounded content (maximum 4,000 characters), score, match legs, and a citation object with redacted source label/kind plus optional document locator, section heading, and one-indexed line/page range. Total rendered content is capped at 20,000 characters and truncates only between results. No match is successful `status: ok` with an empty array.

Add returns `stored`, `replaced`, `unchanged`, or `duplicate` plus source/document IDs and chunk count. Stable tool errors reuse capability/input/runtime errors and add `source_unknown`, `content_too_large`, `content_rejected`, `citation_unavailable`, and `store_conflict`. All responses pass through runtime redaction before MCP translation; the adapter owns no alternate schema or search formatting.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Add document text with title/source label through one validated interface.
- [ ] Treat source label as identity only; never touch path or network.
- [ ] Redact, chunk, hash, and FTS5-index in the separate knowledge store.
- [ ] Make identical re-add idempotent.
- [ ] Namespaced MCP tools list sources and return bounded scoped results.
- [ ] Results carry canonical citations and available locators.
- [ ] /library renders sources/search without shadowing /knowledge.
- [ ] Never auto-inject knowledge into memory context.
- [ ] Parameterize FTS input and frame/redact returned evidence.
- [ ] Behavioral tests prove the entire cited-document path and negative boundaries.
- [ ] add-document, list-sources, and search inputs enforce the exact Design bounds and reject unknown fields.
- [ ] Search output enforces per-result/total bounds and the canonical citation/result schema; no-match remains successful empty output.
- [ ] Add-document returns the specified stored/replaced/unchanged/duplicate statuses and never uses source_uri as an instruction.
- [ ] Stable knowledge error codes and capability errors remain structured MCP tool errors rather than transport failures.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M3. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.
Mechanism contract added: exact add-document, list-sources, and search schemas, bounds, result/citation shapes, statuses, and stable errors.

title: KAS-8 — Surface _kiro/safety/* Infrastructure Safety gate (can block tool calls)
description:
KAS-8 functional gap. `_kiro/safety/{statusChanged,propertiesChanged}` — Infrastructure Safety gate, added in kiro-cli 2.8.0 (embedded @kiro/agent). Cedar/AWS-governance signals that CAN BLOCK A TOOL CALL.

Why this matters more than the other notification gaps: it is ENFORCEMENT, not display. cyril's KAS-2a unknown-variant debug! arm silently drops these today, which means cyril can present a tool as runnable that KAS will refuse, or miss a posture change mid-session. Every other dropped notification just loses information; this one desyncs cyril from what KAS will actually permit.

SCOPE:
- Add a converter arm for `_kiro/safety/statusChanged` + `_kiro/safety/propertiesChanged` (pairs with the KAS-2c GovernanceSource sub-trait — same Cedar/governance family).
- Reflect a safety-blocked tool call in the UI (don't render it as a plain pending/allowed tool).
- Surface the safety status/posture so the user understands why a tool was refused.

REFS: covenant capabilities/safety/*.d.ts (on-disk @kiro/agent 0.3.257; NOT yet in the curated docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md catalog — added after 0.3.224); ROADMAP KAS-8 coverage matrix; memory reference_kiro_2_8_0_diff (notes the safety gate). Probe the live shapes before implementing (no probe exists yet).

notes.content:
LIVE PROBE 2026-07-31 (2.16.0, probe-kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.py). The surface
is REACHABLE but INERT on this account.

Gate found and satisfied: capabilitiesFrom() reads
`infrastructureSafety: kiroMeta.infrastructureSafety === true`, i.e.
initialize.clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.infrastructureSafety. Advertising it
(plus c2sViews) is what earlier probes never did.

Result with the capability advertised:
  _kiro/safety/getProperties -> {"properties": []}   (real response, NOT -32601)
  _kiro/safety/statusChanged / propertiesChanged pushes: ZERO across
  initialize + session/new + a full turn.

Reading: the method is wired and answers, but there are no Cedar/AWS-governance
properties configured for this account, so nothing to report and nothing to
enforce. The BLOCKING behaviour this issue cares about cannot be observed
without an org policy attached — that is an account/backend precondition, not a
client one.

Actionable now: model `{properties: []}` as the empty-but-valid response shape,
and keep the unknown-variant arm from silently dropping statusChanged /
propertiesChanged. Do NOT infer from zero pushes that the notifications are
dormant in the product — we only established they are dormant HERE.

Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.jsonl
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-8

RE-RUN WITH BOTH HALVES SATISFIED — 2026-08-01, still inert
(probe-kas-inconclusive-rerun-2.16.0.py, capture kas-inconclusive-2.16.0.jsonl).

The prior probe was under-specified: the gate is
  _infraSafetyEnabled = clientSupportsSafety && (monitorEnabled || enforceEnabled)
and that run advertised the flags but NOT the capability. This run satisfied both:
  clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.infrastructureSafety = true
  initialize._meta.kiro.settings.infraSafetyMonitor = {enabled:true}
  initialize._meta.kiro.settings.infraSafetyEnforce = {enabled:true}
(settings at INITIALIZE, so they bridge over the backend flags — the same lever that
DID unlock subagentOrchestration in the same session, which proves the mechanism works
and this is not another wiring mistake.)

Result: _kiro/safety/getProperties -> {"properties": []}, and ZERO
statusChanged/propertiesChanged frames across initialize + session/new + two turns,
one of which ran a shell command (the classic thing an enforcement gate would block).

CONCLUSION, now properly grounded rather than under-specified: the safety surface is
wired and answers, but this ACCOUNT has no Cedar/AWS-governance properties attached, so
there is nothing to report and nothing to enforce. Observing the BLOCKING behaviour
requires an org policy — an account/backend precondition cyril cannot create.

Actionable regardless: model {properties: []} as the empty-but-valid shape and keep the
unknown-variant arm from silently dropping statusChanged/propertiesChanged, so the day a
policy IS attached cyril degrades visibly rather than silently.

title: CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO non-Unicode value silently treated as unset (.ok() collapses missing vs corrupt)
description: process_wsl_distro (crates/cyril-core/src/platform/path.rs, the OnceLock init) reads the distro with std::env::var("CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO").ok(), collapsing VarError::NotPresent and VarError::NotUnicode: a corrupt (non-Unicode) distro value silently degrades to no-distro passthrough with no log, contradicting CLAUDE.md Silent Failure Prevention (distinguish missing from corrupt; audit .ok()). Surfaced by PR #89's post-PR review (finding 2), which fixed the identical collapse on CYRIL_AGENT_LOCATION in bind_agent_location; this is the pre-existing cyril-8tq6 twin, deferred to keep that PR's scope tight.
design: Mirror bind_agent_location: match on VarError, warn on NotUnicode(raw) with the raw value, fall back to None. The adjacent current_dir().ok() is fine — an unavailable cwd is not config corruption. Optional fence: a unix child test alongside env_non_unicode_falls_back_via_child_process in tests/win_wsl_wiring.rs (run_child already takes OsStr values).

title: Adopt harness-parity invariants for the vendor-neutral seam (positive identity, opt-in capabilities, per-target literals)
description:
KiroCrew published 15 numbered invariants governing how a non-first-class agent harness may be adapted, each closed by a named test and enforced by a diff-scoped CI gate. It is the most directly transferable artifact found in the whole ACP-seam investigation, written by the team that owns the protocol.

Framing (harness-parity.md:8-21): "an added harness may only adapt itself to the seams the Kiro harness already runs through. It may not move, widen, generalize, or add a branch to those seams. ... The failure mode this file exists to prevent is not a broken adapter - that fails loudly on its own first session. It is the silent capture of the Kiro path."

The ones that map cleanly onto cyril:
- H5 identity is a POSITIVE comparison against a named constant or set; negations forbidden. Rationale: a negative test "reads correctly with two harnesses and then silently hands the third a capability, a sandbox waiver, or a session label nobody granted it - and it fails toward the PERMISSIVE answer". Two such sites shipped before the rule existed.
- H6 capabilities are opt-in membership sets, never inherited by negation.
- H10 protocol version and client capabilities stay per-target literals (see cyril-hg2x).
- H12 model pre-flight: empty/unknown advertised set means ALLOW; never compare ids across vendor namespaces (see cyril-fj6j).
- H14 every capability the app layer reads is declared on the trait WITH A SAFE DEFAULT - never a hasattr/Option probe on the first-class path.
- H15 a capability that is observed elsewhere must ratchet its observability stamp together with itself (a provider that steers but never stamps "steers perfectly well and silently never interrupts a wait - a failure with no error to notice").

Their CI gate self-tests FIRST because "a gate that has silently stopped matching reads as a green signal, which is worse than no gate", and is diff-scoped so a pre-existing backlog is not charged to the next pusher.

Cautionary half: their own RFC audits their seam as failing - 68 direct acp imports across 42 files, and providers/base.py:30 aliases the ACP event type as the "provider-agnostic" one, which put a raw JSON-RPC request id into their browser contract. Cyril crate boundary is far stronger (only cyril-core declares agent-client-protocol), but the four acp:: sites in cyril-core/types/ are the same shape in miniature.

Also worth writing down separately from the wire contract: their agent-host-contract.md enumerates the eight things a backend must declare BEYOND the wire (agent format, session store, auth, sandbox, MCP channel, billing, permission engine, auxiliary runtimes), where "not supported" is a valid declaration and "silence is not an answer".

Design decision needed: which invariants cyril adopts, and whether enforcement is a clippy lint, a script, or review-only.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 7.
acceptance_criteria: A decision record naming which invariants cyril adopts, with the enforcement mechanism chosen for each.

title: Amend .cyril-6bol/spec.md: four decisions shipped without being written back
description: The cyril-6bol deep review found the implementation deliberately deviates from spec.md in four places where the decision was made and reviewed but the artifact never amended: (1) PowerShell compound commands collapse exit codes to 0/1 (findings.md #4 ratified the tradeoff; the spec edge row still says "Preserve the exit code"); (2) simple POSIX/fish commands run via an injected `exec ` prefix for signal fidelity — top-level shell builtins (cd/export/ulimit/source) now fail 127 and builtin-named commands bind to external binaries, which restores pre-PR direct-argv parity but contradicts B8 "no grammar translation" as written; (3) the PATH scan is capped at 256 entries (MAX_PATH_ENTRIES) while spec line 16 promises an unqualified PATH fallback; (4) the "Out of scope" rows for cancellation/reaping and output-drain overlap work the spec itself forces (cyril-2z9g tree fences, cyril-r3t6 create-time drain) and should acknowledge it. Text-only change to .cyril-6bol/spec.md on the PR branch or post-merge.

title: M2: Recall memory through a capability-bound MCP session
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Expose scoped recall to the bound ACP agent through a Cyril-namespaced stdio MCP adapter while preserving ACP session availability. New sessions receive a pending opaque capability in their MCP environment before the agent returns its session ID. After a valid response, Cyril attempts a deadline-bound runtime binding to the returned session and resolved project, then either enables memory or revokes it; `SessionCreated` is published in both outcomes. Loaded sessions use the same capability model with their already-known identity.

The complete demo covers both success and failure: a new session calls the namespaced recall tool and receives only its bound project memory; a deliberately failed bind leaves the MCP tool denied with a typed error while the ACP session still prompts normally. A loaded session receives equivalent access without trusting identity supplied by the agent or tool arguments.

## Placement / boundaries

A new stdio MCP adapter module owns MCP protocol translation and nothing else. It connects to the existing memory runtime and presents typed tool results. The memory runtime owns capability minting, pending/bound/revoked state, authentication, expiry, session/project bindings, and scoped recall. The bridge owns standard ACP MCP-server registration on both new and loaded session requests plus the validate → bind-or-revoke → publish ordering. The UI owns only status projection.

The MCP process environment contains the private runtime endpoint and opaque capability only. It must not contain or trust session ID, project ID, cwd, bank name, or requested scope. Tool arguments may narrow a bound scope but never widen it. Pending, unknown, expired, and revoked capabilities fail closed. A bind failure disables only memory; it cannot suppress a valid `SessionCreated`. Use a namespaced recall tool and do not add mutation, promotion, knowledge, or native-Kiro federation in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New and loaded ACP session requests register a Cyril stdio MCP server using standard ACP fields.
- [ ] New-session registration carries an opaque pending capability and no session/project identity.
- [ ] After a valid new-session response, Cyril attempts binding with a deadline, then binds or revokes before publishing `SessionCreated`.
- [ ] Bind failure, timeout, or runtime loss still publishes the valid session and allows ordinary prompts.
- [ ] Loaded sessions pre-bind the known session/project capability and revoke it if loading fails.
- [ ] The namespaced recall tool returns only memory within the runtime-owned binding.
- [ ] Pending, unknown, expired, revoked, and scope-widening requests return typed denials.
- [ ] Capabilities are revoked on session close, failed create/load, bridge loss, and Cyril shutdown.
- [ ] `/memory status` distinguishes MCP pending, bound, disabled, and revoked states without exposing secrets.
- [ ] A stdio MCP harness proves authentication and scoped recall; the bridge fake-agent harness proves request shape, ordering, and ACP fail-open behavior.

## Blocked by

- cyril-n3j7
design:
## Capability and MCP contract

### Credential classes

The runtime-admin credential from M0 is held only by Cyril's orchestrator and can mint/bind/revoke session capabilities. It is never passed to an agent or MCP subprocess. Each MCP session receives a fresh 32-byte random capability encoded base64url without padding. The runtime stores only a keyed hash plus metadata; the raw value exists only in Cyril until placed in the child environment and in that MCP adapter process.

The MCP environment contains exactly the private runtime endpoint and raw session capability. It contains no session ID, project ID, cwd, target scope, runtime-admin credential, or database path.

### Capability state machine

A capability has exactly three monotonic states:

- Pending: minted for one prospective ACP session, unbound, tool access denied, 30-second bootstrap expiry.
- Bound: atomically associated with one validated ACP session ID, one canonical project ID, runtime instance ID, creation time, and session lifetime. It authorizes only the read operations declared by this slice.
- Revoked: terminal. Stores revocation reason/time and authorizes nothing.

There is no transition from Bound or Revoked back to Pending, and no capability can be rebound to another session/project. Expiry atomically transitions Pending to Revoked. Runtime restart invalidates every capability because bindings are scoped to runtime instance ID.

Session memory status is separate from capability state: Disabled means Cyril has a valid ACP session but no usable capability after memory was off, binding failed/timed out, or the runtime disappeared. Disabled is not a capability state and never authorizes a fallback identity.

### New and loaded session ordering

For `session/new`, Cyril resolves the project, mints Pending through the admin channel, and places the MCP server plus raw capability in the ACP request. The adapter may initialize and advertise tools while Pending, but every call returns `scope_not_bound`. After the agent returns, Cyril validates the session ID and attempts one atomic bind with a 250 ms deadline. Success produces Bound. Failure/timeout performs best-effort revoke and marks that ACP session's memory Disabled. In both cases Cyril then publishes `SessionCreated`; memory failure cannot hide a valid ACP session.

For `session/load`, Cyril already knows and validates the session/project mapping. It mints then binds before sending the load request. Load failure revokes the capability. Session close, bridge loss, agent exit, and Cyril shutdown revoke Bound capabilities best-effort; runtime-instance loss already makes them unusable.

### MCP tool schema

This slice advertises exactly one tool, `cyril_memory_recall`.

Input is an object with required `query` string (1-4,096 Unicode scalar values), optional `limit` integer (1-10, default 5), and optional `kinds` array containing unique values from `lesson`, `fact`, and `episode` (default all). Unknown fields are rejected. The tool exposes no scope, session, project, SQL, path, or confidence argument.

Successful structured output contains `status: ok`, an ordered `results` array, and `omitted_count`. Each result contains opaque memory ID, kind, bounded content, provenance/trust label, originating scope kind (not raw private path), created timestamp, and retrieval score. Total rendered tool content is bounded to 12,000 characters and truncates only between results. Empty valid recall returns `status: ok` with an empty array, not an error.

Tool failures use MCP `isError: true` and a stable structured error with code, safe message, and retryable boolean. Codes are `invalid_input`, `scope_not_bound`, `capability_invalid`, `capability_expired`, `capability_revoked`, `scope_denied`, `memory_unavailable`, and `internal_error`. Authentication/scope errors disclose no existence of other sessions/projects. Transport/protocol failures remain distinct from tool errors.

The MCP adapter validates request shape, forwards capability plus operation to the runtime, and translates the typed result. It owns no identity inference, scope policy, retrieval, fallback, or database access.

### Subagent and peer-session semantics

A session capability represents one top-level ACP session and its canonical project, not an individual model invocation. Agent-internal subagents that inherit the parent session's MCP server necessarily share that same capability and therefore the same read/write ceiling. The MCP protocol currently provides no trusted per-subagent caller identity, so the runtime records provenance as `agent_session` plus the bound top-level session, never a model-authored subagent name. Tool arguments cannot claim a different caller.

Internal subagents may recall and teach only within the parent's bound session/project policy. Their request for broader scope creates the same pending human promotion as a parent-agent request. They cannot approve promotions or gain global access. If an agent does not inherit MCP servers into an internal subagent, that subagent has no Cyril memory access; Cyril does not inject credentials through prompts or infer identity from process ancestry.

ACP peer sessions—including workflow step sessions, explicitly spawned sessions, and separately loaded sessions—are not internal subagents for authorization. Each receives its own minted capability bound to its own validated session ID and canonical project. A parent capability is never reused across peer sessions, even when projects match. Closing one peer revokes only its capability.

Automatic bridge capture records only lifecycle that Cyril actually observes and routes with trusted session/turn identity. Hidden internal-subagent prompts or results are not reconstructed from tool titles and are not claimed as durable transcript. Visible normalized subagent/tool events may be retained as part of the parent turn with their observed provenance.

Behavioral coverage uses one fake agent whose internal subagent shares the MCP adapter and two ACP peer sessions with distinct capabilities. It proves shared ceiling for the internal subagent, isolation/revocation for peers, no identity spoofing, and no fallback when MCP inheritance is absent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Runtime-admin and session-capability credentials are distinct; only the endpoint and raw session capability enter the MCP environment.
- [ ] Capabilities are 32 random bytes, stored hashed, runtime-instance-bound, and follow only Pending → Bound/Revoked or Bound → Revoked.
- [ ] Pending expires to Revoked after 30 seconds and every Pending tool call returns typed scope_not_bound.
- [ ] session/new follows resolve project → mint Pending → send MCP config → validate response → 250 ms bind attempt → bind or revoke/disable → always publish valid SessionCreated.
- [ ] Binding failure/timeout/runtime loss leaves the valid ACP session promptable and never infers fallback identity.
- [ ] session/load pre-binds the validated known session/project and revokes on load failure.
- [ ] Close, bridge loss, agent exit, Cyril shutdown, and runtime-instance loss make capabilities unusable.
- [ ] cyril_memory_recall accepts only query 1-4,096 chars, limit 1-10 default 5, and unique allowed kinds; unknown/scope fields are rejected.
- [ ] Success returns bounded ordered typed results and omitted_count; valid empty recall is success, not error.
- [ ] Tool failures use isError with stable codes/retryability and disclose no other session/project existence.
- [ ] The MCP adapter owns protocol translation only and performs no identity inference, scope policy, retrieval, fallback, or DB access.
- [ ] Stdio MCP and bridge fake-agent harnesses prove tool schema/bounds, every capability transition, new/load ordering, revocation, scoped recall, and ACP fail-open behavior.
- [ ] Internal subagents sharing the parent's MCP adapter share only its capability ceiling and cannot spoof caller identity.
- [ ] ACP peer/workflow/load sessions receive distinct capabilities even for the same project; revoking one does not revoke another.
- [ ] Absence of MCP inheritance yields no memory access and no prompt/process-ancestry credential fallback.
- [ ] Durable capture claims only lifecycle observed with trusted session/turn identity and never fabricates hidden subagent transcript.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M2. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.

AFK-readiness correction: the Design field now pins credential separation, Pending/Bound/Revoked transitions, new/load ordering, expiry/revocation, recall input/output bounds, and stable MCP tool errors.
Mechanism contract added: internal subagents share the parent session capability ceiling; ACP peer/workflow sessions receive separate capabilities; hidden lifecycle is never fabricated.

title: KAS-5b follow-up: reap/kill a session's live terminals on cancel/turn-end (orphan-on-cancel)
description: KAS-5b (cyril-ufie) spawns child processes on the bridge for terminal/create and reaps them on terminal/{release,kill} (the normal KAS flow: create->wait_for_exit->output->release). But if a turn is CANCELLED mid-command, KAS may not send release -> the child keeps running until it exits naturally (e.g. a 60s sleep = a 60s orphan on the bridge process). Scope: on session/cancel (and/or turn-end) kill that session's still-running terminals, keyed by session_id in the terminal registry. Needs the registry to track session_id per terminal (it carries sessionId on every request). Decide policy: kill-on-cancel vs let-finish. Out of KAS-5b's first cut (the happy-path lifecycle); this is the leak-on-cancel edge.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) TRIGGER SITE unnamed in the issue — mechanism (TerminalRegistry, owned by KiroClient at client.rs:26) and trigger (run_loop's Cancel arm bridge.rs:582-598 + TurnCompleted observation) sit on opposite sides of exactly the seam cyril-g9vt deferred. Decide JOINTLY with cyril-g9vt whether this is the ADR-0004 seam's first consumer. Minimal, proportionate option for a P3 leak fix: share Rc<TerminalRegistry> between KiroClient and the loop (same LocalSet thread; registry stays sole owner of process lifecycle) and call reap_session(session_id) from the Cancel arm. A third ad-hoc wiring (e.g. App sending a new reap BridgeCommand) would erode both this and g9vt.
(2) 'Keyed by session_id' should mean a session_id FIELD on Entry (from CreateTerminalRequest.session_id) + linear-scan reap_session — terminal id stays the primary key; a secondary index is over-engineering for a handful of terminals. Reap must follow the existing take-then-await pattern (no RefCell borrow across .await, terminal_io.rs:238-249).
(3) Policy recommendation: apply the existing KILL semantics (id stays valid, partial output cached), NOT release — KAS may still send terminal/output/release for those ids after the cancel, and kill-semantics lets them resolve instead of erroring -32602. Cancel-only for the first cut; reap-at-turn-end can race an in-flight release.
(4) INTERACTION with cyril-r3t6 (see its note): a cancelled turn whose command already wrote >64KB is wedged on the full OS pipe and never exits naturally — kill-on-cancel must also cover pre-wait children, and .kill_on_drop(true) at create is a cheap backstop.

Closed: Fixed: PR #48 (5f97307). Cancelled sessions' running terminals are reaped from run_loop's CancelRequest arm via shared Rc<TerminalRegistry> (session_id on Entry, linear-scan reap_session, KILL semantics — ids stay valid, in-flight children killed through their owning wait). Cancel-only per the issue's first-cut policy. Repro fences: cancel_reaps_sessions_running_terminals (end-to-end, alive-asserted pre-cancel), reap_session_kills_only_that_sessions_children_and_keeps_ids, reap_session_kills_child_owned_by_pending_wait.

title: Steering receipt: parse+strip the [STEERING <id>: note] trailer the model emits, reconcile onto the steer echo
description:
Evidence: AWS GenerateAssistantResponse prompt logs (2026-07-23, private workspace — NOT committed) show `_session/steer` reaches the model as its own user turn:

    [LIVE STEERING - New message from user]
    <user_message id="steer-<uuid>">TEXT</user_message>
    IMPORTANT: ... Use this exact format:
    [STEERING steer-<uuid>: <describe what you did or why it was not applicable>]

The model DOES comply — the captured assistantResponse ends with a well-formed
`[STEERING steer-<uuid>: ...]` trailer (pos 1588 of 1927, i.e. a tail trailer).

cyril has zero handling: the marker rides the AgentMessage stream and renders as raw prose
in the transcript. Meanwhile the SteerEcho chip sits at `applied` with no explanation.

The receipt id shares the id space with the wire queue id: the committed KAS capture
session_info_update_steering_queued.json carries a messageId of the same `steer-<uuid>`
shape. So id-based correlation to the SteerEcho is viable.

Work:
1. Pure parser in cyril-core/types/steer_receipt.rs — harvest complete markers out of a
   streaming buffer; compute the withheld tail so a partially-streamed marker never flashes.
2. UiState: harvest on AgentMessage append, reconcile onto the matching SteerEcho
   (id match, else the single unambiguous id-less Queued echo), keep the note.
3. chat.rs: render the note under the applied steer echo.

Conservative bias: never strip more than a well-formed marker. A `[STEERING ...` that never
terminates commits as ordinary text (todays behaviour, no regression).

Full structural findings: docs/kiro-prompt-assembly.md.

title: Spike SDK 2 client, component, proxy, and conductor topology for Cyril
description:
## Problem

The official ACP Rust SDK 2.0 migration changes more than callback signatures. It introduces first-party `Client`, `Agent`, `Proxy`, and `Conductor` roles, `Send + 'static` `ConnectTo` components, ordered dispatch handlers, frame-preserving transports, an official conductor, process components, and tracing. Cyril's current direct bridge combines transport/dispatch with a `!Send` domain mediator and was designed before those seams were canonical.

A minimal port could preserve the wrong topology and force a second bridge rewrite when proxy stages arrive. A conductor-first rewrite without evidence could instead distribute Kiro/KAS lifecycle, callback, and error-ordering policy across unnecessary layers.

Source-grounded API findings and the candidate architecture comparison are captured in `docs/acp-sdk-2-architecture-research.md`.

## Goal

Run executable, throwaway/experimental proofs against pinned SDK 2.0.0 and select Cyril's target runtime architecture before production migration begins.

Compare three real options:

1. direct hidden-SDK adoption;
2. a proxy-ready private component/endpoint seam with direct and conductor-backed implementations; and
3. conductor-first production topology with zero or more official proxy components.

The spike must investigate proxies, conductor, tracing, MCP attachment, frame inspection, and reusable components as first-class options. ADR-0003 and the ROADMAP are historical evidence, not constraints.

## Required experiments

- **E1 Component boundary:** prove how SDK `Send + 'static` handlers/components interact with Cyril's `Rc`/`RefCell` engine and mediator. Prefer a bounded Send protocol actor → serial domain actor handoff; reject unsafe and blanket shared-lock conversion.
- **E2 Frame integrity:** pass single, batch, malformed, Kiro extension, unknown nested update, and extreme-number frames through SDK channels/inspection and record semantic/lexical preservation.
- **E3 Handler semantics:** prove static registration order, untyped-before-typed containment, fallthrough/claim behavior, forwarding, cancellation, dynamic-handler lifetime, and dispatch-loop nonblocking rules.
- **E4 Process parity:** compare current `AgentProcess` with `AcpAgent` for cwd, stderr diagnostics, process-group/grandchild cleanup, non-zero exit, stall, cancellation, EOF, and shutdown grace. Record whether an upstream cwd enhancement or custom component is required.
- **E5 Direct Kiro parity:** run stable wire-v1 initialize/session/prompt/permission/extension/host-callback flows for v2 and KAS through the SDK direct path; compare normalized Engine/SourceObserver output and turn/error ordering.
- **E6 Conductor parity:** run the same flows through `ConductorImpl::new_agent` with zero proxies, a no-op proxy, and a transforming proxy. Verify lazy initialization, successor envelopes, response identity, cancellation, Kiro extension forwarding, KAS callbacks, and EOF/crash behavior.
- **E7 Real proxy leverage:** prove at least one useful bidirectional concern—context injection, trace/observation, policy interception, or native MCP attachment/polyfill—rather than stopping at transparent forwarding.
- **E8 Observer/fan-out:** characterize a slow observer, permission request while streaming, backpressure, ordering, disconnect, and replay. Explicitly determine what the linear conductor does not solve and whether a separate broadcaster is required.
- **E9 Memory parity:** compare current prompt injection/normalized capture with a proxy/tap for exactly-once behavior, byte budgets, cancellation, session/project identity, and terminal disposition. Do not move the current adapter unless parity passes.
- **E10 Version boundary:** demonstrate SDK 2 on stable ACP wire v1 and separately probe feature-gated draft wire v2 routing without enabling it in production.

## Deliverables

- Reproducible experiment code/captures in the repo's existing experiments convention.
- A new ADR selecting the target topology and explicitly superseding/amending stale parts of ADR-0003.
- A concrete implementation issue/commit decomposition with clean rollback boundaries and no speculative permanent crate or trait.
- Upstream SDK issues/PR proposals for any blocking gap such as process cwd, rather than silently reimplementing broad SDK behavior.

## Non-goals

- Production dependency cutover.
- Shipping draft ACP wire v2.
- Rewriting App/UI/domain state.
- Creating an empty `cyril-stages` crate or placeholder proxy.
- Claiming conductor provides multi-client fan-out without proof.
design:
## Decision rule

- **Option A, direct-only:** choose only if SDK component/handler parity has a reproducible blocker. Record the future insertion point.
- **Option B, proxy-ready endpoint seam:** default hypothesis. It is acceptable only if direct and conductor-backed components pass the same contract suite; one hypothetical adapter is not a seam.
- **Option C, conductor-first:** choose when E5/E6 pass and E7 demonstrates concrete leverage without duplicating Engine conversion, host-callback ownership, or domain observers.

## Architectural constraints

- Preserve `BridgeCommand`, `RoutedNotification`, permission/source events, and the App-facing bridge contract unless the spike proves that interface blocks the selected topology.
- Keep `Engine`/adapters/convert Kiro-scoped. Proxy stages and KAS host callbacks are complementary boundaries.
- Register the unknown standard-update handler statically before typed `SessionNotification`; do not rely on unordered dynamic-handler storage.
- SDK owns frames, batching, response routing, cancellation, proxy envelopes, and conductor routing. Cyril owns domain conversion and observable turn/error/source invariants.
- `SourceObserver` is a normalized domain observer; `Channel::bridge_with_inspection` and conductor tracing are wire observers. Treat them as different contracts.
- No `AgentRuntime`/`AgentEndpoint` trait merely to rename current channels. Introduce a permanent abstraction only when the experiments produce two real adapters or select conductor as the one concrete path.

## Evidence standard

Every conclusion must name the exact SDK type/symbol, input trace, observed output/order, and retained/deleted Cyril module. Compile success alone is not architecture evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/acp-sdk-2-architecture-research.md` is reviewed against the exact pinned SDK 2.0.0 sources used by the experiments.
- [ ] E1 proves a safe Send SDK actor/domain-mediator ownership model or records a minimal reproducible blocker.
- [ ] E2 proves frame/batch/malformed/extension/unknown-update/extreme-number behavior without weakening the existing forward-compatibility fence.
- [ ] E3 proves handler order/fallthrough, forwarding, cancellation, and nonblocking dispatch with a reversed/removed unknown-first mutation expected to fail.
- [ ] E4 records process lifecycle parity and an explicit keep/replace/upstream decision for `AgentProcess` versus `AcpAgent`.
- [ ] E5 runs Kiro v2 and KAS stable-v1 direct parity, including permission and every advertised host-callback family.
- [ ] E6 runs the same matrix through zero-proxy, no-op-proxy, and transforming-proxy conductor paths and records exact divergences.
- [ ] E7 demonstrates one real proxy capability end to end.
- [ ] E8 states the conductor's proven observer/fan-out limits and the required backpressure/ownership model.
- [ ] E9 records a keep/move decision for memory injection and normalized source capture based on adapter-neutral parity.
- [ ] E10 keeps SDK version and wire version separate; draft protocol v2 remains production-disabled.
- [ ] A new ADR selects direct, proxy-ready, or conductor-first topology using evidence, not age-weighted prior ADR authority.
- [ ] The selected design keeps ACP types inside `cyril-core` and preserves or explicitly migrates every App-facing contract.
- [ ] Follow-on Rivets implementation issues are filed with independently green, clean-cutover slices; no production migration starts inside this spike.
- [ ] Any temporary prototype that is not retained as reproducible experiment evidence is removed.

notes.content: Filed as the first child of cyril-1gfe after the SDK 2.0 architecture review. Official sources: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/rust-sdk, https://agentclientprotocol.github.io/rust-sdk/design.html, https://agentclientprotocol.github.io/rust-sdk/conductor.html, and https://docs.rs/agent-client-protocol/2.0.0/agent_client_protocol/concepts/proxies/.

title: Watch: KAS 0.8.0 new surface _kiro/knowledge/indexing{Started,Completed} + _kiro/sandbox/applyConfig
description: The only net-new _kiro/* methods in @kiro/agent 0.3.299->0.8.0 (73->76, zero removals). notes.content:
LIVE-PROBED 2026-07-02 (probe-kas-knowledge-indexing-2.11.0.py). indexing{Started,Completed} = agent->client extNotifications (fire-and-forget; no client cap needed). Started {sessionId,name,fileCount}; Completed {sessionId,name,status,itemCount?} (itemCount only status='success'). --- CYRIL SCOPING (2026-07-02): NO WIRE ADDITION REQUIRED to be upgrade-safe. --- DESIGN SKETCH (2026-07-02, PROPOSAL — not built). A knowledge progress panel styled like crew_panel (bordered block, cyan ` knowledge ` title, `{icon} ` + bold-white `{name:<20}` + status, `+N more` overflow). One row per base; spinner (SPINNER_CHARS) while between Started/Completed, ✓ green (success)/✗ red (failed) once settled. Each row = one wire event:

  ⠋ indexing    -> indexingStarted {fileCount}   (fast/BM25)

title: KAS-8 — Model _meta.kiro.hookConfirm + KAS agent-file hook types; render Stop-hook confirm dialogs
description:
From the 2026-07-17 KAS agent-file schema export (kiro-cli 2.13.0 / @kiro/agent 0.18.2; docs/kiro-kas-agent-*-schema-2.13.0.*, experiments/kas-agent-schema-export/): KAS agent files can embed inline hooks (landed 2.12.3) with a 'confirm' block that is honored on the Stop/agentStop trigger — when the agent tries to end its turn, the user is asked confirm.question with confirm.options[]; run:true options execute the hook command (whose output decides {continue, reason}), run:false options skip it and, with continueReason set, convert the turn-stop into keep-working with that reason fed to the agent (verified in src/hooks/triggers/stop.ts).

Wire shape (rides plain ACP, no new method): synthetic pending tool_call (toolCallId hook-confirm-<uuid>, kind 'other') tagged _meta.kiro.hookConfirm {kind:'stop', hookName, question} -> standard session/request_permission (optionId=option.id, name=label, kind=allow_once if run else reject_once) -> terminal tool_call_update with _meta.kiro.hookConfirm.decision.

Cyril work: (1) model the _meta.kiro.hookConfirm payload in convert/kas.rs (pending + decision variants) per the model-full-wire-surface rule; (2) render hook-confirm approvals as a distinct dialog (hook name + question) instead of a generic tool permission — note cyril filters kind-Other tool_calls from display, so without the _meta tag the pending marker is invisible and the permission prompt shows with no context; (3) verify the permission-response path returns arbitrary optionIds — a confirm block can have MULTIPLE reject_once options distinguished only by optionId/continueReason (cyril-qo13 fixed first-option-only for kind-keyed responses; confirm that fix covers this shape); (4) optionally: type the agent-file HookDocument/HookConfirm/HookAction shapes (committed JSON Schemas are the reference) for any future hooks-panel display of KAS inline hooks — current hooks panel models v2 HookInfo {trigger, command, matcher} only.

Semantics caveats for tests: confirm is Stop-trigger-only (schema allows it anywhere; other triggers ignore it); with no UI attached KAS skips confirm-hooks entirely, so absence of the dialog is not absence of the hook.
acceptance_criteria: convert/kas.rs parses _meta.kiro.hookConfirm (pending question + terminal decision) with unknown-field logging; approval overlay shows hook name + question for hookConfirm requests; regression test proving a 3-option confirm (run/skip/keep-working) can return each optionId; decision recorded on KAS inline-hook display in the hooks panel.

notes.content: WIRE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 (probe-kas-hook-confirm-2.13.0.py, capture kas-hook-confirm-2.13.0.json, all 6 verdicts PASS): (1) pending tool_call hook-confirm-<uuid> kind=other + _meta.kiro.hookConfirm {kind:stop, hookName, question}; (2) requestPermission options run:true->allow_once, run:false->reject_once; (3) continueReason injected as NEW human message wrapped <HOOK_INSTRUCTION>...</HOOK_INSTRUCTION> + graph restart — agent obeyed it (HELLOTURTLES); (4) terminal tool_call_update carries decision=<optionId> with status=FAILED for reject_once picks — rendering caveat: a successful keep-working choice arrives as a failed tool call; (5) once-per-turn guard onAgentStopHooksExecuted (shared-graph-nodes.ts): stop hooks fire at most ONCE per turn, continuation runs unguarded to end_turn; (6) handshake gate = clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.hooks {enabled:true, v2:true} — v2 activates the standalone .kiro/hooks/*.json loader; fresh-git-dir ACP session counted workspaceTrusted.

title: Usage-observer stage: vendor-neutral usage/stats dashboard (omp-parity)
description:
Replicate omp's `omp stats` dashboard (localhost:3847) as a composable cyril observer stage — a per-turn usage-log aggregator + viewer, vendor-neutral by construction. Motivated by the user's running omp dashboard; feasibility mapped 2026-08-21 (memory reference_omp_stats_dashboard, docs/kiro-2.19.1-wire-audit.md OTLP model sweep).

WHAT omp SHOWS (12 /api/stats/* endpoints, source = per-request usage records in ~/.omp/agent/sessions/*.jsonl, each carrying usage{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite,totalTokens,cost{...}}): overview (requests, tokens, cacheRate, cacheSavings, $cost, avgDuration, TTFT, tokens/sec, timeSeries, byAgentType), costs (per-model/provider split), providers, model-dashboard, tools (per-tool calls/errors/tokensShare/costShare), behavior (assistant-text sentiment — engine-agnostic), errors, recent, folders, gain (compaction savings).

THE LOAD-BEARING ASYMMETRY: omp has real token counts + $cost because it is the direct provider-API caller (usage returned per response, cost = price-table multiply). kiro routes through CodeWhisperer's credit abstraction which STRIPS token counts — proven absent across 6 models / 5 providers via the OTLP redirect (metadataEvent.tokenUsage not populated for the Tethys/IdC account). So the token/$cost/cacheRate/cacheSavings/tokens-per-sec panels have NO client-side data for kiro; everything else does, with credits substituted for cost.

SHAPE: an observer/usage-log proxy stage that writes one record per turn from whatever the wire provides, plus an aggregation viewer. Two phases below. Fits the platform vision (composable stages, fan-out observer) — reference_omp_stats_dashboard, project_cyril_platform_vision, project_cyril_enhancing_proxy.
acceptance_criteria: Epic done when both child phases ship: (P1) full-fidelity usage dashboard when driving a standard-ACP agent that emits usage_update (omp); (P2) credits-degraded mode for kiro v2/KAS. Stage is opt-in, degrades gracefully per engine, and no engine-specific assumptions leak into the aggregation/viewer layer.

notes.content: Framing clarification (do not mis-read P1 as "omp integration"): omp is the DEVELOPMENT VEHICLE, not the target. Three reasons the infrastructure is useful regardless of omp usage: (1) the P1 capture reads PromptResponse.usage = STANDARD ACP Usage (cyril already enables unstable_session_usage) — it captures token usage from ANY ACP agent that populates the field, not omp specifically. omp is just the one agent we have that populates it TODAY, so it is the only way to build+validate the full-fidelity record schema against real token/cache/cost data. (2) the log/aggregate/view substrate + client-measured duration/TTFT + tool-call tracking are engine-agnostic and reused wholesale by P2 (kiro credits-mode) — building them once serves every engine. (3) forward-compatible: if kiro/KAS ever populates the standard usage slot (or a backend rollout starts sending tokenUsage), cyril lights up for free, no code change. For a kiro-primary user TODAY: credits-as-cost + per-tool credit attribution + client TTFT/duration + context% + errors + per-model/folder grouping all work; only true token counts are absent (backend-gated). So building P1-against-omp FIRST is correct even for a kiro-only user — it develops the complete substrate with a working data source, so P2/kiro slots in without rediscovering the schema.
Closed: Both child phases shipped: cyril-gfkm and cyril-kryv are closed; PRs #100, #97, #98, and #99 merged with full CI and live v2/KAS acceptance.

title: Process: parallel sessions share one working dir — hitchhiker commits + rebase drops (3rd occurrence)
description: Parallel Claude sessions committing in the same checkout keep landing commits on whichever branch is checked out, and relocation rebases have dropped commits twice (d67e5b8 rivets rows lost, restored by e6ba5c6; transport-layering ROADMAP point re-applied by fa376ec). Third occurrence of the class this run — see .cyril-tpfd/review-decisions.md P3 + R2-8. Fix direction: one git worktree per session (git worktree add), never share a checkout between concurrent sessions; sessions must verify branch before every commit until then.

description:
