title: KAS discovery/auth type-shape cleanup: thiserror errors, parsed ExtractionDir candidates, KiroVersion newtype, injectable gate wiring
description: Deferred design findings from the PR-39 5-agent review (decisions in .cyril-dcc6/review-decisions.md). All verified-real, deferred as a refactor cluster: (1) KasMissing has no Display/Error impl and collapses to String one frame after creation (bridge.rs resolve_spawn_command) — derive thiserror::Error; (2) read_sqlite_store/store_unservable_reason use Result<_,String>/Option<String> — a small StoreError enum (Absent/LoggedOut/Corrupt/Locked/Stale) would let the gate, responder, and tests match variants instead of err.contains() substrings; (3) discovery candidates are (String,bool) tuples parsed INSIDE select_server — an ExtractionDir{name,version,has_server} struct parsed at listing time makes the policy parse-don't-validate; (4) the (u32,u32,u32) semver tuple escaped version.rs — a KiroVersion newtype with Display; (5) resolve_kas_command's login-gate ordering is only live-covered — thread the store path/check through for a unit fence.

title: KAS-2b — Live context-usage breakdown bar (session_info_update:context_usage)
description:
On KAS (v3), the per-category context breakdown is PUSHED proactively on the wire — so cyril can render a live categorized context bar (Files / Tools / Prompts / Responses) in the toolbar WITHOUT the user running /context. On v1/v2 the breakdown only exists as the pulled /context command response; the streaming _kiro.dev/metadata notification there carries only the scalar contextUsagePercentage.

WIRE SHAPE (probe-verified, kiro-cli 2.8.0, 2026-06-19, live KAS turn):
- session/update -> session_info_update, _meta.kiro.kind == 'context_usage', payload {usagePercentage, breakdown?} (covenant ContextUsageBreakdown).
- breakdown = 5 buckets {contextFiles, tools, kiroResponses, yourPrompts, sessionFiles}, each {tokens, percent, items?}.
- ~6 frames pushed per turn.

CONSTRAINTS THAT SHAPE THE UI (all probe-verified):
1. tools bucket is AGGREGATE-ONLY — items is structurally absent (live: {tokens:33703, percent:3.4}). Only contextFiles/sessionFiles ever carry items[]. Do NOT build per-tool drill-down; the wire cannot support it on either engine.
2. breakdown is OPTIONAL PER FRAME — some context_usage frames carry usagePercentage only (breakdown absent). Retain last non-absent; treat absence as 'no update', not 'cleared' (same discipline as the effort field).
3. cyril's existing /context path (kiro.dev/commands/execute) is REJECTED by KAS (-32603 'no persistence classification'). Must read the streaming notification, not the command surface.

MAPPING: breakdown is richer than cyril's flat ContextUsage/TokenCounts — either map usagePercentage to ContextUsage + extend, or model the breakdown as a new type. The itemized buckets can reuse the existing render helper append_context_items (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:900), today wired only to the pulled /context path.

DEPENDS ON: KAS-2a (walking skeleton — turn renders+ends via session_info_update:turn_end; not yet filed). Part of the KAS-2 _kiro/* dialect track, anchored on KAS-0 (cyril-atjw).

REFS: probe experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-context-breakdown-2.8.0.py; ROADMAP KAS-2b (docs/ROADMAP.md:179).
acceptance_criteria:
* On the KAS engine, cyril renders a live categorized context bar fed by session_info_update:context_usage frames — no /context command issued.
* Per-frame 'breakdown absent' is handled: last breakdown retained, not cleared.
* tools bucket renders as an aggregate row (no per-tool UI); contextFiles/sessionFiles render itemized when items[] is present.
* v1/v2 engine behavior is unchanged (still uses the pulled /context command response).
* State + render tests cover (a) a breakdown-absent frame and (b) the aggregate-only tools bucket.

notes.content:
2026-06-21 — Re-confirmed the 5-bucket breakdown independently (experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-context-shows-steering.py): contextFiles itemized the file the agent read; tools aggregate-only (33703 tokens, no items); the v2 /context (kiro.dev/commands/execute) rejected. RELEVANT NEGATIVE for this bar: the breakdown has NO steering bucket and does not itemize steering docs. Steering is a SEPARATE channel (_kiro/steering/documents_changed catalog + session_info_update:steering_inclusion) — so do NOT try to source an 'active rules/steering' view from the context bar; it isn't there. See memory reference_kiro_kas_filematch_steering_source.

Closed: Implemented and merged via PR #33 (merge 9aca2fe); follow-up review fixes in 56f57ec. Deferred items tracked: cyril-1116 (per-file drill-in), cyril-mdbp (narrow-terminal overflow), cyril-cx27 (SessionController lifecycle divergence).
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-2b

title: Steal KAS multi-client observer pattern for cyril's multi-client-observers proxy-stage
description:
Adopt the multi-client observer topology KAS ships (MultiplexStream, discovered in the 2.14.0 audit — @kiro/agent 0.22.7) as the reference design for cyril's platform-vision 'multi-client observers' stage (see project_cyril_platform_vision + CLAUDE.md). Goal: let more than one client (a second TUI, a web view, an audit/observer stage) attach to a running cyril session and observe/participate WITHOUT owning it.

WHY IT'S A GOOD FIT: cyril today is a single stdio client to one agent (effectively always the 'primary'). The observer pattern would live in cyril's proxy-stage / bridge layer, above the single agent connection. cyril already has a PARTIAL precedent: RoutedNotification routes by session_id and fans session notifications to per-subagent streams (CLAUDE.md 'Subagent Support') — that is session-scoped fan-out, which is half the pattern.

REFERENCE: docs/kiro-2.14.1-wire-audit.md (KAS section) + the shipped, commented multiplex-stream.d.ts. Full mechanism write-up in that doc. This is a DESIGN/RESEARCH capture, not a ready-to-build spec — no urgency, no emitter dependency; forward-looking for the enhancing-proxy platform work.
design:
Concrete elements to steal from KAS MultiplexStream:

1. ONE agent connection, MANY attached clients. Fan-in: merge inbound from all clients into the single agent stream, rewriting request IDs to avoid cross-client collisions (restore on the way back). Fan-out: demux agent responses to the originating client by rewritten ID.

2. DECOUPLE request identity from connection identity (the key insight). Agent-initiated requests (permission, user-input) get correlated on a STABLE DOMAIN HANDLE (toolCallId) that every client can see, NOT the connection-bound JSON-RPC id. The mux owns the toolCallId->id map; any client answers via a respond-by-toolCallId method (KAS: _kiro/permission/respond, _kiro/userInput/respond), acked fire-and-forget, and the mux synthesizes the real JSON-RPC response to resolve the agent's pending Promise. This is what makes 'a different client than the one that got the request can answer it' work.

3. PRIMARY vs OBSERVER roles. Primary: resolves permissions via normal JSON-RPC responses, receives ALL agent-initiated requests incl. fs/terminal. Observer: acks immediately, resolves async by toolCallId, direct responses suppressed, does NOT receive fs/terminal. Default = observer. cyril decision: are observers read-only, or can they answer permissions/steer?

4. SESSION-SCOPED notification fan-out. Subscriber map (sessionId -> set of clientIds); broadcast session updates only to subscribers. Two invariants, each from a shipped KAS bug: (a) cross-session isolation (ungated broadcast leaks session A's stream to a client viewing session B); (b) no replay bleed (a loading client's history-replay must unicast on its own path, not fan out into another client's live turn). cyril's RoutedNotification is the seam to extend.

5. SAFETY RAILS: TTL sweeps for stale pending permissions/inputs; double-resolve guards; reject malformed respond (bare {toolCallId} w/o action) with -32602 so a client can't silently consume a pending prompt.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR CYRIL: (a) transport — observers attach to CYRIL (its bridge/App), not to the agent; what protocol (local socket? another ACP leg?); (b) where the mux lives (bridge vs a new proxy-stage); (c) interaction with the existing one-turn guard + RoutedNotification routing; (d) does this compose with the conductor proxy-chain (project_cyril_conductor_integration)?

notes.content:
TRANSPORT LAYERING (from 2.14.1 audit follow-up — evidence in scratchpad carve of @kiro/agent 0.22.7 acp-server.js): the KAS mux is NOT an ACP feature and does NOT run over the ACP wire. Two distinct entry points prove it: startStdio() binds KiroAgent DIRECTLY to a single ndjson stream over process.stdin/stdout (NO mux); startWebSocket() (port 8082) constructs new MultiplexStream() and binds KiroAgent to mux.stream. So the MultiplexStream exists ONLY on KAS's WebSocket server path. cyril spawns KAS over stdio (startStdio), so cyril is the sole ACP peer, answers session/request_permission + _kiro/userInput with normal JSON-RPC responses, and NEVER sees the primary/observer roles or the respond-by-toolCallId methods (those are mux-coordination messages the mux intercepts — they never reach the agent).

DESIGN IMPLICATION FOR CYRIL: multiplexing is a transport/connection-management adapter that sits ABOVE the agent's single ACP endpoint, not on the ACP protocol. If cyril builds multi-client observers, cyril runs its OWN mux ABOVE its single stdio ACP link to kiro-cli, over whatever transport cyril picks for observers to attach to CYRIL (local socket, another process, etc.) — NOT over the agent's ACP wire. The agent link stays strictly 1:1. Topology maps cleanly: KAS's 'one agent conn + mux + N clients' becomes for cyril 'one stdio ACP link to the agent + a cyril-side mux (in the bridge/App) + N observer TUIs/web views'. cyril is NOT constrained to express observer-attach over ACP, and does NOT need the toolCallId-respond methods to speak KAS.

title: Render the todo_list tool as the plan view — kiro-cli never emits the ACP plan variant
description:
convert/mod.rs:434 decodes SessionUpdate::Plan, but kiro-cli 2.14.0 never sends it (KiroCrew types.py:241: "kiro-cli 2.14.0 never emits plan, so UPDATE_PLAN below stays inert and the TODO list is recovered from this tool rawOutput instead"). Cyril is decoding a variant that never arrives while ignoring the tool call that carries the real data.

Wire shape:
  rawOutput = {"items":[{"Json": {description, tasks:[{id, task_description|description|text, completed: bool}]}}]}

Facts that matter for rendering:
- Identified ONLY by _meta.kiro.toolName == "todo_list". The visible title is LLM prose ("Creating task list: ..."), not a discriminator. Depends on cyril-2yn8.
- Every todo command (create/complete/list) echoes the WHOLE list — always a full snapshot, never a delta.
- completed is a plain bool; there is no in-progress state on 2.14.0.
- Caps: 200 tasks, 500 chars each.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 2.1, 4.2.
acceptance_criteria: A todo_list tool call renders as a plan/checklist rather than a generic tool pill; each update replaces the list wholesale. The dead Plan arm is either removed or documented as v2-never-sent.

title: tethys blast-radius step misses cross-module callers: only --lsp finds them, bare == --exclude-speculative
description:
tethys's DB-only resolver does not find cross-module callers, and the documented
"recall net" tier does not recover them either. Only `--lsp` does. This matters
because /sweep-bugs and /ship both use `tethys callers` as the blast-radius step,
where a false negative ships a bug.

(Supersedes cyril-znv8, which was filed on the wrong premise that
`--exclude-speculative` did not exist. It does; the binary on PATH was 363
commits stale. That issue is closed as invalid. This one is the real, measured
finding, taken on a freshly built tethys.)

## Measurement (cyril @ 5f23d51, tethys @ 1473239, 2026-08-02)

Fresh `tethys index --rebuild` — 98 files, 3900 symbols, 29195 references.

  symbol                       bare      --exclude-speculative   --lsp
  UiState::show_picker         12 / 3f   12 / 3f                 14 / 4f
  parse_options_response       11 / 1f   11 / 1f                 12 / 2f
  NotificationRoute             1 / 1f    1 / 1f                  3 / 1f
  classify_notification_route   1 / 1f    1 / 1f                  2 / 1f
  ActiveTurn                    2 / 1f    2 / 1f                  2 / 1f
  split_active_label_suffix     1 / 1f    1 / 1f                  1 / 1f

Two findings:

1. **bare == --exclude-speculative on every symbol tested.** AGENTS.md step 3
   describes a bare invocation as the "recall net" that includes the speculative
   band. On this workspace it returns results identical to the precision tier —
   it recovers nothing. Whatever the cross-module edges are, they are not in the
   speculative band; they are simply absent from the DB resolver's output.

2. **Only --lsp finds production callers.** The extras it surfaces are not
   marginal — they are the entire production call surface:
   - `UiState::show_picker`: `App::handle_notification` (app.rs:426, the live
     picker path) and `App::handle_command_result` (app.rs:863). The 12 that
     bare/ES return are ALL tests. So the precision tier reports a function as
     called only by its own tests when it is in fact on the hot path.
   - `parse_options_response`: `run_loop` at bridge.rs:1430, the sole production
     caller, via `super::convert::kiro::parse_options_response(&value)` — a
     path-qualified cross-module call.

## Why it matters

Blast radius is a RECALL question. A false positive costs a minute of reading; a
false negative ships a bug. The tiering as documented inverts that: it leads with
precision, and its recall fallback is (here) a no-op.

Empirically this was survivable only because the skills also mandate `grep`. In
the 2026-08-02 sweep all three agents found their real callers via rg and
explicitly reported tethys had missed them. Had they trusted the tool as the
docs instruct, `show_picker` and `parse_options_response` would both have been
changed with their production callers unexamined.

## Done already

- `/sweep-bugs` and `/ship` updated to specify `tethys callers <Type::method>
  --lsp`, require QUALIFIED names, note the mutual exclusivity, and keep grep as
  the authority. (`.claude/skills/{sweep-bugs,ship}/SKILL.md`)
- Stale binary replaced: `~/.local/bin/tethys` was built 2026-06-30, 363 commits
  behind. Rebuilt and installed from `~/repos/tethys` 2026-08-02.

## Open questions for tethys

1. Should the DB resolver bind path-qualified cross-module calls
   (`super::convert::kiro::f(..)`, `crate::a::b::f(..)`)? These are statically
   unambiguous — no receiver inference needed — so this looks like resolvable
   recall left on the table rather than an inherent limit.
2. AGENTS.md step 3 should be corrected or explained: if bare is meant to be the
   recall tier, it is not behaving as one here. tethys-k543 is referenced as the
   "LSP recovery tier" — if LSP is in practice the only working recall tier, the
   dogfooding doc should lead with it.
3. `tethys --version` is a hardcoded `0.1.0` that never bumps, so it cannot
   distinguish builds. That is what let a 363-commit-stale binary masquerade as
   current and produce a full page of false conclusions. Consider embedding the
   git describe / build date.
4. Unknown flags print `error:` to stderr but EXIT 0, so `cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
   echo OK` reports success on a failed invocation. Non-zero exit on arg-parse
   failure would make misuse visible.

title: Model KAS _kiro/workflow/* progress protocol (9-event DAG; emitter shipped 2.16.0, 3 captures committed)
description:
Model the KAS _kiro/workflow/* DAG progress protocol.

UNBLOCKED as of kiro-cli 2.16.0 (KAS @kiro/agent 0.27.8) — the deferral
condition ("until an emitter ships") is MET. See docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md.

Emitter: src/workflow/workflow-notification-bridge.ts maps 9 event kinds to
methods, each emitting {...payload, parentSessionId?}:
  run_start node_start node_complete node_paused loop_iteration
  watch_poll paused run_complete steps_queued
Auto-unsubscribes on run_complete with a terminal status; buffered pending
events are flushed on subscribe, so attaching late does not lose the opening.

Control methods (14): invoke cancel pause resume resumeAll retry list
listRecipes listWatchHandlers load new delete inspect update.
NOT advertised in extensionMethods (still 7) — discovery is out-of-band.

Gate: resolveWorkflows() = settings.workflows.enabled ?? false. Opt in via
session/new _meta.kiro.settings.workflows.enabled=true; the resolved value is
reported back as session/new._meta.workflowsEnabled (new field in 2.16.0).

Live-verified 2026-07-30 (probe-kas-workflow-runtime-2.16.0.py, zero credits):
workflowsEnabled=true; list -> {runs:[]} (needs explicit workspacePaths, else
-32603 "workspacePaths is not iterable"); listRecipes -> 7 bundled recipes;
listWatchHandlers -> github-pr + crux-cr.

ARCHITECTURE: workflow steps are FULL PEER SESSIONS (host.newSession per step),
not subagents — correlated by _meta.kiro.workflow.workflowId. Confirms the
session-level design decision already recorded for cyril. Do NOT route these
through SubagentTracker.

Node types are step, repeat, and parallel (a real DAG scheduler, not a chain).
design:
ACTIVE. The deferral condition ("until an emitter ships") was MET by kiro-cli
2.16.0 / @kiro/agent 0.27.8 and the shapes are live-captured, not inferred.
Build against docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md. The former "DEFERRED -- do not
build UI against this protocol" instruction is superseded; see the note dated
2026-08-08 for what it said and why it is wrong now.

RECOGNITION -- simpler than the 2.14.1 guess. These are plain JSON-RPC
notifications: method _kiro/workflow/<kind>, params = the event payload flattened
with parentSessionId injected. They do NOT ride user_message_chunk and carry no
_meta.kiro.notification.kind marker. There is also NO top-level sessionId, so
client.rs promotes them to RoutedNotification::global and they reach the main
pipeline unchanged -- the EVENTS need no routing work. (The step SESSIONS are a
separate problem: cyril-jxfu.)

SHAPE OF THE WORK
  - Converter: 9 arms in convert. Today _kiro/workflow/* falls through the
    unknown-extension-notification debug! arm in convert/kiro.rs and is dropped.
  - State: a pure cyril-core state machine on the SubagentTracker pattern --
    apply_notification(&Notification) -> bool. No async, no bridge access, no UI
    knowledge.
  - Scope boundary: the gate flip (initialize _meta.kiro.settings
    workflows.enabled -- carve from cyril-ea67) and the panel/drill-in rendering
    are each separate work. This issue is protocol + state only.

THE SIX HAZARDS ARE THE SPEC
  1. run_complete does NOT mean the run finished -- it is emitted with
     status "paused" too (live-observed on repeat exhaustion). Only completed /
     failed / aborted are terminal. Treating arrival as end-of-run tears down a
     live, resumable workflow.
  2. node_start fires TWICE per step node; the second carries sessionId. Merge on
     (workflowId, nodeId, nodePath) with partial-field guards -- the same
     discipline as ToolCallUpdate merge_update. Never append. On the resume path
     the re-emit does not happen, so the emission count is not fixed.
  3. steps_queued is overloaded: populated pendingSteps with NO resolution key,
     versus a bare ack with pendingSteps [] plus resolution.outcome. Empty does
     not mean drained.
  4. Step completion rides send_message severity, not the workflow protocol. A
     step outcome is decided by a model-issued tool call, so node_complete is not
     a reliable liveness signal (run-liveness.ts force-pauses stale running
     nodes for exactly this reason).
  5. paused and node_paused are INDEPENDENT, not paired. maxIterations
     exhaustion emitted paused only, node_paused zero times.
  6. nodePath is the only stable node identity. node_complete omits iteration and
     a repeat reuses the same nodeId every pass. Also: finalState names iteration
     wrappers loop#0 / loop#1 while nodePath uses iter-0 / iter-1 -- the two
     schemes DO NOT MATCH and must be translated.

ALSO
  - node_start.prompt carries the RAW, un-interpolated template. Rendering it
    shows template source, not what the agent received.
  - _kiro/workflow/new returns {workflowId, initialState} -- the whole initial
    tree up front, so a client does not need run_start to learn the plan.
  - node_paused is the one payload of nine never observed live (three attempts).
    Treat its {workflowId, nodeId, nodePath, reason} shape as static-only.

OFFLINE, ZERO-CREDIT TDD. Three live captures are already committed:
  experiments/conductor-spike/kas-custom-dag-2.16.0.jsonl     (parallel DAG)
  experiments/conductor-spike/kas-repeat-watch-2.16.0.jsonl   (repeat + watch + steps_queued)
  experiments/conductor-spike/kas-nodepaused-2.16.0.jsonl     (negative: no node_paused)
Fixture-replay is the oracle; no credits and no live agent needed.

The near-term agent-subtask tool-call rendering work is cyril-ebqu -- a DIFFERENT
channel. Workflow steps deliberately do not ride SubagentTracker.

notes.content:
TWO LAYERS (2.14.1 audit, docs/kiro-2.14.1-wire-audit.md): the _kiro/workflow/* PROTOCOL is a facade on BOTH ends — no emitter (KAS 0.22.7 and v2 Rust both zero), and tui.js is parser/converter-only scaffolding: convertAcpUpdateToEvent produces a workflow_progress stream event that appears exactly ONCE in the bundle (the production site), with no consumer, no WorkflowPanel and no renderer. Parse-and-drop.

But the DAG orchestration CAPABILITY it would visualize is real and executing — OrchestrateSubAgent's buildSchema carries task -> stages[] ({name, role, prompt_template, depends_on, inlineAgent?}) plus a repeat block (maxIterations 1-20, stopCondition.containsText, onMaxIterations continue/abort), and the executor runs the loop. Evidence is static (bundle schema + executor read), not a live capture; the 2.14.1 wire capture is still pending.

It reports through the ordinary agent-subtask tool-call channel today, NOT this protocol. That near-term path is cyril-ebqu (split out 2026-07-26 during PR #68 review); this issue is the deferred protocol half only.

Payload shapes now documented: docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md 'Event payload shapes' (all 9 events, NodeDescriptor/WorkflowState/nodePath sub-shapes, enum domains).

Three hazards recorded there that the implementation must handle:
1. node_start fires TWICE per step node (pre-session, then re-emitted with sessionId from onSessionCreated) — merge on (workflowId,nodeId,nodePath), never append. Emission count is NOT fixed: on the resume path sessionId rides the first emission and the re-emit is skipped.
2. steps_queued is overloaded — populated pendingSteps vs a bare ack with pendingSteps:[] + resolution.outcome. Empty != drained.
3. Step completion rides a MODEL-ISSUED send_message call (severity success/warning/fault -> nodeState.completionSignal), not the workflow protocol. If the agent omits it the node sits paused. node_complete is not a reliable liveness signal; run-liveness.ts force-pauses stale running nodes.

Routing note: these notifications carry NO top-level sessionId — workflowId is the only correlation key, so RoutedNotification session-matching will not route them.

LIVE VERIFIED 2026-07-31: a CLIENT-authored inline DAG executes end-to-end. probe-kas-custom-dag-live-2.16.0.py + capture kas-custom-dag-2.16.0.jsonl (parallel/joinPolicy:all, two wf-coder steps, ~4.7s, completed).

Confirms: _kiro/workflow/new accepts an inline workflow object from the client (no model involvement) and invoke runs it; the double node_start is real; steps ARE peer sessions (3 distinct sessionIds on session/update); nodePath, NodeDescriptor and the optional-field guards match the documented shapes; parentSessionId is injected on every event; completionSignal:success lands on the step NodeStates.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the static read:
1. _kiro/workflow/new returns {workflowId, initialState} — the FULL WorkflowState, not {workflowId,status}. A client has the whole plan before run_start.
2. WorkflowState also carries parentSessionId and workspacePath (absent from initState()).
3. NodeState carries startedAt as well as endedAt.

GOTCHA: node_start.prompt is the RAW un-interpolated template ({{token}}, not the substituted value) — interpolation happens downstream of the notification.

STILL STATIC-ONLY (not exercised by this run): node_paused, paused, steps_queued, loop_iteration, watch_poll.

PHASE 2 LIVE VERIFICATION 2026-07-31 (probe-kas-workflow-repeat-watch-2.16.0.py, capture kas-repeat-watch-2.16.0.jsonl). 8 of 9 payload shapes now live-verified.

VERIFIED: watch_poll (outcome terminal-state, github-pr handler on a merged PR — watch nodes are NON-LLM so this phase is FREE), loop_iteration (iteration is ZERO-INDEXED), paused, steps_queued (populated-list form, NO resolution key). nodePath 'iter-<n>' confirmed verbatim: ['wf_...','loop','iter-0','tick']. Double node_start holds inside repeat too.

STILL STATIC-ONLY: node_paused (0 emissions — see pairing correction).

THREE MORE CORRECTIONS:
4. run_complete does NOT mean finished — emitted with status:'paused' (non-terminal, bridge stays subscribed). MUST check status or a client tears down a live resumable workflow. This is now hazard #1.
5. paused and node_paused are INDEPENDENT, not paired. Repeat exhaustion emits paused only.
6. node_complete OMITS iteration (node_start has it), and repeat re-uses the same nodeId per pass — so nodePath is the ONLY stable node identity across start/complete. Also finalState names iteration wrappers 'loop#0'/'loop#1' while nodePath uses 'iter-0'/'iter-1' — the two schemes DO NOT MATCH and need translating.

TRAP in the documented recovery path: update_workflow(replace_remaining) on a maxIterations-paused run returns {updated:true, queued:true, message:'Queued: ... after the current step completes'} and emits steps_queued — but NEVER APPLIES, because a paused run has no step in flight to complete. The replacement step never ran; run stayed paused. replace_remaining alone does not resume an exhausted loop; needs resume/retry too.

node_paused ATTEMPTED AND STILL UNVERIFIED (2026-07-31,
probe-kas-workflow-nodepaused-2.16.0.py). A one-step workflow whose prompt told
the step to signal `send_message` severity "warning" (need user input) did NOT
pause: the step ran to node_complete and the run to run_complete, emitting
run_start / node_start x2 / node_complete / run_complete and no node_paused.
_kiro/session/notify also did not fire.

Why it did not reproduce: the pause is driven by the step agent's OWN
completionSignal, and the model chose "success" despite the instruction. This is
the same model-in-the-control-plane property already recorded as workflow hazard
4 — step outcome is decided by a model-issued tool call, so it cannot be forced
deterministically from a prompt.

node_paused therefore remains the ONE workflow payload of nine not observed
live. Its other documented emit sites (mid-node pause request, throttle retry,
stale-run liveness force-pause) are equally hard to provoke on demand. Cheapest
remaining lever: _kiro/workflow/pause against a run with a step in flight —
that path emits node_paused with reason = state.pauseReason. Worth one more
attempt if node-level pause rendering is on the critical path; otherwise treat
the documented shape {workflowId, nodeId, nodePath, reason} as static-only.

Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-nodepaused-2.16.0.jsonl

Design notes rewritten (2026-08-08). They still carried the pre-2.16.0 stop sign
-- "DEFERRED -- no implementation until an emitter exists. Do not build UI
against this protocol." -- while the description already said UNBLOCKED, so the
issue contradicted itself and read as a stop sign to anyone picking it up.

Two parts of the old notes were not merely stale but WRONG for the shipped
emitter, and are recorded here rather than silently dropped:

1. The recognition heuristic -- "_meta.kiro.notification.kind == workflow-
   progress, OR a _meta.kiro.messageId / notifyId beginning wf-progress-; rides
   user_message_chunk" -- was reverse-engineered in the 2.14.1 audit from
   tui.js's parse-and-drop converter, i.e. from the CLIENT side of a protocol
   whose server half did not exist yet. The shipped 0.27.8 emitter does none of
   that: workflow-notification-bridge.ts maps 9 kinds to plain JSON-RPC
   notifications on _kiro/workflow/<kind> with the payload flattened into
   params. The recognition paths in probe-kas-orchestrate-capture-2.14.1.py are
   kept as history but are not how a consumer detects these frames.

2. "Prerequisite before any design work: confirm a shipped engine actually
   emits. As of KAS 0.22.7 / kiro-cli 2.14.1 the count is zero on both engines."
   -- satisfied. _kiro/workflow occurrences in acp-server.js went 0 -> 118 at
   2.16.0, and three live captures are committed.

Also filed today: cyril-jxfu (workflow step sessions are peer top-level sessions
and currently misroute into the subagent stream). This issue blocks it -- the
session registry there cannot be populated until node_start is parsed here.

GATE ASSUMPTION SUPERSEDED (2026-08-08). This issue's description says the gate
must be flipped via session/new _meta.kiro.settings.workflows.enabled. Live A/B
(probe-kas-workflow-gateoff-2.16.0.py, logs/kas-workflow-gateoff-2.16.0.jsonl)
shows the whole surface routes with the gate OFF: listRecipes / list /
listWatchHandlers / new all answer, and a gate-off invoke ran to run_complete
status=completed while delivering run_start + node_start x2 + node_complete +
run_complete to the gate-off parent, with the step running as a peer session.
resolveWorkflows() gates the five agent-facing TOOLS, not the method dispatch.
Cyril therefore never sets the flag -- see ADR-0011. Everything else in this
issue (the 9 events, the six hazards, the fixtures) stands unchanged.

HAZARD 4 CHANGED IN 2.16.2 — new NodeState field `completionSignalSource`.

Static (bundle schema, @kiro/agent 0.35.11 vs 0.27.8):

  2.16.0:  completionSignal: enum(["success","need_input","error"]).optional()
  2.16.2:  completionSignal: enum(["success","need_input","error"]).optional(),
           completionSignalSource: enum(["send_message","status_update"]).optional()

`completionSignal` refs went 37 -> 62. The stale-run machinery is UNCHANGED
(STALE_RUNNING_PAUSE_REASON 4x, "Awaiting next user message" 1x in both), so the
pause-on-missing-signal path still exists.

What this means for hazard 4 as written in this issue's design notes ("a step's
outcome is decided by a model-issued tool call"): still true as ONE source, but
2.16.2 adds a `status_update` source that is not a model tool call, and records
which one drove the completion. Model this field; do not assume send_message is
the only path.

Runtime corroboration is WEAK (n=1 per version, same one-step DAG, same wf-coder
agent, both runs status=completed):

  2.16.0 finalState node: completionSignal='success'  (key present)
  2.16.2 finalState node: key ABSENT entirely

Under documented 2.16.0 rules an omitted signal PAUSES the node rather than
completing it; the 2.16.2 run completed without one. Consistent with the new
source, but one run each cannot separate schema change from model variance --
`completionSignal` is model-elected, so it varies by construction. Treat as
"mechanism confirmed statically, runtime characterisation still open" and settle
it in the 2.16.1/2.16.2 live A/B.

Also new in the 2.16.1-2.16.2 range, all workflow-internal (the `_kiro/workflow/*`
METHOD SET is byte-identical to 2.16.0 -- verified):
  src/workflow/lifecycle-events.ts     <- the emitter, moved out of
                                          workflow-notification-bridge.ts
  src/workflow/node-state-transforms.ts
  src/workflow/run-disk-operations.ts  <- run persistence; bears on the
                                          reattach-on-demand model (cyril-0qe6)
`_kiro/workflow` references 132 -> 154 between 2.16.1 and 2.16.2.

Captures: logs/kas-workflow-gateoff-2.16.2.jsonl,
          logs/kas-workflow-diskrecipe-2.16.2.jsonl

HAZARD 4 IS NOW LIVE-SETTLED (2026-08-08). The earlier note on this issue marked the
runtime evidence WEAK (n=1 per version, could not separate schema change from model
variance). It is no longer weak. probe-kas-completion-signal-2.16.2.py, three arms,
2 reps each, zero within-arm variance:

  arm         binary   step prompt                completionSignal  completionSignalSource
  C control   2.16.0   neutral (no mention)       success           (field not in schema)
  B           2.16.2   neutral (no mention)       None              None
  A           2.16.2   explicit send_message      success           send_message

Same one-step DAG, same wf-coder agent, same prompt text between B and C. All six runs
reached run status=completed with ZERO paused/node_paused events.

WHAT CHANGED
  * 2.16.0 recorded completionSignal="success" even when the prompt never asked for a
    send_message -- the signal was effectively induced.
  * 2.16.2 leaves BOTH fields unset unless the model genuinely calls send_message, and
    the node still completes.
  * So completionSignal became an HONEST RECORD of what happened rather than a
    precondition for completion, and completionSignalSource says who set it.

CONSUMER RULE FOR 2.16.2+ (this is the actionable part)
  Absent completionSignal on a COMPLETED node is NORMAL. Do NOT treat a missing signal
  as "incomplete", "hung", or "awaiting input". A state machine written to the 2.16.0
  spec -- which this issue's design notes still encode -- would misread every
  neutral-prompt step on 2.16.2 as unfinished. That is a shipped-bug-shaped difference,
  which is why it was worth live turns rather than inference.

  Hazard 4's underlying warning still stands in weakened form: send_message remains ONE
  path, the stale-run force-pause machinery is unchanged (STALE_RUNNING_PAUSE_REASON
  present in both bundles), and a step CAN still stall awaiting user input. It is simply
  no longer true that a node must be signalled to complete.

STILL UNOBSERVED LIVE: completionSignalSource == "status_update". Static evidence is
exact -- the bundle's failed-status transition sets it verbatim:

    case "failed": { target.completionSignal = "error";
                     target.completionSignalSource = "status_update";
                     target.failureReason = statusReason ?? ... }

so "status_update" reads as ENGINE-set on a status transition vs "send_message" as
model-elected. Forcing a genuine engine-side node failure was not attempted; it belongs
with the audit's documented "elective mechanisms" limit (same class as node_paused).
Cheapest lever if it becomes load-bearing: a step whose agent errors out mid-run, or a
status transition driven through _kiro/workflow/update.

Captures: kas-csig-2.16.0-neutral.jsonl, kas-csig-2.16.2-neutral.jsonl,
          kas-csig-2.16.2-explicit.jsonl
Closed: Shipped in PR #92 (merge 71ab7fa): 9-event lifecycle model, WorkflowTracker state machine, App-owned single consumer

title: KAS terminal shell_type responder hardcodes "bash" (+ create runs argv with no shell) — wrong for native Windows
description:
cyril's KAS terminal `shell_type` responder is hardcoded and its terminal `create` runs argv with no shell — both wrong for the native-Windows target.

## Why this matters (native Windows is a committed target)

On the KAS (v3) engine, cyril's `KasEngine` advertises `terminal:true` + fs (engine.rs:127-137), so KAS delegates shell execution to cyril via ACP `terminal/*` (ACPTerminalManager path) — cyril, NOT KAS, owns the shell. KAS decides which shell TOOL to give the model, and how to tokenize/quote the command, from the client's answer to `_kiro/terminal/shell_type`.

Today cyril answers that with a constant:

    // crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/kas/terminal_io.rs:423
    pub(crate) fn respond_shell_type() -> acp::Result<acp::ExtResponse> {
        let body = serde_json::json!({ "shellType": "bash" });
        ...
    }

On Linux/WSL (current shipping target) "bash" is correct, so this is dormant. On native Windows it is wrong: cyril would report "bash", KAS would hand the model `execute_bash` with POSIX quoting, and cyril would then execute that on a Windows host. Result = the same class of quote-mangling users already hit on Kiro's own tui.js path (documented below).

## Secondary defect (same area): create() spawns argv with no shell

    // crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/kas/terminal_io.rs:108
    let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&req.command);
    cmd.args(&req.args)...

KAS pre-splits the model's command string into `{command, args}` using the reported shellType's tokenizer (verified: capture in .cyril-ufie/probe.rs shows `{"command":"echo","args":["done-42"]}`), and cyril spawns that argv DIRECTLY with no shell. Consequences:
- Shell operators/pipes/redirects (`|`, `>`, `&&`) emitted in a command are tokenized by KAS as literal args, not interpreted — they will not behave as the model expects.
- The quoting the model was told to use (POSIX vs PowerShell, driven by shellType) must match how cyril actually runs the command. With no shell, the match is implicit and fragile.

## Upstream context (motivation — NOT cyril's to fix, documents the failure mode)

The bug users see on Kiro's native tui.js+KAS path (confirmed in KAS 0.25.17, shipped 2.14.2/2.15.0):
- KAS `src/tools/shell-tool-ids.ts`: `resolveShellType(x)=x ?? (win32?"cmd":"bash")`; `isWindowsShell` lumps cmd+powershell; tool = `windowsShell?"execute_pwsh":"execute_bash"` (no execute_cmd exists) → any Windows shell → the model gets `execute_pwsh` (PowerShell quoting).
- KAS `src/platform/node/default-terminal-manager.ts` `getDefaultShell()` reads `process.env.COMSPEC` — ALWAYS cmd.exe on Windows, so the powershell branch is dead → runs `cmd.exe /c`.
- Net on tui.js (which advertises terminal:false and never implements shell_type): model told PowerShell, executor runs cmd → quotes mangled. cyril AVOIDS KAS's getDefaultShell by providing its own terminal, but must still report the right shellType and quote correctly itself.

## Proper solution (for cyril's responder + create)

1. Replace the hardcoded shellType with real host detection:
   - Non-Windows: basename of `$SHELL` classified to posix/fish, default "bash".
   - Native Windows priority: honor an explicit cyril setting first; else prefer PowerShell 7 (`pwsh.exe` via PATH / `%ProgramFiles%\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`); else Windows PowerShell (`powershell.exe`; `PSModulePath` is the right "available" signal — same heuristic Kiro's own tui.js `$Ve()` uses correctly); fall to `cmd` only if explicitly chosen. NEVER use COMSPEC as the discriminator.
   - Report the KAS-normalized token KAS expects (posix / powershell / cmd / fish — see KAS toShellType in src/policy/shell-type.ts).
2. Make the reported shellType and cyril's actual execution consistent. Since KAS quotes/tokenizes for the reported shell, cyril must run the resulting argv in a way that matches — reconsider the no-shell `create()` so shell operators and quoting behave as the model was told (e.g. run through the detected shell, or confirm KAS's argv split already yields the exact argv we exec).
3. Reuse the existing Windows seam: platform/path.rs already branches Windows vs Linux (win_to_wsl/wsl_to_win). Shell detection is the terminal-side analogue.

## Acceptance criteria

- respond_shell_type() returns a host-derived shellType (unit-tested per platform: linux→posix/bash; windows→pwsh when pwsh present, else powershell, else cmd), never a hardcoded constant.
- No path yields the wrong KAS shell tool on native Windows (would hand the model execute_bash on a PowerShell/cmd host).
- Decision recorded on the create() no-shell behavior: either (a) documented-safe because KAS argv split == exact exec argv, or (b) fixed to run through the detected shell so operators/quoting work.
- COMSPEC is never used as the shell discriminator anywhere in cyril.

Evidence/refs: terminal_io.rs:{108,423}, engine.rs:127-137, .cyril-ufie/probe.rs (captured terminal/create shape), KAS bundle src/{tools/shell-tool-ids.ts, platform/node/default-terminal-manager.ts, policy/shell-type.ts}. Investigation session 2026-07-27. Follow-up to cyril-ufie (KAS-5b).
design: Primary change is in crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/kas/terminal_io.rs (respond_shell_type + possibly create). Keep shell detection in a small, unit-testable helper (pure fn of platform + env + a PATH probe), mirroring how platform/path.rs isolates the Windows/Linux seam. Do NOT reach for COMSPEC. Prefer detecting pwsh via PATH; PSModulePath is the availability signal for Windows PowerShell. Report the exact KAS-normalized token (posix/powershell/cmd/fish) — cross-check against KAS toShellType() so the string round-trips. Watch: cyril on Windows historically spawns `wsl kiro-cli acp` (path.rs), so 'native Windows' here means the future direct-Windows-kiro path, not the WSL bridge — the detection must key off where the COMMAND actually runs, not merely process.platform. Split into two issues if the create() no-shell decision grows its own design.

notes.content: Closed: PR #80 merged (ce0ea4f): startup-resolved host shell, shell_type reports the resolved family, terminal/create executes through it

title: CommandResultKind::ShowPicker has zero producers — decide remove vs document
description:
`CommandResult::show_picker` / `CommandResultKind::ShowPicker` has ZERO producers
anywhere in the workspace, which makes the dispatch arm in crates/cyril/src/app.rs
(around line 863, `self.ui_state.show_picker(title, options)`) unreachable today.

Every picker that actually opens goes through the OTHER path: the
`Notification::CommandOptionsReceived` cross-cutting handler at app.rs:426, which
calls `show_picker(command.clone(), options.clone())`. That is the notification-
driven flow CLAUDE.md documents (`/model` with no args -> `QueryCommandOptions` ->
`CommandOptionsReceived` -> App opens the picker).

So `CommandResult::ShowPicker` looks like a designed-for-but-never-used escape
hatch: a command that wants to open a picker synchronously from its own
`execute()` rather than via a notification round trip.

Noticed during the cyril-imjx sweep fix (PR #75) while auditing `show_picker`
callers for blast radius.

Decide one of:
  a. Remove the variant and the dead arm (smallest surface, matches the
     "zero dead code" instinct).
  b. Keep it and document WHY it exists unused — e.g. if a future non-Kiro
     engine is expected to answer options synchronously, which the vendor-neutral
     direction in docs/ROADMAP.md makes plausible.

Not a defect on its own; filing so the choice is made deliberately rather than
the arm quietly accumulating maintenance cost. Note that whichever way this goes,
the cyril-imjx fix marks the active row inside `show_picker` itself, so BOTH entry
points get the marker — removing the variant loses nothing.

Discovered 2026-08-01 during the sweep-bugs batch.

title: Engine identity is trusted, never verified — fingerprint the wire at handshake; fail-loud KAS detection must live outside the kas feature
description:
From the 2026-07-02 v2/v3 differentiation-strategy audit. AgentEngine is bound at spawn purely from the flag/config (bridge.rs engine_for); nothing verifies the subprocess actually speaks the assumed dialect, though cheap fingerprints exist: KAS session ids are sess_-prefixed and KAS initialize returns agentCapabilities._meta.kiro (checkpoints/sessionList/extensionMethods); v2 has neither.

The failure mode is ASYMMETRIC because of the kas cargo feature (ADR-0002): a --features kas build meeting v2 degrades gracefully (v2 never calls the responders), but a DEFAULT build meeting KAS breaks with zero diagnostic — V2Engine drops session_info_update turn_end, and _kiro/auth/getAccessToken has no responder compiled in (wrapper spawn), so turns die/hang with nothing actionable. Two realistic triggers: kiro-cli flips its default engine to KAS (clearly the direction), or the engine-flag vocabulary shifts again (kas->v3 already happened at 2.8.0). Related nit: AgentEngine::FromStr rejects 'v3' — kiro-cli's own vocabulary since 2.8.0 is v1/v2/v3, so users will type v3; accept it as an alias for Kas.

Sketch: (a) post-initialize/session-new fingerprint assertion (sess_ prefix, _meta.kiro caps) vs the bound engine; mismatch = loud system message + safe stop, not a debug! line; (b) the DETECTION half compiles unconditionally (outside the kas feature) so a default build can say 'agent is KAS — rebuild with --features kas or pass --agent-engine v2'; (c) FromStr v3 alias. Evidence: audit conversation 2026-07-02; docs/kiro-2.7.1-wire-audit.md (KAS handshake shape); reference client traces experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: A default (no-kas-feature) cyril run against a KAS-speaking subprocess produces an actionable error message, not a hang or silent dead turn; a --features kas build with the wrong --agent-engine detects the mismatch at handshake and says so; '--agent-engine v3' parses as Kas; unit tests cover the fingerprint check both directions and the FromStr alias.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #50 merged to main (4ee37b1). All four ACs fenced: default-build-vs-KAS actionable BridgeDisconnected (fingerprint_stops_v2_bound_on_kas_wire + live POST harness, F4 cascade eliminated); kas-build mismatch detection both directions (unit matrix + kas-lane bridge test); --agent-engine v3 parses as Kas in FromStr AND serde (D7 reversal pause-approved, serialization stays kas); fingerprint unit tests both directions + alias. Two-layer verification: initialize _meta.kiro-object check + sess_ session-id check at session/new (post-response) and session/load (pre-flight), compiled unconditionally outside the kas feature. Fixed in-branch: notify_fingerprint_stop dedup (review finding). Filed: cyril-wkt8 (acp frame-split watch).
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-1

title: Expose KAS per-session disableAutoCompaction (honored since KAS 0.52.1) as a cyril compaction knob
description:
KAS 0.52.1 (kiro-cli 2.19.2) finally honors disableAutoCompaction: resolution is session/new _meta.kiro.settings.disableAutoCompaction.enabled > initialize._meta.kiro.settings > persisted session metadata > false; the value is persisted in session.json, echoed in the session/new result _meta (new field disableAutoCompaction) and in session/list _meta.kiro.settings, and enforced on the execution path ("Context limit reached because the disableAutoCompaction setting is enabled. Compact the conversation manually, then try again."). Through 0.48.0 the key was accepted but consumed by nothing. compaction.excludePercent/excludeMessages are still ignored by KAS.

This is the first per-session compaction knob on the v3 engine and the enabled/disabled half of the omp-style compaction controls previously judged infeasible on KAS (see reference_kiro_compaction_settings_surface). Scope: a /compaction on|off (or settings-driven) toggle that sends the setting at session/new (and initialize for the default), shows the resolved value from the session/new _meta, and pairs with the existing _kiro/session/compact manual trigger. Enforcement was not live-triggered in the audit (needs a real context overflow) — verify with a big fs_read attachment before shipping.

Evidence: docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 2; capture experiments/conductor-spike/kas-surface-2.19.2.jsonl (second session) vs kas-surface-0.48.0pin-2.19.2.jsonl.

title: Wire a host-callback family onto the mediator's cancel/shutdown seam (currently no production opt-in)
description: cyril-g9vt's HostMediator has cancel_scope + shutdown signalling (CancelKey, per-job cancel oneshot, the spawn_host_job select! race) but NO production family opts in: HostCallback::cancels()/cancel_key() always return None. So run_loop's CancelRequest cancel_scope and Shutdown shutdown() sweeps are currently no-ops — hooks cancel flows through the older HookOps mechanism (respond_execute's internal select), and terminals reap via the registry on session cancel. The machinery is unit-fenced (host_mediator::tests) and is the design's extensibility seam, but it's dead in production (Speculative Generality flagged in the cyril-g9vt pre-PR review). Wire the first family — recommend HooksExecute: set cancel_key=operationId, HooksCancel.cancels()=same key, drop the HookOps dual-mechanism (spawn_host_job already drops the dispatch future on cancel, and kill_on_drop reaps the child — same effect as respond_execute's internal select). Then cancel_scope/shutdown become live and the comments in bridge.rs (CancelRequest + Shutdown arms) can drop their 'no production family does yet' caveats. Verify lw67/2z9g/cancel fences still hold.

title: KAS-5 — Host I/O callback responders: fs and terminal (first real cyril-stages interception point)
description: ROADMAP KAS-5 (docs/ROADMAP.md). Depends on KAS-2a (cyril-j16p) — the walking skeleton must render a turn first. Pulled ahead of KAS-3/KAS-4: the first cyril-stages deliverable, converging the KAS track with Phase 2 (ADR-0003). KAS delegates file I/O and shell execution to the host via server->client ACP requests; cyril becomes the executor and therefore the audit/gate/transform point. Scope: implement the HostIo capability sub-trait (the accessor stub pattern is laid down in KAS-0/cyril-atjw) + responders for fs read/write and terminal exec, routed through the single-mediator bridge loop (ADR-0004). INVARIANT INHERITED FROM KAS-0/ADR-0004: the loop forwards requests and NEVER awaits their resolution; cyril-side resolution that is slow (file read / shell exec) spawns OFF-LOOP, the same way the turn prompt does (cyril-84ca). Reintroducing a blocking await in the loop is a regression. Windows/WSL path translation applies at the fs boundary. Filed during KAS-0 budgeted-plan to cite the request-resolution deferral.

notes.content:
2026-06-30 KAS-5a (fs host-callbacks) COMPLETE on branch feat/kas-5-host-io via gilfoyle flow (prove-it -> falsifiable-design -> budgeted-plan -> checkpointed-build; artifacts in .cyril-7bdu/). 6 slices, 429 tests + clippy -D warnings green, AND the live oracle kas_fs_host_io_smoke PASSED (real KAS turn through cyril's bridge: read+write resolvers served, write permission-gated C9). Build-time re-scope: this issue = fs only; terminal split to cyril-ufie (KAS-5b); ADR-0004 loop-mediation gate seam deferred to cyril-g9vt (direct-resolve in #[cfg(kas)] KiroClient overrides; C4 non-blocking holds via acp per-request spawn + tokio::fs offload). Ready for human review/PR.

CI green on Linux/macOS/Windows. Follow-ups remain as separate issues (3lh8, 0v42, 8tq6, g9vt, r3t6, 1rpv, ihj1).

title: Render KAS tool-result wire cap marker (since 0.46.1) and consume _meta.kiro.outputTransformation (0.52.1, dark)
description:
KAS caps terminal tool_call_update content on the ACP wire at 30,000 chars (capToolResultForWire, shipped since KAS 0.46.1 / kiro-cli 2.19.0): content becomes head(500) + "\n...[truncated N chars]...\n" + tail(500), while rawOutput on the same frame still carries the full tool-truncated output (execute_bash itself truncates at ~30k: "[ExecuteBash] Output truncated {toChars:30074}"). Cyril renders the marker verbatim today (acceptable, but unstyled and easy to mistake for tool output).

KAS 0.52.1 also assembles a NEW _meta.kiro.outputTransformation stamp for terminal tool_call_update + tool_result: {kind:"offloaded", absFilePath, totalChars} (full output written to <session>/tool-outputs/<tool>-<id>.txt, model sees a head/tail preview) | {kind:"clipped", originalChars}. Gate: initialize._meta.kiro.settings.largeToolOutputHandler.enabled=true (session-level setting does NOT gate). Live 2026-08-25: with the initialize-level setting the offload FILE was written but the stamp never appeared on the wire in any of 3 configurations — plumbed but dark.

Scope: (1) detect the "...[truncated N chars]..." marker in execute tool content and render it as a distinct elided-region row (N chars) rather than raw text; (2) model _meta.kiro.outputTransformation as Option<OutputTransformation> in convert/kas.rs (offloaded → show path + totalChars, clipped → originalChars) so it lights up when KAS starts emitting it; (3) decide whether cyril should advertise largeToolOutputHandler at initialize (it changes what the MODEL sees, not just the wire).

Evidence: docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 3; captures experiments/conductor-spike/kas-output-transform-{,lth-init-}2.19.2.jsonl; probes probe-kas-output-transform-{,lth-,lth-init-}2.19.2.py.

title: Audit methodology: KAS bundle is minified from 0.54.3 — static source reading no longer valid
description:
KAS 0.54.3 (kiro-cli 2.20.1) minified acp-server.js: 559,734 -> 17,564 lines, 23.33MB -> 11.35MB, identifiers mangled, .d.ts.map sidecars dropped. Not code-splitting (same file list, one bundle; node_modules 530MB -> 519MB). See docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 1.

This invalidates a documented technique. The reference-impl memory ('KAS bundle = the reference impl — the shipped fallback IS the contract') and the wire-audit methodology both assume a readable bundle; that is how prior audits recovered extractCapturedOutput's semantics and quoted source comments.

Survives minification: runtime string literals (wire method names, env keys, user-facing messages, config keys).
Does NOT survive: local/internal symbol names, ALL comments.

Two concrete traps, both hit during this audit:
1. grep -c counts LINES, not matches. On a 17k-line minified file everything collapses onto a few enormous lines, so line counts are not comparable to the 559k-line predecessor. Use grep -o | wc -l.
2. String-count A/B is only valid for TRUE runtime literals. Worked example: 'oversized' counts 3 -> 0, reading as a removed feature; all three 0.52.1 hits are inside JSDoc COMMENTS. Same for 'single message' (1 -> 0). Nearly produced a false finding about 2.20.0's compaction change.

Doctrine change: live probing is now PRIMARY evidence and static diff is only a hypothesis generator — an inversion of the prior playbook. Pinned-bundle control legs (KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH) become mandatory for attribution, not optional.

Scope: update docs/kiro-wire-audit-methodology (and the reference-impl guidance) to record the boundary at KAS 0.54.3, the two traps, and the live-first doctrine.

title: dispatch_steer: optimistic chip+echo leak if bridge.send fails after add_steer_echo
description: app.rs dispatch_steer SteerGate::Send arm calls ui.add_steer_echo(&text) (chip +1, Queued echo committed) BEFORE bridge.send(BridgeCommand::SteerSession).await?. If the channel send errors (bridge thread gone / channel closed), the ? propagates and the function unwinds, but the chip increment and the Queued echo are already committed with no drain path — the steer never reached the backend so no SteeringConsumed/Cleared/Unsupported will arrive. With cyril-7z7u removing the turn-end reset, the chip sticks until /new. Low severity (trigger is a dead bridge, steering already broken) but a real unreconcilable optimistic-UI leak. Fix: either send first and add the echo only on Ok, or roll back (decrement chip + flip the just-added echo to a terminal status) in the Err arm before returning. Found by /code-review of PR 28 (finding #2). app.rs:966.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #40 (bd837e7). Repro: failed_steer_send_leaves_no_phantom_chip.

title: Live capture of KAS pushed methods: governance/state, tools tags, steering bodies; userInput+hooks not provokable by prompt
description:
Live provocation of the agent->client half of the KAS surface
(probe-kas-pushed-methods-2.16.0.py, capture kas-pushed-2.16.0.jsonl, 3 turns).

These 22 methods are PUSHED by the agent, so they cannot be swept like the 47
client->agent ones — they must be provoked. This advertises every capability in
resolveCapabilities() and seeds a .kiro/hooks/ config, then runs turns designed to
elicit distinct pushes.

NEWLY CAPTURED WITH REAL PAYLOADS:

_kiro/governance/state  (notification) — never modelled by cyril:
  {sessionId, isEnterprise:false,
   features:{mcpEnabled, webToolsEnabled, usageAnalytics, contentCollection,
             promptLogging, codeReferenceTracker, autonomousAgents}}
  This is the org feature-flag posture. `contentCollection:true` here is the same
  axis as the content-collection opt-out; `autonomousAgents` and `webToolsEnabled`
  gate whole capabilities. Worth surfacing rather than dropping.

_kiro/tools/didChange  — carries a tool TAG taxonomy:
  {sessionId, tags:[{source:"builtin", tag:"read"|"write"|"shell"|..., description}]}

_kiro/steering/documents_changed — full document bodies inline
  ({name, type, scope, uri:"builtin:<id>", inclusion:"manual", content}), e.g. the
  builtin `architecture-selection` steering doc.

_kiro/powers/items_changed        {sessionId, status, powers:[]}
_kiro/progressive_context/items_changed {sessionId, status, items:[]}
_kiro/fs/{read_file,stat,read_directory}  — see cyril-kf2g (dialect is
  client-selected; read_file is paginated)

NOT PROVOKED, and why:
  _kiro/userInput        — asked the agent to present a 3-way choice via its
                           user-input mechanism; it answered in prose instead.
  _kiro/openExternalUrl  — asked it to open a URL with the capability advertised;
                           it printed the link instead.
  _kiro/hooks/{list,sessionStart,executeHook,didChange,cancel}
                         — a .kiro/hooks/ config was seeded and the client
                           advertised hooks + answered hooks/list, but nothing
                           fired.

All three are ELECTIVE: the agent decides whether to use the mechanism, exactly
like the OrchestrateSubAgent and node_paused cases. Prompting cannot force them.
For hooks specifically the likely additional gate is the `v2Hooks` flag surfaced
by _kiro/hooks/setEnabled ("not available when v2Hooks is disabled") — find and
flip that before concluding the hooks host-callback path is dead.

cyril-qo13 (user_input first-option bug) therefore still has NO live capture of
the real _kiro/userInput shape; the responder in this probe deliberately picks the
LAST option so that a future successful provocation proves the wire carries the
choice.

notes.content:
HOOKS RESOLVED — the v2Hooks gate was found and flipped; see cyril-gk17. The blocker was the advertisement SHAPE: _meta.kiro.hooks must be an OBJECT {enabled:true, v2:true}, not the boolean true this probe sent (kiroMeta?.hooks?.enabled on a boolean is undefined, so the whole block was skipped). With the object form the subsystem works end to end: hooks/list returns the registry, hooks/setEnabled rewrites the backing file, hooks/didChange fires, and both a sessionStart and a preToolUse hook actually executed.

Also: the hook FILE schema this probe seeded was wrong (flat {name,trigger,command}); the real one is kasHookFileSchema {version:'v1', hooks:[{name,trigger,action,...}]}, so even with the gate flipped nothing would have loaded.

Correction to this issue's conclusion: hooks were NOT elective/model-dependent — they were a client-advertisement bug on our side. userInput and openExternalUrl remain genuinely elective and unprovoked.

title: Strengthen workflow test tripwires: feature-exclusion assert + wire-field/manifest reconciliation
description: PR 92 deep review (test findings minor + quality observation). (1) Nothing mechanically asserts default builds exclude cyril-core's test_support module (a [dependencies] entry enabling the test-support feature would go unnoticed; cargo tree -e normal was verified clean by hand on 2026-08-09). title: K1b cross-turn steer echo/chip turn-end semantics unverified (needs backend probe)
description: Code-review (cyril-bm1j, xhigh) found a latent ambiguity in K1b's turn-end handling. TurnCompleted resets the chip (steering_queued=0, claim C9) but leaves any still-Queued SteerEcho in scrollback (negative-space #6). If the backend PERSISTS an end-of-turn-un-consumed steer and drains it on the NEXT turn (the idle-steer capture .k1b-steering/idle-steer-wire-capture.log shows steers survive the idle->turn boundary, suggesting it does), then: (a) the chip UNDER-counts a still-pending steer after turn-end, and (b) the next turn's SteeringConsumed FIFO-flips the stale prior-turn Queued echo. If instead the backend DROPS un-consumed steers at turn-end, the current reset is right but the echo should be finalized too. Both directions bake in an unverified assumption, so the fix was deferred. ACTION: probe whether a steer queued at end-of-turn (no further tool boundary) drains on the next turn; then either (1) stop resetting the chip at turn-end and let it drain naturally, or (2) finalize leftover Queued echoes at turn-end to match the reset. The cross-SESSION variant was already fixed (session_created_finalizes_prior_session_steer_echoes); this is the same mechanism across a TURN boundary within one session.
design:
Falsifiable design: .cyril-7z7u/falsifiable-design.md. Scope = OPTIMISTIC CHIP. Cheapest falsifier passed (claim 2 echo-flip preserved, consumed_flips_oldest_queued_echo green).

FIX (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs only): make steering_queued optimistic, in lockstep with the echo, so invariant steering_queued == #SteerEcho{Queued}.
- add_steer_echo: +1 (NEW)
- SteeringConsumed: -1 + flip oldest Queued->Applied (kept)
- SteeringQueued (wire): no count change (was +1; REMOVED — avoid double-count)
- TurnCompleted: no reset (was =0; REMOVED — late steer's count/echo must survive)
- SteeringUnsupported: =0 (NEW — clear the optimistic count)
- SteeringCleared / SessionCreated: =0 (kept)

SUBTRACTIVE: removes "count==0 after TurnCompleted" (still-holds claim 3: drains via consumed) + "every increment has a wire match" (still-holds claim 4: wire queued must not double-count). echo logic (flip_queued_steer_echoes) UNCHANGED.

REWRITES 2 existing tests that lock the old model: turn_completed_resets_steering_queued (claim 3), steering_queue_mirror (claims 4/6/7). 9 claims total, each a state test fence.

Negative space: doesn't count observer-originated steers (cyril-8lfs); doesn't finalize echo at turn-end (rejects issue option b — probe shows late steer still pending).

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED (worktree fix/cyril-7z7u-cross-turn-steer-semantics). All gilfoyle gates green.
- crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs: steering_queued optimistic (add_steer_echo +1; SteeringConsumed -1; Cleared/Unsupported/SessionCreated =0; wire SteeringQueued no-op; TurnCompleted reset removed). Invariant: steering_queued == #SteerEcho{Queued}.
- 9 fences green incl. RED->GREEN rewrites of turn_completed_resets_steering_queued, steering_queue_mirror, steering_queued_exposed_via_tuistate_trait (locked the old model). Full workspace green, clippy -D clean, fmt clean.
- Discovered: SessionController.steering_depth = unread parallel wire counter, now divergent -> cyril-85py. Multi-observer steers -> cyril-8lfs.
Leave open pending review/merge.

title: KAS-4 constraint: never carry effortLevel across a model switch — re-derive from rebuilt configOptions
description:
Design constraint for the KAS-4 configOptions work, from the 2026-07 'Invalid additionalModelRequestFields' investigation. That error is a server-side ValidationException (the phrase appears in no client code) raised when an effort level invalid for the current model reaches the backend inside GenerateAssistantResponseCommand.additionalModelRequestFields.

KAS guards the live-switch path (applyModelId clamps; set_config_option effortLevel validates enum membership) but has three unguarded seams a client can trip: (1) persisted-session restore sets session.effortLevel from metadata with no validation against the current model; (2) session/new _meta.kiro.settings.effortLevel is a bare zod string().optional() — sent through unvalidated; (3) send time pairs a possibly-stale session.effortLevel with a freshly-looked-up effortSchemaPath and only checks both-present, never level-in-enum. Effort enums differ per provider (Anthropic output_config: low..max vs GPT reasoning: different set), so a carried-over level is a live footgun now that GPT models are in the catalog.

When cyril implements KAS configOptions:
- After sending set_config_option {configId: 'model'}, treat the session's effort as unknown until the rebuilt configOptions arrive; re-derive the valid level list (and currentValue) from the effortLevel select option in that response.
- Never send set_config_option {configId: 'effortLevel'} with a cached value from a previous model.
- Never pre-seed _meta.kiro.settings.effortLevel on session/new from a stored value without validating it against the target model's advertised levels (or simply omit it and let KAS pick defaultEffortLevel).
- On loadSession, trust the effortLevel in the returned configOptions, not any cyril-side cache.

See memory reference-kiro-effort-schema-negotiation for the full mechanism and code sites in the KAS bundle.
acceptance_criteria: KAS-4 implementation demonstrably re-derives effort options from the configOptions rebuild after every model switch (test covering switch-then-set-effort ordering); no code path sends an effortLevel value that did not come from the current model's advertised options; session/new omits or validates _meta.kiro.settings.effortLevel.

notes.content: Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-4

title: Bridge command loop blocks on conn.prompt() for the whole turn — no mid-turn commands (steer/cancel)
description: prove-it-prototype (cyril-bm1j) proved: bridge.rs awaits conn.prompt().await INSIDE the single-consumer command loop (while let Some(cmd)=command_rx.recv()), so it never recv()s a queued command until the turn ends. Wire oracle: SteerSession enqueued at +1.5s did not cross the wire until 12.839s, 1ms after the session/prompt response at 12.838s. Consequences: (1) mid-turn steering (K1b core) is impossible as-is; (2) STRONGLY IMPLICATED but not separately probed: Esc-while-busy CancelRequest goes through the same loop, so mid-turn cancel is also non-functional today. Fix direction: drive the prompt off the command loop (spawn_local the conn.prompt() future; resolve TurnCompleted from that task) so the loop stays free to process SteerSession/CancelRequest concurrently. Repro: .k1b-steering/probe.rs + oracle-wire-capture.log.
acceptance_criteria: A command enqueued mid-turn is sent to the agent before TurnCompleted (probe: steer surfaces before turn end). Esc-cancel aborts a busy turn promptly. Regression fence: an integration test driving the bridge with a slow turn + a mid-turn command, asserting the command's effect precedes turn completion.

notes.content: Implementation complete on fix/bridge-loop-midturn-commands (7 slices, checkpointed-build). Off-loop prompt dispatch: SendPrompt spawn_local's the turn on an Rc<conn>; one-in-flight guard via JoinHandle::is_finished; Shutdown aborts. Fences C1(loop frees) C2(steer mid-turn) C3(cancel resolves Cancelled) C4(single turn) C6(one TurnCompleted) C7(shutdown) C9(guard self-clears) all pass via an in-process fake-agent harness; 734 workspace tests + clippy + fmt clean; prove-it oracles (test_bridge, steer/cancel/notif_order probes) agree vs real kiro 2.8.0. C5 (ordering) resolved empirically — holds for v2 AND KAS, not a cyril-84ca property; theoretical zero-gap library race filed cyril-9akh. Ready for PR; unblocks K1b (cyril-bm1j).

title: Remove/align unread SessionController.steering_depth (diverges from optimistic UiState chip)
description:
SessionController.steering_depth (cyril-core/session.rs) is a wire-driven steer counter (SteeringQueued +1, SteeringConsumed -1, Cleared/SessionCreated =0; NO turn-end reset) with ZERO non-test readers (the chip reads UiState.steering_queued via toolbar.rs:80).

cyril-7z7u makes UiState.steering_queued OPTIMISTIC (counted at add_steer_echo / user-send), so it no longer mirrors the wire-driven steering_depth — the "in lockstep with SessionController.steering_depth" comments (state.rs ~538/1909) are now stale. Harmless today (steering_depth is unread), but it's dead/divergent code.

Action: either (a) delete steering_depth + its tests (it's unused), or (b) make it optimistic to match if a future consumer needs a core-side steer count. Decide when touched. Found during cyril-7z7u checkpointed-build.

notes.content: DONE in feat/cyril-vgcm-steer-clear slice 1 (2026-07-14): SessionController.steering_depth deleted (write-only, zero readers — grep-verified; stale state.rs comment rewritten). steering_unsupported kept, now steer-only (clear--32601 must not set it, vgcm C12). Close when the PR merges.

title: build_wrapper_command probes <program> --version — wsl-prefixed wrapper commands resolve the agent-engine flag from WSL's version
description: kas/version.rs:72 build_wrapper_command calls kiro_cli_version(agent_command.program()). With --agent-command wsl kiro-cli acp (program=wsl), it runs 'wsl --version', parses WSL's own version string, and feeds that to flag_for_version — picking the wrong --agent-engine flag (or erroring) for any wsl-wrapped KAS wrapper spawn. Latent until KAS wrapper mode is exercised through WSL from a Windows host. Version probing should target the kiro-cli argv element, not argv[0], when the command routes through a launcher. Discovered during the cyril-jxmv probe (see .cyril-jxmv/findings.md on that branch).

title: dispatch_code_command Prompt path drops the message when busy (second cyril-2vcc path)
description: Code-review (cyril-bm1j, xhigh) found a SECOND instance of the cyril-2vcc bug class, outside the K1b diff so deferred. crates/cyril/src/app.rs dispatch_code_command's CodeCommandResponse::Prompt arm (app.rs:1152-1171) add_user_message()s + set_activity(Sending) + emits BridgeCommand::SendPrompt with NO busy guard. If a /code response yields a Prompt while session.status()==Busy, the post-cyril-84ca one-turn guard rejects the second SendPrompt with BridgeError -> the injected prompt is committed to chat but never sent, and activity regresses to Sending. cyril-2vcc fixed only submit_input (Enter-while-busy) via classify_submit->dispatch_steer; this /code prompt-injection path was not covered. FIX: gate this path on busy too (advisory or defer), mirroring the submit_input fix. Reachable when a user triggers a /code prompt-injection mid-turn.
design:
Falsifiable design (gilfoyle): .cyril-8ej2/falsifiable-design.md. Cheapest falsifier RUN + PASSED (busy+Prompt currently emits SendPrompt+UserText+Sending — bug confirmed).

DECISION: busy-case = advisory + drop (zero bridge commands, commit nothing, one System advisory), NOT steer — because dispatch_code_command is sync (steer path is async) and the issue specifies advisory/defer. Scope = Busy only, matching classify_submit.

7 claims, each with an independent unit-test falsifier + named buggy impl (non-vacuity) + a distinct regression fence:
1 Active+Prompt unchanged (1 SendPrompt, UserText, Sending) — extend dispatch_code_prompt_returns_deferred_command
2 Busy+Prompt emits zero commands — dispatch_code_prompt_busy_drops_no_send
3 Busy+Prompt commits no UserText — dispatch_code_prompt_busy_commits_no_user_message
4 Busy+Prompt doesn't set Sending — dispatch_code_prompt_busy_leaves_activity
5 Busy+Prompt adds System advisory — dispatch_code_prompt_busy_advises
6 no-session+Prompt unchanged — dispatch_code_prompt_no_session_shows_error (existing)
7 guard scoped to Prompt arm: Panel opens when Busy — dispatch_code_panel_opens_when_busy

Additive change (adds a guard; removes no invariant). Negative space: doesn't steer, doesn't guard Compacting/Initializing/Disconnected, doesn't queue/retry, doesn't touch Panel/Unknown/success-false, doesn't go async.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED on branch fix/cyril-8ej2-code-prompt-busy-guard, commit 1f44a2d. All gilfoyle gates green.
- Fix: runtime busy-guard in dispatch_code_command Prompt arm (crates/cyril/src/app.rs) — Busy => advise + drop (0 commands, no UserText, activity untouched). Scope = Busy only (matches classify_submit). Runtime check, not debug_assert (load-bearing for correctness in release).
- Fences (7, all pass): dispatch_code_prompt_{busy_drops_no_send, busy_commits_no_user_message, busy_leaves_activity, busy_advises}, dispatch_code_panel_opens_when_busy, dispatch_code_prompt_returns_deferred_command (extended: asserts UserText), dispatch_code_prompt_no_session_shows_error.
- RED->GREEN verified (4 busy fences failed pre-guard). Full workspace: 770 tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt --check clean.
- Artifacts: .cyril-8ej2/{falsifiable-design,budgeted-plan}.md.
Leave open pending review/merge (close per the project's PR-close pattern). NOT pushed.

title: Multi-client observer: count/echo steers cyril didn't originate (wire steering_queued)
description:
When cyril-7z7u makes the steer chip OPTIMISTIC (incremented at add_steer_echo / user-send) and stops incrementing on the wire SteeringQueued notification (to avoid double-counting cyril's own steers), a steer that ANOTHER client on the same session originates — surfaced only as a wire SteeringQueued with no local optimistic echo — will not be counted or echoed by cyril.

This is fine for cyril's single-client model TODAY. It becomes a gap if/when the multi-client observer direction lands (ROADMAP session-level workflows / _kiro/sessions/changed). At that point, reintroduce wire-SteeringQueued handling for steers WITHOUT a matching local echo (observer-originated), without double-counting cyril's own optimistic steers — likely needs a correlation key the wire doesn't currently provide (content is advisory).

REF: cyril-7z7u falsifiable-design (.cyril-7z7u/falsifiable-design.md), negative space.

title: KAS host-io: translate WSL-internal paths (/home, /tmp) for a Windows host
description:
cyril's platform::path::wsl_to_win only translates /mnt/<drive> mount paths (/mnt/c/... -> C:\...). WSL-internal paths (/home/<user>, /tmp, /root) pass through unchanged. On a Windows host running `wsl kiro-cli acp`, a KAS workspace under the WSL-native filesystem makes fs/{read,write}_text_file callbacks carry /home/... paths.

After cyril-7bdu's to_native_checked fix these now fail HONESTLY as -32603 NotFound (has_root() accepts them, to_native leaves them unchanged, tokio::fs cannot open a WSL ext4 path from the Windows host) instead of a misleading 'must be absolute' -32602 -- but they still do not RESOLVE. Full Windows+KAS support for WSL-native workspaces needs \\wsl$\<distro>\... (or \\wsl.localhost\...) translation in platform::path.

Latent today: KAS is Linux-only in practice; /mnt/<drive> workspaces already work after the fix. Discovered during max-effort review of PR #34 (KAS-5a).
acceptance_criteria: wsl_to_win maps a WSL-internal path (e.g. /home/u/p/x.txt) to a \\wsl$\<distro>\... UNC path on Windows (no-op on Linux); round-trip + json-translation tests; distro-name resolution decided ($WSL_DISTRO_NAME / config); a KAS fs read+write against a WSL-native workspace succeeds on a Windows host.
