title: Toolbar keeps stale effort badge when a GPT model reports effort: "none"
description:
GPT-family models expose a 'none' effort level that cyril's closed EffortLevel enum rejects, so setting it leaves the toolbar showing the PREVIOUS level.

Chain (all three links verified against kiro-cli 2.14.2, v2 engine):

1. `_kiro.dev/metadata` emits `{"sessionId": ..., "effort": "none"}` — captured live.
2. `EffortLevel::from_wire("none")` (crates/cyril-core/src/types/session.rs:40) has a closed set low/medium/high/xhigh/max, so 'none' falls to the `other =>` arm: debug-logged, returns None.
3. UiState's sticky rule (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs:434, `if let Some(e) = effort`) treats None as "frame omitted effort, no update" — correct for the real context-only frames, wrong here.

Net: after /effort high then /effort none, the toolbar still reads 'high' while the session is actually at none. The wire has three distinguishable states (field absent = no update; "none" = explicitly no reasoning; a level) and `Option<EffortLevel>` encodes only two — the sentinel/absent conflation CLAUDE.md's 'Use Option for absent values, not sentinels' warns about.

Scope: GPT-family only, confirmed by A/B probe:
  gpt-5.6-terra  -> ['none','low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
  claude-opus-5  -> ['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
'none' under Opus is rejected by the agent (`success:false, "invalid value 'none' for 'output_config.effort'"`), and cyril already surfaces that message via format_command_response — no bug there.

Reachability is not hypothetical: gpt-5.6-terra is the account's current default model on session/new, so a fresh cyril session starts on a model whose enum includes 'none'.

Repro without a prompt turn (zero credits): initialize -> session/new -> _kiro.dev/commands/execute {command:{command:'effort',args:{value:'high'}}} -> same with 'none' -> observe metadata frames. Probe script: scratchpad probe-effort-none-2.14.2.py.

Fix direction: add a variant (e.g. EffortLevel::None) so 'none' parses and the toolbar can render it distinctly from 'no level reported'. A display-only patch cannot work — the information is destroyed in from_wire before the toolbar sees it.

Note: the model-switch case is already correct — UiState::set_current_model (state.rs:1093) clears effort on a real model change, and the probe confirms the agent itself prunes effort across a family switch (bare {sessionId} metadata frame, no effort field, active marker gone). Do not regress that.
acceptance_criteria:
1. EffortLevel::from_wire("none") parses to a distinct value rather than None.
2. A metadata frame carrying effort:"none" updates the toolbar (no stale prior level) — regression test at the UiState::apply_notification level asserting high -> none transitions the displayed value.
3. A metadata frame that OMITS effort still does not clear a set level (existing sticky behavior preserved; existing test must still pass).
4. An unrecognized level (e.g. "turbo") still maps to None with the debug log — the closed-set discipline stays.
5. Toolbar rendering distinguishes 'effort = none' from 'no effort reported' (badge text vs absent badge).

notes.content:
2.16.0 wire evidence (paid KAS turn A/B, docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md): KAS now ADVERTISES the effort ladder per model on session/update config_option_update, and for the GPT models it explicitly includes "none":

  GPT 5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna -> effortLevels ["none","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"], defaultEffortLevel "high"

So effort "none" is a LEGITIMATE ADVERTISED LEVEL for GPT models, not a degenerate/missing value to paper over. The badge should render it as a real state rather than falling back to the last non-none value. defaultEffortLevel also gives a real per-model default to diff against. Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-turn-2.16.0.jsonl

Closed: Already fixed by cyril-1gim, not by this sweep. EffortLevel gained Other(String) so from_wire("none") preserves the level, and the wire field became the tri-state EffortUpdate {Unchanged, Clear, Set} - so effort:"none" arrives as Set(Other("none")) and the toolbar follows instead of sticking on the prior level. Verified by fence PR #77: state::tests::advertised_none_effort_replaces_a_stale_level_instead_of_sticking, which PASSES ON ARRIVAL (that is the evidence - an executable claim the bug is closed, not a fix). AC 1/2/3/5 met; AC4 superseded deliberately - unknown levels now render verbatim rather than mapping to None, since effort ladders are schema-negotiated per model and a closed set silently loses backend additions.

title: Explore shrinking the TuiState render seam to valid-state projections (arch review C06)
description:
From the 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review, Candidate 06 (rated Worth Exploring with a mock/prototype label — weaker than the Strong candidates). Reconciled against the ADR corpus 2026-08-02: no ADR conflict; prototype before committing.

PROBLEM. The TuiState renderer interface has grown to 37 getters that nearly mirror UiState (CLAUDE.md still says ~25 — the doc has drifted either way). Its second implementor is a public field-for-field test adapter whose states bypass sorting, filtering, clamping, versioning, and active-voice mutations — so render tests can assert states production cannot produce.

SOLUTION SKETCH. Concentrate render-relevant, already-valid state behind a smaller renderer seam; remove application-lifecycle reads from what widgets and rendering tests must learn. Deletion test from the review: rendered access proves the seam is real; unused and application-only getters plus most mock projection vanish instead of reappearing.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS (2026-08-02 reconciliation):
1. Prototype on ONE widget first; adopt only if the adapter and test surface actually shrink. This candidate is exploratory, not ratified.
2. Preserve the compile-time read-only guarantee (renderer receives a shared trait reference, never mutable state) and the ADR-0005 read-only resolved Theme exposure.
3. Removing the mock adapter means render-order tests construct state through real mutations. That closes the bypass hole (aligned with the testing-layers principle) but budget the migration cost of existing floor and render tests before committing.
4. Update the CLAUDE.md TuiState section in the same pass (method count and contract).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A one-widget prototype exists and the go/no-go decision is recorded on this issue before any wide migration.
2. If adopted: renderer interface shrinks, the public-field mock adapter is gone, and render tests build state through real mutations.
3. Read-only rendering guarantee and ADR-0005 resolved-Theme exposure preserved.
4. CLAUDE.md TuiState section updated in the same PR.

title: Honour KAS replayMarking (_meta.kiro.replay) when session/load lands
description:
KAS 2.16.0 initialize advertises agentCapabilities._meta.kiro.replayMarking:true
(new; absent in 2.15.0, live-verified A/B).

Meaning, from the bundle comment: replayed session/load updates carry
_meta.kiro.replay: true, "letting clients isolate the replay stream from live
updates that interleave during the load."

Cyril does not implement session/load today, but this is a prerequisite worth
recording: without honouring the replay marker, a resumed session's history
would be indistinguishable from live streaming, and UiState would commit
replayed chunks as if they were arriving now (activity spinner, frame-rate
escalation, autoscroll all misfire).

Blocks nothing today; pair with any future session/resume work (cyril-wigv
covers the broader ACP session-discovery parity gap).

notes.content:
replayMarking CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-31 (2.16.0,
probe-kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.py). session/load on a session with one turn
of history produced NINE session/update frames, and the split is semantically
clean:

  _meta.kiro.replay == true  (6) — the replayed CONVERSATION:
      user_message_chunk
      session_info_update[turn_start]
      agent_message_chunk
      session_info_update[context_usage]
      session_info_update[turn_completion]
      session_info_update[turn_end]

  unmarked (3) — LIVE session setup arriving concurrently:
      config_option_update
      available_commands_update
      session_info_update[context_usage]

THE TRAP: `context_usage` appears in BOTH lists. A client that applies every
context_usage frame during a load will apply the historical value AFTER the
current one and end up displaying a stale percentage. The replay flag is the
only discriminator — there is no ordering guarantee to lean on.

So the rule for cyril: during session/load, frames with _meta.kiro.replay==true
must rebuild history WITHOUT driving live UI state (no activity spinner, no
frame-rate escalation, no autoscroll, no context-usage update); unmarked frames
are current and should be applied normally.

Also captured (session/fork, the /tangent substrate): fork succeeds and returns
{sessionId, modes, configOptions, _meta}, but its _meta shape DIFFERS from
session/new's — fork returns `{"kiro": {"parentSessionId": "<origin>"}}` whereas
session/new returns flat session metadata (schemaVersion/id/title/agentMode/...).
Two different _meta shapes on structurally similar responses; model them
separately. The `title` we passed did NOT come back and no `titleSetByUser`
appeared in the fork response, so that field is likely applied to the persisted
session record rather than echoed here — unverified either way.

Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.jsonl

NEW FIELD, live-captured 2026-08-08 on 2.16.2: agent_message_chunk carries
update._meta.kiro.replayId.

  "replayId": "903ef876-f1ff-4a6b-ab21-cab7002369ed-say"

A UUID with a role-ish suffix ("-say"). Absent from the 2.16.0 turn capture,
present in the 2.16.2 one (full-surface KAS turn A/B, capture
logs/../kas-turn-2.16.2.jsonl vs kas-turn-2.16.0.jsonl). It is the per-chunk
companion to the connection-level replayMarking capability this issue tracks
(agentCapabilities._meta.kiro.replayMarking, added 2.15.0) and to the
_meta.kiro.replay flag on replayed session/load updates.

So the replay story now has two halves on the wire: a per-connection capability,
and a per-chunk id. If cyril ever de-duplicates or re-anchors a replayed stream,
replayId is the join key -- model it alongside replay rather than after it.

CAVEAT on attribution: the two captures are NOT same-day (2.16.0 leg from the
original audit, 2.16.2 leg 2026-08-08), so binary and backend axes are conflated
per reference_kiro_wire_audit_methodology. replayId is a structural field rather
than backend-served content, so a binary origin is likely -- but it is not proven
until a same-day re-capture of the 2.16.0 leg.

title: Streamed agent text can render after TurnCompleted (ACP notification-vs-response ordering race)
description: agent-client-protocol (rpc.rs) resolves incoming RESPONSES inline in the read loop (oneshot send) but routes incoming NOTIFICATIONS through a separate incoming_tx queue handled by another task. So when a session/update notification immediately precedes the prompt response on the wire (zero scheduling gap), the response (-> TurnCompleted) can overtake the not-yet-handled notification on cyril's notification channel, committing TurnCompleted before the final streamed AgentMessage. Discovered during cyril-84ca Slice 7 via a zero-gap unit harness. NOT introduced by cyril-84ca (the pre-fix inline conn.prompt().await shares the identical race). Empirically does NOT manifest against real kiro 2.8.0 v2 OR KAS (.cyril-84ca/notif_order.rs: order is [msg,msg,TURN] for v2, [msg,TURN] for KAS) because real backends leave enough timing gap for the notification queue to drain. Low priority: theoretical/edge race, no observed production impact. Possible fixes if it ever surfaces: have the turn task yield/drain pending notifications before emitting TurnCompleted, or coalesce turn-end behind the notification queue.
acceptance_criteria: A unit/integration test reproduces the reorder deterministically AND a fix makes streamed AgentMessages always precede TurnCompleted on the notification channel even at zero wire-gap; verified to still hold against real v2 + KAS.

notes.content:
2026-06-21 — Real-world corroboration: upstream Kiro bug #9542 (https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro/issues/9542) shows the parent agent going Idle while a result is still in flight (trace WARN: 'received a tool execution event for an agent not processing tools ... active_state: Idle, executing_subagents: {}'), dropping the subagent's late result — the same parent-races-its-own-late-result shape as this race, observed in production. Caveat: that bug is the parent<->subagent channel INSIDE kiro (upstream of cyril's ACP wire), so it doesn't directly hit cyril's notification channel, but it proves late/dropped results around turn-end are not purely theoretical. Better repro tool than the synthetic zero-gap harness: KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH=/tmp/acp-trace.jsonl captures full ACP wire traffic as {ts,dir,msg} JSONL (tui.js, confirmed 2.8.1) — use it to capture real notification-vs-response ordering at near-zero gap. Verify any fix on BOTH v2 and v3/KAS (upstream failure mode is engine-specific). Subagent-rendering hazards from #9542 tracked in cyril-fjfu (KAS-3).

2026-07-02 — Ordering ground-truth from a real KAS session (KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH capture, exactly the tool this note recommended). Redacted snapshot committed at experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl (527 frames/880s, 2 turns: id=5 cancelled, id=8 completed). On BOTH completed turn boundaries the ONLY session/update trailing turn_end within 5s is a single session_info_update::context_usage (~10ms after the prompt response); NO agent_message_chunk or tool_call arrives after turn_end on either turn. So in this KAS/v3 session the streamed-text-after-TurnCompleted race did NOT manifest on the wire — only benign context telemetry trails turn_end (matches the 'context_usage trails turn_end' note in kas.rs). CAVEAT: v3/KAS only, 2 turns (one cancelled) = one sample, not proof; still verify any fix on BOTH v2 and v3. This is evidence the race is timing-window-narrow at the source, consistent with it being a cyril-side reordering risk rather than a routine backend emission.

title: Usage aggregation: add p90 (and max) latency percentiles to the summary
description:
The usage rollup in crates/cyril-core/src/usage.rs computes AVG and MAX but has no percentile: grep for p90/percentile/p95/median across crates/ returns zero hits.

v2's own /stats footer shows 'avg=4467ms  p90=7244ms  max=8924ms  errors=0'. An average alone hides the tail, which is the part users actually feel — and with the KAS stall watchdog now bounding dead streams at 300s (docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 2), tail latency is exactly the signal worth watching.

SCOPE: add p90 for duration_ms and ttft_ms to the usage summary, alongside the existing AVG/MAX.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: SQLite has NO built-in percentile function, so this is not a one-line SQL change. Either (a) ORDER BY + LIMIT/OFFSET at the computed index, or (b) pull the column and compute in Rust. Prefer whichever keeps the existing SUMMARY_COLUMNS grouping queries intact — the rollup is grouped by model/provider/agent_type/folder, so a percentile must be computed per group, not once globally. Cover with a fixture whose p90 differs from both mean and max so an accidental AVG/MAX aliasing fails the test.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #107 merged to main (370534cc). Nearest-rank p90 + max for duration_ms/ttft_ms on every rollup carrying UsageSummary; fences C1-C12 incl. sorted-oracle equality, NULL-denominator exclusion, group-locality, and the rendered-panel assertion. Post-review: MAX moved onto SUMMARY_COLUMNS, LatencyMetric enum, shared model_group_keys(), degrade-with-warning on query failure. title: Handle v2 stream_discarded: roll back uncommitted streaming text on mid-stream retry
description: kiro-cli 2.19.0 v2 engine adds session-update kind stream_discarded (binary strings 0->3; tui.js 0->4: "Stream discarded notice received; dropping rendered partial"). When a mid-stream reset triggers the new agent-layer retry, the engine tells the client to DROP the partially rendered stream before the retried attempt re-streams. Cyril appends agent_message_chunk text into streaming_text and never rolls back — ignoring stream_discarded means a retried v2 turn renders the aborted partial PLUS the full retry (duplicated prefix). Cyril today warn-drops the unknown kind, so the failure mode is silent duplication, not a crash. Work: parse stream_discarded (rides the _kiro.dev/session/update ext envelope per string-table co-location; confirm envelope with one live/mock capture — static-only evidence so far, see docs/kiro-2.19.0-wire-audit.md), map to a notification, and clear the uncommitted streaming_text buffer for that session (committed messages stay). KAS unaffected (0 occurrences in 0.46.1).
acceptance_criteria: stream_discarded clears streaming_text without touching committed messages; state lifecycle test: chunks -> stream_discarded -> retried chunks -> TurnCompleted yields exactly one copy of the retried text; envelope confirmed on a capture before merging.

title: Persist source-turn fragments as rows instead of rewriting the projection per batch
description:
## Context

PR #105 review finding #15 (store.rs capture_batch) was partially addressed: an identical replay now writes nothing, and stored data is never re-redacted or re-validated on reload. What remains is write amplification — every accepted batch rewrites the turn's whole projection (prompt, assistant, tools, tools_text, assembly JSON), so a 1 MB turn delivered in 16 batches writes ~16 MB (O(N) bytes per batch, O(N^2) per turn). The runtime services connections serially ahead of prepare_prompt, so this sits in front of the 250 ms first-prompt path.

## Proposed shape

- New table source_turn_fragments(source_turn_id, sequence, kind, block_index, text, ...) keyed by (source_turn_id, sequence); a batch appends only its new events and reads only the digests it needs for replay equality.
- source_turns keeps header/state columns while incomplete; prompt/assistant/tools_text/assembly are materialized once at terminal commit (that is also where whole-text redaction and the canonical hash already run). Incomplete-turn reads (list_turns/inspect_turn) assemble on demand.
- FTS content columns stay on source_turns, so the single AFTER UPDATE trigger and the project_id FTS column are unaffected.
- Keep StoredSourceTurn/SourceTurnDraft::from_stored as the seam: the draft should not know whether its assembly came from one row or many.

## Not in scope

Changing the wire protocol, batch limits, or recall ranking.
acceptance_criteria:
- Measured per-batch cost for a 16 x 64 KiB assistant turn is flat (does not grow with the number of batches already applied), with a fence that asserts the bytes written per batch are bounded by the batch size plus a constant.
- Identical replay still writes no row; conflicting replay still returns IntegrityConflict with an audit row.
- c3/c4/c5/c6/c8 store fences and the real-runtime restart replay test stay green; schema v3 validator lists every new object.
- A v3 store from before the change either migrates in one Immediate transaction or is rejected as unsupported — never half-migrated.

title: Tool-call interruption/recovery is unverified — both 2.16.1 and 2.16.2 fixed it, and it lands on cyril's merge_update path
description:
BOTH 2.16.1 and 2.16.2 fixed tool-call interruption handling, and no probe in the
tree exercises it -- so cyril's behaviour against the fixed engine is unverified.

  2.16.1  "Fixed some V3 sessions failing to continue after an interrupted tool
           call or inconsistent tool-call record"   (official notes; ABSENT from
           the embedded changelog)
  2.16.2  "Subagents recover from a tool call interrupted mid-arguments instead of
           faulting the turn"

WHY THIS IS ON CYRIL'S PATH
cyril renders tool_call / tool_call_update and merges partial updates in place
(merge_update, guarded so an update that omits a field does not clobber it). A
change in WHICH frames arrive for an interrupted call -- a tool_call that never
completes, a tool_call_update with partial rawInput, a recovery frame that
re-opens a call cyril already committed -- lands directly on that merge path and on
the streaming/commit ordering in UiState.

The 2.16.2 wording is specific and suggestive: "interrupted mid-arguments" implies
a tool_call whose rawInput is partial at the time of interruption. cyril's
TrackedToolCall derives display from rawInput (primary_path(), command_text()), so
a partial-argument frame is exactly the shape that could render wrong or panic a
display helper.

WHAT TO DO
Provoke an interrupted tool call against 2.16.2 (cancel mid-tool-call is the
obvious lever; session/cancel during a long-running terminal or fs op) and capture
the frame sequence. Then assert cyril's merge + commit path handles it: no
duplicate committed tool call, no clobbered fields, no stuck in-progress entry.

Costs credits (a real turn with a real tool call). Cheap relative to discovering it
as a stuck spinner in a live session.

Recorded as a residual gap in docs/kiro-2.16.2-wire-audit.md.
acceptance_criteria:
REVISED 2026-08-18 (original live mid-arguments capture requirement discharged as unsatisfiable: six attempts across 2.16.2 and 2.18.1, see notes).
1. Wire-representability check (source-derived, cyril-vhfz precedent): read the extracted @kiro/agent KAS source (current bundle) at every tool_call / tool_call_update emission site and determine whether a frame can ever carry an absent or partial rawInput. Record the finding with source citations in .cyril-a5wo/. If unrepresentable, criterion 3 closes as unreachable-by-construction. If representable, build a source-derived fixture (provenance recorded, SHA-256 pinned, fixture-README style) exercising that shape.
2. Cancel-recovery lifecycle fences: the six committed captures (captures/attempt-1..3 on 2.16.2, captures-2.18.1/attempt-1..3 on 2.18.1) drive fences on cyril's tool-call merge/commit path: replaying the same-toolCallId pending, in_progress, failed sequence yields no duplicate committed tool call, no clobbered fields (merge_update guards preserve content, locations, title, raw_input), and no stuck in-progress entry after the terminal update and turn end.
3. Partial-rawInput display handling, contingent on 1: either closed as unreachable with citation, or convert/ and TrackedToolCall display helpers (primary_path, command_text) are asserted against the criterion-1 fixture: no panic, no wrong rendering on absent or partial rawInput.

notes.content: 2026-08-09 prove-it-prototype blocked after three authenticated kiro-cli 2.16.2 KAS attempts. Each injected session/cancel on the first observable agent-subtask tool_call and captured same-ID pending -> in_progress -> failed recovery, but rawInput was already complete in every frame; the required mid-arguments/partial-rawInput ACP shape never appeared. Evidence: feat/cyril-a5wo-interruption commit 327d048, .cyril-a5wo/findings.md and captures/attempt-{1,2,3}.jsonl. Resume only with a way to trigger or obtain the upstream internal mid-arguments frame sequence, or after explicitly revising the live-evidence acceptance criterion.

2026-08-18 reprobe on kiro-cli 2.18.1 (current engine): identical to 2.16.2 on every oracle predicate — three fresh attempts, cancel injected, same-toolCallId pending->in_progress->failed recovery, rawInput COMPLETE in every frame. Six attempts across two engine generations; mid-arguments never crosses the ACP seam. Evidence: feat/cyril-a5wo-interruption 816c0bc (.cyril-a5wo/captures-2.18.1/ + findings.md). Still blocked on the live partial-rawInput criterion; disposition = revise criterion (vhfz source-derived-fixture precedent) or refocus on the twice-confirmed cancel-recovery lifecycle.

2026-08-18: acceptance criteria revised per the block's second resume condition — the live partial-rawInput capture is discharged as unsatisfiable at the ACP seam (six attempts, two engine generations). Reoriented to (1) source-derived wire-representability, (2) lifecycle fences off the six committed captures, (3) display handling contingent on 1. Unblocked.

Closed: Completed on feat/cyril-a5wo-interruption. Source audit/fixture fence: 12b40fc. Absent/partial display fence: 1684877. Six-capture cancel-recovery fence: e2c3922. Gilfoyle checkpoint record: 622e738. Verified pinned @kiro/agent 0.38.7/SHA source representability, exact generated fixture, all C1-C6 named mutations, focused core/UI/lifecycle/merge fences, two clean workspace runs (1,671 passed each), clippy -D warnings, rustfmt, no upstream drift, and independent review with no findings.

title: KAS-2a follow-up: turn-seq dedup so a stale TurnCompleted can't clear a later same-session turn
description:
Slice 3 of cyril-j16p dedupes the double TurnCompleted (turn_end notification + prompt response) with a 'drop when turn_in_flight is None' guard in the bridge loop observer (bridge.rs:1370). Correct for the common case but has a residual: turn A's late prompt-response TurnCompleted, arriving AFTER turn_end cleared the flag AND a new same-session turn B started, would match B's turn_in_flight (session id is not per-turn unique) and wrongly clear it. Fix: give TurnCompleted a monotonic per-turn id (bridge.rs:562 already anticipates 'a turn id field to TurnCompleted'); the observer clears/forwards only on an id match. Low-risk for the KAS-2a walking skeleton (narrow window, trivial turns); deferred from cyril-j16p Slice 3. Ref ROADMAP:KAS-2a.

CROSS-SESSION DIMENSION (independently surfaced by all 5 /code-review max finders, 2026-06-29 — strong observability signal): the same turn_in_flight: Option<SessionId> gate is also session-blind. The observer (bridge.rs:1385) matches TurnCompleted by variant only and never compares routed.session_id. A non-in-flight session's turn_end -> TurnCompleted (e.g. a future KAS spec/secondary/parallel-turn session, per docs/kiro-2.7.1-wire-audit) would clear the MAIN turn's gate (premature un-busy + early SendPrompt accept), or be dropped when the gate is None. NOT reachable in KAS-2a (single session; KAS subagents are tool_calls with no per-session turn_end). The monotonic per-turn-id fix above ALSO resolves this, provided the id is globally unique across (session, turn). CONSTRAINT for the fixer: the off-loop prompt-response TurnCompleted is sent as RoutedNotification::global (session_id None, event.rs:251), so a naive 'clear only when routed.session_id == turn_in_flight' fix WITHOUT a turn id would break v2 — the global signal never matches Some(main), freezing every v2 turn busy. The fix must key on a turn id, not a bare session id.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) HOLE in the turn-id fix as sketched: the bridge loop can stamp only the SYNTHESIZED prompt-response TurnCompleted; the KAS turn_end TurnCompleted is produced by the converter (convert/kas.rs:34) from a wire frame the bridge cannot stamp — a stale same-session turn_end still matches by session, so the residual survives for that signal. Either (a) probe whether session_info_update carries a native turn identifier, or (b) the observer tracks 'one duplicate still expected for the previous (session, seq)'. The variant likely needs Option<TurnId> with dual matching (id-match for synthesized, session-match for wire-scoped turn_end) — a legitimate Option-for-absent, not a sentinel. Make it a TurnId(u64) newtype per CLAUDE.md (mirror TerminalRegistry's saturating_add counter idiom, terminal_io.rs:106).
(2) Design JOINTLY with cyril-pnwb — same observer code (bridge.rs:1370-1393); turn identity and stop-reason precedence are one 'which signal is authoritative' question, not two.
(3) Cross-session nuance to fold in: a non-in-flight session's turn_end clears the bridge gate while the App routes the scoped TurnCompleted to a subagent stream — a SPLIT-BRAIN (bridge accepts a new prompt, main UI stays Busy) rather than the premature un-busy described. Same fix covers it.

Closed: Shipped: PR #69 merged to main (af12663). Per-turn TurnId ownership; mediator matches on owner (stamped) or session+companion-ledger (identity-free wire turn_end), absorb-first. Fixes two observable defects: stale same-session completion clearing a newer turn, and the cross-session split-brain where a foreign turn_end cleared the main busy guard. Claims C1-C10 each fenced; 6 fences mutation-verified. Runtime oracle 6/9 -> 9/9, moving only at the two slices the plan predicted. Filed: cyril-ns0o (spec-named bridge fences the build substituted), cyril-upjh (ActiveTurn missing engine -> KAS-only companion guard unconditional), cyril-b4y4 (extract TurnMediator). design.md gains blindnesses B16-B18.

title: Harden bridge against unknown sessionUpdate variants on standard session/update (latent hard-fail; steering receipts may migrate methods)
description: CLAUDE.md records that SessionUpdate is a serde-tagged enum with NO #[serde(other)] catch-all: an unknown typed variant on the STANDARD session/update method hard-fails at deserialization before reaching convert/. Today cyril is safe by accident: v2 steering receipts (steering_queued/consumed/cleared) arrive on the ext method _kiro.dev/session/update and are handled in convert/kiro.rs ~746 — and cyril ALREADY sends session/steer (K1a/b shipped), so receipts flow in live sessions. KiroCrew, the sibling AWS client, defends both methods and its comment claims receipts ride the standard method since kiro 2.9. If kiro migrates the receipts (or ships any new typed variant) onto standard session/update, the bridge deserialization hard-fails — blast radius depends on how the acp crate surfaces the error (single notification lost vs connection torn down), which is currently uncharacterized. This is resilience work: the bridge must survive ANY unknown sessionUpdate discriminant, logging and routing it rather than failing.
acceptance_criteria: Failure mode characterized first: a test feeds a raw session/update frame with an unknown sessionUpdate discriminant through the current agent-client-protocol 0.10.2 path and documents exactly what breaks (notification dropped, error surfaced, or connection killed); an A/B capture against current kiro-cli establishes which method carries v2 steering receipts today (arbitrating the 2.7.0 capture vs the KiroCrew v2.9 claim); the bridge is made resilient — an unknown discriminant on standard session/update is routed to the extension-notification path (or dropped with a warn-level log naming the discriminant), never a hard-fail, matching the KAS-side kas_engine_drops_unknown_ext_frame precedent; regression fence with a raw-frame fixture containing steering_queued AND a nonsense discriminant on the standard method; findings recorded in docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md with provenance tags.

notes.content: Source: kirocrew @ e44259ce src/kiro_crew/acp/_dispatch.py:131-149 — classifies steering_queued/consumed/cleared (plus legacy AgentExecutionUserMessageQueued / AgentExecutionSteeringInjected) on BOTH the standard session/update method AND _kiro.dev/session/update, with comment "v2.9 session/update / v2.7 _kiro.dev/session/update". Conflicts with the cyril 2.7.0 capture (receipts on _kiro.dev/session/update only) — an A/B capture on current kiro-cli must arbitrate. Critic caveat: verify how agent-client-protocol 0.10.2 actually fails on an unknown variant BEFORE designing the fix — the right shape differs if the envelope already tolerates unknowns. See docs/kirocrew-deep-dive.md top adoption #2.

title: KAS-8 — decide model-or-explicitly-ignore for three additive 2.16.1/2.16.2 fields (prompts[].serverName, sessions/changed.updatedAt, spec/phaseCheckpoint)
description:
Three additive fields landed in 2.16.1/2.16.2 that cyril neither models nor
explicitly ignores. Per feedback_model_full_wire_surface, each needs a decision --
model it, or explicit-ignore plus an unknown-key debug log -- rather than silence.

  session/update (v2 settle)  prompts[].serverName
      cyril DOES parse prompts (convert/kiro.rs -> PromptInfo), selectively, so the
      field is dropped today. It would disambiguate MCP-server-provided prompts.

  _kiro/sessions/changed      upserted[].updatedAt
      Joins source + executionTarget.kind (2.16.0) on the same frame. cyril
      tolerates this notification and consumes nothing. Related but NOT the same
      message as cyril-nn85 (_kiro/session/list response shape).

  _kiro/spec/phaseCheckpoint  new method (2.16.1)
      Emitter src/spec/session/spec-phase-checkpoint-emitter.ts; matches the
      "spec sessions self-repair malformed spec artifacts" release note. Spec is a
      standing KAS-7 NON-GOAL, so the expected outcome here is a recorded decline
      -- but KAS-8 exists precisely so every unhandled surface is DECIDED rather
      than silently missing, and this one is currently silent.

None of these is urgent; all three are cheap. Grouped because they share one
resolution shape.

Evidence: docs/kiro-2.16.2-wire-audit.md
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each of the three has an explicit outcome recorded: modelled, or explicitly ignored with an unknown-key debug log.
2. spec/phaseCheckpoint's decline is written down as a decision referencing the KAS-7 spec non-goal, not left absent.
3. No silent drops remain for these fields.

title: Probe: is the rules+file-tree injection stack ACP-driven or subagent-driven? (~2.1k tok/session at stake)
description:
From the 2026-07-23 AWS prompt-log analysis (docs/kiro-prompt-assembly.md).

All 33 records carrying `<current_context>Machine ID: acp-client</current_context>` ALSO
carry the subagent scaffold (`<progress_reporting>` + `<response_requirement>`). So two
hypotheses are perfectly confounded in that sample:

  H1  an ACP client gets `## Included Rules` + `<session_start_snapshot>` file tree
  H2  a SUBAGENT gets them, regardless of how the parent was driven

Why it matters: the `session_start_snapshot` fileTree was a fixed 8,582 chars (~2.1k
tokens) — 45% of the turn it appeared in. Under H1 every cyril session silently pays that
on the first turn for a file tree cyril never requested and cannot display. Under H2 it
only affects spawned subagents.

Probe (one axis at a time, per reference_kiro_wire_audit_methodology): same binary, same
day, one plain MAIN-AGENT turn over ACP vs one over the native TUI. The prompt log is the
only place the answer is visible — the ACP wire is upstream of assembly, so a proxy
capture cannot answer this. Needs an account with prompt logging enabled.

If H1 holds, follow-on question: can the snapshot be suppressed, and should cyril surface
its token cost in the context display (project_cyril_enhancing_proxy context-display gap)?

title: KAS-0 — Engine trait + v2 port
description: Engine abstraction trait + port of current v2 (Rust) behavior behind it. Will later absorb K1a's three new convert/kiro.rs steering arms into the V2Engine impl at negligible cost. First milestone of the KAS engine integration track.
design:
KAS-0 design — synthesized via grill-with-docs (2026-06-21). Decisions D1-D9; full rationale in ADR-0004 + ADR-0001/0002. Acceptance = strict v2 behavioral parity (no visible change).

D1 Turn-end ownership: KAS-0 OWNS the v2 turn-end rewiring (not deferred to KAS-2a) — only way to prove the seam under v2 parity.
D2 Turn-end marker: no predicate/enum. Notification::TurnCompleted is the universal marker both engines converge on (v2 synthesizes from prompt() response; KAS maps session_info_update->turn_end). Busy-state becomes a flag cleared by observing the marker.
D3 Flag location: loop-local turn_in_flight: Option<SessionId>, set on SendPrompt, cleared when the loop observes TurnCompleted. Replaces prompt_task.is_finished() at bridge.rs:395 (busy-guard) + :455 (cancel-target). JoinHandle retained ONLY for Shutdown abort (bridge.rs:1233).
D4 Single-mediator loop (ADR-0004): run_loop select!s over an internal BridgeInbound{Notification,Request} channel. KiroClient + prompt_task feed it; loop forwards to App + clears flag on TurnCompleted. convert STAYS in KiroClient (loop forwards already-converted internal types). Engine shared as Rc<dyn Engine> (KiroClient=convert, loop=client_capabilities at bridge.rs:320).
D5 Request path through loop too, NON-BLOCKING (hard invariant): request_permission builds PermissionRequest with its embedded responder oneshot, sends to loop; loop forwards to App (identity mediation in v2); App replies on the oneshot BYPASSING the loop. Loop never awaits a human decision. Slow KAS-5 resolution spawns off-loop. Captured in ADR-0004.
D6 Capability sub-traits via defaulted accessors on Engine: fn as_auth_responder(&self)->Option<&dyn AuthResponder>{None}. KAS-0 stubs ONE worked example (AuthResponder, KAS-1's) + accessor; V2Engine overrides nothing. Open/closed: new surface = 1 sub-trait + 1 defaulted accessor, v2 untouched.
D7 AgentEngine{V2,Kas} typed selector (--agent-engine flag/config, default v2), NOT argv-sniffed from AgentCommand. run_bridge picks Box<dyn Engine> at spawn: V2=>V2Engine; Kas=>clean "not available yet" via existing error path. No KAS spawn / flag-version resolution (both KAS-1).
D8 kas cargo feature: cyril-core owns kas=[] (empty), cyril forwards kas=["cyril-core/kas"], cyril-ui none. Dedicated "kas-feature" CI job: build+clippy(-D warnings)+test -p cyril --features kas.
D9 Verification spike (parallel, NON-gating): reuse experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-* to capture a live KAS turn's session/update frames -> commit fixtures -> Rust test deserializes each into acp::SessionNotification, asserts Ok (CI-able, no live KAS). A failing variant = documented KAS-2a upgrade-trigger (no #[serde(other)] on SessionUpdate), not a KAS-0 blocker.

V2Engine = thin wrapper delegating to existing convert::session_update_to_notification (mod.rs:393) + convert::kiro::to_ext_notification (kiro.rs:173) — functions don't move.

Suggested slices (each ends green on all v2 tests): (1) Engine trait + V2Engine + client_capabilities-from-engine; (2) single-mediator loop (notifications + requests; flag replaces is_finished); (3) AgentEngine selector + run_bridge gate; (4) kas feature + AuthResponder stub + accessor + CI job; (5) verification spike fixtures+test.

Hazards handed forward — KAS-2a: post-turn_end, the still-running prompt task must not emit a competing late TurnCompleted, and a new SendPrompt must not orphan a live JoinHandle. KAS-5: slow request resolution spawns off-loop, never await in the loop (ADR-0004).
acceptance_criteria: Invisible foundation — ZERO user-visible change. Oracle is behavioral: (a) every existing v2 test passes; (b) a live `kiro-cli acp` session streams text/thoughts, runs tool calls, renders subagents, handles permission approve/cancel, and mode-picks IDENTICALLY to pre-refactor; (c) `--agent-engine kas` cleanly reports "not available yet" (no panic); (d) `kas-feature` CI job (build+clippy+test --features kas) is green; (e) verification-spike deser test passes on captured KAS session/update fixtures. Per-slice: each slice ends with all v2 tests + clippy -D warnings + fmt clean.

notes.content:
Reconstructed 2026-06-17 from .k1a-steering/related-issues.md; detail from ROADMAP KAS track.

Turn-end coupling (from PR #22 / cyril-84ca, 2026-06-17): the off-loop prompt dispatch made TurnCompleted be emitted when conn.prompt().await resolves, and the one-turn busy-guard keys off prompt_task.is_finished(). Both assume 'prompt response == turn end' — true for v2, FALSE for KAS (KAS-2a: turn-end is session_info_update->turn_end; the prompt response is secondary/late). Under KAS, is_finished() stays false after a logical turn-end, so a legitimate next prompt is wrongly rejected with 'a turn is already in progress', and TurnCompleted fires late/never. When this milestone introduces the Engine trait's turn-end detection and ports v2 behind V2Engine, route BOTH the busy-guard and TurnCompleted emission through the engine's turn-end signal, NOT prompt_task.is_finished()/prompt().await. Concrete code: bridge.rs SendPrompt guard + the spawned prompt_task.

title: usage_turns grows without bound — no retention, pruning or vacuum on usage.sqlite3
description:
crates/cyril-core/src/usage.rs appends one usage_turns row per turn and never removes any: a grep for delete/retention/prune/vacuum across the module finds nothing. RECENT_LIMIT = 20 (usage.rs:50) caps only the 'recent' listing, not the table. usage.sqlite3 therefore grows for the life of the install.

Surfaced as a T3 production-scale risk while routing cyril-9kyk (.cyril-9kyk/route.md). That change adds nearest-rank p90/max computed per group via CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY ...), which sorts every partition — so query cost now scales with total row count, not just with the number of groups. cyril-9kyk pins a budget (<= 250 ms added to snapshot() at 100,000 rows across >= 20 (provider, model) groups) and its regression fence holds that bound, but a budget is not a bound on the table itself: past some size the fence fails and there is no mechanism to recover.

SCOPE: decide and implement a retention policy for usage_turns and its child tables (usage_tools, usage_compactions, and any FK'd rows) — options include a row cap with oldest-first deletion, an age cutoff, rollup-then-discard of old detail, or an explicit user-invoked prune. Whatever is chosen must keep the aggregation semantics honest: silently dropping rows changes every all-time average and percentile the summary reports, so either the summary states its window or retention preserves pre-aggregated totals.

NOT in scope here: per-request granularity (permanent non-goal, cyril-uvrf).

title: Extract a TurnMediator from run_loop's notification arm
description:
Pre-PR review of cyril-a71q raised three related structural smells in the bridge notification arm, all pointing at one missing type.

Data Clumps / Divergent Change: `active_turn`, `turn_alloc` and `companion` are three run_loop locals that only ever mutate together, driven by a ~110-line decision inlined in the select! arm. That trio plus the block is a `TurnMediator` waiting to be born — `fn observe(&mut self, routed: &RoutedNotification) -> Disposition` — which would also make the mediation unit-testable without the async harness. Several build-time blindnesses (design.md B16-B18) exist precisely because the policy can only be observed through the harness; a mediator type would make some of them directly assertable.

Duplicated Code: the two absorb blocks (stamped arm and identity-free arm) are byte-identical apart from the CompanionSource in the log line, and the two `companion = Some(Companion { .. })` registrations differ only in `awaiting`/`first`.

Message Chains: `scope_is` reaches into `session.0.as_ref()` to string-compare cyril's SessionId against agent_client_protocol's. A conversion or comparison helper on the newtype boundary would hide the walk.

Deliberately NOT done during cyril-a71q's build: these are refactors of working, fenced code, and reshaping the mediator at pre-PR review time would have invalidated the slice-by-slice mutation testing that established the fences discriminate. The extraction is worth doing on its own, with those fences already in place to protect it.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-01: independently corroborated; promoted P4->P3; now GATES cyril-g9vt ---

The 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review reached this independently as Candidate 02, "Deepen the turn lifecycle module", rated Strong — co-equal with Candidate 01 (cyril-g9vt), which was its top recommendation. Its Before-diagram marks as leakage exactly the run_loop state this issue names, plus two more: active_turn, companion, prompt_tasks, deferred_disconnect, and the owner stamp the App ignores. It scopes the extraction slightly wider than this ticket did — accepted-turn state, prompt-task lifetime, terminal-source reconciliation, cancel targeting, shutdown, AND disconnect ordering in one bridge-internal module.

WHY IT NOW GOES FIRST. The review's amber box notes that Candidate 02 would "reopen ADR-0004's early conversion of both raw terminal sources into the same pre-mediation TurnCompleted marker". That is ADR-0004's OWN turn-completion section — the same ADR the g9vt callback-mediator amendment touches. Landing g9vt first means amending ADR-0004 now and again later on overlapping ground, with the second amendment partially reopening the first. Landing this first means ONE coherent amendment covering both directions of mediation, and lands the callback mediator in a run_loop that has already shed ~110 lines of inline turn policy (it is ~1,405 lines today).

Its deletion test: deleting the current turn module moves only a counter into bridge.rs; deleting lifecycle knowledge recreates stale-completion, KAS deduplication, and cancel logic across the loop.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Ownership mediation lives in a type with an observe()-style entry point, unit-testable without the async harness.
2. The duplicated absorb and registration blocks are expressed once.
3. All existing a71q fences still pass unchanged.
4. design.md's B16-B18 are re-assessed: any that become directly assertable are promoted to real fences.
5. If the extraction takes the review's wider scope (prompt-task lifetime, cancel targeting, shutdown, disconnect ordering), ADR-0004's turn-completion section is amended in the SAME pass — not left for cyril-g9vt to amend a second time.

notes.content: 2026-08-02 ADR/glossary reconciliation — source-authority constraint for the extraction: the lifecycle module owns the STATE MACHINE (transitions, dedup, cancel targeting, shutdown, disconnect ordering), but terminal-source AUTHORITY is an Engine fact. Ask the bound Engine which turn terminal is authoritative rather than branching on engine.kind() inside the module — kind-matching reintroduces the enum-match pattern ADR-0001 rejected, and the CONTEXT.md Turn-end entry now pins the rule: only the bound engine may declare a turn over. Live-confirmed KAS behavior (turn-end-ordering captures): BOTH terminals arrive every turn, turn_end first, prompt response 0-1ms behind — reconciliation is mandatory per-turn, not defensive.

Closed: Shipped: PR #81 merged to main (decef9e45). All 5 ACs met: observe()-style TurnMediator (pub(crate), sync, zero acp/AgentEngine imports) unit-testable without the harness; absorb+registration each expressed once; a71q fences unchanged (nextest-list diff: only planned upjh-test replacement); B16 PROMOTED (mutation M2 killed at matrix f3), B18-policy PROMOTED (matrix f4), B17 stays signed; ADR-0004 turn-completion amendment landed same pass. Fences: mediator_matrix_all_dispositions, turn_mediation_probe_scenario, terminal_source_matrix. Fixed in-branch: none. Filed: none. Unblocks cyril-g9vt.

title: Render commands/execute result data, not the lossy message stub — /usage and friends are showing a summary line
description:
The kiro.dev/commands/execute RESPONSE carries structured content in result.data; the result.message field is a lossy format template. KiroCrew shipped a fix for exactly this (their issue #5008).

Their close comment: "format_command_result now serializes every non-agent/model field in result.data as a readable JSON block instead of showing only the terse message (Plan: ... | N usage breakdowns). That preserves usageBreakdowns, reset/plan fields, and credit fields returned by /usage."

Root cause they document: kiro-cli has two /usage render paths — a rich Ink/React TUI panel, and a plain-text fallback of the shape "Plan: {planName} | {N} usage breakdowns". An ACP client has no Ink renderer, so it always gets path 2 unless it reads data itself.

Related trap (their issue #4972): routing a slash command through session/prompt instead of commands/execute hands it to the MODEL, which summarizes kiro-cli output instead of returning it — a silent wrong answer, not a degradation.

Full routing matrix worth encoding:
  set_mode / set_model      -> fire-and-forget, do NOT await (kiro usually never responds)
  /compact, /help           -> session/prompt ONLY (commands/execute string form: rc=0, no response)
  everything else on kiro   -> commands/execute, OBJECT form, awaited
  anything on KAS           -> session/prompt (fail-closed; _kiro.dev/* is kiro-only)

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 4.1, 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: /usage, /context, /tools and /mcp render the structured data payload rather than the message stub. Command routing follows the matrix above.

title: KAS terminals orphaned on Shutdown/bridge death — no kill_on_drop, no Shutdown-arm sweep
description: Found by the 2026-07-01 issue-set reliability review (grounded in code, not speculative): BridgeCommand::Shutdown aborts only prompt_task (bridge.rs:1363-1365); TerminalRegistry children are spawned WITHOUT kill_on_drop (terminal_io.rs:85-104), and when run_loop breaks, dropping the LocalSet kills nothing — live terminal children survive cyril exiting entirely. cyril-3lh8 covers only the session/cancel + turn-end reaping paths; this is the bridge-LIFETIME path (Shutdown, bridge thread death, app exit mid-command). Cheapest fix: .kill_on_drop(true) on the Command at create (also backstops the cyril-3lh8/cyril-r3t6 cancel-wedge interaction) + an explicit registry sweep in the Shutdown arm. Coordinate with cyril-3lh8's session-keyed reaping so the sweep reuses the same registry mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: No KAS-spawned terminal child outlives the cyril process: exiting cyril (or bridge Shutdown) while a long-running terminal command is in flight kills the child. Verified with a sleep-60 terminal command + a process-tree check after exit.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #43 (a875cba + 8cc9ae7 portable fence probe). Repro: dropped_registry_kills_running_terminal + dropped_inflight_wait_kills_terminal. kill_on_drop alone met criteria — no Shutdown sweep, no g9vt seam wiring needed.

title: Research intermittent missing KAS turn terminal after complete streamed response
description:
## Problem

A live cyril-core KAS consumer repeatedly streamed a complete agent response, including a finished Wayfinder question round, but intermittently received no `TurnCompleted`. Without an authoritative terminal, the consumer cannot safely decide that the logical turn ended or submit the next answer on the same session.

This is distinct from cyril-w0vy: no exact security-filter interruption marker was observed. It is also the inverse of cyril-9akh: the problem is an absent terminal after visible text, not text arriving after an early terminal.

## Expected

Every completed logical KAS turn emits one authoritative terminal after its streamed content, and a second prompt is accepted on the same session.

## Reproduction

1. Authenticate the locally installed Kiro CLI.
2. Start one KAS ACP session through cyril-core in a disposable repository.
3. Send a long Wayfinder-style prompt that streams agent text and tool activity, then asks the user an ordered set of questions.
4. Submit answers through several successive rounds on the same session.
5. Record the raw ACP frames and cyril notification timeline through each response.
6. Observe that some runs deliver the complete next question round but never deliver `TurnCompleted`; shorter runs can complete normally.

## Research question

Determine whether the authoritative KAS `session_info_update` `turn_end` is absent on the wire, lost or rejected during conversion, reordered or suppressed during bridge mediation, or associated with the wrong turn/session. Establish whether response length, tool activity, repeated prompts, or connection state is required to trigger it.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable probe or bounded stress fixture captures both a passing and failing run; the report includes raw ACP frame order and cyril notification order; the missing terminal is localized to KAS, agent-client-protocol transport, conversion, or bridge mediation; cyril-w0vy and cyril-9akh are explicitly confirmed or ruled out; the result either identifies a concrete fix contract with a regression oracle or files narrower implementation issue(s).

notes.content: Research sharpening: healthy KAS turns have two candidate terminal sources: the wire `session_info_update` `turn_end` and the prompt RPC response, with first-source-wins mediation and companion absorption. A failing capture must record both sources and the mediation disposition; a terminal that is unowned or mis-scoped can be dropped before reaching the consumer. Confirm the concrete recovery behavior by sending the next prompt: the expected wedged-session symptom is `a turn is already in progress`, requiring process teardown. Contrast with fail-stop agent death, which should surface BridgeError, TurnCompleted, then BridgeDisconnected.

2026-08-11 live capture LOCALIZES one mechanism (wire tap via KIRO_AGENT_PATH node shim + instrumented cyril-core probe; artifacts: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-turn-stall-{wire,verdict}-2.16.2.{jsonl,json,md}). Run of 4 turns: 1-3 delivered canonical turn_completion->turn_end->response (<=2ms apart; mediator forwarded+absorbed each); turn 4 WEDGED. Wire proof: after prompt id=5 only turn_start, focus_update, one tool_call_update ('charting the map now'), 2 context_usage - then ZERO frames ever. ABSENT ON THE WIRE; conversion/mediation/transport exonerated (lossless .send().await channels, tolerant turn_end conversion, mediator traces show nothing arrived). Root cause of captured instance: the turn never ended - KAS's 2nd model leg (long map-creation call) stalled ~16min on the backend stream (NO KAS timeout; ECONNRESET on telemetry flush mid-window); execution never succeeded; assistant text persisted 23:23:42Z AFTER the client died. Phenomenology decoded: the 'complete streamed question round' is the PREVIOUS turn's output; the wedged turn streams only a tool blip. RESIDUAL (still needs-info): the Aug 11 13:07-14:46 Tauri runs show a DIFFERENT signature - Execution succeeded + turn_end persisted in seconds for the wedged round (5 sessions), delivery unproven either way (no tap); consumer logs requested from the driving agent. The 14:27+ runs are auth casualties (hard-expired token, no execution) - not reproductions. w0vy ruled out for captured instance (no marker chunk, engine busy not idle); 9akh ruled out (no reorder - nothing arrived). Also: acp-server.js does NOT exit on stdin EOF -> ~30 orphaned node processes accumulated from probe research; bridge teardown must kill the child. Fix contract direction: do NOT synthesize terminals on silence (turn completed 16min late - synthesis would race a genuine terminal, the a71q/pnwb hazard); surface turn-liveness instead - follow-up issue filed.

2026-08-12 batch results CLOSE the reproducible half. Two tapped batches tonight (9 runs with real turns, ~27 turns, 2.16.2 bundle pinned): ZERO wedges; runs 5-6 charted end-to-end (PERSISTED_WAYFINDER_MAP, clean shutdown). Combined with the afternoon near-every-run wedge rate, the stall mechanism is a BACKEND CONDITION WINDOW, not a per-turn probability - liveness design in cyril-14ou should assume long clean stretches punctuated by bad windows. Residual signature A (internal-complete, no delivery; the 5 Tauri sessions): NOT reproduced under the tap; the driving session is gone (peer 'cyril-b0' turned out to be the /ship cyril-0qe6 session, not the awf-chart driver), so its consumer logs are unrecoverable. Leading hypothesis documented: consumer-side drain stall - the Tauri prototype makes blocking rivets Command::output() calls inside its async notification arm; a hang there freezes the drain chain and produces exactly the observed KAS-side evidence (internal success + parked frames). That is a trailblazer consumer defect class, not a cyril-core one. Cancel-under-stall arm never fired (no wedge) - stays in cyril-14ou scope. Harness preserved at experiments/bh7g-harness/ (wire tap + auto-driver + classifier; pin updated per release) for instant re-capture when a bad window returns. Acceptance criteria met: probe repeatable, both run classes captured (batch 1: pass rounds + wedged round in one session), frame+notification order recorded, mechanism localized (KAS/backend), w0vy+9akh ruled out, narrower fix issue filed (cyril-14ou). Closing.

title: Probe: <user-rule> fence is unescaped — can a steering file escape into top-level prompt scaffolding?
description:
From the 2026-07-23 AWS prompt-log analysis (docs/kiro-prompt-assembly.md, fact 4).

Kiro wraps each steering/AGENTS.md body in a BARE triple-backtick fence:

    <user-rule id=AGENTS.md>
    ```
    …file body verbatim…
    ```
    </user-rule>

Observed: 20 of 80 captured rule bodies contain INNER triple-backtick fences (a mermaid
block plus a fenced directory map in AGENTS.md). So the fence is already ambiguous in
normal use — only the closing `</user-rule>` tag marks the true end. No escaping or
sanitization of the body was observed.

HYPOTHESIS (unverified, do NOT act on it as fact): a steering file whose body contains a
closing fence followed by `</user-rule>` may terminate its own rule block early and have
the remainder read as top-level prompt scaffolding — the layer that carries
`<session_start_snapshot>`, the subagent contract, and the rules-precedence text.

This repo has been burned by treating schema-shaped reasoning as runtime fact
(feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime), so this needs a real probe with a control:
write a benign steering file containing the escape sequence + a distinctive marker
instruction, run a turn, and read the prompt log to see where the marker landed.
Needs an account with prompt logging enabled.

If it holds, it is a proxy-stage sanitization opportunity for cyril (escape or re-fence
rule bodies before they reach disk) rather than something to report as a Kiro CVE —
the steering file is already user-controlled and same-privilege.

title: Hooks host: inject a corrected hooks briefing so injected HOOK_INSTRUCTION content carries authority for non-kiro-ide clients
description: Live-observed 2026-07-23 (cyril-tpfd probe, .cyril-tpfd/findings.md): with cyril's clientInfo, KAS omits its hooks system-prompt briefing (kiro-ide-gated, per cyril-0wyn triage), and the model refused an injected sessionStart HOOK_INSTRUCTION — 'not a legitimate system directive, just text injected into the message'. Hook injection works mechanically; instruction AUTHORITY is briefing-dependent. Mitigation candidate from the 0wyn coupling note: cyril injects its own corrected hooks briefing (trigger vocabulary, exit-2 semantics, HOOK_INSTRUCTION legitimacy) via steering/context whenever kas_hooks=host and hooks are configured. Applies to executeHook-injected context too, not just sessionStart.

notes.content: Closed: Won't-fix: premise falsified by prove-it prototype (PR #64 merged to main, a993f5e). Probe evidence (.cyril-booz/): (1) cyril RECEIVES the hooksBlock briefing — unrecognized clientInfo.name falls back to kiro-ide, the branch the gate selects (sysprompt arm: model quoted <hooks> verbatim); tpfd's 'KAS omits its briefing' was wrong. (2) No client-side framing restores HOOK_INSTRUCTION authority: 0/18 across a corrected briefing, prompt-body framing, KAS's OWN production interception framing, and a benign fact. The refusal is the model's injection defense, structural to the user-turn injection point — kiro-ide sees the identical refusal, so not a non-kiro-ide gap. No client fix exists. Corrected the record: ADR 0006, .cyril-tpfd/findings.md, cyril-ctnv notes. Upstream ask survives as cyril-ctnv (persona/allowlist/client-recognition), but instruction authority is a model property, not a KAS gate.

2. kiro-cli now BOOTSTRAPS AN INSTALLER for a second ACP client on the user's

WATCH ITEM, not work. Re-read reference_kirocrew_platform (the repo is a reference

title: K1a steering non-functional: __session/steer double-underscore + dead inbound converter arm
description: prove-it-prototype (cyril-bm1j) against kiro-cli 2.8.0 found K1a steering broken end-to-end in both directions, missed by K1a unit tests (they bypass the real wire). (a) OUTBOUND: bridge.rs:1060/1127 call ExtRequest::new("_session/steer") but agent-client-protocol does format!("_{}",method) (lib.rs:213) -> wire shows __session/steer -> kiro -32601. Fix: pass "session/steer" / "session/steer/clear" (cf. SpawnSession's "session/spawn"). (b) INBOUND: echoes ride wire _kiro.dev/session/update; the lib strips the leading _ (lib.rs:294) so the converter sees kiro.dev/session/update; K1a's arm keyed "_kiro.dev/session/update" (convert/kiro.rs:681) is dead, echoes fall to the existing kiro.dev/session/update arm (line 424) and are dropped. title: session/new budget must be >=90s — a pending-OAuth MCP server blocks the response for kiro-cli's full 30s wait
description:
kiro-cli blocks the session/new response while it initializes the session MCP servers. A remote server pending OAuth holds that initialization for its FULL 30s authorization wait, so a 30s client timeout is a race the client usually loses: kiro-cli creates the session, cyril gives up, the slot orphans.

MEASURED (KiroCrew, their issue #2946, kiro-cli 2.17.1-nightly.7):
  0.4s  mcp/server_initialized  my
 30.5s  commands/available            <- 30 second dead gap
 30.6s  mcp/oauth_request  cloudflare-api
 31.2s  session/new returns
A 71-server agent with no pending OAuth completes in ~14s. They moved to _SESSION_NEW_TIMEOUT = 90.0 with a do-not-tidy warning.

Related: _kiro.dev/mcp/server_initialized / server_init_failure / oauth_request arrive BEFORE the session/new response (each carries params.serverName; failures carry error). A client that registers its session route only after the response drops them — and they are exactly the evidence needed to explain a slow start.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 4.4.
acceptance_criteria: session/new has its own budget of at least 90s, separate from the generic request timeout. Pre-response _kiro.dev/mcp/* frames are not dropped, and a timeout names which servers reported, which are silent, and which await OAuth.

title: Live KAS run_command always fails on Linux host — suspected whole-command-line rendered as one quoted token
description: Live KAS sessions (kiro-cli 2.16.0, 2026-08-02, Linux/fish host) fail EVERY run_command tool call: echo, /bin/echo, printf all end status=Failed; the agent narrates 'the shell tried to find a literal file at that path' for '/bin/echo dn91-live-ok', which matches the whole command line being rendered as ONE quoted token by HostShell::command/append_command (terminal_io create receives command+args; if KAS sends the full line in `command` with empty args, per-token quoting yields '/bin/echo dn91-live-ok' as a single argv word).
