title: Build Cyril-owned scoped memory and cited knowledge
description:
## Problem Statement

Cyril carries conversations across ACP sessions but owns no durable transcript, cross-session memory, or vendor-neutral document knowledge. Users must repeatedly restate preferences, project decisions, prior failures, and operating constraints. Exact details in design documents and runbooks are available only when the bound agent happens to expose a vendor-specific knowledge feature. Cyril cannot consistently give Kiro, future ACP agents, and subagents the same scoped memory or cited source material.

Neither candidate integration point solves the complete problem alone. A TUI-only implementation would couple domain behavior to presentation state, miss authoritative bridge lifecycle events, and inherit the UI transcript's bounded retention. An MCP-only implementation would be pull-only: an agent may never call it, so it cannot guarantee initial recall, complete transcript capture, turn-finalization, or consolidation. Cyril needs one durable memory and knowledge implementation with separate host, MCP, and TUI adapters.

This epic belongs to ROADMAP Phase 5+ (stages catalog growth), under its existing persistent-memory capability. The implementation is divided into memory-specific milestones M0-M4; these names do not replace Cyril's ROADMAP Phase 1-5+ numbering. ADR-0003 remains authoritative: the near-term integration uses Cyril's bridge and host process, not the deferred sacp-proxy stack.

## Solution

Cyril provides a local-first memory system with two intentionally separate data planes:

- Memory is compact, scoped, user-specific context. It contains explicit lessons, structured facts, and relevant episodes. A bounded block is injected automatically before the first prompt of a session, and agents can recall or teach memory explicitly.
- Knowledge is a durable, source-owned document corpus. It stores chunks with citations and is searched explicitly through MCP. It is never dumped into every prompt.

A shared memory runtime owns persistence, retrieval, consolidation jobs, embedding generation, scope enforcement, and audit events. The ACP bridge supplies authoritative session and turn lifecycle events and requests bounded first-prompt context. A stdio MCP adapter exposes explicit tools to the bound ACP agent and its subagents. The TUI provides human inspection, approval, editing, forgetting, source management, indexing status, and audit views without opening the databases or running model work itself.

Memory failure is isolated from the ACP session. If the runtime is unavailable, times out, or cannot bind an MCP capability, Cyril logs and surfaces the memory failure, sends the original prompt unchanged, and still publishes a valid ACP session. Memory access fails closed; session creation fails open.

## User Stories

1. As a Cyril user, I want my explicit working preferences to carry into a new session, so that I do not repeat them every time.
2. As a Cyril user, I want project decisions remembered across sessions, so that agents remain consistent with prior architecture choices.
3. As a Cyril user, I want prior failures and successful workflows recalled when relevant, so that agents do not repeat avoidable mistakes.
4. As a Cyril user, I want explicit lessons to outrank inferred facts, so that my direct instructions remain authoritative.
5. As a Cyril user, I want memory scoped to the current session, project, or global user context, so that unrelated projects do not contaminate one another.
6. As a Cyril user, I want automatic extraction to stay in its narrow originating scope, so that a model cannot widen access by claiming high confidence.
7. As a Cyril user, I want to approve promotion from session memory to project memory, so that durable project context remains intentional.
8. As a Cyril user, I want global promotion to require explicit human action, so that one project's assumptions do not become universal behavior.
9. As a Cyril user, I want a new session's first prompt enriched with a small relevant memory block, so that recall works even if the agent does not call a tool.
10. As a Cyril user, I want later prompts to avoid repeated automatic memory dumps, so that native session history is not crowded with duplicate context.
11. As a Cyril user, I want knowledge searched only when needed, so that long documents do not consume every prompt's context budget.
12. As a Cyril user, I want every knowledge result to identify its source and exact locator when available, so that I can verify the agent's claims.
13. As a Cyril user, I want to add a file or folder to the knowledge library deliberately, so that indexing scope and cost are visible before work begins.
14. As a Cyril user, I want folder ingestion to reject sensitive paths and unsafe link escapes, so that credentials and private material are not indexed accidentally.
15. As a Cyril user, I want an agent to preserve a load-bearing document it already read, so that useful external material remains searchable later.
16. As a Cyril user, I want an agent-provided source URI treated only as an identity label, so that a memory tool never opens or fetches an untrusted path on its own.
17. As a Cyril user, I want duplicate documents collapsed without losing their alternate source locations, so that results remain concise and citations remain complete.
18. As a Cyril user, I want to browse, edit, invalidate, forget, and promote memories from the TUI, so that the system remains understandable and correctable.
19. As a Cyril user, I want to see indexing, consolidation, re-embedding, and failure status in the TUI, so that background behavior is observable.
20. As a Cyril user, I want unfinished background work checkpointed and resumed after restart, so that quitting Cyril does not silently lose durable work.
21. As a Cyril user, I want memory to degrade to lexical retrieval when embeddings are unavailable, so that model setup is not a hard dependency.
22. As a Cyril user, I want a memory failure to leave the ACP conversation usable, so that an optional feature cannot strand a session.
23. As a Cyril user loading an existing session, I want the same memory tools and scope as a new session, so that resumed work behaves consistently.
24. As an ACP agent, I want a namespaced recall tool, so that I can retrieve relevant memories without knowing storage details.
25. As an ACP agent, I want a namespaced teaching tool, so that explicit user corrections can become durable lessons through one validated path.
26. As an ACP agent, I want a namespaced forgetting tool, so that I can honor user requests to invalidate editable memory without manipulating database rows.
27. As an ACP agent, I want a knowledge-source listing tool, so that I can discover valid source scopes instead of guessing identifiers.
28. As an ACP agent, I want knowledge search to return bounded cited chunks, so that I can answer from evidence without flooding the context window.
29. As a subagent, I want inherited access constrained to the parent session and project capability, so that I cannot read or write unrelated memory.
30. As a security-conscious operator, I want every MCP request authenticated by a runtime-owned capability, so that caller-supplied session or project identifiers are not trusted.
31. As a security-conscious operator, I want pending, unknown, expired, and revoked capabilities denied, so that session bootstrap races do not create unscoped access.
32. As a security-conscious operator, I want credentials and exfiltration-shaped URLs redacted before persistence and before retrieval output, so that memory does not amplify secret exposure.
33. As a security-conscious operator, I want retrieved facts and documents labeled as data with provenance and trust, so that stored content cannot silently become system instruction.
34. As a maintainer, I want one deep memory interface shared by bridge, MCP, and TUI adapters, so that storage and policy changes remain local.
35. As a maintainer, I want transcript capture before UI projection and turn mediation, so that bounded rendering state and absorbed lifecycle frames cannot corrupt durable history.
36. As a maintainer, I want original prompts stored separately from memory-enriched wire prompts, so that injected context does not recursively teach itself.
37. As a maintainer, I want project identity resolved once from the session workspace and retained by session ID, so that later events never fall back to the process working directory.
38. As a maintainer, I want the same design to work with Kiro and future ACP agents, so that Cyril's memory does not depend on Kiro-native knowledge or memory flags.
39. As a maintainer, I want SQLite-stored vectors generated by one local embedding runtime, so that the TUI and MCP adapter do not load duplicate models.
40. As a maintainer, I want retrieval quality evaluated against frozen queries and expected citations, so that ranking changes are evidence-driven.
41. As a maintainer, I want the proxy-stage adapter deferred behind the accepted ADR, so that this feature does not revive the proxy stack before its justified use case.
42. As a maintainer, I want memory-specific milestones traceable to ROADMAP Phase 5+, so that implementation sequencing does not collide with Cyril's existing phase vocabulary.

## Implementation Decisions

- Assign the epic to ROADMAP Phase 5+ and use M0-M4 only as local milestone names.
- M0 establishes the deep memory module, configuration, data locations, typed identifiers, scope rules, capability lifecycle, databases, versioned migrations, audit events, and durable job model.
- M1 integrates bridge-side transcript capture and first-prompt memory preparation. It stores original user content, observes authoritative routed lifecycle events before UI projection, assembles durable turns, and sends the original prompt unchanged on memory failure.
- M2 adds the stdio MCP adapter and namespaced agent tools. Cyril registers the adapter on both new-session and load-session ACP requests.
- M3 adds the cited knowledge plane, explicit source ingestion, document chunking, lexical retrieval, citation types, source management, and TUI library controls.
- M4 adds restart-safe consolidation, semantic and episodic extraction, local embeddings, SQLite-stored vectors, cosine retrieval, re-embedding, retrieval benchmarks, and bounded TUI observability.
- The memory implementation lives outside the UI module. The UI owns only immutable view state, interaction, and rendering.
- The memory runtime is a separate local process owned by Cyril. It owns both databases, the embedding backend, and background jobs so native-model failure or memory pressure cannot crash the TUI and so only one embedding model is loaded.
- The runtime and adapters communicate over user-private local IPC. Unix uses an owner-only local socket; Windows uses a user-only named pipe. Authentication remains required as defense in depth.
- Memory and knowledge use separate SQLite databases because their data volume, backup behavior, and retention differ. Both use WAL mode, versioned migrations, bounded transactions, and owner-only storage.
- Memory records carry provenance, trust, timestamps, session and project scope, importance, validity and supersession state, and memory type. Lessons remain a distinct priority tier rather than ordinary semantic facts.
- Knowledge records preserve source, document, chunk, section, line/page or artifact locator, content hash, embedding signature, and alternate source locations.
- FTS5 is the lexical retrieval floor for both planes. Embeddings are optional for availability, not for schema. While unavailable, searches remain lexical.
- The embedding runtime generates vectors locally. Vectors are stored in SQLite; initial retrieval computes cosine similarity over bounded candidates. No vector database or FAISS index is introduced until a benchmark demonstrates need.
- Entity-graph extraction is deferred until a frozen multi-hop benchmark demonstrates measurable retrieval lift beyond FTS5 plus vectors.
- Automatic memory context is injected before the first prompt of a session. It contains explicit lessons, scoped facts, and relevant episodes under deterministic character budgets. Knowledge is never automatically injected.
- Subsequent turns use native ACP history and explicit recall by default. Any future repeated automatic recall requires an explicit deterministic policy and a duplicate-context fence.
- Injected lessons are clearly separated from memory data. Derived memory and knowledge content are framed as untrusted data and cannot override explicit lessons.
- The bridge records the original user content and never treats the enriched prompt as new source material.
- Project scope is derived once from the canonical session workspace. Git worktrees on the same local repository share project identity through the canonical Git common directory; non-Git projects use the canonical workspace identity. Display paths remain separate from identity.
- Automatic extraction writes to the narrowest originating scope. Confidence affects candidate retention, ranking, and same-scope conflict resolution only. It never grants project or global scope.
- Session-to-project promotion requires explicit user action or a separately specified deterministic policy. Global promotion requires explicit human action in this version.
- The MCP adapter accepts only a runtime-issued opaque capability. Tool arguments may narrow a bound scope but never widen it.
- New-session bootstrap mints a cryptographically random pending capability before sending the ACP request. The MCP environment receives only the private runtime endpoint and capability; it receives no session or project identifier.
- After a valid new-session response, Cyril validates the returned session ID, attempts capability binding with a deadline, then either binds it to the returned session and resolved project or revokes/disables it. Cyril publishes SessionCreated in both outcomes. Memory fails closed, but valid ACP session creation fails open.
- Before binding, every MCP tool returns a typed scope-not-bound error. Unknown, expired, and revoked capabilities are denied.
- A loaded session uses the same capability model. Because its session ID is known, Cyril may pre-bind the capability before load and revokes it if loading fails.
- Capabilities are revoked on session close, failed creation/load, bridge loss, and Cyril shutdown.
- MCP tool names are Cyril-namespaced to avoid collisions with agent-native memory and knowledge tools.
- The teaching tool writes only explicit lessons or facts in the bound scope. A request for global scope creates a pending human promotion rather than writing globally.
- The agent document-ingestion tool accepts document text already read plus a source identity label. It never opens, resolves, stats, or fetches that label.
- Folder and file source registration is a human TUI action with cost/scope preview and explicit confirmation. Automatic project scanning is disabled initially.
- Cyril's existing agent-provided /knowledge command remains agent-owned. Cyril uses /memory for memory management and /library for its own knowledge source controls.
- Cyril-native memory remains independent from Kiro's memoryEnable, search_memories, and native knowledge implementation. Native federation may be considered later but cannot be authoritative.
- Memory configuration is opt-in initially. Configuration includes enabled state, context budget, retention limits, storage location overrides, embedding model, and ingestion limits. Invalid configuration fails loudly and cannot silently widen scope.
- Runtime startup failure is logged and surfaced once; it does not prevent bridge startup. Prompt preparation has a deadline and falls back to the original prompt.
- Durable transcript append occurs before asynchronous consolidation. Consolidation jobs are idempotent, checkpointed, retryable, and resumable after restart.
- Consolidation uses a dedicated ACP worker with no side-effect tools and strict structured output. Model-derived values retain source trust and narrow scope. The active user session is never repurposed as the consolidation worker.
- The deferred proxy-stage architecture remains out of scope under ADR-0003. The deep memory interface permits a later proxy adapter without replacing storage, MCP, or TUI behavior.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert user-visible and protocol-visible behavior, not table layouts, private helper calls, SQL strings, or embedding implementation details.
- The primary acceptance seam is the existing bridge fake-agent harness with a real memory runtime client. It exercises session creation, capability bootstrap, prompt preparation, routed lifecycle capture, turn completion, and fail-open ACP behavior as one flow.
- At that seam, a new-session request must advertise the Cyril memory MCP server with a pending capability, never a session/project identity.
- At that seam, a successful response followed by successful binding must publish SessionCreated and allow the first prompt to carry bounded memory context.
- At that seam, a binding timeout or failure must revoke/disable memory and still publish SessionCreated; the next prompt must reach the fake agent unchanged.
- At that seam, all production prompt producers converge on the same preparation path so startup prompts, ordinary input, and generated follow-up prompts cannot bypass memory policy.
- At that seam, transcript capture must store original user content and final normalized assistant/tool lifecycle while excluding the injected memory block as source material.
- The second required acceptance seam is a stdio MCP protocol harness connected to a real temporary memory runtime. This is irreducible because the agent-facing contract is not exercised by ordinary bridge notification tests.
- The MCP harness tests pending, bound, unknown, expired, and revoked capabilities; scope narrowing; scope-widening refusal; typed errors; and lifecycle revocation.
- The MCP harness tests source discovery, bounded cited search, explicit teaching, forgetting, and document-text ingestion without path access.
- The memory module's public interface receives contract tests for scope precedence, explicit-lesson priority, supersession, deduplication, deterministic budgets, missing versus corrupt storage, and restart-safe jobs.
- Retrieval tests use a frozen corpus with expected chunk IDs and citations. They report recall at a fixed result count, reciprocal rank, abstention behavior, and citation fidelity.
- Embedding-enabled and lexical-only retrieval tests must preserve the same scope and trust filters even when their ranking differs.
- TUI tests use the existing pure-state and rendering patterns. They verify status, pending promotion, source/indexing views, error messages, and commands without opening a database or starting a model.
- Cross-platform tests use temporary owner-controlled directories and fully fake environment/path probes. Unix-only process assertions are gated; Windows IPC and ACL behavior is compiled and exercised in Windows CI.
- Tests never read the operator's real home, configuration, repositories, model cache, or knowledge database.
- Runtime crash/restart tests prove that durable turns remain stored, incomplete jobs resume exactly once, and capability records do not survive beyond their intended runtime/session lifetime.
- Load-session tests prove pre-binding, revocation on load failure, and correct project restoration without relying on process current directory.
- Security tests prove sensitive-path refusal, canonical containment, symlink escape refusal, credential redaction, untrusted-content framing, parameterized FTS input, and non-widening by confidence.
- Performance tests assert bounded candidate counts, character budgets, and query shapes rather than tight wall-clock timings.

## Out of Scope

- Reviving the sacp-proxy/conductor stack or implementing a memory proxy stage before ADR-0003's revisit condition is met.
- Replacing, modifying, or depending on Kiro-native memory, search_memories, or knowledge indexing.
- Remote/cloud memory backends, cross-device synchronization, multi-user sharing, or enterprise retention policy.
- Automatic global memory promotion.
- Automatic project document scanning in the initial release.
- Fetching arbitrary URLs or opening paths supplied to an MCP ingestion tool.
- A hosted vector database, FAISS knowledge index, or approximate-nearest-neighbor service before benchmark evidence.
- Entity-graph extraction before a multi-hop benchmark shows incremental value.
- Full-text editing of source documents from the memory or library panel.
- Treating the UI transcript as the durable transcript source.
- Guaranteeing automatic memory for clients that bypass Cyril's bridge; a future proxy adapter is the extension point.

## Further Notes

The domain vocabulary follows Cyril's existing terms: ACP bridge, turn mediation, host-callback mediation, capability adapter, proxy stage, session, and turn. Memory observation is not host-callback mediation: it consumes outgoing prompts and normalized inbound lifecycle. It is also not a proxy stage in this epic.

The design deliberately combines Oh My Pi's backend and explicit-tool discipline with Kiro Crew's distinction between automatically injected memory and explicitly searched cited knowledge. The implementation remains Cyril-owned and vendor-neutral.

Test-seam selection was synthesized from the existing architecture as requested without a user interview. The two highest observable seams are necessary: the bridge fake-agent seam proves automatic lifecycle behavior, and the stdio MCP seam proves agent-controlled behavior. Lower-level tests exist only for invariants that cannot be diagnosed safely through those protocols.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The epic is implemented as ROADMAP Phase 5+ memory milestones M0-M4 without renaming Cyril's existing phases.
- [ ] A non-UI memory module owns scoped memory, cited knowledge, persistence, retrieval, policy, and audit behavior.
- [ ] The bridge captures authoritative prompts and lifecycle events before UI projection and stores original prompts separately from injected context.
- [ ] The first prompt of a session receives bounded scoped memory when available; memory failure sends the original prompt unchanged.
- [ ] Memory failure never prevents a valid SessionCreated notification from reaching App.
- [ ] New and loaded sessions receive a Cyril-namespaced stdio MCP adapter through standard ACP mcpServers.
- [ ] New-session MCP bootstrap uses a pending opaque capability; no session/project identity is trusted from MCP environment or arguments.
- [ ] Capability binding follows validate → deadline-bound bind attempt → bind or revoke/disable → publish SessionCreated.
- [ ] Pending, unknown, expired, and revoked capabilities fail closed with typed errors.
- [ ] Automatic writes remain in the narrowest originating scope; confidence cannot widen scope.
- [ ] Global promotion requires explicit human action.
- [ ] Memory, knowledge, and MCP failures are observable through structured errors and TUI status.
- [ ] Memory and knowledge persist in separate versioned SQLite stores with FTS5 lexical fallback.
- [ ] Knowledge search returns bounded chunks with canonical source and locator citations.
- [ ] Agent document ingestion accepts text plus an opaque source label and never opens or fetches that label.
- [ ] Embeddings are generated once by the local runtime, stored in SQLite, and are optional for retrieval availability.
- [ ] Durable turns precede asynchronous consolidation; jobs are idempotent, checkpointed, and restart-safe.
- [ ] /memory and /library provide Cyril-owned management without shadowing the agent-provided /knowledge command.
- [ ] The bridge fake-agent behavioral suite covers automatic injection, capture, capability binding failure, and session fail-open behavior.
- [ ] The stdio MCP behavioral suite covers authenticated tool use, scoping, revocation, citations, and document ingestion.
- [ ] Security tests cover sensitive paths, containment, redaction, untrusted framing, FTS input, and scope non-widening.
- [ ] The implementation is independent of Kiro-native memory and knowledge features.
- [ ] The proxy-stage adapter remains deferred under ADR-0003.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+. The installed Rivets CLI does not expose the documented --external-ref option, so the reference is recorded here and in the specification body; the ROADMAP entry will also name this epic.

Architecture decision recorded: ADR-0003 now contains the accepted persistent-memory exception. M1 may use bounded bridge-local first-session injection as an interim adapter; when the proxy stack activates, the equivalent proxy-stage adapter must pass the same behavioral contract and replace the bridge adapter cleanly.

ADR-0003 clarification: injection uses the bridge prompt seam for the bounded first-prompt memory block. Durable capture is a separate pre-UI bridge observer over original outbound prompts and normalized inbound turn/tool lifecycle. The later proxy-stage adapter replaces both interim bridge adapters only after passing the same behavioral contract.

title: Upstream ask: KAS should recognize third-party ACP clients (or key persona/allowlist/hooks off capabilities, not clientInfo.name)
description: DEFERRED FROM the cyril-0wyn ADR. Evidence in .cyril-0wyn/ (probes + carves, KAS 2.13.0): resolveAgentContext recognizes only kiro-web|kiro-ide|kiro-cli; any other clientInfo.name silently becomes kiro-ide (local) — the misclassification is invisible on the wire (initialize responses byte-identical across names, findings.md Q3). At least FOUR behaviors key off the resolved client: system-prompt persona (getIdentity), remote-tool allowlist (resolveRemoteToolAllowlist: memoryEnabled gate is kiro-cli-only), hooksBlock system-prompt injection (kiro-ide-only), and honorsRepositories (kiro-web/sandbox-only). ASK (human action, raising with the Kiro team): recognize third-party ACP clients — e.g. treat unknown names as a generic 'acp-client' with an explicit capability-negotiated feature set, or key persona/allowlist/hooks off KiroClientMeta capabilities instead of the name; at minimum, surface the resolved client type in the initialize response so clients can fail loud. cyril's interest: honest clientInfo.name (see ADR in docs/adr/ from cyril-0wyn) without losing the memoryEnabled path (cyril-jrl1 is the impersonation escape hatch we'd rather not build). Related: cyril-jiyn (hooksBlock coupling).

notes.content: cyril-booz (2026-07-23) probed the hooksBlock angle specifically: the briefing is NOT the lever for hook-instruction authority. cyril already RECEIVES hooksBlock (unrecognized name -> kiro-ide fallback), and NO client-side briefing/framing makes injected HOOK_INSTRUCTION output authoritative (0/18, incl KAS's own production framing) — the model's injection defense is structural to the user-turn injection point, kiro-ide included. So the upstream ask stands for persona/allowlist/client-recognition, but 'key hooks off capabilities' would NOT by itself restore instruction authority; that is a model-injection-defense property, not a KAS gate. Evidence: .cyril-booz/findings.md.

title: SessionController.context_usage not reset on SessionCreated/BridgeDisconnected (diverges from UiState)
description:
Latent divergence surfaced during the cyril-5et2 (KAS-2b) code review (PR #33), deliberately left unfixed to avoid scope creep into a file the PR didn't touch.

PR #33 added a SessionController arm for Notification::ContextBreakdownUpdated (crates/cyril-core/src/session.rs) so the documented 'context usage flows to both state machines' invariant (the context_usage_flows_to_both routing test) holds under KAS, where the scalar arrives only via that notification. UiState was also updated to RESET context_usage + context_breakdown on SessionCreated and BridgeDisconnected (so a prior session's 'Context: N%'/bars don't leak across /new or linger on a dead connection).

SessionController's SessionCreated and BridgeDisconnected arms do NOT clear self.context_usage, so after /new or disconnect SessionController retains the prior session's value while UiState clears it — the two state machines the App feeds (app.rs:307-308) now disagree on context lifecycle.

UNOBSERVABLE TODAY: nothing in non-test code reads SessionController::context_usage() (only the toolbar shows context, and it reads UiState). This is a trap for the next CommandContext consumer that reads session.context_usage() (e.g. a future /context- or /stats-style command), which would see stale-after-/new data. Note the gap is engine-agnostic — SessionController never reset context_usage on /new even on the v2 MetadataUpdated path; KAS-2b made it newly relevant because SessionController now tracks the KAS scalar too.

FIX (trivial, ~1 line each): add self.context_usage = None; to SessionController's SessionCreated and BridgeDisconnected arms, mirroring the UiState fix. No observable behavior change today.

PRECEDENT: cyril-85py tracks the analogous unread/divergent SessionController.steering_depth vs the optimistic UiState chip.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #46 (6918f99). SessionController now resets context_usage on SessionCreated and BridgeDisconnected, mirroring UiState. Repro fences: context_usage_resets_on_session_created, context_usage_resets_on_disconnect (the latter ingests via ContextBreakdownUpdated so the KAS path is fenced).

title: KAS wrapper mode: extend the C14a login gate (or record why free-path-only) — unservable store currently fails at first callback, not at spawn
description: Flagged during the PR-39 simplifier pass. Both KAS spawn modes run --auth=acp-callback and depend on cyril's getAccessToken responder, but the C14a spawn gate (store_unservable_reason) runs only on the free path (discovery.rs resolve_kas_command); wrapper mode (bridge.rs resolve_spawn_command -> build_wrapper_command) is ungated, so an absent/stale/corrupt store fails as a dead first turn — warn-logged since PR-39 (F1) but not fail-at-spawn. dcc6's design framed C14 free-path-only, possibly deliberately (kiro-cli-the-parent maintains its own login state and may refresh the store; wrapper stale behavior was not probed). Resolution: either extend the gate to wrapper spawns (probe first: does a wrapper spawn with an unservable store fail the same way live?) or record the free-path-only rationale in the code + design doc. Related: cyril-taba (stale affordance), cyril-l7tw (turn-failure visibility).

title: Lift config_options from the session/new response — KAS populates it, and 2.16.2 now includes the model picker there
description:
2.16.2 promotes the `model` config option into the `session/new` RESPONSE. Same-day
A/B (docs/kiro-2.16.2-wire-audit.md):

  2.16.0 session/new configOptions: [mode, autopilot, contentCollection]
  2.16.2 session/new configOptions: [mode, MODEL, autopilot, contentCollection]

Both versions also push the full set later via config_option_update, so this is a
promotion into the initial response, not a new option overall. 19 model options,
each with _meta.kiro.{hasEffort, rateMultiplier, rateUnit}; the 9 with
hasEffort:true also carry effortLevels + defaultEffortLevel. `value` is null at
session/new -- no model is pre-selected, so the current model still needs the later
push or an explicit read.

THE UNDERLYING GAP (this is the actual work, and it has never been tracked):
`session_created_from_response` (crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/convert/mod.rs)
reads only modes+models and IGNORES config_options entirely. That was correct for
v2, where config_options is always null. Under KAS it is populated, and as of
2.16.2 it is populated with the model picker at session creation. ROADMAP KAS-4
named this gap ("the initial set must be lifted here") but no issue carried it.

Consequence today: cyril learns KAS config state only from a later
config_option_update, and on the set path KAS fires no echo -- so the initial read
is the only reliable way to learn the starting mode/autopilot.

Not a duplicate of cyril-lxuo (render per-model capability in the picker),
cyril-4jt7 (consume effortLevels/defaultEffortLevel) or cyril-838u (don't carry
effortLevel across a switch). Those consume the data; this is the plumbing that
makes it available at session creation. They are all downstream of this.
acceptance_criteria:
1. session_created_from_response parses config_options from the session/new result under KAS (v2 unaffected — it is always null there).
2. The initial mode/autopilot/contentCollection/model state is available to the App without waiting for a config_option_update.
3. A null/absent config_options is handled as legitimate (v2) rather than as an error.
4. cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass, including --features kas.

notes.content: 2.17.0 live A/B finding (probe-kas-configoptions-ab-2.17.0.py, kas-turn-2.17.0.jsonl): the model configOption is NOT guaranteed present on session/new — when KAS's backend model-list fetch fails/degrades it omits the option gracefully (paid capture had only mode/autopilot/contentCollection; same-day re-probe served all 4 with 19 models). Whatever lifts config_options must treat model as OPTIONAL and LATE-ARRIVING (config_option_update push exists for recovery). Do not gate session readiness on the model picker.

title: KAS on kiro 2.11.0: bundle discovery misses versioned dirs; prompt errors instantly even with KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH
description: Found 2026-07-02 during cyril-qo13 final integration (C8 live check). Two layers: (1) DISCOVERY: cyril-core kas/discovery.rs expects ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/kas/node_modules/@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js, but kiro >=2.10.0 self-extracts to VERSIONED dirs (kas/<ver>-<sha>/node_modules/...) — both 2.10.0 and 2.11.0 dirs present on this machine, so default discovery fails with 'KAS bundle not found'. Discovery should glob the versioned dirs and pick the one matching the kiro-cli version (or newest). (2) FAST-ERROR TURN: with KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH pointed at the 2.11.0 bundle, kas_fs_host_io_smoke -- --ignored dies ~1.7s after SendPrompt with TurnCompleted and zero agent activity (no permission request, no fs callbacks). Token file ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json is VALID (checked expiry). Bisect: identical failure at pre-qo13 commit ac30697 => environment/upstream, not the qo13 slices. Prime suspect: @kiro/agent 0.3.299->0.8.0 RENUMBER in 2.11.0 (reference_kiro_2_11_0_diff) changing a handshake/contract cyril's KAS client relies on — needs a KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH-style capture of cyril-vs-KAS to see the actual error frame. NOTE: all kas_*_smoke tests are #[ignore] so CI never catches this class; consider a cheap 'bundle discoverable' non-ignored check.

notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-07-02, qo13 C8 probe): the 'fast-error turn' = backend HTTP 403 'bearer token invalid'. ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json holds a DEAD GitHub-social identity (authMethod:social, provider:Github) whose expiresAt looks fresh but whose bearer the backend rejects; the LIVE credential is the CLI's IDC token in data.sqlite3 auth_kv 'kirocli:odic:token' (+ profileArn in state 'api.codewhisperer.profile'). Standalone-spawned KAS logs 'Auth: default token file' and NEVER calls _kiro/auth/getAccessToken — file-auth-only in this mode; with the file absent it errors 'No auth token found' (no callback fallback). Writing the sqlite IDC token into the file shape {accessToken,refreshToken,profileArn,expiresAt} made KAS 2.11.0 fully functional (real turn, tool approvals honored). => cyril impact: cyril's KAS auth path reads the same file (kas/discovery.rs), so cyril inherits the dead-identity failure; fix should source auth from the CLI sqlite store (or refresh/validate the file) in addition to fixing versioned-dir discovery. CAUTION: KAS self-refreshes the file token — seeding it with the CLI's refresh_token risks consuming a single-use refresh and invalidating the CLI login; any fix must not share the refresh token family carelessly.

WORKAROUND REFINED (2026-07-03, qo13 C8 re-run): seeding kiro-auth-token.json with {accessToken, profileArn, expiresAt} ONLY — no refreshToken — is sufficient for standalone KAS 2.11.0 (a full spec-mode session ran on the bare access token). This removes the refresh-token-family risk from the original workaround: a cyril auth fix can materialize a refresh-less token file per spawn and never endanger the CLI's single-use refresh token. Also re-confirmed the trap: KAS self-refreshes the DEAD GitHub-social identity in the file (expiresAt was bumped during a failed run minutes before), so a fresh-looking expiresAt is NOT a validity signal — identity must be checked (authMethod/provider fields), or auth sourced from the CLI sqlite store directly.

AUTH ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (2026-07-03, live process table): CLI-launched KAS (acp --agent-engine v3) runs with --auth=acp-callback — auth via the _kiro/auth/getAccessToken callback from the CLI's sqlite store; no token file involved. The 2.5.0-era kiro-auth-token-cli.json sync contract is dead (file is a Jun 9 relic). So the default-SSO-file path this issue describes is hit ONLY by standalone spawns, and NO user action (re-login, opening KAS sessions) ever bridges sqlite -> that file. Fix direction sharpened: cyril should spawn acp-server.js with --auth=acp-callback and answer the callback from the sqlite store (profileArn from the state table), OR synthesize a refresh-less private token file and pass --token-path — never depend on the shared default file.

PROBE COMPLETE (2026-07-03, prove-it-prototype, branch feat/dcc6-kas-discovery-auth, artifacts .cyril-dcc6/): BOTH fix halves proven live against KAS 2.11.0. Probe A (versioned-dir glob + exact-version-match + newest/legacy fallback) chose the identical acp-server.js path kiro-cli itself spawns (oracle: /proc/<child>/cmdline of kiro-cli's own KAS spawn — byte-equal). Probe B (--auth=acp-callback + responder answering _kiro/auth/getAccessToken from sqlite auth_kv token + state-table profileArn) completed authenticated turns twice (backend = auth ground truth). KEY DISCOVERY via a broken-oracle detour: kiro-cli WRAPPER mode FORWARDS getAccessToken to its outer ACP client — an unanswered callback kills the turn with TokenInvalidError('Host refresh callback returned no access token'). So ONE sqlite-backed responder fixes both spawn modes, and cyril's current file-reading responder is the wrapper-mode failure cause. Expiry behavior NOT probed (all runs >=10min pre-expiry) — stale-token responder policy stays with cyril-taba. Next: falsifiable-design (open q: version-match tiebreak when no dir matches CLI version).

DESIGN READY (2026-07-04, falsifiable-design): .cyril-dcc6/design.md. Core: (A) discovery.rs selection policy exact-CLI-version > newest-semver > legacy > KasMissing::Server, dir grammar <semver>-<sha64> with inner-entry check, free-path argv gains --auth=acp-callback; (B) auth.rs source swap read_token_file -> read_sqlite_store (rusqlite bundled, optional, kas-gated, READ_ONLY, spawn_blocking), login gate = auth_kv row presence (logout deletes row). 14 claims w/ per-claim fences; cheapest falsifier 7/7 PASS (falsifier-selection-policy.py, incl. real-machine /proc cross-check); C8 fence fails against today's code by construction. Removed-invariant sweep: free-path now DEPENDS on responder dispatch (C14), file gate deleted (C10), sqlite newly opened (C12). Deferrals: taba (stale policy, reframed), lwpm (Windows store, filed), 0pms, l7tw, 6iek. Next: budgeted-plan after design approval.

PLAN READY (2026-07-04, budgeted-plan): .cyril-dcc6/plan.md — 7 slices, expand/contract (workspace green both feature sets after every slice): 1 pure select_server policy (C1-C4 fences incl. semver-vs-lex + partial-extraction) -> 2 wire into resolve w/ legacy fallback + override bypass + real CLI version (C5-C7) -> 3 rusqlite dep plumbing kas-gated (dep-tree oracle) -> 4 read_sqlite_store w/ snake_case + keyed-row + readonly-never-creates fences (C9/C11/C12) -> 5 responder swap + per-call re-read (C10/C13, logout/re-login mid-session fixtures) -> 6 argv flip --auth=acp-callback + sqlite login gate (C8/C14a; argv fence fails pre-slice by construction) -> 7 contract: delete SSO-file path, grep-zero fixture, smoke/doc alignment. KEY ORDERING: responder sqlite-backed BEFORE argv flip. Post-slice: one-time user-gated live smoke run (C14b), deterministic fences are the CI-permanent form. Next: checkpointed-build.

BUILD COMPLETE (2026-07-04, checkpointed-build, feat/dcc6-kas-discovery-auth): 6 commits (2768521 slice1 selection policy, 2d94448 slice2 wiring, 5395107 slice3 rusqlite dep, ff42b5d slices4+5 sqlite responder, 54df9e9 slice6 argv+gate, 0c59c1a slice7 contract). All fences green: C1-C7 selection/fallback/override, C8 argv byte-equal to kiro-cli's /proc-captured spawn, C9-C13 sqlite source (keyed rows, snake_case, readonly-never-creates, logout/re-login/corrupt), C14a gate_is_sqlite_not_file, grep 'kiro-auth-token' = 0 hits (resurrection tripwire). Workspace green both feature sets (default + kas), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, python falsifier 7/7 every slice. Plan deviations (all no-dead-code driven): slice1 wired select_server inertly; slices 4+5 merged; contract deletions landed incrementally (4+5: read_token_file; 6: TOKEN_FILE_REL). Dep deviation: rusqlite 0.39 not 0.40 (0.40's libsqlite3-sys needs unstable cfg_select, breaks pinned 1.94.0). REMAINING: C14b one-time live validation (user-gated, fresh token window): cargo test -p cyril-core --features kas --test kas_freepath_smoke --test kas_wrapper_smoke -- --ignored --nocapture.

C14b LIVE COMPLETE (2026-07-04 04:07Z, fresh token window): both hardened smokes PASS with the KAS_SMOKE_OK sentinel echoed through cyril's real bridge — free path (--auth=acp-callback + sqlite responder, 3.48s) AND wrapper (forwarded callback, 3.50s). Smokes hardened first: TurnCompleted-only was l7tw-vulnerable (an error turn collapses into TurnCompleted), and contains('ok') would false-green on TokenInvalidError ('ok' in 'token'). ALL design claims C1-C14 now verified incl. live. Branch feat/dcc6-kas-discovery-auth ready to merge.

PR OPEN (2026-07-04): https://github.com/dwalleck/cyril/pull/39. CI surfaced two gaps: (1) rustfmt diffs in the smoke prompts (python-scripted edits bypassed the format hook AND the local check read the pipe's exit, not rustfmt's — check exit codes directly); (2) commitlint (PR-only, first enforcement on this style) rejects probe/design/plan types and scopes with spaces — branch history REWRITTEN to conforming messages and force-pushed; COMMIT HASHES IN EARLIER NOTES ARE PRE-REWRITE (slice subjects now 'feat(cyril-dcc6): slice N - ...', probe->chore, design/plan->docs). Residual commitlint failure: the inherited main commit 'probe(cyril-qo13): ...' stays in the PR range until main is pushed.

Closed: Shipped: PR #39 merged to main (f8987e2, 2026-07-04). Versioned-dir KAS discovery (exact-CLI-version > newest-semver > legacy) + sqlite-backed --auth=acp-callback responder; all C1-C14 fences green incl. C14b live smokes (free path 3.48s, wrapper 3.50s, KAS_SMOKE_OK sentinel). Deferred: cyril-taba (stale-token policy), cyril-lwpm (Windows store), cyril-l7tw (error visibility).

title: Send clientInfo.name=kiro-cli: cyril is silently identified as kiro-ide and gets a heavier system prompt
description:
KAS resolves a client PERSONA from the standard ACP `initialize.params.clientInfo.name`,
and cyril has been silently identified as an IDE because it sends no clientInfo.

THE MECHANISM (src/types/shared-types.ts):
    this.clientInfo = params.clientInfo ?? undefined;
    if (clientInfo?.name && !CLIENT_TYPES.includes(clientInfo.name))
        logger.warn("Unrecognized clientInfo.name ... falling back to inferred client type");
    agentContext = resolveAgentContext(executionEnvironment, clientInfo?.name, {
        specLinks: kiroMeta?.specLinks,
        requirementsAnalysis: kiroMeta?.requirementsAnalysis,
        userInput: kiroMeta?.userInput });

    resolveAgentContext: "kiro-web" | "kiro-ide" | "kiro-cli" pass through;
    otherwise env==="sandbox" -> "kiro-web", ELSE -> "kiro-ide".

NOTE `_meta.kiro.clientName` is NOT read for this. Every probe in this repo has
been sending that field and no clientInfo, so every capture we hold was taken
under the kiro-ide persona by fall-through.

LIVE A/B, 4 arms, handshake+session/new only, FREE
(probe-kas-client-persona-2.16.0.py; captures kas-persona-2.16.0-{control,
kiro-cli,kiro-ide,kiro-web}.jsonl):

1. kiro-ide is STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to control (no clientInfo). Confirms the
   fall-through empirically, not just from the source.

2. THE ADVERTISED SURFACE DOES NOT CHANGE. Identical across all four arms:
   authMethods, modes (7), configOptions, extensionMethods (7), the 5 advertised
   agent/skill commands, and the session-start push set. So persona does NOT gate
   method availability.

3. THE SYSTEM PROMPT DOES CHANGE — measurable via context usage on an empty
   session: kiro-ide/control 0.9%, kiro-cli 0.8%, kiro-web 0.8%. kiro-cli and
   kiro-web get a LEANER prompt than the IDE persona cyril currently receives.

4. kiro-web ALSO RUNS TWO TOOLS AT SESSION START (21 frames vs 16), before any
   prompt:
       get_learnings_for_prompt  rawInput {"repositories": [], "limit": 50}
       get_steering_files
   both kind:"other". This is the honorsRepositories() branch
   (client === "kiro-web" || environment === "sandbox").

CONSEQUENCE FOR EARLIER FINDINGS: persona is NOT the explanation for
OrchestrateSubAgent being unavailable, or for _kiro/userInput and
_kiro/openExternalUrl never firing. The advertised surface is persona-invariant,
so those conclusions stand as written.

ACTION FOR CYRIL: send clientInfo {name:"kiro-cli", version:...} at initialize.
It is the honest identity, it is one of the three recognised values (so no
"Unrecognized clientInfo.name" warning in Kiro's logs), and it yields a leaner
system prompt than the IDE fall-through. It also affects telemetry attribution
(see reference_kiro_acp_telemetry) and gives cyril-0wyn a measured answer rather
than a judgement call. Do NOT send kiro-web: it triggers repository/learnings
tool calls at session start that a local TUI has no use for.

STILL UNTESTED: the three agentContext capability flags
(_meta.kiro.{specLinks, requirementsAnalysis, userInput}) were advertised in all
four arms but nothing new appeared at the handshake; their effect is presumably
in-turn (specLinks and requirementsAnalysis feed spec-mode prompt sections).

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #55 merged to main (e94117d). All 4 ACs fenced: chrome_widgets_have_no_legacy_color_sources (zero literals, AC1), no_color_status_distinguishable (AC2), chrome_baseline_equivalence + baseline_covers_probe_inventory vs frozen 3440-cell TSV (AC3), full workspace gate green (AC4). First pure re-mapping batch (no contract expansion); voice twins soft_accent/muted/accent_alt; marker fences pin all three value-twin pairs. Fixed in-branch: none. Filed: none. Unblocks a14l/9ode/qaq0/6r3a/lme2.

title: KAS host callbacks gated by cargo feature, not bound engine — implement ADR-0001 capability accessors or amend the ADR
description:
Found by the 2026-07-01 KAS implementation review (SoC lens). In a --features kas build running the V2 engine, KiroClient still answers kiro/auth/getAccessToken with the real token and answers fs/* and terminal/* callbacks if the subprocess sends them (client.rs:192-281) — despite V2Engine advertising no such capabilities, and despite ADR-0001's design intent that these are surfaces 'KAS implements and v2 does not.' The cargo feature quietly replaced the bound engine as the availability gate for host callbacks.

ADR-0001's consequences also promise the capability sub-trait mechanism ('the accessor pattern is introduced in KAS-1, where AuthResponder gets a real implementation and consumer') — no AuthResponder trait exists anywhere; auth landed as a static feature-gated handler, fs/terminal as feature-gated KiroClient overrides. The ADR text is stale.

Practical risk is LOW today (the subprocess is kiro-cli; v2 never sends these callbacks — the code says so at client.rs:23-24,180). But the next capability (KAS-7 hooks, _kiro/safety/*, cyril-3ald) will copy whatever precedent exists, so resolve before then. DISTINCT from cyril-g9vt: that issue is about the ADR-0004 stage-interception seam; this one is engine-vs-feature gating of responder availability.

Cheapest fix short of sub-traits: have the responders consult the bound engine (KiroClient already holds Rc<dyn Engine>) before answering — refuse with method-not-found when the engine does not advertise the capability. Either way, amend ADR-0001's consequences to match what shipped.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-01: ADR-0001 amended; the escape hatch in the old acceptance criteria is CLOSED ---

ADR-0001 now carries a host-callback capability-adapter amendment (driven by the 2026-07-30 architecture review, Candidate 01). It does NOT take the "document feature-level gating as the accepted design" branch — it takes the opposite one, so that branch of the old acceptance criteria is void. What the ADR now decides:

1. THE ADAPTER SET IS DATA, ADVERTISEMENT IS DERIVED FROM IT. `Engine::adapters() -> Adapters { auth, host_io, hooks }` (each optional), with client_capabilities() derived from that set rather than written independently. The `as_*`-accessor phrasing from the original ADR is WITHDRAWN: a defaulted downcast-style accessor leaves advertisement and execution as two facts a future engine can desynchronize — exactly this bug. Deriving one from the other makes the invariant mechanical instead of conventional. The review reached the same conclusion independently via its deletion test ("deepen around the Engine module").

2. REFUSE, DO NOT DEFAULT. An engine with no adapter for a family refuses those callbacks. It must NOT fall through to the protocol-default null: unhandled_ext_response's own doc comment records that the agent reads a null result as SUCCESS WITH AN EMPTY RESULT — the silent-failure shape this codebase forbids.

3. THE INVARIANT IS PER DIRECTION — new since this issue was filed, and it is a counterexample to the naive form. ADR-0010 (2026-08-01, cyril-gk17) established that _kiro/hooks/list is BIDIRECTIONAL: under kas_hooks="host" cyril serves it inbound; under "kas" cyril SENDS it outbound as a BridgeCommand and the agent executes hooks itself. So "kas" mode legitimately advertises hooks ({enabled:true, v2:true} in engine.rs) with NO inbound adapter, while client.rs:57 installs an empty HookRegistry. "An absent execution adapter cannot be advertised" is therefore FALSE as stated — it holds only for the INBOUND direction. Do not reconcile this by treating the empty registry as the adapter: an empty adapter standing for "absent" is a sentinel, against the project's no-sentinel rule. Hooks is the one family where cyril is both server and client of the same method name; the Hooks adapter must hold both directions or it will fit host mode and silently exclude the shipped kas mode.

Now on the critical path: cyril-g9vt's mediator dispatches to this adapter set, so this lands first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A --features kas build running the v2 engine REFUSES getAccessToken / fs/* / terminal/* (method-not-found or equivalent — never the protocol-default null), test-fenced.
2. Engine exposes the adapter set as data and derives inbound client_capabilities() from it; no engine can advertise an inbound capability it installs no adapter for.
3. One test walks the adapter set to prove advertisement and execution reachability TOGETHER (separate tests of those two facts are explicitly insufficient).
4. The per-direction carve-out is fenced: kas_hooks="kas" advertises hooks with no inbound adapter and is NOT reconciled by an empty-registry sentinel.
5. Stale AuthResponder consequence text in ADR-0001 corrected. (DONE 2026-08-01 — struck and marked superseded.)

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #82 merged to main (05ffd29). All ACs fenced: AC1 refusal fences (auth/typed-fs/kiro-fs-walked/terminal), AC2 Adapters-as-data + derived client_capabilities free fn, AC3 adapter_matrix_advertise_iff_answer (mutation-checked, per-bit fs pairing), AC4 registry Option-iff-Inbound + Outbound-refuses-inbound fences, AC5 pre-done, AC6 live v2 full pass + live KAS session/fs/hooks pass with run_command failure parity-proven pre-existing. Fixed in-branch: cyril-y14u. Filed: cyril-y14u, cyril-cb93.

title: Docs claim Windows spawns wsl kiro-cli acp — code spawns kiro-cli acp natively
description:
The WSL spawn was never wired as a default: --agent-command defaults to ["kiro-cli","acp"] on every platform (crates/cyril/src/main.rs:27) and AgentProcess::spawn execs it verbatim with no platform-conditional wrapping (crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/transport.rs:174). On a Windows machine with the Kiro MSI installed, PATH resolves kiro-cli to the native kiro-cli.exe — no WSL involved.

Three places still describe WSL spawning as current behavior:
1. CLAUDE.md 'Platform Constraints': 'Windows: spawns wsl kiro-cli acp; requires WSL with kiro-cli installed and authenticated'.
2. transport.rs:181-182 comment: 'Windows spawns wsl kiro-cli acp and has no Unix process groups'.
3. README Prerequisites WSL-only line (docs/ROADMAP.md already flags dropping it now that Kiro ships a native Windows binary).

This misdirection has real cost: it produced wrong platform-reach conclusions twice, most recently the 2.16.0 wire-audit voice addendum ('Kiro voice unreachable on cyril's entire platform matrix'), corrected 2026-08-01 (see the addendum in docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md and memory feedback_cyril_native_windows_not_wsl_ceiling).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CLAUDE.md Platform Constraints describes actual behavior: native spawn by default on all platforms; WSL only via explicit --agent-command wsl kiro-cli acp; notes the path-translation caveat (companion issue)
- [ ] transport.rs:181-182 comment corrected (kill_on_drop backstop rationale restated without the WSL claim)
- [ ] README Prerequisites drops the WSL-only line (closes the ROADMAP line-41 item)

title: KAS settings sweep: 5/21 flags change the handshake; workflows adds 4 slash commands we never saw
description:
Systematic per-flag A/B of all 21 KAS client-settings keys
(probe-kas-settings-sweep-2.16.0.py, captures kas-settings-2.16.0-*.jsonl, FREE —
handshake + session/new only, no prompt turn).

THE MASTER LEVER, from the initialize handler: settings sent at INITIALIZE
override the BACKEND model-config feature flags, not just session config —

    const rawKeys = new Set(Object.keys(kiroMeta.settings));
    const bridgedIsFeatureEnabled = (feature) =>
      rawKeys.has(feature) ? isSettingEnabled(initSettings, feature)
                           : prev.isFeatureEnabled(feature);
    setModelConfigProvider(bridgeFeatureFlags(prev, bridgedIsFeatureEnabled));

So `initialize._meta.kiro.settings` is a client-side override of backend flags.
Prior probes only sent settings at session/new.

5 of 21 flags produce a handshake-visible delta:

  workflows          -> workflowsEnabled:true AND FOUR NEW SLASH COMMANDS:
                        workflow-run, workflow-status, workflow-cancel,
                        workflow-resume.  ** We never saw these. ** Every workflow
                        probe drove _kiro/workflow/* directly and never noticed the
                        command surface appear. This is the USER-FACING half of the
                        workflow feature and it is one settings key away.
  fta                -> adds MODE `functional_task_alignment` (7 modes -> 8)
                        and ftaEnabled:true
  goal               -> adds the `goal` command
  specPlan           -> specPlanEnabled:true
  steeringSupervisor -> steeringSupervisorEnabled:true — a field that does NOT
                        EXIST in session/new._meta by default (null -> true), so
                        it is invisible unless you ask for it

No handshake delta (13): checkpoint, codeIntelligence, compaction,
disableAutoCompaction, inlineAgents, knowledge, largeToolOutputHandler,
semanticReview, sessionEviction, tangentMode, thinking, todoList, toolSearch.
These may still change IN-TURN behaviour (prompt content, tool selection); this
sweep only observes the handshake.

TWO INCONCLUSIVE, NOT NEGATIVE — my own probe was under-specified:
  subagentOrchestration — no handshake delta even via the initialize bridge. But
    the surface it drives is chosen during PROMPT construction
    (getDelegationToolId(getModelConfigProvider().isFeatureEnabled(...)) in
    prompts.ts), which a handshake-only sweep cannot see. Needs ONE paid turn with
    the flag set at initialize to settle whether OrchestrateSubAgent appears.
    Do not read this as confirming cyril-ucii's "backend-gated" conclusion.
  infraSafetyEnforce / infraSafetyMonitor — no delta, but the gate is
    `clientSupportsSafety && (monitorEnabled || enforceEnabled)` and THIS SWEEP DID
    NOT ADVERTISE `infrastructureSafety`. The arms were missing half the condition.
    Re-run with the capability advertised before concluding anything for cyril-3ald.

notes.content:
The  arm of this sweep concluded the user-facing half is 'one settings
key away'. True but no longer load-bearing for cyril: the four slash commands and
five tools that key unlocks are exactly what cyril has decided NOT to enable
(ADR-0011), because the methods route ungated and enabling the tools lets the model
launch runs. The other four handshake-visible flags (fta, goal, specPlan,
steeringSupervisor) are unaffected by that decision and remain the useful part of
this sweep.

Correction to the note above: its first line lost a word to a shell substitution.
It should read "The `workflows` arm of this sweep concluded ...". No other line was affected.

title: Render KAS agent-subtask pipelines from the existing tool-call stream (ToolKind::Other filter exception)
description:
Render KAS OrchestrateSubAgent / agent-subtask pipelines from the tool-call stream cyril ALREADY receives — no new protocol required.

Trace-verified (experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl, KAS 0.8.0): subagent runs surface as ordinary session/update tool_call + tool_call_update frames tagged _meta.kiro {kind: "agent-subtask", agentSubtaskId: <uuid>}, with the plan in the initial tool_call's rawInput (invoke path {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles, preset}); group by agentSubtaskId. Sample: 5 subtask groups, 44 tool_call + 113 tool_call_update + 8 session_info_update.

THE BLOCKER IS CLIENT-SIDE: these arrive with ACP kind "other", which cyril filters as agent "planning" steps (CLAUDE.md ToolKind::Other rule), so the entire run is dropped. cyril must check _meta.kiro.kind == "agent-subtask" BEFORE that filter. That exception is the prerequisite for any KAS crew rendering.

Split out of cyril-6beh (2026-07-26 PR #68 review): 6beh keeps the deferred _kiro/workflow/* protocol scope, which must not ship until an emitter exists. This issue is the near-term half and is actionable today.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN — trace-verified emission shape (from experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl, KAS 2.11.0/0.8.0):

1. KAS subagent runs surface as ordinary session/update tool_call + tool_call_update frames, tagged _meta.kiro: {kind: 'agent-subtask', agentSubtaskId: <uuid>}. Sample: 5 distinct agentSubtaskId groups, 44 tool_call + 113 tool_call_update + 8 session_info_update carrying the tags (frames/subtask 9-93).
2. The PLAN is in the initial tool_call's rawInput. Invoke path (verified in trace): {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles, preset}. Orchestrate path (from KAS buildSchema, NOT yet wire-verified): {task, stages[]{name,role,prompt_template,depends_on,inlineAgent?}, repeat{maxIterations,stopCondition,onMaxIterations}}.
3. Group frames by agentSubtaskId to reconstruct which stage is which + live progress; title = 'Sub-agent: <name>'.

*** KEY GAP / real blocker for the observe path ***: agent-subtask tool_calls arrive with ACP kind == 'other'. cyril FILTERS ToolKind::Other from display (CLAUDE.md: 'Tool calls with kind == ToolKind::Other are planning steps... filtered from display'), so cyril currently DROPS the entire subagent run. FIX: check _meta.kiro.kind == 'agent-subtask' BEFORE the ToolKind::Other filter (one branch). This is the unblock, not a missing emitter.

LIVE ORCHESTRATE CAPTURE (2.14.1): harness built + committed (experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-orchestrate-capture-2.14.1.py) but BLOCKED — all on-disk kiro tokens expired (kiro-auth-token.json exp 2026-07-19, kiro-auth-token-cli.json exp 2026-06-10; auth_kv not plaintext-extractable), so KAS rejected the getAccessToken reply with -32000 TokenInvalidError after 7 retries and the turn never orchestrated. The probe is correct (reached KAS, faithful kiro-cli-chat acp --agent-engine kas spawn); it needs a FRESH token (run right after kiro login, or wire OIDC refresh into the probe). So the orchestrate {task,stages,repeat} on-wire rawInput + loop_iteration behavior remain live-unverified; the KAS bundle schema+executor confirm they exist.

SPLIT EXECUTED (2026-07-26, PR #68 review): this issue IS the near-term half — render agent-subtask pipelines from the existing tool-call stream, gated only by the ToolKind::Other filter exception. The deferred _kiro/workflow/* live-progress protocol is cyril-6beh and must not be built against until an emitter ships.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tool calls tagged _meta.kiro.kind == "agent-subtask" survive the ToolKind::Other filter and reach the UI.
2. Calls sharing an agentSubtaskId render as one grouped run, not N unrelated tool calls.
3. The initial tool_call's rawInput (name/prompt/explanation) is surfaced as the run's plan.
4. A regression fence asserts an agent-subtask tool_call with kind "other" is NOT filtered, and that a genuine planning step with no _meta.kiro.kind still IS.

notes.content:
2.16.0 LIVE RE-CONFIRMATION (paid capture, kas-turn-2.16.0.jsonl +
kas-orchestrate-stages-2.16.0.jsonl): the invoke-path shape this issue is built
on is unchanged from the 2.11.0 trace and is what cyril will actually see —
OrchestrateSubAgent is gated OFF by default (see cyril-ucii), so the invoke path
is the only subagent surface reachable today.

Confirmed on the wire at 2.16.0:
  tool_call        _meta.kiro {kind:"agent-subtask", agentSubtaskId:<uuid>}
                   rawInput {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles}
                   title "Sub-agent: general-task-execution"
                   acp kind "other"   <-- the ToolKind::Other exception this issue needs
  tool_call_update same agentSubtaskId, status pending -> in_progress -> completed
                   (the in_progress update carries title: null)
  tool_call_update title "Subagent Response", rawInput {response, files}

Note the lifecycle: three updates share one agentSubtaskId, and the middle one
has a null title — so grouping must key on agentSubtaskId, never on title.

RENDER CONTRACT CAPTURED 2026-08-01 (kas-inconclusive-2.16.0.jsonl). With subagentOrchestration enabled at INITIALIZE, the OrchestrateSubAgent tool_call carries _meta.kiro.pipeline:
  {groupId: 'pipeline-<task-slug>', stages:[{name, role, status, dependsOn[], agentSubtaskId}]}
That is the grouping key this issue needs: agentSubtaskId links each pipeline stage to its individual agent-subtask tool_call/tool_call_update frames, and dependsOn gives the DAG edges for rendering. Envelope: title 'Orchestrate Sub-agent', acp kind 'other' (the ToolKind::Other exception), status in_progress.

Note this is the ORCHESTRATE path, which requires the client to opt in. With it off (cyril today) only the INVOKE path appears — rawInput {name,prompt,explanation,contextFiles}, title 'Sub-agent: <name>', no pipeline meta. Rendering must handle BOTH.

ITERATION TRAP (measured 2026-08-01, kas-repeat-shape-2.16.0.jsonl). Across an OrchestrateSubAgent repeat loop the _meta.kiro.pipeline stage entry is REUSED: groupId constant, stages[] keeps one entry per stage, status cycles pending->running->completed->running->completed. Rendering from pipeline status alone makes a completed stage appear to un-complete on the next iteration.

The discriminator is agentSubtaskId — 6 agent-subtask frames carried 2 DISTINCT ids, one per iteration. So: group the pipeline by groupId, but key each RUN of a stage on agentSubtaskId. Same class of bug as the workflow nodePath/iteration finding.

ERROR-PATH TRAP — measured 2026-08-01 (probe-kas-orchestrate-variants-2.16.0.py, capture kas-orch-variants-2.16.0.jsonl). This is the most dangerous rendering finding for this issue.

On an ABORTED OrchestrateSubAgent run (repeat exhausted with onMaxIterations:'abort'), the payload CONTRADICTS the status:

  tool_call_update status = 'failed'          <-- the ONLY truthful signal
  _meta.kiro.pipeline stages = [('pick','completed')]   <-- says completed
  rawOutput.response = 'Pipeline completed: 2 stages finished. ...'  <-- says COMPLETED

So every per-stage status reads 'completed' and the human-readable summary literally begins 'Pipeline completed' on a run that FAILED. A renderer keying off stage status, or echoing rawOutput.response, will show a green successful pipeline for an aborted one.

RULE: the top-level tool_call_update.status is the only authority for pipeline outcome. Treat _meta.kiro.pipeline[].status and rawOutput.response as per-stage/for-display detail that is NOT outcome-bearing.

Status transitions observed (abort): tool_call in_progress -> update in_progress(running) -> in_progress(completed) -> in_progress(running) -> in_progress(completed) -> **failed**. Note the Orchestrate tool_call stays in_progress for the whole loop and only flips at the end.

Contrast, satisfied stopCondition (early exit): 1 iteration, ends status 'completed', 'Pipeline completed: 1 stages finished.' Clean.

Also: rawOutput carries its OWN nested pipeline summary {groupId, stages[{name,role,status,dependsOn,agentSubtaskId}]}, in addition to _meta.kiro.pipeline on the frames.

title: Windows ProcessTree drop path kills the shell but leaks pipeline children
description: impl Drop for ProcessTree (terminal_io.rs) is cfg(unix)-only. On native Windows an un-reaped drop (LocalSet teardown, bridge death, app exit) falls back to tokio kill_on_drop(true), which terminates only the outer shell process — pipeline children survive, exactly the leak the cyril-2z9g tree fences exist to prevent. The explicit terminate_process_tree (taskkill /T /F) path covers kill/release/cancel but not drops. The type name promises cleanup one platform does not get on the drop path. Fix: a Windows drop-path tree kill (or a documented decision that drops may leak there and why), plus a Windows-gated fence once runnable-in-CI.

title: Dead stream_buffer module: StreamBuffer has zero production consumers
description:
Found while probing cyril-nd4h (see .cyril-nd4h/findings.md, finding #2).

crates/cyril-ui/src/stream_buffer.rs defines StreamBuffer (a debounced
streaming-text accumulator that flushes on natural boundaries or after a
timeout). It is exported as `pub mod stream_buffer` from cyril-ui/src/lib.rs
but has ZERO references anywhere outside its own file — grep -w for
'StreamBuffer' and 'stream_buffer' across crates/ returns only lib.rs:12 (the
mod declaration) and the file itself. It is never constructed in production.

cyril-nd4h removes the ui.stream_buffer_timeout_ms config field, which was the
only thing that referenced this component's existence (and it too had no
consumer). That closes the config-surface half; the dead module itself is out
of nd4h's scope and remains.

Decide: (a) delete the module, matching the cyril-85py precedent for
zero-reader code, or (b) wire it into the streaming path it was written for —
agent text currently accumulates in UiState.streaming_text with no debounce
(CLAUDE.md 'Streaming Content Model'), which is plausibly what StreamBuffer was
built to solve.

title: KAS-1 — Engine selection + _kiro/auth/getAccessToken responder (the entry gate)
description:
The precondition for every KAS milestone below. Without a host-supplied token, every KAS turn dies immediately ([TokenInvalidError] ... Host refresh callback returned no access token).

SCOPE (ROADMAP KAS-1, docs/ROADMAP.md:154):
- Make the KAS spawn real: the AgentEngine gate from KAS-0 (cyril-atjw) resolves the KAS engine to a live process; default stays v2. All new KAS code lands behind the 'kas' cargo feature from KAS-0.
  NOTE / CORRECTION: the engine flag was renamed 'kas' -> 'v3' as of kiro-cli 2.8.0 (probe-verified: 'kas' is rejected, possible values are v1/v2/v3; spawn is 'kiro-cli acp --agent-engine v3'). 2.7.1 accepted 'kas'. Resolve the engine string per installed version, don't hardcode 'kas'.
- Implement a '_kiro/auth/getAccessToken' server->client request responder: reply {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn}. KAS validates expiresAt > now + ~3 min and REQUIRES profileArn (backend 400s 'profileArn is required' without it).
- Token sourcing — MIRROR Kiro's own responder, don't just read the sqlite row. Kiro (crates/chat-cli-v2/src/auth/{kas_token,refresh_coordinator,social,builder_id,external_idp}.rs): (1) resolves the active token across THREE types — social (GitHub -> kirocli:social:token, carries profile_arn), AWS Builder ID, external IdP (kirocli:external-idp:token); (2) proactively OIDC-refreshes before the ~3-min pre-expiry buffer via a lock-guarded refresh_coordinator; (3) answers {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn}. A naive 'read kirocli:social:token and return it' responder breaks on the refresh buffer (the failure our probes hit) and on Builder-ID/external-IdP users. Cleanest: DELEGATE to kiro-cli's own auth rather than reimplement OIDC refresh + multi-type resolution.
- This makes cyril a CUSTODIAN of a kiro credential — handle as such (no logging, read-only, minimal lifetime). See ROADMAP Open Tension #7.

This is the AUTH half of the initialize._meta.kiro (KiroClientMeta) handshake; the SETTINGS half is cyril-nhzw (AgentSettings).

REFS: ROADMAP KAS-1 (docs/ROADMAP.md:154); covenant docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md (KiroClientMeta handshake); memory reference_kiro_kas_launch_contract.
acceptance_criteria:
* Engine-select plumbing resolves the KAS engine to a live spawn (version-correct flag: v3 on >=2.8.0, kas on 2.7.1); default remains v2.
* '_kiro/auth/getAccessToken' responder replies {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn} and is exercised in a gated end-to-end smoke against a live KAS session.
* Auth-responder unit test covers the reply shape AND expired-token rejection (expiresAt <= now + ~3 min).
* profileArn is always present in the reply (Builder-ID / external-IdP users included), sourced by delegating to kiro-cli's own auth.
* Credential is never logged; token read is read-only and minimal-lifetime.

notes.content:
2026-06-21 — FREE PATH CONFIRMED; de-risks the entry gate (auth responder is no longer a hard prerequisite for a first live KAS turn).

Verified live: kiro-cli 2.8.1, @kiro/agent 0.3.257, experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-direct-spawn-2.8.1.py. KAS's selectAuthProvider resolves a --auth=user|machine|acp-callback flag (default user). The two spawn shapes differ:
  - WRAPPER spawn `kiro-cli acp --agent-engine v3` injects --auth=acp-callback -> KAS calls _kiro/auth/getAccessToken back on cyril -> the responder (this issue's main scope) is MANDATORY. This is the [TokenInvalidError] failure our earlier probes hit.
  - DIRECT spawn `node --experimental-wasm-modules <.../@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js> --transport=stdio` with NO --auth flag -> default FileAuthProvider reads ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json and self-refreshes via the file's refreshToken. _kiro/auth/getAccessToken fired 0 times across a full initialize + session/new + tool-using turn (stopReason end_turn). stderr logged "[INFO] Auth: default token file".

IMPLICATION: a first live KAS turn (cyril-j16p / KAS-2a) is reachable with ZERO credential-custodian code as long as the user has run `kiro-cli login`. Open Tension #7 moves OFF the walking-skeleton critical path.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (for triage, not yet applied):
  - tier-1 = free-path direct spawn, no responder. Unblocks the demo.
  - tier-2 = the _kiro/auth/getAccessToken acp-callback responder for the blessed wrapper lifecycle (kiro-cli token-sync + lock-guarded refresh-coordinator) and Builder-ID / external-IdP users.

Direct-spawn trade-off: cyril must locate the server entry (KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH env, else walk node_modules/@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js), the node runtime (KIRO_AGENT_PATH), and pass --experimental-wasm-modules — all of which the wrapper handles for free.

ROADMAP KAS-1 updated with this. Full --auth/--transport/sandbox flag contract + 5-tier auth priority in memory reference_kiro_kas_launch_contract.

2026-06-21 (fileMatch-steering probe session) — FOURTH token type for the tier-2 acp-callback responder, NOT covered by the three above: an IAM Identity Center / OIDC-PKCE login stores under auth_kv key `kirocli:odic:token` = {access_token, expires_at, refresh_token, region, start_url, oauth_flow, scopes} and carries NO profile_arn. For that case the matching profileArn lives in a SEPARATE row: auth_kv->`state` table, key `api.codewhisperer.profile`. Proven pitfall: pairing an OIDC accessToken with a DIFFERENT identity's profileArn (e.g. a stale ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token*.json, different account/region) -> backend 'Access denied'; accessToken and profileArn MUST be the same identity. Reinforces 'don't naively read one sqlite row': the responder must resolve profileArn per token type (social/Builder-ID embed it; odic splits it into state/api.codewhisperer.profile). Working assembly verified end-to-end in experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-filematch-steering-v2.py (odic access_token + state profileArn -> live KAS turn succeeded). Caveat for the direct-spawn 'free path': it reads ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json, but those files can be STALE/expired (they were expired this session for an odic-active user), so the free path depends on that file being kept fresh. See memory reference_kiro_kas_filematch_steering_source.
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-1

title: Absent contextUsagePercentage on kiro.dev/metadata stamps main context to 0.0 (sentinel fallback)
description: Discovered during cyril-fh06 (PR #54): real 2.4.1 captures contain v2 _kiro.dev/metadata frames with NO contextUsagePercentage (e.g. {"sessionId":…, "turnDurationMs":2281, "effort":"high"} in experiments/conductor-spike/trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl). convert/kiro.rs warns and falls back to 0.0, so a main-session frame of this shape stamps the toolbar context-usage to 0.0% — a plausible-looking wrong value, violating the workspace 'errors are not default values' rule. Fix shape: make the notification field Option<f64> (absent = no-change, same retain-last discipline as effort) or skip the context update when the key is absent; keep metering/duration/effort applying. Left byte-identical in cyril-fh06 on purpose.
acceptance_criteria: A metadata frame without contextUsagePercentage leaves context usage unchanged while still applying its metering/duration/effort; a frame with the field still updates; regression test replays the captured no-context frame shape.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #56 (52fa590).
