title: M1: Teach and inject one project lesson
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Deliver the first useful memory behavior: a user teaches one explicit lesson for the current project, sees it in `/memory`, starts a fresh ACP session in that project, and the agent receives it in a bounded first-prompt memory block before the original prompt. The visible chat continues to show only the user's original text. Disabled, missing, failed, or timed-out memory sends the original prompt unchanged.

The teaching action validates and redacts the lesson, records user-explicit provenance and an audit event, and stores it under the resolved project scope. The first-prompt block clearly identifies explicit lessons as instructions and keeps later derived-memory data in a separate trust class. The block is injected exactly once per session; later prompts rely on native ACP history unless a future policy explicitly changes that contract.

## Placement / boundaries

The memory module owns lesson validation, project scope, provenance, audit, ordering, budgeting, and rendering into the memory-context domain result. The bridge prompt adapter owns only the interim M1 integration authorized by ADR-0003: request a context block with a deadline, prepend it to the wire prompt, and fall back to the untouched original blocks. It must not open storage or reproduce lesson policy. The TUI and `/memory` command own teaching input and read-only projection; they call the memory interface rather than validating or formatting stored rows themselves.

Resolve project identity once from the canonical session workspace. Git worktrees sharing a canonical Git common directory share project lessons; non-Git workspaces use canonical workspace identity. Do not use process cwd as a later fallback. Store original prompts separately from injected context and never feed the injected block back as source material. Do not add transcript-derived episodes, MCP tools, global promotion, or embeddings in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can teach, list, and inspect an explicit lesson in the current project through Cyril.
- [ ] The lesson persists across Cyril and ACP session restarts.
- [ ] A fresh session's first prompt receives one bounded first-prompt memory block containing the lesson before the original user content.
- [ ] The TUI transcript displays the original user message without the injected block.
- [ ] A second prompt in the same session does not receive the block again.
- [ ] Memory disabled, unavailable, failed, or over deadline sends byte-equivalent original prompt blocks and leaves the turn usable.
- [ ] Lesson values are validated, secret-redacted, provenance-labeled as user explicit, scoped to the resolved project, and audit recorded.
- [ ] Explicit lessons are framed as instructions; no derived or document content can enter that instruction block.
- [ ] Project identity is stable across local Git worktrees and never re-derived from process cwd.
- [ ] The existing bridge fake-agent harness proves wire ordering, exactly-once injection, visible transcript separation, and fallback behavior.

## Blocked by

- cyril-j7um
design:
## Mechanism contract established by this slice

This slice creates the first real memory record: an explicit project lesson. A lesson stores an opaque memory ID, canonical project ID, redacted instruction text, normalized content hash, `user_explicit` provenance, `instruction` trust, active/invalidated status, creation/update timestamps, and the audit event that created or changed it. Exact normalized text within one project is idempotent. A later explicit edit supersedes the prior active row rather than mutating history in place.

Project identity is resolved once when the ACP session is created. Git worktrees use the canonical Git common directory as their local project identity; non-Git workspaces use canonical cwd. The store keeps a separate display path. No process-cwd fallback is permitted after the session-to-project binding exists.

The memory interface introduced here has one high-level operation for prompt preparation: given the bound session/project, the original first user text, and a character budget, return either a complete framed context block or no block. Callers do not query rows or format lessons. The initial lesson budget defaults to 4,000 characters, truncates only between lessons, and reports omitted count. Active project lessons render deterministically, newest explicit lesson first, inside a dedicated `CYRIL_LESSONS` instruction section. The bridge prepends that returned block as its own text content block and then sends the original prompt blocks unchanged.

Prompt preparation is attempted only for the first prompt accepted for a session. The bridge records the original prompt separately and never feeds the prepared block into memory. Runtime missing/error/deadline returns no block and cannot alter the original request.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Teach/list/inspect one explicit project lesson through Cyril.
- [ ] Lesson persists across Cyril and ACP session restarts.
- [ ] Fresh-session first prompt receives one bounded first-prompt memory block before original content.
- [ ] TUI displays only the original user message.
- [ ] Later prompts do not repeat automatic injection.
- [ ] Runtime failure/timeout sends byte-equivalent original prompt blocks.
- [ ] Lesson is validated, redacted, user-explicit, project-scoped, and audited.
- [ ] Explicit lessons remain separate from untrusted derived/document data.
- [ ] Project identity is stable across local Git worktrees and never falls back to process cwd.
- [ ] Bridge fake-agent tests prove ordering, exactly-once injection, and fallback.

title: WorkflowTracker: discriminate node_paused kind=retry-wait (KAS 0.46.1 in-place step retry)
description: KAS 0.46.1 (kiro-cli 2.19.0) adds in-place transient retry for workflow steps (new src/workflow/step-error-classifier.ts): on throttle/transient-network/transient-service errors it emits _kiro/workflow node_paused with a NEW payload field kind:"retry-wait" and reason "Throttled, retrying in Ns (attempt X/Y).", sleeps (delays [10,20,60,120]s throttle / [10,20,60]s network; env-overridable), then RE-EMITS node_start for the SAME node/session and continues the SAME step session. Doc comment: the persisted node status stays running — the event is the only client-visible signal. Cyril impact: WorkflowNodePaused models only reason (no kind), so apply_node_paused marks the node Paused — rendered as parked-awaiting-input until the re-emitted node_start merges it back (merge-not-append already tolerates repeated node_start, so no stuck state — but the semantic is wrong and cyril-zd8u plans to key immediacy off node_paused, which now has TWO meanings). Work: add pause kind to WorkflowNodePaused (Option, explicit-ignore-unknown per model-full-wire-surface discipline), parse it in the converter, track retry-wait distinctly from parked (e.g. WorkflowNodeStatus or a pause_kind field), and add a regression fence for node_paused(retry-wait) -> node_start resume. Note 2.18.0 finding "workflow paused moved pre-run_complete (key off node_paused)" now needs the kind discriminator. See docs/kiro-2.19.0-wire-audit.md.
acceptance_criteria: node_paused with kind:"retry-wait" tracked as retrying (not parked); re-emitted node_start restores running without duplicate rows; unknown pause kinds degrade to the current parked treatment with a debug log; tracker tests cover the retry-wait->node_start cycle and repeated cycles.

title: Route _kiro.dev/metadata by params.sessionId — subagent metadata frames currently stamp the main toolbar
description:
v2 _kiro.dev/metadata frames carry a params-level sessionId, and during agent_crew runs subagent sessions emit their OWN metadata frames: the committed captures prove it (experiments/conductor-spike/trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl has metadata frames for 5 distinct sessionIds; trace-2.4.1-tui-recorder.jsonl has 4). Kiro's own TUI filters them — carved 2.12.1 tui.js handleMetadataUpdate begins: let n=e.sessionId; if(n && n!==this.sessionId) return.

Cyril does not: client.rs ext_notification routes everything except ToolCallChunk as RoutedNotification::global, so MetadataUpdated from a subagent session is applied to the main SessionController/UiState. Consequences during any multi-subagent v2 turn: main toolbar context-usage % flickers with subagent percentages, subagent per-turn credits/duration are attributed to the main session, and a subagent effort value could overwrite the main badge.

Fix shape: extract params.sessionId in convert (or promote it in client.rs the way ToolCallChunk already does) and route MetadataUpdated scoped; frames with no sessionId stay global. Decide explicitly what a subagent-scoped metadata frame updates (likely: the subagent stream state or nothing, mirroring Kiro TUI's drop) — and keep main-session behavior byte-identical for single-session turns.
acceptance_criteria: MetadataUpdated from a frame whose sessionId matches a known subagent no longer mutates main-session context_usage/metering/effort; single-session metadata behavior unchanged (existing tests pass); regression test replays a main-metadata + subagent-metadata sequence and asserts main toolbar values come only from the main frame; frames without sessionId still apply to main.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #54 (8d28784). Repro: metadata_routing_tests::subagent_metadata_does_not_stamp_main_session (wire-shaped frames from trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl replayed through real ext_notification + App routing contract). Companion fence: metadata_without_session_id_still_applies_to_main. Fix mirrors the ToolCallChunk scoped-promotion idiom; empty/absent sessionId stays global.

title: /model picker has no entitlement guard — kiro-cli accepts an unusable model, then every turn fails -32603 mid-prompt
description:
Cyril drives the model picker from commands/options and sends whatever the user selects. kiro-cli ACCEPTS an id the account cannot serve, so nothing fails locally — the service rejects it mid-prompt, on the user turn, every turn, until the model is changed back.

First-party (KiroCrew test_acp_provider.py:1048-1053): "kiro-cli ACCEPTS the id at session/set_model, so nothing fails locally, and only the service rejects it mid-prompt as -32603 ... model is not available."

The entitlement source is session/new response models.availableModels. Rules KiroCrew settled on:
- empty/unknown advertised set means ALLOW (never "nothing is allowed")
- never compare ids across vendor namespaces (kiro advertises bare ids)
- an explicit user pick that is unusable RAISES a dedicated non-retryable error — never silently swap
- re-probe before refusing: the session/new snapshot can be a transient degraded answer (2 free-tier models for a fully-entitled account; the same binary+account advertised all 20 fifty minutes later — their issue #6355)

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 4.1, 5.3.

---
## Severity upgraded FIRST-PARTY -> MEASURED (2026-08-30, kiro-cli 2.20.1)

experiments/conductor-spike/probe-v2-set-model-2.20.1.py confirms the chain end to end:

- session/set_model {modelId:"definitely-not-a-model-9x"} -> ACCEPTED in 0.4ms with an empty {}. No
  validation, no error, nothing catchable at pick time.
- The very next session/prompt -> FAILS in 0.4s: -32603, data "Encountered an error in the response
  stream: The model 'definitely-not-a-model-9x' is not available. Please use '/model' to select a
  different model and try again. (request_id: ...)", and ZERO session/update frames — the turn produces
  nothing at all.

A bad pick is silent when made and fatal on every later turn until changed back.

Guard source confirmed available: v2 session/new returns models.availableModels with 19 entries.

CLASSIFIER WARNING: this is the NAMED rejection. KiroCrew reports >=2.16 reworded the CAPACITY rejection
to a NAMELESS form ("The model you've selected is temporarily unavailable"). Same "Encountered an error
in the response stream:" envelope, opposite retryability — classify on what is inside the envelope.
acceptance_criteria: A pick outside a known-non-empty availableModels is refused with a clear message instead of being sent. An empty or absent advertised set still allows the pick. Refusal path re-probes once before raising.

title: KAS-3 — Subagent rendering must handle dropped/empty/never-terminal results (upstream Kiro #9542)
description:
KAS subagent results can legitimately be empty, dropped, or never delivered — cyril's KAS-3 agent-subtask rendering (ROADMAP KAS-3; unfiled until now) must degrade gracefully. Surfaced by upstream Kiro bug #9542 (subagent "No result").

THREE upstream failure modes cyril will observe on the wire:
1. (v2) premature channel close: parent goes Idle before the subagent's `summary` is delivered -> stage result = "No result" (trace WARN: 'tool execution event for an agent not processing tools ... active_state: Idle, executing_subagents: {}').
2. (v3/KAS) null-response schema-validation fail: subagent hits max_tokens on long output -> response=null -> "No result". Intermittent, output-length-driven.
3. session-level channel corruption: a CANCELLED multi-stage `depends_on` pipeline leaves the multiplexer channel un-reset -> ALL subsequent subagent calls return "No result" until CLI restart.

cyril impact (cyril is an OBSERVER — can't fix upstream, must render robustly):
- Crew panel / SubagentUiState must NOT show a subagent as perpetually 'running' when its result is dropped/never-terminal. Treat a quiet subagent with no terminal result as a terminal 'no result / interrupted' state. On KAS the "No result" arrives as the parent's `orchestrate_subagent` tool_call_update content — render faithfully.
- HAZARD cyril can TRIGGER: Esc -> session/cancel during a KAS multi-stage subagent pipeline is exactly the Ctrl+C path that triggers upstream mode 3 (session-wide channel corruption). cyril should guard/warn, and if subagent results start coming back empty, surface a 'subagent channel may be wedged — /new to recover' hint.
- Repro/verify with the ACP wire recorder KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH=/tmp/acp-trace.jsonl ({ts,dir,msg} JSONL; lives in tui.js, confirmed 2.8.1).

Engine note: failure mode differs v2 vs v3. Related: cyril-9akh (notification-vs-response ordering race this validates), cyril-j16p (KAS-2a walking skeleton this builds on).

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review — split acceptance criteria BY ENGINE (current wording conflates v2 and KAS paths):
- The 'Crew panel / SubagentUiState must not show perpetually running' line applies ONLY to v2 failure mode #1. On KAS those components receive nothing (no list_update); feeding KAS subtask data into SubagentTracker would violate the CLAUDE.md separate-path rule.
- KAS modes #2/#3 belong to the greenfield KAS-3 subtask path: a distinct grouper keyed on _meta.kiro.kind == 'agent-subtask' / agentSubtaskId, with _meta parsing in convert/kas.rs producing engine-neutral typed fields (UiState never reads raw _meta). Nothing in the crates handles agent-subtask yet — KAS-3 is greenfield, right moment to pin this.
- The never-terminal inference (quiet subagent with no terminal result -> render interrupted) and the wedge heuristic (empty results -> hint /new) are stateful inferences that live in that KAS-3 component, NOT SubagentTracker.
- The orchestrate_subagent tool_call_update rendering approach and the App-altitude Esc-hazard guard are architecturally clean as filed.

title: /usage Providers shows — for Kiro despite ACP handshake identity
description:
The /usage Providers page renders a dash for current Kiro turns even though ACP identifies the connected agent during initialize.

The initialize response has optional agentInfo (observed as {name: "Kiro CLI Agent", version: ...}), and Cyril also knows the bound AgentEngine (v2 or KAS). Cyril currently discards agentInfo after engine fingerprinting. Usage attribution instead splits the selected model string only when it has provider/model form; a Kiro model such as gpt-5.6-terra becomes provider=NULL, model=gpt-5.6-terra. The Providers rollup groups the NULL provider and the UI renders its missing name as —.

Observed locally: current Kiro usage rows have provider=NULL and model=gpt-5.6-terra, while the Models page can still show the model. This is an attribution/display bug, not evidence that Kiro is absent from the ACP handshake. Keep this issue focused on agent/provider attribution; global usage-history scoping is a separate concern.
design: Define the usage identity boundary explicitly: retain the underlying model provider when the model id supplies one, and separately capture the outer ACP agent/vendor identity from initialize agentInfo with a reliable AgentEngine fallback when agentInfo is absent. Make the Providers view use the resolved outer vendor when the current engine is Kiro, without relabeling arbitrary provider-less records as Kiro. Add the identity to the typed usage context/record path and persist it for new turns; do not silently reinterpret historical rows whose provenance is unknown.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A v2/Kiro session whose model id is provider-less (for example gpt-5.6-terra) records a resolved Kiro provider/vendor, and /usage Providers displays Kiro instead of —.
2. A KAS/Kiro session also displays Kiro when initialize omits agentInfo but the bound engine identifies KAS.
3. An explicit provider/model id (for example openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol) retains openai-codex as the model-provider identity and is not relabeled Kiro.
4. Unknown provider-less records remain explicitly unknown rather than being guessed as Kiro.
5. Regression tests cover initialize identity/engine fallback, persistence into usage records, Providers-page grouping, and the existing model/provider split behavior.

title: _kiro/system/notify is session-less: stall signals cannot be attributed to a session
description:
Live capture (docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 2): the watchdog's notification frame carries ONLY {level, message} — no sessionId, no _meta.

  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"_kiro/system/notify",
   "params":{"level":"warning","message":"The model response paused unexpectedly. Waiting for it to resume…"}}

Consequence: like _kiro/workflow/*, this is a GLOBAL notification. With parallel sessions in flight — subagents, workflow steps (which are peer sessions), or a v2 connection running parallel turns — cyril cannot tell WHICH session stalled, so it cannot attach the warning to the right stream or drill-in view.

Contrast: _kiro/powers/items_changed DOES carry sessionId, so this is an inconsistency in the KAS ext dialect rather than a blanket rule.

Options: (a) render it as a global/toolbar-level notice only, never per-session — safe but coarse; (b) heuristically attribute to the single active turn when exactly one is in flight, and fall back to global otherwise; (c) raise upstream as a wire gap.

Blocks the per-session half of cyril-0w3u.

--- PARTIAL MITIGATION found in the 2.20.1 new-field sweep (docs § 8) ---
The stall error arrives TWICE. Besides the JSON-RPC -32000 response, the same error also rides session/update -> session_info_update with kind:"display_error":

  {"displayError": {"message": "The model response stalled and timed out...",
                    "errorType": "StreamIdleTimeoutError",
                    "retryErrorType": "TRANSIENT"},
   "kind": "display_error", "message": "...",
   "errorType": "StreamIdleTimeoutError", "retryErrorType": "TRANSIENT"}
  (fields appear BOTH nested under displayError AND flattened on _meta.kiro)

That frame IS session-scoped, unlike _kiro/system/notify. So the TERMINAL stall error can be attributed to a session even with peers in flight — render it from display_error rather than from the session-less notify.

Scope reduction: this issue now covers only the SOFT warnings ("paused unexpectedly", "Retrying..."), which remain session-less and unattributable. The terminal case is solved.

title: All handled host callbacks cross the bridge mediator (ADR-0004 amendment)
description:
Deferred from KAS-5a (cyril-7bdu) during checkpointed-build. ADR-0004 decided that server->client host-io requests (fs, terminal) route THROUGH the bridge run_loop's host-io arm so the engine's capability sub-traits / a cyril-stages gate can observe/transform them. KAS-5a instead resolves fs DIRECTLY in #[cfg(feature=kas)] KiroClient overrides (kas::host_io::{read,write}_text_file) because: (1) the loop seam has no consumer yet — no stages gate exists (the codebase's engine.rs:12 rule says capability sub-traits land WITH their first consumer, not as consumer-less stubs); (2) routing through run_loop forces a #[cfg]'d run_loop parameter (can't cleanly cfg a single fn param) — either ship HostIoRequest+channel un-gated in every v2 build (violates ADR-0002 'default build links no KAS code') or maintain two cfg'd run_loop signatures; (3) the non-blocking invariant (KAS-5a claim C4) is already satisfied WITHOUT the loop arm — the acp ClientSideConnection spawns each inbound request as its own spawn_local task (rpc.rs:272, wired bridge.rs:390), so a direct async tokio::fs resolve is off-loop and never starves the loop.

WHEN TO BUILD THIS: when the first real consumer of the seam lands — a cyril-stages host-io gate (audit/policy/transform of file reads+writes+shell execs, ADR-0003/Phase 2) or KAS-7 hooks. At that point, move fs+terminal resolution behind a HostIoRequest channel + run_loop arm so the consumer can intercept, and resolve ADR-0002's cfg-threading (likely: gate the whole host-io module + a kas-only run_loop variant, or accept un-gated host-io once it's no longer kas-only). Until then, direct-resolve in the cfg'd overrides is the right altitude.

REFS: ADR-0004 (docs/adr/0004); .cyril-7bdu/falsifiable-design.md claim C3 + Negative-space #3; KAS-5a cyril-7bdu.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-01: deferral expired; scope widened; design settled in ADR-0004 amendment ---

Driven by the 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review (Candidate 01, its TOP recommendation) and now recorded as the ADR-0004 amendment. This is a DRIFT-CLOSURE ticket, not a new feature: ADR-0004's original Decision already routed "KAS-5 fs/terminal, KAS-1 auth later" through the loop. The three deferral reasons above, reassessed:

(1) "no consumer yet" — EXPIRED. The consumer is lifecycle unification, already visible as two ad-hoc escapes: the terminal-registry Rc grabbed out of KiroClient before the ACP connection takes ownership (cyril-3lh8, bridge.rs:586), and hook cancel handled inline in ext_notification (client.rs:199). Two adapters, two bespoke routes; a third capability invents a third.

(2) "forces a #[cfg]'d run_loop parameter" — DISSOLVED by our own later work. InternalChannels (bridge.rs:672) already threads a #[cfg(feature="kas")] field through ONE parameter, destructured with `..`. ADR-0002 is preserved by making the callback payload uninhabited in a default build (`enum HostCallback {}`): the select! arm compiles, its match is exhaustively empty, and no KAS code links.

(3) "non-blocking already satisfied without the loop arm" — CORRECT, AND CONCEDED. It is a constraint to preserve, not a benefit this delivers. Same for shutdown-abort: kill_on_drop(true) + LocalSet teardown already reap callback children; formalizing that is worth doing but is not a leak being fixed.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TITLE SUGGESTED. Not just host-io: every handled host-callback request AND control notification. Size from the variant count, not the family count — ~19 handled non-permission variants today: 7 typed acp::Client overrides, 5 ext requests, the 5 _kiro/fs/* ops added by ADR-0009 (which postdate the review), and 2 control notifications (hooks cancel/didChange).

DESIGN NOW SETTLED IN ADR-0004's AMENDMENT. Load-bearing points: the mediator is a TYPE with an accept()-style entry point (NOT more select! arms — run_loop is already ~1,405 lines), and it stays THIN. The review's deletion test concluded "deepen around the Engine module", so depth accretes on the ADR-0001 adapter set, not here; adding a capability must touch the mediator zero times. Cutover is sliced per adapter (Auth, then Host I/O, then Hooks), parity-preserving, deleting the direct paths it replaces.

SEQUENCING: blocked on cyril-b4y4 (review Candidate 02) and cyril-dn91. b4y4 amends ADR-0004's OWN turn-completion section — landing it first keeps ADR-0004 to one coherent amendment instead of two on overlapping ground, and lands this mediator in a run_loop that has already shed its inline turn policy. dn91 supplies the Engine-selected adapter set this mediator dispatches to.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every handled host-callback request and control notification crosses one bridge-internal mediator type; the direct KiroClient paths it replaces are deleted.
2. The mediator has an accept()-style entry point that is unit-testable without the async bridge harness; run_loop's arm holds no callback policy inline.
3. A default (non-kas) build still links no KAS code — ADR-0002's compile-time posture verified, not assumed.
4. Seam scenarios prove: non-blocking mediation, ordered acceptance with concurrent resolution, bounded backpressure, callback-specific cancellation, responder drop, shutdown, and notification-before-error-response ordering.
5. Every handled callback variant has an exhaustive mediation-wiring case (~19 today).
6. Strict behavior parity per slice, confirmed against a live kiro-cli acp session for both engines.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #85 merged to main (41cecec). All 6 ACs fenced: AC1 every-handled-variant census (19 methods, mutation-checked) + zero direct responder calls; AC2 8 sync host_mediator unit tests + policy-free drain; AC3 probe_g9vt_c13 both configs; AC4 concurrency/backpressure/drop/shutdown/ordering fences (cancel seam opt-in tracked cyril-740a); AC5 census+count; AC6 live v2+KAS both engines. Both ADR-0004 escapes (3lh8 terminal Rc, inline hook arms) deleted. Live-caught deadlock (in-loop drain) fixed via dedicated drain task. Filed: cyril-740a.

title: P1 — Usage observer: live full-fidelity capture from usage_update (omp path)
description:
Phase 1 of the usage-observer stage (cyril-4h6i). Full-fidelity path: when cyril drives a standard-ACP agent that emits the standard `usage_update` session-update kind (omp — LIVE-PROVEN in reference_omp_acp_agent that cyril's unmodified bridge already receives it), capture per-turn usage on the wire and aggregate. No file-scan — cyril is the live client.

SCOPE: (1) parse usage_update {inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheRead,cacheWrite,...} into a typed per-turn UsageRecord (tokens; cost via a per-model price table like omp, or read cost from _meta if the agent supplies it — verify omp's usage_update payload shape live first); (2) per-turn log keyed by session/folder/model/provider/agentType with duration+TTFT+toolCalls (cyril already tracks tool_call notifications) + errors; (3) aggregation over the log (overview/costs/providers/models/tools/recent/errors/folders — the panels whose data is fully present); (4) a viewer (TUI panel and/or a small local HTTP surface — decide during design). Keep aggregation engine-agnostic (no kiro/omp specifics in the rollup layer — that seam is the whole point of the vendor-neutral stage).

Design-first: confirm the live usage_update payload (tokens only vs tokens+cost) with a probe before committing the record schema — schema vs runtime (feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime).

title: Enable KAS v2 hooks: gate is _meta.kiro.hooks={enabled,v2}; agent executes hooks host-side
description:
The KAS v2 hooks subsystem is fully reachable, and cyril has never turned it on.
Live-verified 2026-07-31 (probe-kas-v2hooks-2.16.0.py, capture
kas-v2hooks-2.16.0.jsonl, kiro-cli 2.16.0 / KAS 0.27.8).

THE GATE (two earlier probes got this wrong):
  clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.hooks = { "enabled": true, "v2": true }
It must be an OBJECT. The bundle reads `kiroMeta?.hooks?.enabled` and then
`hooksConfig.v2 === true`; advertising the BOOLEAN `true` makes `?.enabled`
undefined and silently skips the whole block — which is what
probe-kas-pushed-methods-2.16.0.py did, and why _kiro/hooks/setEnabled answered
"not available when v2Hooks is disabled" in the RPC sweep.

HOOK FILES: <workspace>/.kiro/hooks/*.json, validated by kasHookFileSchema:
  { "version": "v1",
    "hooks": [ { name, description?, trigger, matcher?, action,
                 timeout?, enabled?, confirm? } ] }
  trigger (file, camelCase): preToolUse | postToolUse | sessionStart | stop
  action: discriminated union on `type` — command | prompt | agent

VERIFIED WORKING:
- _kiro/hooks/list  {sessionId, workspacePaths, includeDisabled} -> {hooks:[...]}
- _kiro/hooks/setEnabled {sessionId, hookId, enabled} -> {success:true}, both
  directions; it rewrites the enabled flag in the backing FILE.
- _kiro/hooks/didChange fires as a notification carrying the full registry.
- Hooks ACTUALLY EXECUTE. Both a sessionStart and a preToolUse hook ran during a
  normal turn; the host-side evidence file contained
  "cyril-audit-hook-fired-start | cyril-audit-hook-fired-pre".

WIRE SHAPE (differs from the file shape in two ways cyril must translate):
  { "id": "<absolute filePath>#hook-<n>",       // composite, not a bare name
    "name": "cyril-audit-pre",
    "action": { "type": "runCommand", "command": "..." },   // file says "command",
                                                            // wire says "runCommand"
    "_meta": { "trigger": "PreToolUse",          // PascalCase on the wire,
                                                 // camelCase in the file
               "source": "standalone-file",
               "filePath": "...",
               "enabled": true } }

ARCHITECTURAL FINDING — v1 and v2 hooks execute in DIFFERENT PROCESSES:
  v2 (this): the AGENT runs the command itself via its own processRunner.
             _kiro/hooks/executeHook is never sent to the client.
  v1:        the agent asks the CLIENT to run hooks (that is what the
             agent->client _kiro/hooks/{list,sessionStart,executeHook} are for).
So `_kiro/hooks/list` really is bidirectional, and WHICH direction is live depends
on which hook generation the client advertised.

SECURITY NOTE, worth a deliberate decision rather than a default: with v2 enabled,
a `.kiro/hooks/*.json` in the workspace causes the AGENT to execute arbitrary shell
commands on the host, and no session/request_permission was raised for either hook
in this capture. The workspaceTrusted flag feeds a `disabledReason:
"untrusted-workspace"` field, so trust state is the intended guard. cyril should
not advertise `hooks.v2` without deciding how it establishes workspace trust and
whether it surfaces hook execution in the transcript.

title: KAS allow_always consent-scope echo: live control probe, then optional consent passthrough on permission responses
description: Split from cyril-qo13 (its widened-scope halves b+c for KAS). The qo13 prove-it probe RESOLVED the allow_once case: the reference client itself omitted the _meta.kiro.consent echo on trace requests 8/9 (present on 6/7, all consentRound=1) and all four fs_writes completed -> consent echo is OPTIONAL for invocation-scope grants; cyril need not send it. UNVERIFIED remainder: allow_always. The reference outcome shape for allow_once was scope:'invocation'; presumably always-accept echoes scope:'session'|'always', and it is unknown whether KAS persists the grant scope WITHOUT that echo (schema-present != required, feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime). CONTROL PROBE: live KAS session (python raw JSON-RPC template in experiments/conductor-spike/), trigger fs_write approval, reply optionId:'always-accept' WITH NO consent _meta, then re-trigger the same capability+resource and check whether KAS re-asks (grant not persisted) or proceeds (persisted). If required: add an engine-conditional consent{capability,scope,workspaceRoot} passthrough on the permission response via convert/kas.rs (the KAS seam), echoing request _meta.kiro.consent.capability/workspaceRoot + scope derived from the picked option. Evidence base: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl + .cyril-qo13/probe-findings.md.

notes.content:
CONSENT SHAPE DRIFTS ACROSS BUNDLES (2026-07-02, KAS modes probe — docs/kiro-kas-modes-2.10.0.md wire delta #4): the request-side consent _meta is not a stable struct. 2.10.0 bundle (@kiro/agent 0.3.299, modes-probe capture): {capability, resource, askType, triggeringResource, workspaceRoot} — consentRound ABSENT, triggeringResource present. 2.11.0 trace (0.8.0): consentRound present (=1 on reqs 6/7), no triggeringResource observed. Implication for the passthrough half of this issue: do NOT model consent as a typed struct with required fields — echo the request's consent object opaquely (serde_json::Value or all-optional fields), adding only the derived scope. A typed consent that requires consentRound or triggeringResource will break on the other bundle line. Raw evidence: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-modes-dumps/bug-fix.json (first permission frame) vs kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl.

LIVE DATAPOINT (2026-07-02, qo13 C8 probe, KAS 2.11.0 direct-spawn): replied {outcome:{outcome:'selected',optionId:'always-accept'}} (NO consent _meta) to the first execute approval; turn proceeded BUT two further permission requests still arrived in the same turn (different resources/commands). Consistent with per-resource/per-capability consent scoping rather than the always grant failing outright — but ambiguous without inspecting the follow-up requests' consent.resource. The control probe this issue plans should compare same-resource re-asks specifically.

title: Render v2 model-refusal alerts: parse refusal object on kiro.dev/metadata (2.12.1)
description:
kiro-cli 2.12.1 adds Model Refusal Alerts: when the backend refuses (content policy / content filter), the v2 engine emits an optional refusal object on the kiro.dev/metadata notification — {category, explanation, recommendedModel} (camelCase on wire; confirmed from carved 2.12.1 tui.js handler: broadcastStreamEvent({type:'model_refusal', stopReason, category:r?.category, explanation:r?.explanation, recommendedModel:r?.recommendedModel})) — and metadata stopReason can be 'CONTENT_FILTERED'. The session/prompt response can also return ACP stop_reason: refusal.

Cyril today: to_stop_reason maps Refusal correctly and toolbar shows 'Refused' (red), but convert/kiro.rs kiro.dev/metadata parsing (to_ext_notification) reads only contextUsagePercentage/meteringUsage/tokens/effort — the refusal object is silently dropped. Kiro's own TUI shows a transient error alert plus a system chat message with the explanation (fallback text suggests switching model / new conversation / rewind). Cyril users get a bare 'Refused' with no why and no recommended model.

Scope: extend the MetadataUpdated notification (or add a dedicated notification) with Option<RefusalInfo {category, explanation, recommended_model}>, surface it in UiState as a system message + toolbar state. Guard partial updates per design principles (all three fields optional). Note: runtime emission not yet live-verified (cannot force a backend refusal on demand) — schema evidence is from binary serde strings + tui.js handler; per feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime treat wire keys as provisional until first live refusal capture. Stale doc comment types/session.rs:497-499 ('bridge currently hardcodes EndTurn') should be deleted in passing — bridge.rs:794 extracts the real stop reason.

2.12.3 audit addendum (docs/kiro-2.12.3-wire-audit.md): refusal handling grew in tui.js (8->13 tokens); 'refusal' is now a FIRST-CLASS stopReason zod literal with two emit paths -> model_refusal {stopReason, category, explanation, recommendedModel} (KAS/_kiro side). When implementing, tolerate stopReason 'refusal' in addition to metadata stopReason 'CONTENT_FILTERED'. Still no live refusal capture; keys remain provisional.

title: protocolVersion and clientCapabilities must be per-agent literals — KAS rejects the kiro-cli date string
description:
Cyril sends one ACP protocol version for every target. KAS validates the field against a NUMERIC schema and rejects the kiro-cli date string with "expected number, received string" (KiroCrew runtime.py:385-388). This is a hard initialize failure that presents as a spawn or auth bug.

  kiro-cli : protocolVersion = "2025-08-22"  (string)
  KAS      : protocolVersion = 1             (integer) -- "what the ACP SDK and KAS own TUI send"
  claude   : protocolVersion = 1             (integer)

Client capabilities differ too: KAS reads only fs.readTextFile / fs.writeTextFile / terminal from the TOP LEVEL of clientCapabilities; everything else it honours lives under _meta.kiro, and those are CALLBACK capabilities (types.py:213-222).

KiroCrew treats collapsing these into one universal handshake as a CI-blocking defect (harness-parity H10): "Protocol version and client capabilities stay per-harness literals. Collapsing them to one handshake that every harness accepts silently downgrades the Kiro session declared capabilities." Pinned by a test asserting the two capability dicts are UNEQUAL.

Blocks any non-Kiro ACP agent work.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 6.2, 7.
acceptance_criteria: protocolVersion and clientCapabilities are resolved per agent target (keyed off the resolved spawn command), not global constants. A test asserts two targets produce non-identical handshakes.

title: Two KAS probes write a live bearer token into their capture file
description:
FIXED 2026-07-31. Emit-time redaction retrofitted onto both named probes:

  probe-kas-compact-summarization-2.9.0.py
  probe-kas-orchestrate-wire-2.9.0.py

Both now define SECRET_KEYS + redact() and apply it inside rec(), so the real
token still reaches KAS and the frame shape survives, but the log gets
"<redacted>". Verified with a synthetic auth frame through each file's actual
extracted helper: bearer token, refreshToken (nested) and profileArn all
redacted; non-secret values and the key set preserved.

Scope widened slightly, deliberately:
- ALL FOUR bidirectional-logging probes now share ONE identical 13-key set
  (the two above, the canonical probe-kas-orchestrate-capture-2.14.1.py, and the
  new probe-kas-turn-traffic-ab-2.16.0.py). The canonical set gained
  profileArn/profile_arn/authorization/Authorization so there is one convention
  rather than three variants.

The "49 probes answer getAccessToken" concern in the original description is
narrower than it looks. The defect requires logging BOTH directions. Swept the 5
other probes that both answer getAccessToken and write a capture file
(custom-dag-live-2.16.0, hostinit-2.15.0, turnend-capture,
workflow-repeat-watch-2.16.0, workflow-runtime-2.16.0): all are structurally
immune — their rep()/send() writes only to the child process stdin, while the
file writer only takes RECEIVED frames. Confirmed empirically too (their
captures scanned clean before commit). So the real predicate is
"logs outbound frames", not "answers getAccessToken", and that set is now
fully covered.

Pre-existing captures on disk are out of scope here — see the account-id issue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Neither probe writes an unredacted accessToken to its capture; verified by running the redact helper over a synthetic auth frame.
2. KAS still receives the real token (redaction applies only on the path to the log).
3. A grep over experiments/conductor-spike shows no probe persisting an auth reply without redaction.

notes.content: probe-kas-turn-traffic-ab-2.16.0.py (added 2026-07-31) would have been a THIRD offender — its client_to_agent records include our own reply to _kiro/auth/getAccessToken, which carries the live bearer token. Fixed at the source rather than post-hoc: the probe now scrubs at emit time via a SECRET_KEYS set (accessToken/access_token/profileArn/profile_arn/idToken/refreshToken/authorization), so its captures are committable by construction. Verified the scrub does not change the diff-acp-wire result. That emit-time scrub is the pattern to retrofit onto the two existing probes this issue tracks.

title: KAS terminal wait_for_exit stalls when a clean-exiting command leaves a daemonized pipe holder
description: A command that exits cleanly but leaves a background child holding the shared output pipe delays the terminal/wait_for_exit reply until that orphan closes the pipe: join_output (terminal_io.rs) joins the drain reader AFTER child.wait(), and the reader only reaches EOF when every writer fd closes. Measured in the cyril-6bol deep review with `sh -c "sleep 3 & printf done"`: child.wait() returned in 1.9ms, read_to_end in 3.00s — the wait reply is silently delayed for the whole window. kill/release recover via the process-tree kill; a CLEAN-exiting daemonizing command does not. The module doc claims the create-time drain prevents deadlocks and never mentions this bound. Fix direction: an exit-detection escape for the drain (e.g. bounded post-exit grace then snapshot what was read), plus a module-doc correction.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #83 (cde0ea9). Drain reader publishes into a shared buffer; join_output bounds the EOF join with a 500ms post-exit grace then snapshots (applies at wait/kill/release). Repro fence: wait_reply_not_held_hostage_by_daemonized_pipe_holder (3.08s stall red -> 0.64s green). Module doc corrected.

title: Surface meta.subcommands in help and autocomplete (10 of 24 agent commands advertise them)
description:
commands/available carries a meta.subcommands array that cyril's CommandInfo drops, so cyril's help and autocomplete never mention any subcommand. Users have to already know they exist.

NOT a wire bug — the mechanism works today. Verified at 2.14.2: args.value is a free-form string and the agent's own per-command parser splits subcommand + arguments. `_kiro.dev/commands/execute {command:{command:'context',args:{value:'show'}}}` returns the full context breakdown, so typing `/context show` in cyril already works via AgentCommand::execute's {value: args} path (commands/mod.rs:281-285). This is purely discoverability.

Advertised subcommands, captured live (2.14.2, v2, 24 commands total):
  /agent      selection  [create, edit, swap]
  /chat       selection  [save, load, new]
  /code       panel      [status, init, logs, overview, summary]
  /context    panel      [show, add, remove, clear]
  /effort     selection  [set-current-as-default]
  /goal       panel      [clear]
  /knowledge  panel      [show, add, remove, update, clear, cancel]
  /mcp        panel      [list, add, remove]
  /model      selection  [set-current-as-default]
  /tools      panel      [trust-all, trust, untrust, reset]

CommandInfo (crates/cyril-core/src/types/command.rs) models name/label/description/has_options/is_selection/is_local and discards the rest of meta (subcommands, hint, searchable). Adding subcommands is additive.

Worth noting why /effort's entry matters beyond autocomplete: set-current-as-default is the 2.14.x persistence flip surfacing on the wire. /effort and /model are session-scoped now (the disableAutoDefault{Model,Effort} settings are gone from the 2.14.2 binary — 0 string hits, set-current-as-default at 13), so saving a default is an explicit user action. kiro.dev's effort docs still claim effort persists automatically; the binary disagrees. cyril users currently have no discoverable way to save a default.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CommandInfo carries subcommands from commands/available meta (absent => empty, not an error).
2. /help output lists a command's subcommands when it advertises any.
3. Slash-command autocomplete offers subcommands after the command name plus a space.
4. Commands advertising no subcommands render exactly as today (no empty brackets or trailing separators).
5. A unit test covers the parse of a commands/available entry with and without meta.subcommands.

notes.content: 2.17.0 additive wire delta (v2-turn-2.17.0.jsonl frame 3): commands/available meta now ALSO carries subcommandDescriptions — per-subcommand description strings beside the existing subcommands/subcommandHints (e.g. /context: show/add/remove/clear each with a description). Surface these in the autocomplete popup when present; capture-derived fixture available.

title: KAS host-io: bounded read for fs/read_text_file (don't load whole file when line/limit set)
description:
kas::host_io::read_text_file uses tokio::fs::read_to_string, loading the ENTIRE file into memory before slice_lines selects [line, line+limit). For a large file with a small limit (KAS's chunked-read pattern), the whole file is read and allocated regardless of how few lines were requested -- a memory spike / OOM risk proportional to file size, not request size.

Consider tokio::io::BufReader + AsyncBufReadExt: skip(start), take(limit), stop early; keep the read-whole path for the None/None case. Must preserve slice_lines' byte-exact semantics (split_inclusive keeps trailing newline; CRLF intact) and the non-UTF-8 -> Err behavior. Per-callback, not a hot loop -- low priority. Discovered during review of PR #34 (KAS-5a).
acceptance_criteria: A read with line/limit on a large file allocates ~O(requested window), not O(file size); slice byte-exactness (trailing newline, CRLF) and non-UTF-8 -> Err preserved; whole-file (None/None) behavior unchanged; existing host_io read tests still pass.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) Do NOT use the lines() adapter — it strips the \n AND a trailing \r, destroying the documented byte-exact/CRLF semantics. Correct idiom: manual read_line (or read_until(b'\n')) loop — delimiter included, so \r\n survives; clear a reused buffer for the `start` skipped lines, accumulate `limit` lines, break on Ok(0). O(longest line + window) memory; no meaningfully simpler idiom exists.
(2) One acceptance criterion is unachievable by construction: 'non-UTF-8 -> Err' today validates the WHOLE file (read_to_string); a bounded read cannot validate bytes it never reads. Relax to Err-for-invalid-UTF-8-within-the-read-region and document the divergence (reading to EOF just to validate defeats the issue's purpose).
(3) line-beyond-EOF still yields "" under a streaming loop — matches current behavior, no special case needed.

title: Picker never marks the active option — /model and /effort options carry no `current` field on 2.14.2
description:
cyril's picker draws its check mark from CommandOption::is_current (crates/cyril-ui/src/widgets/picker.rs:84), parsed from an option's `current` boolean (commands/mod.rs:328). Live captures at 2.14.2 show the agent never sends that field, so the mark never renders and the picker gives no indication of what is currently selected.

Captured live (v2 engine, session default model gpt-5.6-terra):

  /model  options -> keys: [description, group, label, value]        (no `current`)
          nothing marked, even though gpt-5.6-terra IS the active model
  /effort options -> keys: [label, value]                            (no `current`)
          fresh session: nothing marked
          after an in-session change: the active level rides INSIDE the label,
          e.g. {"value":"low","label":"Low  [active]"} / "None  [active]"

So there are two distinct defects:
1. No marker at all for /model, and for /effort until the user changes it once in-session.
2. When /effort does mark it, cyril renders the raw "[active]" suffix as label text instead of using its own marker.

parse_options_response's `current` handling is not wrong, just dead against current kiro-cli — the existing test asserting is_current (commands/mod.rs:745) runs on a synthetic fixture, not a live shape, which is why this went unnoticed.

Fix direction: cyril already knows both values without the wire telling it — UiState::current_model and UiState::effort (state.rs:54-58) feed the toolbar. Marking the picker row that matches cyril's own state covers both commands and both defects. Parsing the "[active]" suffix would also work for /effort but is string-sniffing a display string, and it would still leave /model unmarked. Keep the `current` parse as a fallback for agents that do send it.

Related: cyril-cc5e (Keep picker selection visible) covered scroll/selection visibility, not the active-value marker.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Opening /model marks the row matching the session's current model.
2. Opening /effort marks the row matching the session's current effort level, including on a fresh session before any in-session change.
3. A label arriving with an "[active]" suffix does not render that suffix verbatim.
4. An option list that DOES carry current: true still marks correctly (fallback preserved).
5. Render test over a picker fixture asserting exactly one marked row.

title: KAS-2a — Walking skeleton: a plain KAS turn renders and ends
description:
The milestone that earns a demo: select KAS, authenticate, prompt, watch text + tool calls stream, turn completes, input is live again. The MINIMUM for a plain turn to render and end cleanly. Other _kiro/* surfaces (governance, mcp/status, powers, progressive_context) and the other session_info_update kinds all fire on a plain turn too, but cyril's existing unknown-variant debug! arm drops them gracefully — deferred to 2b-2d without hanging anything.

SCOPE (ROADMAP KAS-2a, docs/ROADMAP.md:165):
- Converter arm (engine-keyed, in the Engine-trait structure from KAS-0) for agent_message_chunk / agent_thought_chunk / tool_call / tool_call_update ONLY.
- session_info_update -> kind:'turn_end' mapped to cyril's turn-completion / busy-clear. THIS — not the session/prompt response — is the turn-completion signal under KAS. HANG-PROOFING: cyril's prompt-response await must be NON-BLOCKING under KAS — drive completion off turn_end, treat the prompt response as secondary/whenever-it-arrives, so a non-returning response cannot freeze the skeleton. Verify with existing probe-kas-* scripts (no new probe needed).
- Answer _kiro/terminal/shell_type ({sessionId} -> {shellType: bash|zsh|fish|powershell|sh}) — lightest host callback, called once at session setup; missing reply yields 'Shell: undefined' in the system prompt.
- Handle sess_*-prefixed session ids and per-run log dirs under ~/.kiro/logs/<ts>/.
- Defensive unknown-variant tolerance for everything else (one debug! line noting _kiro/* surfaces are intentionally dormant pre-2b).

CRITICAL REWORK (ROADMAP note, docs/ROADMAP.md:177): the off-loop busy-guard + TurnCompleted emission from PR #22 (cyril-84ca) must be reworked here. That PR emits TurnCompleted when conn.prompt().await resolves and keys the one-turn busy-guard off prompt_task.is_finished() — both encode 'prompt response == turn end', correct for v2 but FALSE for KAS (turn-end is session_info_update->turn_end; the prompt response is secondary/late). Under KAS, is_finished() stays false after a logical turn-end (next prompt wrongly rejected 'a turn is already in progress') and TurnCompleted fires late/never — the exact hang the non-blocking criterion guards against. Fix: route BOTH the busy-guard and TurnCompleted through the engine's turn-end signal (KAS-0 turn-end detection in the Engine trait), not prompt_task.is_finished()/prompt().await. Concrete code: the SendPrompt guard + spawned prompt_task in bridge.rs.

REFS: ROADMAP KAS-2a (docs/ROADMAP.md:165); existing experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-*.py.
acceptance_criteria:

* Turn completion is driven by session_info_update->turn_end, NOT the session/prompt response; the prompt-response await is non-blocking (a non-returning response cannot freeze the skeleton).
* The busy-guard and TurnCompleted emission are routed through the engine turn-end signal (not prompt_task.is_finished()/prompt().await); a second prompt after a logical turn-end is accepted, not rejected with 'a turn is already in progress'.
* _kiro/terminal/shell_type is answered (no 'Shell: undefined').

* v1/v2 engine path unchanged.

title: M0: Show memory runtime health in Cyril
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Add the first complete Cyril-owned memory tracer: when memory is enabled, Cyril starts an isolated local memory runtime, establishes authenticated user-private IPC, initializes versioned empty memory and knowledge stores, and reports health through `/memory status` and TUI state. When memory is disabled or runtime startup fails, the ACP bridge and ordinary chat remain usable and the TUI reports the actual memory state. Runtime shutdown is bounded and reopening preserves the initialized stores.

This slice intentionally stores no user memories, runs no production background jobs, and exposes no agent tools. Its demo is operational: enable memory, see a ready runtime and store versions, restart Cyril and see the same stores; break startup and see memory unavailable while chat still starts.

## Placement / boundaries

The new `cyril-memory` domain/runtime module owns configuration validation, data-location resolution, store migrations, runtime health, and IPC authentication. A dedicated memory-runtime process owns database connections and later model workers. The `cyril` orchestrator owns process startup, bounded shutdown, and translation of runtime status into application events. `cyril-ui` owns immutable status projection and rendering only; it must not open stores, resolve data paths, or start work. `cyril-core` may carry typed status/events but must not depend on UI or persistence libraries.

Use separate versioned SQLite stores for memory and knowledge, WAL mode, owner-only storage, atomic initialization, and OS-appropriate user data directories. Use an owner-only local socket on Unix and a user-only named pipe on Windows, plus an ephemeral runtime credential. Missing and corrupt configuration/store states are distinct typed failures. Do not add job tables or queue interfaces, retrieval, embeddings, MCP registration, transcript capture, or prompt injection in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Memory is opt-in and disabled startup leaves current ACP/TUI behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Enabling memory starts one isolated runtime and initializes separate versioned memory and knowledge stores.
- [ ] `/memory status` and the TUI distinguish disabled, starting, ready, degraded, and failed states with actionable failure detail.
- [ ] Runtime startup failure does not prevent bridge startup, session creation, or ordinary prompting.
- [ ] IPC is user-private and rejects missing or invalid runtime credentials.
- [ ] Store and IPC paths use canonical OS-appropriate user data locations rather than process cwd.
- [ ] Cyril performs bounded graceful runtime shutdown without hanging terminal restoration.
- [ ] Restarting Cyril reopens the existing stores without destructive reinitialization.
- [ ] M0 introduces no speculative durable-job schema or queue interface.
- [ ] Behavioral tests run against temporary data roots and a real runtime process without reading the operator's home.
- [ ] UI tests exercise status projection/rendering without opening SQLite or starting the runtime.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
design:
## Runtime foundation contract

### Launch and ownership

When memory is enabled, the Cyril orchestrator launches one dedicated memory-runtime child using an absolute installed executable path. It passes the resolved data root, private IPC endpoint, and a freshly generated 256-bit runtime-admin credential through the child environment; credentials never appear in argv or persistent config. The runtime acquires an exclusive OS-released lock for the canonical data root before opening either database. A second owner for that root exits with typed `already_running` status. The lock is held for process lifetime and is not represented by a manually deleted stale PID sentinel.

The runtime reaches Ready only after it owns the lock, creates/tightens the data root, opens and migrates both stores, binds the IPC listener, and successfully answers a health handshake. Cyril waits at most 10 seconds for readiness. Timeout, child exit, incompatible protocol, migration failure, or permission failure marks memory Failed and leaves bridge startup unaffected.

Shutdown sends one authenticated shutdown request, allows a two-second grace period for open transactions/connections to close, then reaps the process tree. No production queue exists in M0. The stores must reopen after either graceful exit or forced termination without destructive initialization.

### Data and configuration

Configuration adds a `[memory]` section with `enabled` defaulting to false, optional absolute `data_root`, `startup_timeout_ms` default 10,000, and `request_timeout_ms` default 2,000. Invalid types, non-absolute overrides, inaccessible roots, and roots that cannot be tightened to the current user are configuration errors, not defaults. Default roots follow the platform user-data convention: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/cyril` (or `~/.local/share/cyril`) on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/Cyril` on macOS, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Cyril` on Windows.

The canonical data root contains `memory.sqlite3`, `knowledge.sqlite3`, and the runtime ownership lock. IPC endpoints live under the platform runtime directory rather than the persistent data root. Both databases enable WAL and foreign keys, carry an explicit schema-version row, and are created with owner-only access. M0 migrations create only schema/version metadata needed to prove open/reopen; no speculative memory, knowledge, vector, or job tables.

### IPC contract

IPC uses bounded length-delimited JSON frames over an owner-only Unix socket or user-only Windows named pipe. Every frame is capped at 1 MiB. A request envelope carries protocol version, unique request ID, operation name, payload, and authentication. A response echoes version and request ID and contains either a result or a stable error object with machine code, safe message, and retryable boolean. Unknown operations, malformed frames, oversized frames, missing/invalid authentication, and unsupported versions return typed errors and close only the offending connection.

Protocol version 1 initially exposes only `health` and `shutdown`. `health` returns runtime instance ID, runtime state, protocol version, and both store schema versions; it never returns credentials or paths outside safe display metadata. Runtime-admin authentication uses constant-time comparison and is accepted only by the orchestration connection. The later session capability is a separate restricted credential class and must never grant admin operations.

The TUI receives typed runtime status from the orchestrator; it does not parse IPC envelopes or inspect process/stdout text.

### Presence-aware config loading

Cyril's existing broad config fallback remains compatible for non-memory settings, but memory startup uses a presence-aware load report rather than treating every parse/type failure as an absent table. The load report carries the effective ordinary config plus a memory state and diagnostics:

- Missing config file or a well-formed file without `[memory]`: memory is Absent and therefore disabled by default.
- Well-formed valid `[memory]`: memory is Valid with its validated values.
- Well-formed invalid `[memory]` (wrong type, unknown field, invalid range, non-absolute override): memory is Invalid with field-level diagnostics. No runtime starts.
- Entire TOML malformed: existing defaults may still drive non-memory behavior, but memory is ConfigUnparseable, no runtime starts, and startup/TUI surfaces the parse diagnostic. Cyril must not infer that memory was absent.

Validation applies even when `enabled = false`, so a misspelled or malformed memory field is not hidden until the user later enables it. Values are not truthiness-coerced. The compatibility `load_from_path` behavior may remain for existing callers/tests, but main/runtime startup must consume the richer load report. `/memory status` distinguishes Absent/disabled from Invalid and ConfigUnparseable and includes a safe actionable diagnostic.

### Evolving deep client interface

The single external seam is the versioned `MemoryRequest → MemoryResponse` domain protocol implemented by the runtime. Typed Rust clients wrap that seam; bridge, MCP, TUI orchestration, and behavioral tests do not define parallel storage/retrieval interfaces. Domain requests and responses contain no ACP, MCP, ratatui, SQLite, or native-model types. External-library errors are mapped once into stable memory-domain errors at the runtime/client boundary.

Privilege is represented by two client handles over the same protocol, not by caller-supplied scope fields:

- The orchestrator-only admin handle carries the runtime-admin credential. It gains operations incrementally as real consumers land: M0 health/shutdown; M1 prompt preparation, source-event recording, and human inspection; M2 capability lifecycle and approved human mutation; M3 source administration; M4 job administration.
- The MCP adapter uses a scoped handle constructed from the session capability. It can invoke only operations explicitly authorized for that capability: recall in M2, scoped teach/forget/promotion request in the governance slice, and knowledge operations in M3. It has no health/shutdown, capability-admin, arbitrary-scope, raw-query, migration, or job-control operation.

Each slice adds only methods it consumes; M0 must not ship dead future stubs. UI state receives immutable domain view models from the admin client. The bridge receives only optional prepared context or typed capture acknowledgment. Tests exercise the same typed clients against a real temporary runtime; test-only in-memory adapters may implement the domain seam but cannot create a second public contract.

### Local-only backend decision

The first release has one real implementation: Cyril's local memory runtime. `enabled = false` means the feature is not started; it is configuration, not a no-op backend adapter. M0 introduces no `MemoryBackend` trait, backend enum/selector, remote stub, or fake success implementation. Callers depend on the versioned memory-domain protocol and typed clients, not on SQLite/native-model details; that protocol is the replacement seam if another implementation becomes real.

A selectable backend is added only with an approved second production adapter and behavioral-parity contract covering recall, mutation, scoping, deletion, lifecycle, latency/failure, and privacy. That work requires its own design decision because remote authentication, bank ownership, consistency, and upstream clear semantics cannot be guessed by the local implementation. Tests may use an in-memory fake of the domain protocol, but a test fake does not justify a public backend selector.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Memory is opt-in; disabled startup leaves current ACP/TUI behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Cyril launches one isolated runtime by absolute executable path and never exposes the runtime-admin credential through argv or persistent config.
- [ ] Ready is reported only after exclusive data-root lock, owner-only root, both migrations, IPC bind, and authenticated health succeed.
- [ ] A second runtime for the same canonical data root exits with typed already_running status; OS release, not stale-PID deletion, releases ownership.
- [ ] Invalid config/root overrides fail distinctly; platform defaults and schema-version-only M0 stores match the Design contract.
- [ ] IPC v1 uses authenticated length-delimited JSON, 1 MiB frame cap, request correlation, typed safe errors, and only health/shutdown operations.
- [ ] Unsupported version, malformed/oversized frame, unknown operation, and invalid auth cannot crash or authorize the runtime.
- [ ] /memory status and TUI distinguish disabled, starting, ready, degraded, and failed without parsing process text.
- [ ] Startup failure/timeout never prevents bridge startup, valid session creation, or ordinary prompting.
- [ ] Bounded graceful shutdown cannot hang terminal restoration; forced termination still leaves stores reopenable.
- [ ] M0 introduces no memory/knowledge/vector/job tables beyond version metadata and no speculative queue interface.
- [ ] Behavioral tests use temporary roots and real runtime IPC; UI tests remain persistence/process-free; Windows CI covers named-pipe/ACL behavior.
- [ ] Config loading distinguishes missing/absent memory from valid, invalid, and whole-file-unparseable states without changing established fallback behavior for non-memory settings.
- [ ] Wrong types, unknown memory fields, invalid ranges, and non-absolute overrides prevent runtime launch and surface field-level startup/TUI diagnostics even when memory is disabled.
- [ ] A malformed entire TOML file never silently becomes “memory disabled”; memory reports ConfigUnparseable while ordinary fallback behavior remains available.
- [ ] Bridge, MCP, TUI orchestration, and tests use the one versioned memory-domain request/response seam; no parallel public storage/retrieval interface appears.
- [ ] Runtime-admin and scoped clients expose disjoint authorized operations, and each slice adds only operations with a production consumer.
- [ ] Domain requests/responses and errors leak no ACP, MCP, ratatui, SQLite, or native-model types.
- [ ] First release remains disabled-or-local only with no hypothetical backend selector/trait or remote/no-op adapter.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M0. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.

Scope correction: M0 owns no production background job and therefore defines no durable job table or queue contract. Bounded runtime shutdown/reopen remains; durable checkpoint semantics begin with the first real consumer in M3/M4.
AFK-readiness correction: the Design field now pins launch/readiness, data-root/config defaults, single-owner locking, IPC v1 envelopes/auth/errors/frame bound, and shutdown/reopen behavior.
Config contract correction: memory startup consumes a presence-aware validated load report; existing broad fallback remains only for non-memory compatibility.
Mechanism contract: one versioned memory-domain request/response seam, wrapped by privilege-safe admin and scoped clients; operations land only with real consumers.
Divergence decision: first release is disabled-or-local only. No hypothetical backend trait/selector; the versioned domain protocol is the future seam when a second production adapter exists.

Implemented in stacked draft PRs #101 (storage foundation), #102 (runtime protocol/process), and #103 (Cyril status integration). Full-stack rollup CI run 32622783355 passed all 12 jobs on Linux, macOS, and Windows; issue remains in_progress until the stack lands.
