title: clientInfo presentAs escape hatch: opt-in 'kiro-cli' impersonation for the memoryEnabled remote-tools branch
description:
DEFERRED FROM the cyril-0wyn ADR (clientInfo.name decision). If a real user needs KAS memory tools (searchMemories), the honest name cannot reach them: the memoryEnabled gate exists only on the kiro-cli allowlist branch (.cyril-0wyn/oracle-resolveRemoteToolAllowlist.txt), and probes proved there is NO env/config override for client type (.cyril-0wyn/findings.md fact 1). Scope: a config knob (e.g. kas.presentAs='kiro-cli') that swaps clientInfo.name, clearly documented as impersonation with telemetry consequences (reference_kiro_acp_telemetry). BEFORE building: (a) check KIRO_LOAD_ALL_REMOTE_TOOLS=true covers the need (forces allowlist '*', no name change); (b) runtime-probe that memoryEnabled=true + name=kiro-cli actually surfaces searchMemories (schema-accepted != functional); (c) re-check whether upstream recognition (see the upstream-ask issue filed alongside this) landed first. Blocked conceptually on the cyril-0wyn ADR being accepted.

NARROWED 2026-07-19 (cyril-0wyn slice 6): the presentAs knob is IMPLEMENTED on PR #61 (pending merge; "shipped" only after merge) ([agent] present_as = "kiro-cli", ADR-0006) — this issue now covers ONLY the residue: live-verify under an auth-serviceable KAS session that name=kiro-cli + memoryEnable=true actually surfaces search_memories in the resolved remote-tool allowlist (observable: debug log line '[RemoteToolsDiscovery] Allowlist resolved'; probe template .cyril-0wyn/probe-c-memory-tools.py — standalone spawn was INCONCLUSIVE on TokenExpired, both arms; control arm = name=cyril must NOT get it). Settings key pinned: memoryEnable (bundle-carved).

WIRE-SHAPE CORRECTION (review 2026-07-19, finding 10): the AgentSettings capability shape is memoryEnable: {enabled: true} (an object, NOT a bare boolean — docs/kiro-2.13.0-wire-audit.md cap-injection table; cyril's own marshal maps booleans to {enabled:<bool>}, protocol/kas/settings.rs BOOL_MAP docs). probe-c-memory-tools.py has been corrected accordingly; any authenticated rerun must use the object shape or the gate never arms.

title: Host-shell execute check uses access(2) real-uid semantics and fails under root CI
description: SystemHost::is_runnable (host_shell.rs) uses nix::unistd::access(X_OK), which checks the REAL uid/gid, while the test system_host_checks_effective_execute_permission and the Cargo.toml nix-feature comment both claim "effective" access — both are misnamed. Worse: for root, access(X_OK) succeeds when ANY execute bit is set, so the 0o001 fixture (owner-cannot-execute) fails under a root CI container. nix::unistd::eaccess is Linux/FreeBSD-only (nix 0.31), so the portable fix is faccessat(AT_FDCWD, path, X_OK, AtFlags::AT_EACCESS). Minimum fallback: rename test+comment to match access(2) and skip the fixture when geteuid()==0.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #86 (ff70c8771). Repro: unshare -r run of system_host_checks_effective_execute_permission failed pre-fix exactly as predicted; is_runnable now uses faccessat AT_EACCESS (effective uid) with a root-skip guard on the 0o001 fixture. Side-issue cyril-uu8m filed for the same class in host_io.

title: KAS workflow step sessions misroute to the subagent stream — needs a peer-session route + node_start session registry
description:
KAS workflow steps are FULL PEER SESSIONS (buildWorkflowDriverHost ->
host.newSession per step, correlated by _meta.kiro.workflow.workflowId), so a
running workflow produces N concurrent top-level sessions each emitting ordinary
session/update streams.

cyril has no route for them. classify_notification_route (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:1059)
is total over (scope, main, tracked_subagent) and sends every scoped-and-not-main
frame to NotificationRoute::Subagent. Consequence for a workflow run:

  - each step session gets a SubagentUiState stream created optimistically
  - crew_panel renders from SubagentTracker, which is fed by the v2
    kiro.dev/subagent/list_update -- KAS emits NO list_update for workflow steps
  - so the streams exist but are unlistable and undrillable (focus_subagent
    validates a stream, but nothing ever names the session)

Not a crash -- a silent misfile. The step output is captured into a structure the
UI cannot reach, and it is filed under the wrong domain concept.

EVIDENCE
  docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md, sections "Architecture -- workflow steps are
  full sessions, not subagents" and "Live end-to-end verification -- a
  CLIENT-authored DAG executes". The live capture
  experiments/conductor-spike/kas-custom-dag-2.16.0.jsonl shows three distinct
  sessionIds on session/update for a two-step parallel DAG: the parent plus one
  per step.

WHAT IS NEEDED
  1. A workflow-owned session registry, populated from
     _kiro/workflow/node_start.sessionId, keyed by (workflowId, nodePath).
  2. A third NotificationRoute for those sessions, so their frames reach a
     workflow stream instead of the subagent stream.

ORDERING TRAP (live-observed, not hypothetical)
  node_start fires TWICE per step node: once before session creation (no
  sessionId), then re-emitted from executeStep onSessionCreated with sessionId
  populated. In the captured DAG BOTH branches emit their first node_start
  before EITHER receives a session, so start/session pairs do not arrive
  adjacently. A step session/update can therefore arrive before cyril knows the
  id is workflow-owned -- the registry must support LATE CLAIM (the mirror image
  of today optimistic-subagent guess).

  Emission count is also not fixed: on the resume path a paused node already
  holds a sessionId at re-entry, so it rides the FIRST emission and the re-emit
  never happens.

RELATION TO THE RECORDED DESIGN DECISION
  project_cyril_session_level_workflows (2026-05-23) already calls for
  SubagentTracker -> SessionTracker, on the grounds that cyril owns session
  lifecycle rather than observing agent-crew state. Kiro shipping the same
  peer-session model in 2.16.0 corroborates it. This issue is the first concrete
  consumer of that rename, and the place to decide whether to do the rename now
  or add the third route alongside the existing tracker.

NOT cyril-ebqu / cyril-fjfu. Those cover the agent-subtask tool-call channel,
a different mechanism. Workflow steps deliberately do not ride SubagentTracker.
design:
KEEP THE CLASSIFIER TOTAL. classify_notification_route is deliberately a pure
function, total over its inputs, because cyril-tglp was exactly a routing
decision leaking back into the caller. Adding a destination means adding an
INPUT (is this id workflow-owned?), not adding an if-guard at the call site. The
truth table test (classify_notification_route_truth_table) must be extended
across the new input for every existing combination, not just the new rows.

LATE CLAIM, NOT DROP. The Drop arm is reserved for genuinely unattributable
frames (scoped, no main session, nothing has named the id). A step frame that
beats its sessionId-bearing node_start is attributable -- just not yet. Prefer
re-parenting an already-created stream when the claim lands over dropping the
opening frames. Whichever way it goes, the choice needs a fence: the ordering is
live-observed, unlike the cyril-tglp ordering that no shipped engine produces.

DO NOT ROUTE THROUGH SubagentTracker. Vendor-corroborated: KAS emits no
subagent list_update for workflow steps, so the tracker would stay empty and the
crew panel would stay blank no matter how the streams are keyed.

SEQUENCING. The registry cannot be populated until node_start is parsed, so this
lands after (or with) cyril-6beh. The stream/rendering machinery it feeds is
separate again -- this issue is routing and attribution only, not the panel.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Replaying experiments/conductor-spike/kas-custom-dag-2.16.0.jsonl attributes all three sessionIds correctly: parent -> main pipeline, both step sessions -> the workflow route. No step frame reaches SubagentUiState or the crew panel.
2. classify_notification_route_truth_table is extended across the new workflow-owned input for EVERY existing (scope, main, tracked) combination, not only the new rows.
3. Late-claim fence: a session/update whose id is only claimed by a LATER node_start is attributed to the workflow rather than stranded in a subagent stream (or, if the chosen design drops it, the drop is fenced and warn-logged deliberately).
4. Resume-path fence: a node whose sessionId rides the FIRST node_start (no re-emit) is registered just as reliably as the double-emit case.
5. cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass, including with --features kas.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #93 merged to main (3389323). AC1: capture_replay_attributes_every_forwarded_frame replays kas-custom-dag-2.16.0.jsonl through the real KasEngine converters — parent→main, both steps→workflow streams, subagent store empty, tracker untouched. AC2: truth table extended across workflow_owned for every existing combination incl. value-equality row. AC3: late_claim_reparents_optimistic_stream_with_history (re-parent, history intact, focus cleared). AC4: session_owner_resolves_first_emission_resume_claim. AC5: green on default + --features kas, all CI legs. All 9 fences mutation-tested red. Fixed in-branch: 2 pre-PR review findings (stale comment, AC2 gap). Filed: cyril-zd8u (renderer), cyril-kzke (SessionTracker rename). Known-flake encountered: cyril-2rgp (pre-existing).

title: Path translation keyed on cyril's OS, not agent location — native Windows kiro-cli.exe gets WSL paths
description:
platform/path.rs translates paths whenever cfg!(target_os = "windows") (to_native/to_agent, crates/cyril-core/src/platform/path.rs:25-37) — keyed on the OS cyril runs on, not on where the agent lives. The layer assumes a Windows cyril always talks to a WSL-hosted, Linux-path agent.

That assumption no longer matches the default configuration: the default agent command is native (kiro-cli acp, no wsl prefix — see cyril-duz0), and Kiro ships a native Windows kiro-cli.exe whose MSI puts it on PATH. So on Windows today cyril spawns the native exe and then mistranslates every path crossing the boundary: C:\Users\u -> /mnt/c/Users/u is sent to an agent that wants C:\ paths, and inbound agent paths get wrongly converted the other way. Native-Windows agent support (the ROADMAP native-any-OS direction) is blocked on this, and KAS-5 fs/terminal host callbacks make path.rs load-bearing, compounding the cost.

Verified context: the Windows-native kiro-cli.exe is a full build including acp (docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md voice addendum, 2026-08-01).
design: Key translation off the agent's location, not cyril's OS. Suggested default heuristic: translation active only when the spawned AgentCommand routes through WSL (program == "wsl" or "wsl.exe"); native-Windows agent => no-op passthrough exactly like Linux. Consider an explicit override (CLI flag or env, alongside the existing CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO) for exotic wrappers (scripts that invoke wsl internally). AgentCommand is the natural carrier for the decision — resolve once at spawn, thread the mode to the translation layer rather than re-deriving per call. The existing OnceLock distro resolution (cyril-8tq6) stays, gated behind the new agent-location check.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With a native agent command on Windows, to_native/to_agent are no-ops: C:\ paths reach the agent untouched, agent paths come back untouched
- [ ] With an agent command routed through wsl, current translation behavior is preserved (drive mounts unconditional, wsl$ family when distro known — cyril-8tq6 semantics)
- [ ] Linux remains a no-op in all configurations
- [ ] tests/win_wsl_wiring.rs gains a native-agent fence (no rewrite when the agent is native) alongside the existing WSL fences
- [ ] CLAUDE.md path-translation sections describe the agent-location conditionality (coordinates with cyril-duz0)

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #89 merged to main (37939ce). All 5 ACs fenced: native-agent no-op (gate matrix + native_agent_no_rewrite child fence, unset+explicit), WSL behavior preserved (8tq6 corpus run gated-on, drive unconditional, no-distro passthrough), Linux no-op with Wsl adversarially bound, win_wsl_wiring native fence, CLAUDE.md agent-location conditionality (duz0 surfaces untouched). Location binds in run_bridge from the RESOLVED spawn command (KAS-free divergence fenced); CYRIL_AGENT_LOCATION override incl. non-Unicode fallback. Filed: cyril-861q (wrapper version probe), cyril-3br3 (CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO non-Unicode twin).

title: Own modal lifecycle and priority in one module above modal::place (arch review C05)
description:
From the 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review, Candidate 05 (rated Strong). Reconciled against the ADR corpus 2026-08-02: no ADR conflict; the constraints below are binding.

PROBLEM. Four independent modal slots in UiState; render draws all in fixed order, keyboard is first-present-wins, mouse duplicates presence checks. One policy, three implementations — priority drift between the key chain and render order is possible. [INFERENCE flagged in the review: simultaneous slots can paint and receive input inconsistently.]

SOLUTION. One module owns active-modal lifecycle, priority/z-order, keyboard and mouse ownership, and closing behavior. Each modal rendering implementation and the proven modal::place placement module stay beneath the seam. Deletion test: modal::place passes and stays; deleting the distributed priority branches reveals the same policy already repeated in App and render.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS (2026-08-02 reconciliation):
1. The approval overlay stays top-priority unconditionally. It is the human-decision half of the ADR-0004 non-blocking permission mediation; the lifecycle module must never let another modal delay, mask, or reorder a pending permission responder.
2. The CLAUDE.md Key Handling Layers section and the rule that new overlays must be added to both the chain and the mouse-scroll guard describe the convention this module replaces — update CLAUDE.md in the same pass, or it will instruct future agents to maintain a chain that no longer exists.
3. Preserve Esc ordering semantics (drill-in exit before cancelling a busy session).
4. UiState purity is unchanged: no async, no bridge access; the module lives in cyril-ui with App consuming its decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One module answers which modal renders on top and which receives keys/mouse; state, render, and App no longer duplicate presence checks.
2. Approval priority is fenced by a test: approval plus any other modal open means approval wins both input and paint order.
3. Esc-order behaviors preserved under test.
4. CLAUDE.md Key Handling Layers section updated in the same PR.

title: KAS refusal surface: adapter-normalized refusal object is dropped (mirror of v2 cyril-h8zb)
description: tui.js 2.15.0 KAS adapter normalizes refusal from a session update and emits model_refusal with hardcoded stopReason CONTENT_FILTERED (probe site 1, .cyril-h8zb/findings.md on the cyril-h8zb branch). Cyril's KAS path (convert/kas.rs / session_info_update handling) has no refusal parsing — a KAS-side refusal is dropped exactly the way the v2 one was pre-h8zb. Needs: locate the KAS wire shape (read the acp-type-covenant FIRST per reference), then mirror the v2 RefusalAlert rendering. Discovered during cyril-h8zb probes.

title: KAS fs dialect is client-selected: advertise fs._meta.kiro.* for paginated _kiro/fs/read_file
description:
KAS's fs host-callback dialect is CLIENT-SELECTED, and cyril is currently opting
into the weaker one by omission.

resolveCapabilities() (src/platform/resolved-capabilities.ts) gates the Kiro fs
family on capabilities nested under `fs`, NOT under top-level `_meta.kiro`:

    clientCapabilities.fs._meta.kiro.readFile      -> kiroFsReadFile
    clientCapabilities.fs._meta.kiro.writeFile     -> kiroFsWriteFile
    clientCapabilities.fs._meta.kiro.stat          -> kiroFsStat
    clientCapabilities.fs._meta.kiro.readDirectory -> kiroFsReadDirectory
    clientCapabilities.fs._meta.kiro.delete        -> kiroFsDelete

LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-31 (probe-kas-pushed-methods-2.16.0.py, capture
kas-pushed-2.16.0.jsonl): with only `fs.readTextFile/writeTextFile` advertised,
KAS calls the plain ACP `fs/read_text_file`. Advertising the nested set above
switches it to the Kiro dialect and it then calls:

    _kiro/fs/read_file      {sessionId, path, line, limit}
    _kiro/fs/stat           {sessionId, path}
    _kiro/fs/read_directory {sessionId, path}

WHY IT MATTERS: `_kiro/fs/read_file` carries PAGINATION (`line`, `limit` —
observed `{line: 0, limit: 2001}`) that ACP's `fs/read_text_file` has no field
for. A client on the ACP dialect must return whole files; on the Kiro dialect the
agent asks for a window. For large files that is the difference between shipping
a megabyte per read and shipping 2000 lines.

An earlier attempt in probe-kas-rpc-sweep-2.16.0.py advertised
`_meta.kiro.kiroFsReadFile` (top-level, using the RESOLVED field name) and had no
effect — the resolved-capability name is not the wire name. That mistake is why
the sweep concluded the trigger was "unknown".

Scope for cyril: decide whether to advertise the Kiro fs family, and if so
implement the five responders including pagination semantics for read_file and
entry typing for read_directory. Also note `_kiro/fs/delete` exists — advertising
it grants the agent a delete path, so it should be a deliberate choice, not part
of a blanket opt-in.

title: P2 — Usage observer: kiro credits-degraded mode (v2/KAS)
description:
Phase 2 of the usage-observer stage (cyril-4h6i), building on the P1 aggregation/viewer layer. kiro has NO client-side token counts or $cost (backend-gated, proven zero across 6 models — docs/kiro-2.19.1-wire-audit.md), so this mode substitutes CREDITS as the cost currency and fills the rest from what kiro does expose.

AVAILABLE for kiro, map into the same UsageRecord/aggregation: credits (session_info_update kind:turn_completion promptTurnSummaries; _kiro/account/getUsage for plan/overages; sidecar ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/{uuid}.json — reference_kiro_session_sidecar_metering), request/success/error counts, duration, TTFT (QApi.timeToFirstToken via the OTLP redirect OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT — no bundle mod; probe-kas-otel-tokens-2.19.1.py), context-usage % + breakdown (reference_kiro_context_usage_breakdown), tool-call counts, per-folder/model/session grouping, compaction gain (kiro.dev/compaction/status). Engine-agnostic panels (behavior sentiment, tool attribution by call/chars) carry over unchanged.

UNAVAILABLE (render as "n/a (backend-gated)", never a 0 sentinel): token counts, $cost, cacheRate, cacheSavings, tokens/sec. Add a wire watch: if a backend rollout starts populating metadataEvent.tokenUsage (or KAS fills usage_update / the session/prompt usage slot), the token panels light up for free — re-probe trigger noted in the 2.19.0/2.19.1 diffs.

DECISION: whether kiro TTFT/latency depends on the OTLP-redirect stage being present (extra moving part) or whether duration-from-wire suffices — settle in design.
acceptance_criteria: Driving kiro-cli acp (v2 and KAS), the same dashboard renders credits-as-cost + requests/errors/duration/TTFT/context%/tool-counts/per-folder-model grouping; token/$ panels show an explicit backend-gated placeholder (no 0 sentinels). No regression to P1 omp fidelity. If TTFT via OTLP is included, its absence degrades gracefully (duration-only).

notes.content: Data-source finding (2026-08-21, from real ~/.kiro JSONL): TOOL usage is richly captured for kiro, SKILL usage is NOT. Tools: v2 CLI ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/{uuid}.jsonl records per-call {name, toolUseId} (shell/write/read/grep/todo_list); KAS ~/.kiro/sessions/<hash>/<sid>/messages.jsonl records tool_call + tool_result {toolName, args, result} (144+144 in one session) PLUS per-turn usage_summary.promptTurnSummaries[].usedTools[]. So a per-tool panel (calls/errors, and for KAS per-turn usedTools) is fully feasible for kiro. SKILLS: no skill-invocation record anywhere — no skill_call/usedSkills type or field (usage_summary has usedTools but NO usedSkills), the literal "skill" only appears as prose in tool_result/system-prompt/user content, and no skill-named tool. Skills reach the model via steering_inclusion.documents[] (KAS: which docs/AGENTS.md were IN CONTEXT — inclusion, not invocation) or collapse into ordinary tool/prompt activity. Net: tools panel YES for kiro; skills-usage panel NOT feasible for kiro (data does not exist) — and omp has no skill endpoint either, so it is a genuine ecosystem gap, not a cyril limitation. Scope the tools panel, drop any per-skill-usage panel.

Saw omp Tools panel live (screenshot). Attribution mechanism (subtitle: "Tokens/cost are the invoking turns real provider usage, split across each turns tool calls"): omp does NOT measure token/cost per tool — it ATTRIBUTES the turns real provider usage across that turns tool calls. Columns: TOOL / CALLS / ERROR RATE / ATTR.TOKENS / ATTR.COST / RESULT TEXT chars / LAST USED, plus a By-Model breakdown (which models call which tools). REFINES kiro scope: CALLS, ERROR RATE, RESULT TEXT chars, CALL ARGUMENTS chars, LAST USED, By-Model all come straight from tool_call/tool_result records = fully feasible for kiro. ATTR.TOKENS/ATTR.COST need the turns token usage (backend-gated, absent) — BUT kiro HAS per-turn CREDITS (turn_completion.promptTurnSummaries.usage) + usedTools[] + tool_call records, so cyril can attribute CREDITS-per-tool by the same split omp uses for tokens → an "attributed credits" column that is the credits-mode analogue of ATTR.COST. So the kiro Tools panel keeps every column with credits substituted for $, not a degraded stub.

DECISION RESOLVED (OTLP-redirect dependency): DROP it for the usage dashboard. Compared the 125 OTLP metric streams vs KAS messages.jsonl payload types. OTLP adds NOTHING the dashboard needs beyond message/wire records — everything content-shaped (tool calls, credits, context%, success/error, requestIds→retry count, byte sizes, duration) is in the JSONL/wire, and token counts are absent from BOTH (backend-gated). OTLP uniquely carries only AGENT-INTERNAL INSTRUMENTATION: precise TTFT/timeToFirstInference, retry delay, per-graph-node latencies (ModelInvoke/ProcessModelStream/RouteIntent/TurnApproval), fs/network IO latency, steering-scan time+effectiveness, summarization-detection, model-settlement wait, hook latency, policy-load failures. NONE of that is usage/cost/tools data. AND cyril is the LIVE client: it measures TTFT+duration itself (prompt-sent→first agent_message_chunk / →turn_end) — more honest as a user-facing "how fast" metric than the server-internal number. So sources are: (1) live wire + cyril client timestamps = primary; (2) JSONL = historical backfill for unobserved sessions; (3) OTLP = NOT needed here, reserve only for a future agent-APM/perf-diagnostics product (graph-node/IO/steering internals). Removes the extra moving part (spawn env var + collector process).

Implemented on feat/cyril-kryv-usage-modal (PR #99 stack). Review F1-F16 resolved with permanent fences; F17 refuted; F18 remains a credential-limited live-acceptance note. Verified cargo test (1415 passed), cargo test --features kas (1721 passed), default/KAS clippy -D warnings, rustfmt, and live /usage Overview/Costs TUI smoke. Keep in_progress until the stacked PRs merge.

Post-review final evidence: KAS authentication recovered and live acceptance succeeded. A no-tool turn returned OK; /usage refreshed 4→5 turns with providerRequests=1, retries=0, and 0.1698 credits, and Costs showed live plan/quota/overage fields. Only live v2 remains credential-blocked because this host is logged out.
Closed: Shipped in stacked PRs #100, #97, #98, and #99; default/KAS/live v2 acceptance and all CI gates passed.

title: SubagentTracker to SessionTracker rename (generalize session-lifecycle tracking)
description:
Recorded decision project_cyril_session_level_workflows (2026-05-23) calls for renaming SubagentTracker to SessionTracker on the grounds that cyril owns session lifecycle rather than observing agent-crew state; Kiro shipping the peer-session workflow model in 2.16.0 corroborates it. cyril-jxfu — the first concrete consumer — DECIDED to add the workflow route alongside the existing tracker instead of renaming inline, because the rename touches the crew panel, /sessions|/spawn|/kill|/msg command lookups, and CommandContext, and none of that is on the jxfu routing path.

Do the rename when the next consumer of generalized session tracking appears, or fold it into cyril-mys8 (concentrate notification routing behind one App-seam module), which touches the same seams. Scope: rename + move v2-crew-specific fields behind a role; not a behavior change.

notes.content: cyril-jxfu pre-PR review (2026-08-10) queued two more items for this rename: (1) SubagentStream is now also the workflow-step stream type (UiState::workflow_streams() returns SubagentStream values) — glossary says Avoid: subagent for steps, so rename to a neutral SessionStream here; (2) classify_notification_route now takes two positional bools (tracked_subagent, workflow_owned) — fold a self-describing routing-inputs struct/enum into this rename or cyril-mys8.

title: Bridge: engine death and prompt failure are invisible — prompt Err collapses to TurnCompleted(EndTurn); io-task death log-only; fail-stop BridgeDisconnected droppable
description:
Found by the 2026-07-01 KAS implementation review. Engine-agnostic bridge code, but KAS makes it material: the most likely real-world KAS failure (the node process crashing or wedging mid-turn) currently presents as an agent that quietly stopped answering.

(1) The off-loop prompt task maps conn.prompt() Err to StopReason::EndTurn and emits ONLY TurnCompleted — no BridgeError (bridge.rs:563-577). Directly violates CLAUDE.md 'Bridge errors must notify the App — logging alone is invisible.'
(2) The io pump's death is tracing::error! only (bridge.rs:395-399). The acp crate clears pending_responses when io ends (rpc.rs:78), so a mid-turn crash resolves the prompt as Err -> the user sees the turn just end with zero output and zero explanation. The loop stays alive against the dead connection: every subsequent SendPrompt errors fast and again produces a silent instant TurnCompleted — the session looks idle-and-ignoring-me until the user happens to run /new (whose arm DOES emit BridgeDisconnected).
(3) This also swallows the auth responder's actionable errors: auth.rs:160-163 returns 'kiro token expired; run kiro-cli login' TO KAS, not to the App — KAS fails the turn and the user gets silence.
(4) Sub-item: the fail-stop BridgeDisconnected uses try_send (bridge.rs:163-174) and is dropped with only a warn! if the notification channel is full — plausible exactly during a heavy streaming backlog, the moment a crash is most likely. Use a bounded send with timeout or a reserved slot.

NOTE: the turn_in_flight gate itself is safe (the Err arm still synthesizes TurnCompleted, so the gate always clears) — the problem is purely that the failure is mute.
acceptance_criteria: Killing the agent process mid-turn surfaces a visible error to the user (BridgeError and/or BridgeDisconnected) in the same turn; a SendPrompt against a dead connection produces an actionable error message, not a silent TurnCompleted; the fail-stop disconnect signal cannot be dropped by a full channel; auth-stale turn failures reach the user with the actionable login hint.

notes.content:
EVIDENCE (2026-07-04, dcc6 C14b): the collapse is live-confirmed dangerous — the un-hardened KAS smokes green-lit on TurnCompleted alone, which would also pass on an auth-failed turn. Interim mitigation: kas_freepath_smoke + kas_wrapper_smoke now assert an echoed KAS_SMOKE_OK sentinel. The real fix (prompt Err surfacing as its own notification, not TurnCompleted(EndTurn)) remains this issue's scope.

PR-39 REVIEW MITIGATION (2026-07-04): item (3)'s invisibility is now half-addressed — every getAccessToken failure path warn-logs locally (cyril.log breadcrumb) before the JSON-RPC error travels to KAS (get_access_token_from, auth.rs; review finding F1). The App-notification half (surfacing to the UI, plus the general prompt-Err collapse) remains this issue's scope; the responder is a free function with no channel access, so the fix belongs with this issue's bridge rework.

STDERR-TAIL HANDOFF (2026-07-04, cyril-0gke PR #41): AgentProcess now drains stderr and exposes stderr_tail() (last-50-line StderrTail ring buffer); the IO-pump failure log includes the snapshot. Remaining for THIS issue: thread the tail into user-facing BridgeDisconnected reasons — the bridge-exit BridgeDisconnected emission (bridge.rs ~:167) lives OUTSIDE run_bridge, so the tail handle must be passed up to that layer.

Closed: Shipped: PR #45 merged to main (252a620). All 4 sub-items + ACs fenced: (1) prompt Err emits BridgeError before TurnCompleted (prompt_error_emits_bridge_error_before_completion, death_mid_turn_* fences); (2) io-pump watcher — probe found SIGKILL is a CLEAN EOF so the watcher keys on pump END not Err; idle death disconnects+exits, mid-turn death defers disconnect until the turn's terminal marker (BridgeError->TurnCompleted->BridgeDisconnected); (3) KAS auth-callback Err emits BridgeError(auth) with LOGIN_HINT; v2 login hint reaches the user via stderr tail in disconnect reasons (live-verified: logged-out kiro-cli 2.11.0 run 4 shows 'not logged in' in the reason); (4) fail-stop disconnect survives a full channel via 5s-bounded send (mutation-verified fence). Build caught+fixed a real drain-dedup bug (KAS dual completion could reach the App twice). Fixed in-branch: scope-creep commit rebuilt, named C6 fence restored. Filed: cyril-gua0 (respawn/reconnect). Audit trail: .cyril-l7tw/ (probe runs 1-4, design 13 claims, plan 8 slices).

title: Restore readable Cyril Dark semantic-role contrast
description: Review finding #1: the conversation-theme migration replaced terminal-resolved named ANSI colors with dim VGA RGB values, making links and other roles unreadable on dark terminals. Define and enforce a readable fixed-palette contract before theme activation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Cyril Dark conversation roles meet explicit contrast targets on representative dark backgrounds.
- [ ] The decision about fixed RGB versus terminal-palette remapping is documented.
- [ ] Regression tests fail on the current dim VGA values.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped in PR #67 (merge 76aa53d): per-tier contrast contract for Cyril Dark — 5 dim roles brightened, contrast + hue fences added, ADR-0007 recorded.

title: Approval-wait time is charged to the backend — TurnStalled fires falsely on every tool approval
description:
TurnLiveness treats a pending session/request_permission as agent silence, so the quiet clock keeps running while the user reads an approval overlay. Any approval held longer than the 30s threshold emits a spurious TurnStalled chip.

turn_liveness.rs:85 counts only HostMediator::in_flight() as host activity — that table holds fs/terminal callbacks (and is cfg(kas)-gated). A permission request cyril owes the agent an answer to is not in it.

First-party corroboration (KiroCrew, session_handle.py:2060-2067): "the wait a consumer spends on an approval, an IM send, or a hook is charged to the backend — and a turn can be cancelled moments after a human approves it." They bank the human interval into a parked-time accumulator and subtract it from both idle clocks, and treat awaiting_permission as a separate state entirely: "A turn parked here is waiting for a HUMAN, which is not a stall ... otherwise every approval prompt reads as a stalled turn, and two components end up racing to end the same wait on different budgets."

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 2.1.
acceptance_criteria: A pending approval suppresses (or excludes its duration from) the quiet clock; a stall emitted after an approval measures only post-answer silence. Regression test: begin turn, open approval, advance clock past threshold, assert no TurnStalled; answer, advance again, assert one emission.

title: Make crew status responsive
description:
## What to build

Present crew members and pending stages through a responsive display-only table when space permits, then collapse to a one-line status summary when height is constrained. The compact summary must preserve the distinction between a crew member and a pending stage.

## Blocked by

- cyril-dij8
- cyril-a14l
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Standard layouts show deterministic crew rows with responsive name and status columns.
- [ ] Constrained layouts prioritize working, waiting, and completed counts over member names.
- [ ] Pending stages contribute to waiting work but are never labeled as crew members.
- [ ] Overflow and constrained-size tests plus the full workspace quality gate pass.

title: Overview page pinned at MAX_DATA_ROWS: Credits and Monetary cost fall below the fold at 24 rows
description:
REGRESSION from cyril-9kyk (PR #107, merged 370534cc), found by the pre-PR review of cyril-nanu and reproduced.

cyril-9kyk added two latency-tail lines to the /usage Overview page, taking UsagePanelState::row_count() for Overview from 16 to 18 (crates/cyril-ui/src/traits.rs). MAX_DATA_ROWS is also 18 (crates/cyril-ui/src/widgets/usage_panel.rs:7), so Overview now sits exactly at the cap.

The height chain: desired_rows = row_count().clamp(1, MAX_DATA_ROWS) -> 18; popup height = desired + 5 = 23; modal::place clamps that to the region above the input; visible_rows = popup.height - 4. On a 24-row terminal the popup gets 20 rows, so 16 data lines are visible against 18 emitted.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-28 by rendering Overview at three terminal heights and grepping the buffer:

  height  24: row_count=18 Credits=false Monetary=false
  height  30: row_count=18 Credits=true  Monetary=true
  height  40: row_count=18 Credits=true  Monetary=true

So on a 24-row terminal the last two Overview metrics -- Credits and Monetary cost -- require scrolling, where before cyril-9kyk all 16 fit. Those are arguably the two lines an operator opens /usage to see.

Because Overview now sits AT the cap, any further metric line makes this worse rather than growing the modal.

SCOPE: options to weigh -- raise MAX_DATA_ROWS (it bounds every page, so check the others); let the modal grow when the terminal allows and clamp only when it does not; move the latency tails to a page that is not already full; or reorder so the highest-value metrics survive the fold. Whatever is chosen should carry a render fence at 24 rows, since that is the height where this appeared and no existing test rendered Overview there.

NOT in scope for cyril-nanu: its spec explicitly excludes changing what the panel displays beyond the in-flight marker and failure status.

title: Design review: ProcessTree::drop SIGKILLs the leftover process group after EVERY completed wait — intentional background servers never survive
description: Pre-existing semantics surfaced during cyril-ho7o (PR #83): after a command's wait completes, ProcessTree::drop kills the whole leftover process group, so an agent that deliberately starts a background server (sh -c 'server & echo started') has never had it survive the wait cycle. PR #83 moved that kill to ~500ms after command exit (previously at pipe-close) but the kill itself predates it. Decide: is kill-on-wait the intended policy (document it as such in the module doc + covenant notes), or should terminals support surviving daemons (needs a lifecycle design — interacts with cyril-3lh8 reap-on-cancel and ba5x shutdown sweep)?

title: KAS terminal registry: kill/release during pending wait_for_exit are silent no-ops; release-then-wait resurrects the freed id
description:
Found by the 2026-07-01 KAS implementation review (perf/reliability lens) — untracked by any existing terminal issue (distinct from cyril-3lh8 orphan-on-cancel, cyril-ba5x Shutdown orphans, cyril-r3t6 pipe drain).

wait() takes the Child out of the registry (Entry::Running(None)) and awaits wait_with_output(). The acp rpc layer spawns every inbound request as its own concurrent spawn_local task (verified in agent-client-protocol-0.10.2 rpc.rs handle_incoming), so terminal/kill or terminal/release arriving WHILE wait is pending hits take_child -> Taken::InFlight, and both handlers use `if let Taken::Child(..)` — the InFlight case FALLS THROUGH and returns Ok without signaling the process:

- kill (terminal_io.rs:213): returns KillTerminalResponse having killed nothing. The module's own docs say KAS calls wait immediately after create (:16-17) and that kill-then-read-partial-output is KAS's command-timeout pattern (:205-208) — so EVERY kill arrives during a pending wait. Failure: KAS runs a hung command via create+wait; on its timeout it sends kill -> cyril replies Ok, process keeps running; the pending wait never resolves; the turn hangs (or the hung child leaks as a live orphan forever).
- release (terminal_io.rs:188): same fall-through (child not killed), then :200 unconditionally remove()s the id. When the still-pending wait() later completes, :151 insert()s an Exited entry BACK under the released id — violating the released-id -> -32602 contract and leaking the entry + captured output for the life of the bridge.

Root cause is one spot (the InFlight fall-through). A fix needs a kill signal that does not require owning the Child — e.g. retain the pid at create, or store a kill handle before wait takes the Child. The single-request-at-a-time tests never exercise the concurrent case.
acceptance_criteria: kill during a pending wait actually terminates the process and the pending wait resolves with the killed status; release during a pending wait kills the child and the id stays unknown (-32602) after the wait completes (no re-insert); concurrency tests added for kill-during-wait and release-during-wait on a current_thread runtime.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #42 (02718e0). Repro: kill_during_pending_wait_terminates_child + release_during_pending_wait_frees_id (current_thread concurrency fences).

title: KAS auth on Windows host: sqlite store lives inside WSL — free-path discovery+responder need a WSL-aware store path
description: cyril-dcc6 moves the KAS auth source to ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3 (CLI sqlite store) and free-path discovery to ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/kas/<ver>-<sha>/. On Windows, cyril spawns 'wsl kiro-cli acp' and both paths are WSL-internal — a Windows-host cyril cannot read them via native paths (would need \\wsl$ translation via platform/path.rs, and rusqlite over \\wsl$ is untested). dcc6 scopes to Linux/WSL-side execution; this issue tracks the Windows-host story (or an explicit unsupported-with-actionable-error decision).
acceptance_criteria: Windows-host KAS spawn either works (store+bundle resolved through WSL translation) or fails loud with an actionable message; decision recorded in docs.

title: Model picker: surface per-model capability (hasEffort + credit rate) from KAS model options
description: KAS model options (session/new configOptions[model].options[]._meta.kiro) carry structured per-model metadata cyril currently DROPS: hasEffort (bool — does the model support thinking-effort levels), rateMultiplier (numeric credit rate), rateUnit, effortSchemaPath. cyril's convert layer discards _meta and CommandOption only has {label,value,description,group,is_current}; hasEffort is consumed nowhere. Goal: parse hasEffort + rateMultiplier from model options and surface in the model picker — a 'supports effort' badge and a credit-cost hint — so the user sees which models are thinking-capable before selecting, and optionally gate the /effort control on the selected model's hasEffort. ENGINE ASYMMETRY (diffed 2026-07-02): hasEffort is KAS-ONLY on the wire. v2 session/new models.availableModels are bare {modelId,name,description}; v2 encodes the rate as a display string in the picker group ('2.20x credits', == KAS rateMultiplier 2.2) and has NO hasEffort — so on v2, effort-capability must keep being inferred from whether /effort is registered in commands/available (2.4.1). So: KAS-first; v2 gets the credit hint via group only. NOTE: showing the CURRENT effort level is ALREADY implemented (toolbar ◇ {effort} from MetadataUpdated.effort) — this issue is about the model-picker capability display, not the current-level indicator.
acceptance_criteria: Model picker shows an effort-capable badge (from KAS hasEffort) + credit-rate hint; /effort optionally gated on selected-model hasEffort (KAS) / commands/available presence (v2); v2 degrades gracefully (no hasEffort on wire).

title: KAS _kiro/config/template: session-less config-options compose surface for pre-session mode/model pickers (KAS-4)
description: New _kiro/* method in KAS @kiro/agent 0.22.7 (kiro-cli 2.14.0), advertised UNCONDITIONALLY in the initialize handshake extensionMethods (confirmed live in the host-init leg; see docs/kiro-2.14.1-wire-audit.md). Session-LESS 'pre-session compose surface': a client queries the answering agent's own mode/model registries to build config-options BEFORE creating a session. Classified localOnly + transient (never forwarded to a relayed session, never persisted). Relevance to cyril KAS-4 (configOptions track): lets cyril populate /model and mode pickers with NO session in flight, instead of waiting for session/new's config_options (which KAS populates but v2 leaves null). Task: model the _kiro/config/template request/response, and consider using it to pre-warm cyril's mode/model pickers on KAS. Companion to the KAS-4 configOptions work.

title: Measure the unmeasured cyril-6bol success criteria (SC2 poison-after-resolution, C4 one-resolution)
description: Three spec.md measurements were never implemented, leaving the properties guaranteed only structurally: (1) SC2 response/executor agreement — no state-transition test poisons $SHELL/PATH AFTER resolution and asserts shell_type + create still use the startup snapshot (currently guaranteed by the single Rc<HostShell> handed to the registry); (2) C4 exactly-one-resolution-per-startup — no injection/counting test (sole call site is spawn_bridge; FakeHost.probes counts is_runnable calls, not resolutions); (3) minor: create_honors_cwd_missing_dir_errors asserts the spawn error but not counter==0, so spawn-failure id conservation is fenced only on the empty-command path. All three are cheap resolver-injection/registry tests.

title: Usage panel reports Idle while a coalesced follow-up snapshot is still running
description:
Found by the cyril-nanu pre-PR review (finding 4). Filed rather than fixed in that PR because closing it needs an addition to the App/worker protocol, which is a revision to the approved cyril-nanu design.

UiState::refresh_usage_panel sets UsageRefreshStatus::Idle on every landed snapshot. Idle is documented as 'a snapshot is held and nothing is in flight'. But the worker coalesces: N requests during one run produce ONE follow-up, so a result can land while a further recompute is already queued or running.

Concrete window, using the KAS burst cyril-nanu measured (18 refresh triggers in a single turn, .cyril-nanu/evidence.md P1):

  request R1        -> worker runs snapshot A
  R2..R18 arrive    -> queued
  A lands           -> App sets Idle          <-- marker cleared
  worker drains R2..R18, runs snapshot B      <-- ~700 ms in flight
  B lands           -> App sets Idle

For the duration of B the panel shows Idle while displaying values that are already one snapshot behind the log and carrying no marker. That is precisely the silent staleness the status field exists to prevent (cyril-nanu D1: lag is acceptable only because it is stated).

Impact is bounded -- the values are current as of A, and B lands within a snapshot -- which is why this is P3 rather than higher.

SCOPE: the App cannot infer this today, because the worker signals only completion. Options to weigh: have the worker emit a 'started' event before each run so the App can mark Refreshing again (smallest, but adds a variant to what is currently a result-only channel); or carry a request generation counter both ways so a landed result can be compared against the newest request issued; or have the worker report queue depth alongside the result. Whichever is chosen, the fence should drive a burst through the real worker and assert the panel is never Idle while a run is outstanding.

RELATED: cyril-nanu (the change that introduced coalescing and the status field).

title: Make the killpg/process_group(0) coupling structural with a ProcessGroupId newtype
description: ProcessTree::kill (terminal_io.rs) kills the group whose id equals the child pid; that is only a real process group because of the #[cfg(unix)] cmd.process_group(0) call ~140 lines away in create(). Remove that line and killpg gets ESRCH — which the kill path explicitly swallows — so ALL process-tree cleanup silently degrades to a no-op with zero diagnostics (the exact shape CLAUDE.md Silent Failure Prevention targets). Fence: a ProcessGroupId newtype constructible only at the spawn site that actually creates the group, held by ProcessTree instead of a bare pid, so dropping the process_group(0) call becomes a compile error rather than a silent no-op.

title: KAS context bar can overflow the status line on narrow terminals (clips credits + scroll hint)
description:
Introduced by KAS-2b (cyril-5et2, PR #33). render_status_bar (crates/cyril-ui/src/widgets/toolbar.rs:136) appends the 5-label KAS context breakdown bar ('Context Files X%  Session Files Y%  Tools Z%  Prompts P%  Responses R%', ~70 cols) to the same single, non-wrapping Line that already carries 'Context: N%', credits, tokens, stop-reason, and the browse-mode 'SCROLL ↓ PgDn' hint. The Paragraph renders without wrap, so on a narrow terminal (e.g. 80 cols) everything past the right edge is clipped.

REPRO: run a KAS session in an ~80-col terminal; once a context_usage frame with a breakdown arrives, both 'Context: N%' and the 5-label bar render. The breakdown bar is pushed BEFORE credits and the scroll hint, so those later segments fall off-screen — hiding the affordance that tells the user how to leave browse/follow mode.

Pre-existing single-line truncation mechanism, but the wide unconditional bar newly makes it reachable. Graceful (no panic) — purely a layout/UX regression.

FIX is a design choice, not a one-liner: e.g. a compact/responsive form when width is constrained, eliding the redundant scalar when the breakdown is present, abbreviating labels, or measuring remaining width before appending. Out of scope for the KAS-2b bar itself; surfaced by /code-review max on PR #33.

REFS: toolbar.rs:115-156 (render_status_bar); related cyril-5et2 (KAS-2b).

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #47 (c7d0ed5). render_status_bar measures the full line first and omits the KAS breakdown bar when it would clip trailing segments (credits, stop reason, SCROLL hint); the Context scalar always stays. Repro fences: narrow_status_bar_keeps_scroll_hint_over_breakdown (80 cols), wide_status_bar_keeps_breakdown_bar (200 cols). Gemini perf note (double status_bar_spans call) rejected with evidence: ~15 spans at max 20fps is microseconds; drain-variant couples caller to span indices.

title: docs: re-sync kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md to @kiro/agent 0.8.0 (synced at 0.3.224; 0.8.0 renumber + this week's probe findings)
description: The covenant is the authoritative _kiro/* wire contract but was synced at @kiro/agent 0.3.224 and carries its own currency warning (6 methods uncataloged by 0.3.257 incl. safety/sessions/search — e.g. _kiro/sessions/changed, _kiro/hooks/setEnabled from 2.8.1). We now run 0.8.0 (kiro 2.11.0). SCOPE: (1) re-extract the type surface from the 0.8.0 bundle — covenant types are bundled into acp-server.js itself since the versioned-dir extractions (>=2.10.0), path ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/kas/2.11.0-<sha>/node_modules/@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js; (2) catalog the 0.8.0 additions: _kiro/knowledge/indexingStarted, _kiro/knowledge/indexingCompleted, _kiro/sandbox/applyConfig, _session/steer/clear (see reference_kiro_2_11_0_diff / cyril-45ld watch item); (3) backfill the 0.3.257 uncataloged six; (4) fold in the 2026-07-05 probe-verified contract facts: per-turn _meta.kiro.modeId on session/prompt is the ONLY functional mid-session mode/agent switch (set_config_option AND session/set_mode are accepted-but-cosmetic after the first prompt); customAgents register ONLY via _meta.kiro.customAgents on session/new (top-level silently ignored); spec/invoke runAllTasks verified with full param shape {sessionId, featureName, tasksFilePath, specDocuments, makeAllRequired?} -> {sessionId, executionId} + sequential spec-task-execution subagents + tasks.meta.json checkpoint sidecar; spec/resolveSession strategy fresh-vs-reuse semantics; configOption choices are {value,name} keyed by value. Sources: docs/kiro-kas-modes-2.10.0.md addenda, probe-kas-plan-handoff{,2}-2.11.0.py, probe-kas-plan-to-custom-2.11.0.py, probe-kas-runalltasks-2.11.0.py + dumps. Keep the covenant's read-covenant-FIRST role (CLAUDE.md) intact — this is a re-sync, not a restructure. Related: cyril-45ld (0.8.0 new-surface watch), cyril-jd8e (v2 doc counterpart).

title: Wire KAS workspaceTrusted so v2 hooks can be gated rather than trusted wholesale
description:
Follow-up to cyril-gk17. With kas_hooks = "kas" the agent executes .kiro/hooks/*.json shell commands on the host with no session/request_permission (live-verified 2.16.0). cyril-gk17 decided to keep the mode opt-in and surface every execution in the transcript (Notification::HookExecuted), and explicitly NOT to invent a trust prompt cyril has no store to back.

The real mechanism exists upstream: KAS carries a workspaceTrusted flag that feeds disabledReason: "untrusted-workspace" on listed hooks. Wiring it lets cyril distinguish "this workspace is trusted" from "this workspace has hooks I have never seen", and gate accordingly.

Scope: carve where workspaceTrusted is read in @kiro/agent; decide where cyril trust state lives (per-workspace, persisted?); surface disabledReason in the /hooks panel so an untrusted-workspace hook reads differently from a user-disabled one.
acceptance_criteria: cyril can mark a workspace trusted/untrusted; untrusted workspaces do not execute v2 hooks; the /hooks panel distinguishes user-disabled from untrusted-workspace-disabled.

title: Subscribe to _kiro/spec/taskStatusChanged (KAS spec-mode task checkbox updates; TUI consumes it since 2.19.2)
description:
KAS emits the extension notification _kiro/spec/taskStatusChanged {sessionId, tasksFilePath, changes} from SpecTaskStatusTracker whenever it flips a task checkbox ([ ]/[x]/[-]/[~]) in a spec tasks.md. The emitter has existed since at least KAS 0.48.0; kiro-cli 2.19.2 adds the host relay (spec_task_status_changed stream event) and tui.js now consumes it (0 -> 1 hits), so it is a first-class TUI feature. Cyril currently warn-drops it as an unknown ext notification.

Scope: parse it in convert/kas.rs into a typed Notification (session-scoped; changes[] shape to be captured live in spec mode), route via UiState, and render a small task-progress chip / list for spec-mode sessions. Spec mode is now entered ONLY via the mode config option (KAS 0.52.1 removed intent classification), so the trigger is deterministic: set_config_option mode=spec (or quick-spec) then drive a spec to the tasks phase.

Evidence: docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 6; KAS bundle src/spec/session/spec-task-status-tracker (emitTaskStatusChanged).

title: Concentrate notification routing and application behind one App-seam module (arch review C03)
description:
From the 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review, Candidate 03 (rated Strong). Reconciled against the ADR corpus 2026-08-02: no ADR conflict; the constraints below are binding.

PROBLEM. The pure classifier (classify_notification_route) knows only scope + main session. The real routing policy lives in App callers, which add tracker membership, no-main readiness, global ordering, optimistic subagent-stream creation, redraw, and deferred bridge commands. Tests call the projections directly, so the tested seam is smaller than the policy.

SOLUTION. One module owns ownership classification AND application to exactly one destination (main state / subagent stream / global state) plus resulting commands; App delegates; tests exercise the same seam App uses. Deletion test from the review: deleting classify_notification_route removes almost all of it; deleting full routing recreates destination choice and ordering across App callers.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS (2026-08-02 reconciliation):
1. The module lives in the cyril binary crate. cyril-ui must not learn bridge commands; cyril-core cannot import UI. The review file list touches cyril-ui/state.rs — keep those changes presentation-side only.
2. Design the seam engine-aware from day one. The optimistic unknown-session-to-subagent-stream rule is WRONG for KAS peer sessions: workflow steps are peer sessions, not subagents (session-level-workflows decision; 2.16.0 shipped the _kiro/workflow/* emitter). The routing policy needs a peer-vs-subagent axis. Coordinate with cyril-fjfu (KAS-3 rendering), which lands work on the same ground.
3. Key behavior off the bound engine, never cfg(feature = kas) — ADR-0002 discipline; see the identity.rs trap note and the uninhabited-enum pattern in the ADR-0004 amendment.
4. Update the CLAUDE.md App-role section in the same pass: App stays the thin orchestrator; routing becomes a component per the existing rule that logic that can live in a component must not live in App. Preserve ADR-0004 converted-notification mediation: the module consumes internal Notification types, never acp types.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One module owns classification + application; the App notification arm delegates to it.
2. Routing tests exercise the module seam (real ordering, optimistic creation, deferred commands), not direct projections.
3. No cyril-ui-to-bridge knowledge introduced; no acp:: types cross into the module.
4. The peer-session-vs-subagent routing axis is representable in the seam, even if KAS peers initially route to a stub.
5. CLAUDE.md App section updated in the same PR.

title: KAS hooks host: execute agent-type hook actions (v1 skips with warn; runCommand only)
description: DEFERRED FROM cyril-jiyn v1. kasHookFileSchema action types: command (v1: executed) and agent (append a prompt to model context — v1: skipped with a warn). Executing agent-type in HOST mode needs a wire path for prompt injection from the hooks provider (covenant AcpContextualHook shape is runCommand-oriented); investigate whether list can return them or whether steering/_message-send is the vehicle.

notes.content: 2026-07-23 (cyril-tpfd carve): the open investigation is ANSWERED for SessionStart — precomputed results ARE the wire path for agent-type hooks there. KAS's own v2 provider packages SessionStart askAgent hooks as {originalType:'askAgent', content:<the appendix/prompt text>} elements in the _kiro/hooks/sessionStart reply; no execution needed, the text injects as HOOK_INSTRUCTION context. cyril's packager already emits the carved shape (hooks.rs package_session_start_results) — supporting askAgent for SessionStart = load agent-type actions into the registry + push content verbatim with originalType 'askAgent'. Other triggers still need the injection-vehicle investigation.

title: M1: Capture a completed turn and recall it next session
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Capture one authoritative completed ACP turn and make it useful in a later session. Cyril observes the original outbound prompt and normalized inbound assistant and tool lifecycle before UI projection, assembles them under the bridge's session and turn identities, durably commits the completed turn, and exposes it for inspection. A fresh session in the same project uses FTS5 to select a relevant prior episode for its first-prompt memory block.

The demo is end to end: discuss a distinctive project decision, complete the turn, start another session in the same project, ask about that decision, and receive the relevant prior episode with provenance. UI truncation, streaming presentation, and turn-mediator companion absorption cannot alter the durable record. An interrupted or incomplete turn remains distinguishable and is not represented as successfully completed.

## Placement / boundaries

ADR-0003 defines two separate interim bridge adapters. Injection remains at the prompt seam from the preceding slice. Durable capture is a pre-UI bridge observer over original outbound commands and normalized inbound turn/tool lifecycle. The observer emits typed memory events and owns no SQLite, ranking, or UI behavior. The memory runtime owns stream assembly, completeness state, durable turn storage, FTS5 indexing, retrieval, provenance formatting, and restart behavior. The UI owns an inspection projection only.

The existing single-consumer notification channel must not be misused as an observer subscription. Add deliberate fan-out at authoritative ingress or mediation so recording cannot depend on bounded `UiState`. Preserve session and turn identifiers. Record original prompt blocks, not the enriched wire request. Do not add LLM consolidation, semantic fact extraction, MCP tools, embeddings, or automatic scope promotion in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Original outbound prompts and normalized inbound assistant/tool lifecycle are observed before UI projection.
- [ ] One completed turn is durably assembled with session, turn, project, provenance, and completion state.
- [ ] The injected memory block is excluded from durable source content.
- [ ] Streaming chunks and tool updates produce one coherent completed-turn record without display artifacts.
- [ ] Interrupted, failed, and incomplete turns remain distinguishable and are never marked successfully completed.
- [ ] Restarting Cyril preserves committed turns and does not duplicate them.
- [ ] A later session in the same project can retrieve a relevant prior episode through FTS5 and receive it in the first-prompt memory block.
- [ ] A different project cannot retrieve the episode.
- [ ] `/memory` can inspect the stored turn and its provenance independently of UI transcript retention.
- [ ] Bridge behavioral tests prove capture around turn mediation, UI truncation independence, exact-once commit, scoped recall, and original-versus-enriched separation.

## Blocked by

- cyril-ezgo
design:
## Mechanism contract established by this slice

The bridge observer emits typed source events keyed by `(session ID, turn ID)`: original prompt accepted, normalized assistant text chunk, normalized tool start/update/result, and terminal disposition. The runtime owns an in-memory turn assembler and commits one immutable source-turn record under a uniqueness constraint on that key. The record contains canonical project ID, original prompt blocks, assembled assistant text, bounded/redacted tool lifecycle, start/end timestamps, terminal disposition, and a source-content hash. Only the bridge's authoritative terminal disposition marks a turn completed; interrupted, failed, abandoned, and incomplete states remain queryable but are excluded from automatic episodic recall.

FTS5 indexes completed source-turn prompt text, assistant text, and tool names/results. Retrieval first filters active completed rows to the bound project, then applies literal-token FTS ranking, then uses completion recency and stable memory ID as deterministic tie-breakers. The query is the original user's first text block, not attached-file blocks or injected memory. This slice returns at most three episodes, at most 1,200 characters per episode and 3,600 characters total, truncating on UTF-8 boundaries.

Episodes render in a separate `CYRIL_EPISODES` section labeled derived data, each with source session/turn and timestamp provenance. They follow the lesson section and cannot override it. The runtime's prompt-preparation operation composes both sections under independent budgets; the bridge still receives one optional context result and owns no ranking logic.

Exact-once restart behavior comes from the `(session ID, turn ID)` uniqueness constraint plus content hash. Replayed session history may confirm an identical record but cannot append a duplicate. A conflicting replay is surfaced as a typed integrity failure and audit event rather than silently replacing the committed turn.

### No independent working-memory tier

Cyril does not create a queryable or prompt-injected working-memory/scratchpad tier in this release. The ACP agent's native session history is the active conversational context. Bridge/runtime turn assembly is capture infrastructure, not memory: partial source events may be durably staged for crash recovery and audit, but incomplete turns are excluded from recall, prompt preparation, fact conflict resolution, and consolidation until an authoritative terminal disposition makes them eligible.

Consequently this slice adds no working-memory table, scratchpad tool, automatic goal/unresolved-question extractor, TTL/eviction policy, or working-memory prompt section. Cross-session memory begins with explicit lessons/facts and completed source turns. A future working tier requires evidence that vendor history/compaction loses task continuity and a separate design decision; it must not be introduced as an implementation convenience.

### Interim bridge adapters and proxy cutover

The prompt injector and pre-UI capture observer are intentionally bridge-local interim adapters under ADR-0003. They are not generalized into a proxy framework in this epic. Their tests form an adapter-neutral behavioral contract. When the proxy stack is activated, the proxy implementation must produce identical original-prompt preservation, exactly-once first-prompt context bytes and budgets, trusted session/project identity, normalized assistant/tool lifecycle and terminal dispositions, and memory-unavailable fail-open behavior.

During cutover, bridge and proxy implementations may run together only in a verification mode where one is non-writing; production must have exactly one injection owner and one capture owner. The bridge adapters are removed in the same cutover after equivalence passes, so no permanent alias, dual-write path, or duplicated context remains. Until then, clients outside Cyril's bridge receive explicit MCP memory only, not automatic capture/injection.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Observe original outbound prompts and normalized inbound assistant/tool lifecycle before UI projection.
- [ ] Durably assemble one completed turn with session, turn, project, provenance, and completion state.
- [ ] Exclude injected context from source content.
- [ ] Coalesce streaming and tool updates into one coherent record.
- [ ] Preserve interrupted/failed/incomplete states without false completion.
- [ ] Restart without lost or duplicate completed turns.
- [ ] Recall a relevant prior episode through FTS5 in a later same-project first prompt.
- [ ] Prevent cross-project retrieval.
- [ ] Inspect the turn independently of UI retention.
- [ ] Bridge tests prove mediation-safe capture, exact-once commit, scope, and prompt separation.
- [ ] No working-memory/scratchpad table, tool, extractor, TTL, or prompt section is introduced; incomplete source-turn staging is excluded from recall/context/consolidation.
- [ ] The future proxy adapter must pass byte/budget, identity, lifecycle, terminal, fail-open, and no-double-capture equivalence before both bridge adapters are removed.

title: KAS terminal drain: setsid escapee pins a blocking-pool thread until it closes the pipe
description: Residual bound documented during cyril-ho7o (PR #83): the wait reply is now bounded by the 500ms post-exit grace, and ProcessTree::drop's group SIGKILL closes ordinary stragglers' fds — but a daemon that calls setsid() survives the group kill and the abandoned blocking-pool drain thread lingers until that process closes the shared pipe. Functional impact: none on replies; one blocking-pool thread pinned per such terminal. Full fix needs an O_NONBLOCK/AsyncFd drain redesign.

title: snapshot() recomputes every rollup on each context sample — always-on cost on the usage-panel refresh path
description:
MEASURED while building cyril-9kyk. UsageLog::snapshot() rebuilds the ENTIRE snapshot — overview, provider/model/folder/agent_type rollups, cost and charge totals, tools, context, recent, errors — and it runs on an always-on path.

refresh_usage_panel_from_log() (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:936) fires on:
  - every usage-record append   (app.rs:1016, per turn end)
  - every context sample        (app.rs:1041, MULTIPLE TIMES DURING a turn)
  - every sidecar enrichment    (app.rs:968)
each guarded only by has_usage_panel(). So while the usage panel is open, ordinary operation re-runs the whole rollup repeatedly within a single turn.

Measured at 100,000 rows / 13 groups (test profile, in-memory):
  baseline snapshot()  ~342 ms   <-- PRE-EXISTING, before any cyril-9kyk change
  with p90/max added    942 ms

The pre-existing 342 ms already exceeds the 250 ms budget cyril-9kyk originally pinned, so this is not caused by the percentile work — that work made an existing problem more visible and was re-budgeted around it (spec.md revised to 700 ms; user decision 2026-08-28).

SCOPE: stop recomputing everything per refresh. Options to weigh: debounce the refresh (coalesce bursts of context samples), cache the snapshot and invalidate on append only, split the panel's cheap fields from the expensive rollups so a context tick refreshes only what changed, or compute rollups off the UI path. Whatever is chosen must keep the panel's displayed numbers honest — a stale cache that silently lags a completed turn is worse than a slow refresh.

RELATED: cyril-b163 (usage_turns has no retention, so row count grows without bound and this cost grows with it). Fixing retention shrinks this but does not fix the recompute-per-sample shape.

RE-FLAGGED by the cyril-9kyk code review (xhigh, 2026-08-28) as the top finding
on PR #107: "snapshot() runs synchronously on the App event loop, so the TUI
freezes for roughly a second per context sample while the usage panel is open."
Kept here rather than fixed in that PR — the 2026-08-28 operator decision was
"Raise budget + ticket the refresh", and the fix is an architectural change to
how the App owns UsageLog (a read-only second connection plus spawn_blocking,
delivering through the event loop), not a query tweak.

What the review DID change, so the numbers above are now stale:
  - MAX(duration_ms)/MAX(ttft_ms) moved off the ranked subquery onto
    SUMMARY_COLUMNS, where they are free.
  - added latency cost: 600 ms -> 565/573/568/601 ms across four runs
    (100k rows, 20 groups, test profile, in-memory).
Two attempts to do better were built and rejected BY MEASUREMENT: merging both
metrics into one scan ran 70% SLOWER (756 ms vs 441 ms), and a ROW_NUMBER
formulation 58% slower again. prepare_cached would save 0.028 ms of ~570 ms.
The cost is the per-partition sort, so the only remaining lever is this issue:
stop running it on the event loop, or stop running it per sample.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #108 merged to main (3692e953). No event-loop path computes a snapshot: a dedicated reader thread does, results arrive through the select! loop, and requests coalesce so a burst of N yields one follow-up. Fences: usage_refresh_does_not_block_the_event_loop, snapshot_worker_coalesces_a_burst_to_one_followup (0->1, 1->2, 10->2), snapshot_is_atomic_under_concurrent_append, snapshot_worker_reader_takes_no_write_lock, reader_refuses_to_open_a_log_that_is_not_in_wal_mode, refresh_marker_matches_panel_state, failed_refresh_keeps_values_and_states_the_failure, an_unread_log_never_renders_as_an_empty_one, snapshot_result_applies_only_while_a_panel_is_open, snapshot_worker_unavailable_surfaces_as_failure_status; both scale fences unregressed (589ms/700ms, 680ms/2s). Evidence in .cyril-nanu/: v2 fires 1 context sample per turn, KAS up to 17 (18 triggers) -- coalescing is load-bearing, not insurance. Fixed in-branch from the pre-PR review: non-WAL reader guard (would have cost turns their usage rows on DrvFs/SMB), unread-log-renders-as-empty conflation, failed-first-read same conflation, and caching a snapshot that lands after the panel closes. Out of scope by operator decision: snapshot() cost itself (cyril-b163 covers row growth).

title: KAS — Marshal kiro-cli settings into the _meta.kiro.settings (AgentSettings) handshake
description:
On KAS (v3), per-session feature flags ride the wire as AgentSettings in the initialize handshake: clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.settings (KiroClientMeta; covenant docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md section 3, lines 98-104). cyril sends only {cwd, mcpServers} with NO _meta.kiro.settings, so on KAS EVERY feature flag is off: toolSearch (MCP token savings), thinking, knowledge, codeIntelligence, subagentOrchestration, compaction, todoList, checkpoint, semanticReview, fta, tangentMode, disableAutoCompaction, and the _c2s/_subagent/_delegate/_providerPowers/_parallelTasks/etc. family. KAS thus runs in a degraded all-flags-off mode.

The v2 TUI assembles this object from the kiro-cli settings file (function zme() in tui.js) and hands it to the ACP client constructor. cyril has no equivalent and no AgentSettings type (called out as a gap in covenant section 10).

CONTRAST WITH v2 (why this is KAS-only): the v2 Rust backend reads toolSearch (and other settings) DIRECTLY from the kiro-cli settings file across the ACP boundary — free for cyril, same pattern as trust-persistence. KAS is a separate Node process that cannot read the Rust settings store, so the client must marshal settings over the wire. See memory reference_kiro_tool_search_setting.

SCOPE: read kiro-cli settings (global + workspace) and build _meta.kiro.settings matching the AgentSettings shape, sent in the KAS initialize handshake. Default-sensitive flags (covenant section 3): semanticReview default ON if absent; fta default OFF; subagentOrchestration true -> orchestrate_subagent tool, false/absent -> invoke_sub_agent (CHANGES the subagent tool — directly affects KAS-3 rendering); toolSearch: {enabled, minPct, minTokens, neverDefer}; knowledge/compaction nested objects.

WHY IT MATTERS: gates MCP token savings via toolSearch (governs the tools-bucket size in cyril-5et2's context bar), thinking, and subagent-engine selection (KAS-3). Foundational enabler shared by multiple downstream KAS milestones.

DEPENDS ON: KAS-1 auth responder (KAS sessions must actually run first; not yet filed as its own issue) and the KAS-0 engine gate (cyril-atjw). This is the SETTINGS half of the same initialize._meta.kiro handshake whose AUTH half is KAS-1.

ROADMAP NOTE: the ROADMAP currently spells out only the auth half of the KAS-1 handshake; AgentSettings appears only piecemeal (subagentOrchestration at docs/ROADMAP.md:209). Recommend making AgentSettings explicit under KAS-1 (doc edit, separate from this ticket).

REFS: covenant docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md section 3; memory reference_kiro_tool_search_setting; v2 TUI zme().
acceptance_criteria:
* On the KAS engine, cyril sends clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.settings in initialize, populated from kiro-cli settings (global + workspace) and matching the AgentSettings shape.
* toolSearch.{enabled,minPct,minTokens} is forwarded and observably takes effect on KAS (tool_search advertised, MCP tools deferred out of the loaded set).
* Default-sensitive flags handled correctly: semanticReview default-ON-if-absent, fta default-OFF, subagentOrchestration selects orchestrate_subagent vs invoke_sub_agent.
* A new AgentSettings type in cyril-core with serde camelCase, unit-tested for wire shape + the default-sensitive flags.
* v1/v2 engine path is unchanged (no _meta.kiro.settings sent or required there).

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #37 (settings handshake, merged 2026-07-01) + PR #38 ($KIRO_HOME + zme knowledge block, code-review follow-up). A/B probe f08ba87 confirms KAS honors _meta.kiro.settings via the subagentOrchestration oracle (orchestrate_subagent vs invoke_sub_agent). CAVEAT: the toolSearch AC (tool_search advertised + MCP tools deferred) was NOT the probed flag, and tool_search availability has a backend axis (2.13.0 finding) — if toolSearch misbehaves on KAS, probe that flag specifically before reopening. Workspace-overlay slice split to cyril-sa39.

title: KAS-8 — MCP management subsystem under KAS (_kiro/mcp/*)
description:
KAS-8 functional gap. `_kiro/mcp/*` — the MCP-management subsystem under KAS. v2 exposes MCP via the `/mcp` slash command; KAS exposes it as this `_kiro/*` dialect, which cyril has no handling for.

Surface (covenant):
- Notifications (agent->client): `_kiro/mcp/status`, `_kiro/mcp/governance_disabled`.

- Host callback (agent->client request, gated by advertising): `_kiro/mcp/elicitation {sessionId, toolCallId, elicitation}` -> ElicitationResolveResponse.

SCOPE:
- Consume `_kiro/mcp/status` / `governance_disabled` for an MCP panel (server list + state), the KAS analog of v2 `/mcp`.
- Wire `resetServer` (incl. the OAuth-reset flow — relevant to the 2.8.1 MCP-OAuth clipboard fix) and optionally getPrompt/getResource.
- Decide whether to advertise `mcp/elicitation` (pairs with the userInput / richer-question overlay from CN1).

CAVEAT: this user runs 0 MCP servers, so live capture needs an MCP server configured first.

title: KAS session-listing: model _kiro/session/list response-shape change (source/executionTarget/status/warnings)
description:
KAS 0.17.2 (kiro-cli 2.12.3) changed _kiro/session/list on the wire. cyril does NOT consume session/list today (v2 has empty sessionCapabilities; KAS session-listing is future KAS work) — this is a MODELING task for when cyril adds KAS session management, not an urgent parser fix.

REQUEST (additive, gated — safe): dispatch fields ride on _meta.kiro, all optional-with-defaults: sessionSource ('local'|'remote'|'all', default local), listScope ('workspace'|'user', default workspace), executionTarget ({kind:'local'|'cloud-sandbox'}). Non-default listScope/remote source -> InvalidParamsError unless the agent is remoteConfigured (KIRO_REMOTE_SESSIONS_ENDPOINT set). A client sending nothing gets exactly the old behavior.

RESPONSE (CHANGED shape): 2.12.1 returned bare summaries (listSessions({})). 2.12.3 returns { sessions: [ { sessionId, cwd, title, updatedAt, _meta: { kiro: { agentMode, createdAt, source:'local'|'remote', executionTarget:{kind}, status (active-aware, default 'idle'), parentSessionId?, description? } } } ], _meta?: { kiro: { warnings } } }. buildSessionInfoRow folds source+executionTarget+status per entry; top-level _meta.kiro.warnings aggregates partial-failure notices (e.g. remote-list timeout under Promise.allSettled).

When cyril models KAS session-listing, cover: source tag, executionTarget placement (local vs relayed cloud-sandbox), active-aware status, parent linkage, and the warnings channel. Ref: docs/kiro-2.12.3-wire-audit.md; per feedback_model_full_wire_surface, model all fields or explicit-ignore + debug-log unknowns. Sibling of cyril-tikf (handshake caps that gate this).
