title: cyril-a71q follow-up: bridge-level fences the spec named but the build substituted
description:
Pre-PR review of cyril-a71q (2026-07-26) found four places where the SIGNED spec named a bridge-level fence and the build substituted a narrower one. None is a live defect — the behaviour is correct and fenced — but each is a commitment in .cyril-a71q/spec.md that the merged branch does not meet.

1. C8 has no bridge-level fence. spec.md:225 asks for "the next request starts 0 turns/futures; exactly 1 visible fail-closed signal — via dependency-injected counter state". `run_loop` hardcodes `TurnAllocator::new()`; there is no injection seam, so the "turn identity space exhausted" BridgeError arm is unexercised. Slice 1 fences fail-closed at the unit level (turn_owner_exhaustion_fails_closed) but never through the loop.

2. C9 does not run through the mediator. spec.md:229 asks for "257/257 notifications accounted for ... with release and companion absorption applied in mediator receipt order after resume". The shipped fence (owned_terminal_survives_256_backlog) uses a raw channel pair, asserts the 257th try_send FAILS, and never delivers it or drives run_loop.

3. The <=2 live-future bound is unenforced. spec.md:284 constrains "At most 2 (active + companion-pending)". `prompt_tasks` prunes finished handles and merely logs when the count exceeds 2; there is no `active_prompt_futures_bounded` fence.

4. Three design-named fences do not exist under their names: `terminal_scope_owner_matrix` (design C3 specifies a 9-cell scope x ownership matrix; the branch fences one cell), `only_owned_completion_mutates_main` with a public-state delta table in cyril/tests/event_routing.rs (C7 is fenced instead by a routing truth table in app.rs), and `rate_limited_turn_releases_via_response` (substituted by an agent_message_chunk observation, documented at the fixture).

Filed rather than fixed in-branch because the PR is already large and none of these changes behaviour. Each is a fence, so the work is test-only apart from item 1's injection seam.
acceptance_criteria:
1. run_loop takes an injectable turn allocator; a fence drives it to exhaustion and asserts one BridgeError plus zero started turns.
2. A 257-notification backlog is driven THROUGH run_loop, asserting release and companion absorption in receipt order.
3. active_prompt_futures_bounded asserts the <=2 bound rather than logging it.
4. terminal_scope_owner_matrix covers all 9 scope x ownership cells.

title: Optimistic steer chip can stick >0 when a turn-tail steer never drains (no next turn / non-EndTurn / backend drop)
description: cyril-7z7u removed the unconditional TurnCompleted reset of UiState.steering_queued so a steer DEFERRED by the backend to the next turn keeps its chip across turn-end (correct per probe). Residual: the optimistic chip now drains ONLY via SteeringConsumed/Cleared/Unsupported/SessionCreated. If a steer is queued at a turn's tail and NO draining event ever arrives, the chip shows a phantom count until /new. Reachable paths: (a) user steers as the turn ends, then sends no further prompt (no next turn -> no deferred SteeringConsumed); (b) turn ends non-EndTurn / cancelled / errored with the steer un-consumed; (c) backend accepts the steer (Ok queued:true, bridge emits nothing) but never streams a consume. The old code masked all of these by resetting every turn-end. Decide a BOUNDED safety net that does not regress the deferred-steer case (e.g. reset on Activity::Idle rather than Ready, or on the 2nd consecutive TurnCompleted with no intervening SteeringConsumed) — needs the .cyril-7z7u probe to confirm whether consume is guaranteed-eventual. Found by /code-review of PR 28 (finding #1). state.rs:418 TurnCompleted arm.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) The Activity::Idle option is a near-no-op — Idle is set only at startup and on BridgeDisconnected (state.rs:475 / app.rs:166); TurnCompleted sets Ready (state.rs:462), so an Idle-keyed reset never drains the chip during a live session. Rule it out.
(2) Prefer the 2-consecutive-TurnCompleted-without-SteeringConsumed rule: heuristic but CONTRACT-BACKED by the .cyril-7z7u probe (a tail steer's queued+consumed pair defers to exactly the next turn, so two turn-ends without a consume means the steer is provably gone) — still gated on the probe confirming consume-is-guaranteed-eventual, as the issue says.
(3) Path (a) is TRUTHFUL, not phantom: per the probe the steer really is still queued backend-side through an idle tail and will consume when a next turn starts. A chip persisting through an idle tail is correct — scope the safety net to (b)/(c), leave (a) alone.
(4) NEW path (d): BridgeDisconnected (state.rs:465-476) clears context/tokens/activity but NOT steering_queued — a dead bridge leaves the phantom chip too. Make disconnect an explicit drain point of whatever net is chosen.

CALCULUS CHANGE (cyril-vgcm, 2026-07-14): the steering echo pipeline is live again on both engines — queued/consumed/cleared reconcile chips id-scoped now, so the phantom-chip window shrinks to genuine backend drops / no-next-turn cases. Cleared is NO LONGER a full drain point when ids are present (id-scoped, one chip per named id; empty ids = drain-all preserved). Re-evaluate this issue's bounded safety net against the new reconciliation before building it.

Closed: Fixed: PR #66 merged to main (23b1814). Phantom optimistic steer chip drained via a private turns_since_steer_activity counter: reset steering_queued on the 2nd consecutive TurnCompleted with no intervening SteeringConsumed (paths b/c), plus BridgeDisconnected as an explicit drain point (path d); counter reset on SteeringConsumed/Cleared/Unsupported/SessionCreated. Path (a) idle-tail preserved (single turn-end never drains). Queued echoes finalized to Cleared on drain to keep the cyril-7z7u oracle (steering_queued == #Queued echoes). Repro/fence (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs): steer_chip_drains_after_two_turns_without_consume, steer_chip_drains_after_cancelled_turn_without_consume, steer_chip_drains_on_disconnect, steer_chip_survives_single_idle_tail, steer_chip_consume_resets_drain_counter.

title: M4: Consolidate completed turns into scoped durable memory
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Turn durable completed transcripts into compact scoped memory through a restart-safe background job. After a deterministic idle/threshold trigger or explicit enqueue, Cyril claims unconsolidated completed turns, sends only the bounded source material to a dedicated tool-free ACP worker, validates strict structured output, redacts it, and writes semantic facts and episodic summaries under the originating session/project trust and scope. `/memory` shows queued/running/completed/failed jobs and the resulting memories; subsequent recall uses them.

The demo proves durability and policy: complete a turn containing a project decision and a correction, enqueue consolidation, observe the job and extracted project memory, restart during work and see it resume exactly once, then recall the result in a later same-project session. A malformed or unavailable worker leaves the source turn durable and retryable without writing partial or globally widened memory.

## Placement / boundaries

The memory runtime owns consolidation eligibility, leases, checkpoints, retries, source offsets, structured-output validation, redaction, deduplication, trust, scope, conflict handling, and atomic finalization. A dedicated ACP worker adapter owns agent startup and one request/response contract; it has no side-effect tools and never reuses the active user session. The TUI owns enqueue/cancel/retry actions and job/result projection only. The bridge observer remains responsible only for durable source turns.

Persist the source turn before enqueueing any model work. Jobs are idempotent and restart-safe; only successful atomic finalization advances the source marker. Model output is untrusted and cannot set its own authoritative source, scope, trust, or timestamps. Automatic extraction remains in the narrowest originating scope; confidence affects retention/ranking/conflict only. Explicit lessons already stored through teaching are not re-extracted as new model-authored lessons. Do not add embeddings, graph extraction, remote memory, or active-session consolidation turns here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deterministic trigger and explicit TUI action enqueue only unconsolidated completed turns.
- [ ] Source turns are durable before worker dispatch and remain retryable after worker/runtime failure.
- [ ] Consolidation uses a dedicated tool-free ACP worker, never the active user session.
- [ ] Input is bounded and output must satisfy a strict versioned structured contract before any write.
- [ ] Model output is redacted, provenance-labeled, and forced into the originating narrow scope regardless of reported confidence/scope.
- [ ] Semantic facts and episodic summaries finalize atomically with source progress and audit events.
- [ ] Restart during queued/running work resumes exactly once without duplicate memories or skipped turns.
- [ ] Malformed output, timeout, cancellation, and unavailable worker produce distinct retryable job states and no partial memory.
- [ ] `/memory` displays job progress/failure and resulting scoped memory; later recall uses successful output.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover correction/conflict, idempotence, restart, malformed output, timeout, cancellation, non-widening, and explicit-lesson non-duplication.

## Blocked by

- cyril-n3j7
- cyril-s7gn
design:
## Mechanism contract established by this slice

A consolidation job is identified by a deterministic fingerprint of its ordered source-turn IDs and consolidation-contract version. Its durable state is queued, leased/running, retryable-failed, completed, or cancelled, with attempt count, lease expiry, source IDs, last error, timestamps, and output fingerprint. The completed fingerprint is unique. A crashed lease returns to queued after expiry. Only one transaction may write derived memory, advance every source turn's consolidated marker, append audit events, and mark the job completed.

The dedicated ACP worker receives a bounded transcript envelope and a versioned strict output contract with exactly two result collections:

- Semantic facts: validated key, bounded JSON value, confidence, and one or more evidence turn IDs.
- Episodic summaries: bounded summary, importance in `[0,1]`, bounded tags, and one or more evidence turn IDs.

The worker does not return authoritative IDs, scope, trust, provenance, timestamps, or lifecycle state; the runtime derives those from the job and rejects unknown fields, missing evidence, invalid types, excess collection sizes, or references outside the source set. One job may emit at most 20 facts and 10 episodes. Explicit lessons are absent from this contract and are not re-extracted.

Derived semantic facts use the scoped conflict contract established by the governance slice: confidence below 0.8 is rejected, user-explicit facts cannot be replaced, and confidence affects same-scope conflict only. Derived episodes are exact-deduplicated by normalized summary hash in this lexical-only slice. Both retain evidence links and derived-data trust.

Worker error, timeout, malformed output, cancellation, or runtime restart writes no partial memory and advances no source marker. The preserved source turns and durable job state make retry safe and observable.

### Trigger and worker-selection policy

Consolidation is project-scoped and single-flight per runtime. A job contains ordered completed, unconsolidated turns from one canonical project and never mixes projects. It becomes eligible through one of three deterministic paths: an explicit `/memory consolidate`; 20 newly completed turns since the last successful project consolidation; or three hours of project inactivity with at least one unconsolidated completed turn. One job consumes at most 50 turns and 100,000 source characters; excess remains for the next job. Configuration may raise or lower positive thresholds within validated bounds but cannot use zero to mean unbounded.

This is an explicit deterministic scope policy: output derived from a project-bound session is written to that canonical project, never global. The model does not choose or return scope, and confidence does not widen it. Sessions without a project binding are consolidated only into their session scope.

Worker selection never hardcodes a model ID. A `ConsolidationWorkerFactory` receives a snapshot of Cyril's bound ACP agent command/engine and an optional validated memory-specific agent-command override. With no override it starts a separate subprocess using the bound command and inherits that agent's served default model; it never borrows the active session. The job records the non-secret worker fingerprint needed for reproducibility.

The worker opens a fresh minimal ACP session with no Cyril memory/knowledge MCP server and no external MCP servers. Cyril refuses every permission request, treats any observed tool call as `worker_used_tool`, cancels that worker turn, and writes no memory. If a bound agent cannot provide a tool-free/minimal session contract, automatic consolidation is Disabled with actionable `worker_not_confined`; source turns remain durable and explicit retry can use a configured safe worker. One worker processes jobs sequentially and is restarted after protocol/process failure.

Configuration defaults are automatic consolidation enabled once memory itself is enabled, turn threshold 20, idle threshold 180 minutes, maximum 50 turns, maximum 100,000 source characters, concurrency one, and no command/model override. Every trigger and worker selection is visible in job audit/status.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Enqueue only unconsolidated completed turns through deterministic/explicit triggers.
- [ ] Persist source turns before worker dispatch and preserve retryability.
- [ ] Use a dedicated tool-free ACP worker, never the active session.
- [ ] Bound input and strictly validate versioned structured output.
- [ ] Redact and force output into originating trust/scope regardless of model claims.
- [ ] Atomically finalize semantic/episodic memory, progress, and audit.
- [ ] Resume exactly once after restart without duplicates or skipped turns.
- [ ] Distinguish malformed/timeout/cancel/unavailable failures with no partial writes.
- [ ] Show jobs/results in /memory and use successful output in recall.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover policy, lifecycle, conflict, and non-duplication.
- [ ] Automatic jobs trigger at 20 completed turns or 180 idle minutes with at least one turn; explicit enqueue remains available.
- [ ] One job contains one project, at most 50 turns and 100,000 source characters, and concurrency is one.
- [ ] Worker selection inherits the bound agent command by default, never hardcodes a model, and records its non-secret fingerprint.
- [ ] Worker session has no MCP servers; any permission/tool use fails the job with no memory writes.
- [ ] Project-bound jobs write only project scope and unbound sessions write only session scope by deterministic runtime policy.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M4. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.
Mechanism contract added: exact consolidation triggers/bounds, deterministic project scope, agent-command selection, tool-free enforcement, and worker failure policy.

title: Determine the dispatch contract for future KAS-advertised commands
description:
PR #95 / cyril-0qe6 removed the W1 user-visible failure: Cyril keeps workflows.enabled off, owns /workflow natively, and convert/kas.rs suppresses the exact gate-advertised workflow-run, workflow-status, workflow-cancel, and workflow-resume commands. KAS workflow support therefore does not depend on agent-command dispatch.

A narrower latent gap remains. BridgeCommand::ExecuteAgentCommand still sends the v2-only kiro.dev/commands/execute method, while CommandRegistry::register_agent_commands is otherwise engine-agnostic. If a future gate-off KAS release advertises a non-workflow command, Cyril could offer a command it cannot invoke.

Scope:
- Obtain a real KAS-advertised non-workflow command, or establish from a live/settings probe that current gate-off KAS advertises none.
- Determine whether KAS has a client-invoked command method distinct from kiro.dev/commands/execute.
- If KAS supports dispatch, make the bound Engine select the method/shape. If it does not, make command registration engine-aware so unsupported KAS commands are suppressed rather than offered.

Non-goals: changing the W1 /workflow control plane, enabling workflows.enabled, proxying Kiro's four workflow commands, or changing v2 dispatch.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Evidence records the current gate-off KAS advertised-command set and exercises a genuine non-workflow KAS command if one exists.
2. The KAS client-invoked command contract is established from a live response or definitive bundle implementation; absence is recorded explicitly.
3. Cyril never registers a KAS agent command it cannot dispatch; v2 kiro.dev/commands/execute behavior remains unchanged.
4. Regression tests cover the engine-specific registration/dispatch decision, and cargo test plus cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass both by default and with --features kas.

notes.content: Narrowed after PR #95 merged. The original W1 workflow impact is resolved and exact workflow-* suppression is already fenced; this ticket now tracks only the generic future KAS advertised-command contract.

title: acp 0.10.2 hard-fails session/request_permission on unknown PermissionOptionKind — release-audit watch item
description: Discovered by the cyril-qo13 design falsifier (probe_qo13_unknown_option_kind_parse): acp::PermissionOptionKind has no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so a request_permission whose options[] carries a kind outside {allow_once, allow_always, reject_once, reject_always} fails deserialization inside the acp crate -- the agent gets a JSON-RPC error and cyril's overlay never opens. Same class as the SessionUpdate hard-fail documented in CLAUDE.md ACP notes. Consequence: if a future kiro/KAS release introduces a new option kind, cyril's permission handling breaks at parse, upstream of convert/. WATCH: each release wire-audit should grep new traces for unseen 'kind' values in permission options; also re-check on any agent-client-protocol crate upgrade whether the enum gained a catch-all (the sentinel test in crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/convert/probe_qo13.rs flips if parsing starts succeeding). The dead '_ =>' defensive arm in to_permission_options only becomes live if the crate adds variants.

title: KAS steeringSupervisor: client-settable gate that costs a hidden fast-model call per mutating tool call (shadow today)
description:
LIVE on kiro-cli 2.20.1 / KAS 0.54.3. See docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 7; probe experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-steering-supervisor-2.20.1.py.

WHAT IT IS: a pre-execution verifier on individual tool calls (PreToolUse position), NOT a stream watcher. For each qualifying call it makes a SECOND fast-model call (agentName 'steering-supervisor', ~18.5k-char system prompt) that judges the pending call's parameters against the workspace steering docs and returns PASS / a corrected JSON object / REJECT: <reason>. Default allow-list is mutating tools only (execute_bash, execute_pwsh, control_bash_process, control_pwsh_process, fs_write, str_replace).

IT IS SHADOW. The dispatch is fire-and-forget and the verdict is discarded. The running binary prints it verbatim: 'verifier dispatched for "execute_bash" (shadow: non-blocking, verdict not applied)'. Metrics are named SteeringSupervisorWouldRewrite / WouldReject — a measurement phase, not an unfinished feature.

CLIENT-SETTABLE — and this is the counter-example to the cyril-34yq finding. steeringSupervisor is in the AgentSettings schema (next to disableAutoCompaction, subagentOrchestration, workflows) and resolves as clientSetting ?? featureFlag, so the CLIENT SETTING WINS:
  _meta.kiro.settings.steeringSupervisor {enabled: true}   (+ optional toolAllowList)
Verified live: this alone activates it with no KIRO_FEATURE_STEERING_SUPERVISOR_ENABLED. So 'can a client set this gate?' has no single answer in KAS — the feature-config registry is env/experiment-only, but AgentSettings overrides it. Check per knob.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR CYRIL:
1. If cyril exposes KAS settings (see cyril-q8gq BOOL_MAP drift), steeringSupervisor is a row that could be added — but enabling it TODAY is pure cost: one extra model call per mutating tool call, invisible on the ACP wire (no frame attributes it — same shape as the 2.19.2 memory-extraction subagent), with the answer thrown away. Recommend NOT exposing it until it enforces.
2. Track for an enforcing build: it sits in PreToolUse and can REWRITE parameters, so a future release could silently alter a user's fs_write args. That would be worth surfacing in the UI.

Live notes: every verdict observed was PASS across three deliberate attempts to induce a violation (forbidden touch; run_in_background must be true; timeout must be 999) — the main agent self-complied every time, because steering is in ITS context too. In the normal case the supervisor is a redundant duplicate check. The prefilter also has a blind spot: it matches the COMMAND STRING against steering, so a steering rule about a tool PARAMETER on a read-only command is never verified.

title: KAS-2a follow-up: turn_end vs prompt-response stop_reason fidelity on KAS cancel (first-to-arrive wins)
description:
Under KAS a turn produces TWO TurnCompleted: the agent's session_info_update -> turn_end (stop_reason from _meta.kiro.stopReason, scoped to the session) and the off-loop prompt-response synthesis (bridge.rs:563-574, sent as RoutedNotification::global). The bridge dedup (bridge.rs:1385) forwards whichever arrives FIRST and drops the second. For a normal turn both are EndTurn, so it is moot. On a USER CANCEL the prompt resolves Cancelled while turn_end's stopReason may differ; if turn_end wins the race carrying stopReason 'end_turn', the App records EndTurn instead of Cancelled — nondeterministic, dependent on KAS wire behavior on cancel (currently UNOBSERVED; no cancel turn_end has been captured).

Distinct from cyril-a71q: that residual is about clearing the WRONG turn; a per-turn id does NOT decide which of two same-turn signals carries the authoritative stop_reason. The design comment (bridge.rs:560-562) explicitly accepts 'either order' for the common (EndTurn) case.

ACTION before deciding a fix: capture a live KAS cancel (experiments/conductor-spike probe) — does turn_end fire on cancel? with what stopReason? If KAS already reports 'cancelled' in turn_end, there is no bug. If it reports 'end_turn' (or omits turn_end and only the prompt resolves Cancelled), decide whether the off-loop Cancelled must take precedence. Surfaced by /code-review max finders 2026-06-29. LOW severity: only manifests if KAS misreports the cancel stopReason in turn_end AND that frame wins the race.

title: Steering echoes silently dead: backend rollout (Jun 17 - Jul 9 2026) renamed v2 echoes to AgentExecution*; KAS kinds unmapped
description: Live-probed 2026-07-09 on 2.12.0 (.cyril-vgcm/findings.md F2/F3/F8). A BACKEND rollout between 2026-06-17 (K1b capture, binary 2.8.0: steering_queued{message} live) and 2026-07-09 (archived 2.7.0 binary now emits the new family) renamed the v2 steering echoes for ALL binary versions: steering_queued{message} -> AgentExecutionUserMessageQueued{messageId,content}; steering_consumed -> AgentExecutionSteeringInjected{messageId,content}; steering_cleared -> AgentExecutionUserMessageCleared{messageIds}. NOT a binary change (strings rename-table dating was a red herring; wire = binary x backend). convert/kiro.rs matches only the old literals -> unknown-variant Err -> every echo dropped; the optimistic steer chip increments at send and never reconciles (phantom chip on EVERY steer today; overlaps cyril-nvmh paths b/c). KAS echoes ride session_info_update _meta.kiro.kind steering_queued/steering_injected/steering_cleared, which convert/kas.rs also drops (matches only turn_end/context_usage). Fix: converter re-base handling BOTH v2 literal families (rollouts can stage/revert) + KAS kinds. Being fixed on the cyril-vgcm branch.

title: Investigate KAS Powers / the open Agent Plugin format (_kiro/powers/list, 2.16.2) — candidate substrate for the Phase-5 skill resolver
description:
2.16.2 ships "Powers" aligned with an OPEN AGENT PLUGIN FORMAT. From the official
release notes (NOT the embedded changelog, which omits it entirely):

  "Powers aligned with the open Agent Plugin format now load in V3 sessions. Kiro
   now supports plugins that bundle skills and MCP, making powers easier to share
   across compatible agent tools."

Wire/bundle evidence:
  _kiro/powers/list                  new client-callable method (2.16.2)
  _kiro/powers/items_changed         pre-existing notification, already tolerated
  src/powers/agent-plugin-loader.ts  new KAS module (2.16.1)

WHY THIS IS NOT A KAS-8 FOOTNOTE
A plugin format that (a) bundles SKILLS + MCP and (b) is explicitly cross-tool is the
same problem the platform vision's "Skill resolver" stage was scoped to solve
(ROADMAP Phase 5): supplement whatever skill system the underlying agent has. If the
format is genuinely open, cyril has two possible roles rather than one -- CONSUME
plugins so a cyril user gets the same powers Kiro users do, and/or SUPPLY them so
cyril-authored skills load in any compatible agent. Either would be the first
vendor-neutral artifact cyril traffics in.

It also sits directly beside reference_kiro_kas_command_surface (KAS advertises ONLY
skills to a client -- no v2 TUI commands), which is currently recorded as a hole in
cyril's slash layer under KAS. A plugin/skill format is the other half of that story.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE (probe, do not infer)
  1. What IS the "open Agent Plugin format"? Is there a published spec, or is "open"
     marketing for a Kiro-defined JSON shape? Check the bundle's loader for the
     schema it parses.
  2. _kiro/powers/list -- call it. Response shape, and does it route gate-free the
     way _kiro/workflow/* does, or need a settings key?
  3. Is `list` the only client-facing verb, or are there install/enable counterparts?
  4. Do powers appear to the client at all today (tools? skills? commands?), or are
     they purely server-side prompt assembly?
  5. Relationship to `session/new _meta.kiro.customAgents` (CLIENT_PROVIDED agents),
     which is the injection hook the Phase-5 skill-resolver work already proved.

Cheap: questions 1 and 4 are static reads of the bundle; 2 and 3 are a free handshake
probe (no prompt turn). Nothing here needs credits to start.

Ref: docs/kiro-2.16.2-wire-audit.md
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Agent Plugin format is characterized from the bundle loader: schema, whether a published spec exists, and whether 'open' is real or Kiro-defined.
2. _kiro/powers/list is called live; response shape recorded, and gate behaviour established (routes free vs needs a settings key).
3. A decision is recorded: cyril consumes plugins, supplies them, both, or neither -- with the reason.
4. Relationship to session/new _meta.kiro.customAgents (the proven CLIENT_PROVIDED injection hook) is stated explicitly.

title: KAS settings marshal BOOL_MAP is stale vs the 2.19.2 TUI table — missing memory.enabled → userMemoryOptIn (the per-connection veto for KAS native memory)
description:
crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/kas/settings.rs documents BOOL_MAP as "verbatim from kiro-tui-2.8.1.js (the independent source of truth)". The 2.19.2 tui.js table (`zme()` successor, anchor `["chat.enableThinking","thinking"]`) has drifted:

  BOOL_MAP rows (unchanged): chat.enableThinking→thinking, chat.enableKnowledge→knowledge, chat.enableCodeIntelligence→codeIntelligence, chat.enableTodoList→todoList, chat.enableCheckpoint→checkpoint, chat.enableTangentMode→tangentMode, chat.disableAutoCompaction→disableAutoCompaction, chat.enableSubagent→_subagent, chat.enableDelegate→_delegate
  NEW unconditional row (missing in cyril): ["memory.enabled","userMemoryOptIn"]
  NEW conditional rows (missing): if KIRO_INFRA_SAFETY_ROLLOUT_ENABLED=1 → chat.enableInfraSafetyMonitor→infraSafetyMonitor, chat.enableInfraSafetyEnforce→infraSafetyEnforce; if c2s feature enabled → chat.enableC2s→c2s
  Also new object-valued entries: workflows/goal {enabled} from workflow availability, workflowNotifications {enabled, delivery}, plus the toolSearch/compaction/knowledge objects (verify which of these cyril already marshals).
  A separate legacy map Szn=[["memory","memoryEnable"]] exists (older nightly builds send memoryEnable; KAS treats it as the insider-channel fallback).

Why P3 and not P4: `userMemoryOptIn` is the ONLY client-side lever over KAS native persistent memory (AB_MEMORY_EXTERNAL, dark today; docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 11). KAS resolveMemoryEnabled: userOptIn = settings has own property "userMemoryOptIn" ? settings.userMemoryOptIn.enabled : undefined; isMemoryEnabled returns false whenever userOptIn === false, regardless of the experiment/env. When memory_external_enabled ramps, KAS will inject its own "# Memory" block into msg0 AND its turn-end extraction subagent will read cyril's injected <CYRIL_LESSONS>/<CYRIL_EPISODES> blocks out of the parent history and re-file them as KAS memories (duplicate store, higher authority slot, hidden per-turn model call). Sending {userMemoryOptIn:{enabled:false}} at initialize is the one-line defense.

Scope:
1. Add ("memory.enabled","userMemoryOptIn") to BOOL_MAP; update the doc comment to name the 2.19.2 table as the source of truth and record the conditional rows.
2. Decide the default: when cyril-memory is enabled/injecting, default userMemoryOptIn to {enabled:false} unless the user explicitly sets memory.enabled=true in cli.json (do not silently override an explicit true). Surface the resolved value in /memory status.
3. Re-run the marshal_live_fixture test against a 2.19.2-derived fixture; add the conditional rows behind the same env checks the TUI uses, or document why they are deliberately not replicated.
4. Live-verify with probe-kas-memory-external-2.19.2.py: env override ON + initialize settings userMemoryOptIn {enabled:false} → roster must stay at 16 tools, no memories.jsonl, no extraction dumps.

Evidence: kiro-tui-2.19.2.js table (anchor above); KAS acp-server.js 0.52.1 resolveMemoryEnabled / isSettingEnabled; docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 11; related cyril-s21o, cyril-jrl1 (memoryEnable / searchMemories allowlist), cyril-nhzw (original marshal).

title: Wire KIRO_MOCK_CHAT_RESPONSE into CI as a credit-free ACP test backend (text + turn lifecycle only)
description:
`KIRO_MOCK_CHAT_RESPONSE=<file>` makes kiro-cli serve scripted responses from a real `kiro-cli acp` process — genuine JSON-RPC, genuine `session/new`, genuine streaming — at zero credits, zero latency, fully offline. Proven end-to-end 2026-07-26 (`experiments/conductor-spike/probe-mock-backend-2.14.2.py`, and section A of `probe-mock-objects-2.14.2.py`): the sentinel text is served verbatim, `stopReason: end_turn`, 0.0s per turn, and no `meteringUsage` frame appears on any turn.

Value over the current fake-bridge tests: it exercises the actual protocol path — `protocol/convert/`, the `!Send` bridge thread and its channels, `UiState::apply_notification` streaming accumulation, and chronological commit ordering — rather than a hand-rolled stand-in that can drift from the wire. `cargo run --example test_bridge` could run in CI with no credentials and no credits.

SCOPE IS BOUNDED BY A KIRO DEFECT, NOT BY CHOICE. The script format is `[["chunk1"," chunk2"],["turn two"]]` — one outer element per turn; inner strings stream as separate `agent_message_chunk`s and concatenate, so chunk boundaries are scriptable too. The parser's reject message advertises "array of arrays of strings **or objects**", and the object form was designed to script tool calls, thinking chunks and injectable transport errors (`MockStreamItem` = `{kind: event|streamError|sendError, data: …}` wrapping the 14-variant adjacently-tagged `ChatResponseStream`). Objects are unusable on every release that offers them: ANY object, including a bare `{}`, panics kiro-cli at `initialize` with `called Option::unwrap() on a None value` at `crates/chat-cli/src/api_client/mod.rs:1107`. The v1 crate (`chat_cli`) reads the same env var and unwraps unconditionally on the object branch, aborting the process before `chat_cli_v2`'s parser — the one that understands the shape — ever runs. `--agent-engine v1|v2|v3` and `kiro-cli acp` all panic identically; there is no dodge. Broken since 2.6.0 introduced object support (panics unbroken 2.6.0 → 2.14.2). Full shape matrix + version sweep: `experiments/conductor-spike/probe-mock-objects-2.14.2.py`.

=> This ticket therefore covers AGENT TEXT AND TURN LIFECYCLE ONLY. Tool-call rendering, the approval overlay, and subagent/crew paths stay on a fake bridge until AWS fixes the panic — worth re-checking on each release audit.

Two behaviors any harness must encode:

- Exhaustion hard-fails. A prompt past the end of the script returns `-32603 "Kiro failed to generate a response"` immediately. It does NOT fall through to the real backend, so an over-running suite cannot silently start billing — but tests must expect that error rather than a hang.
- Isolation is mandatory. Spawn with `HOME=<tmp>` plus a real `XDG_DATA_HOME` (feedback_isolate_kiro_probes_with_home), or probe runs prune the real `~/.kiro/logs`. Verified unchanged (10 dirs before and after) across every run in the 2026-07-26 session.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A reusable test helper spawns `kiro-cli acp` under `KIRO_MOCK_CHAT_RESPONSE` with the `HOME=<tmp>` + real `XDG_DATA_HOME` isolation recipe, and tears the child process down deterministically (no orphans on panic or early return).
2. At least one integration test drives a full turn through the real bridge and asserts committed message CONTENT AND ORDER — chunks concatenating into one `AgentText`, and text committed in arrival order — not merely that some string arrived.
3. A multi-turn test asserts that turn N is served by outer script element N (turn 2 returns different text from turn 1).
4. A test asserts the exhaustion case: prompting past the end of the script surfaces the `-32603` error as a recoverable UI state, with `is_busy` cleared — not a hang and not a stuck toolbar.
5. The suite SKIPS with a clear message (rather than failing) when `kiro-cli` is not on PATH, so contributors without it can still run `cargo test`.
6. CI runs the mock-backed job with no Kiro credentials configured, demonstrating the credit-free property rather than asserting it in prose.
7. A guard fails the build if any `meteringUsage` credit is non-zero during the run, so a regression that silently reaches the real backend is caught instead of quietly billing.
8. CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section documents the invocation, and records that the mock is STRINGS-ONLY plus the reason (the object-form panic), so the limitation is not re-derived from scratch.

title: KAS _kiro/frontendToolCall: model agent->client frontend-tool callback, reply declining (KAS-2)
description: New in kiro-cli 2.13.0 (KAS @kiro/agent 0.18.2 / observed in v2 TUI client): KAS can ask its client to execute a client-hosted ('frontend') tool via ext request _kiro/frontendToolCall. Request carries a ToolCallUpdate-like payload ({toolCallId, title, rawInput?, ...}); the client advertises the capability as frontendToolCall:true in KiroClientMeta handshake caps. The v2 TUI (2.13.0) registers a handler that declines every call with {outcome:"cancelled"} (log: 'declining unhosted client tool'). In relayed/cloud sessions it is one of three consent-callback kinds (permission/frontendToolCall/openUrl) with disconnect policy fail (permission defers 5min). Cyril's KAS dialect (ROADMAP KAS-2) should model the method and reply the same {outcome:"cancelled"} decline until cyril hosts client tools — an unhandled ext request risks hanging a KAS turn. Reference: docs/kiro-2.13.0-wire-audit.md.

notes.content: 2026-07-23 audit update (docs/kiro-2.14.1-wire-audit.md): the v2 bun TUI REMOVED its client-side _kiro/frontendToolCall handler + cap advertisement in 2.14.0 (tui.js frontendToolCall string count 2->0; openExternalUrl handler now leads straight into secrets.json, TL() block gone). No shipped 2.14.x client advertises the cap. KAS agent side RETAINS emit support (@kiro/agent 0.22.7: 15 refs, was 19), gated on the client advertising frontendToolCall:true. Since KAS only emits when the client opts in, cyril never receives the call unless cyril itself advertises the cap. Revised posture: cyril does NOT advertise frontendToolCall (matches every shipped 2.14.x client) => no decline handler needed to avoid a hang. Keep decline-{outcome:cancelled} only as a safety net if cyril ever advertises it. Dropped P2->P3.

title: Stall recovery: use session/cancel as a non-lethal liveness probe with stale_recover reclassification
description:
Cyril rule "NEVER synthesize a turn end on silence" is correct but leaves the session hung forever. KiroCrew found the missing third option: do not guess, ASK.

  idle past threshold, evidence says not-working
    -> send session/cancel (bounded 5s) as a PROBE, not a termination
       |- ack arrives (stopReason: cancelled)
       |    -> the turn was really done and the response frame was lost
       |    -> RECLASSIFY to stale_recover; never surface as "cancelled by user"
       |- no ack within 10s
            -> CONFIRMED WEDGE (a done-but-missing-frame turn would have acked)
            -> synthesize a LABELLED terminal

The reclassification is load-bearing (session_handle.py:2284-2300): "kiro-cli acks session/cancel on a LIVE mid-generation turn too, so a probe-induced cancelled must NOT surface as a user cancellation (the turn would die silently - the original session-killer)." Their safety summary: "An oracle mistake therefore costs a regeneration, never a session."

Works on BOTH engines, needs nothing from 2.20.1, and cyril already sends session/cancel on Esc.

IMPORTANT - the first-party position is not "never synthesize". client.py:4292 literally logs "Treating as complete." after 90s, and only a WORKING verdict defers: DEAD, UNKNOWN, probe failure and no-/proc-at-all all END the turn ("fail toward reaping, never toward hanging"). The five constraints that make it survivable:
  1. never end_turn - every synthetic terminal carries a distinct reason
  2. an EMPTY stop reason is not neutral - theirs was misread one layer up as a timeout and escalated to a HARD KILL of the shared runtime; fall back to a benign non-empty end_turn
  3. synthesis implies a mandatory session reset - the backend still counts the turn in progress and the next prompt collides with "prompt already in progress"
  4. drain leftover frames at the next turn start - the abandoned turn keeps emitting and contaminates the next transcript; permission REQUESTS are answered, never dropped
  5. bounded 3-attempt budget, not reset on exhaustion, then a visible "Session stuck - start a new chat"

Also clamp every window to 0.9x the turn timeout: "A default above it silently disables the branch it governs on every install, which is exactly how the UNKNOWN class became dead code."

Note cyril is architecturally in their session_handle position (killing the agent kills the user session), NOT their client.py position - so copy the probe doctrine, not the 90s blind reap.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 3.2, 3.3, 3.6.
acceptance_criteria: A stalled turn is probed rather than only reported. A probe ack completes the turn under a distinct stale_recover reason and never renders as a user cancellation. An unacked probe produces a labelled terminal plus a session reset, bounded to 3 attempts.

title: KAS user_input questions: cyril can only return the FIRST option (kind-keyed permission response drops the choice)
description: KAS's user_input clarifying-question flow (spec/quick-spec) surfaces each question three ways at once: (1) tool_call kind:'other' _meta.kiro.toolId:'user_input' (display card — NOTE cyril FILTERS kind==Other tool calls, so this card is suppressed), (2) session_info_update pending_interaction (KAS-native mirror — cyril drops unknown session_info_update kinds), (3) session/request_permission (the id'd REQUEST cyril actually handles via its approval overlay). So the question reaches the user through the permission overlay. BUG: these questions carry N answer options ALL with kind 'allow_once' (e.g. 'A list of discrete note entries' / 'Keep the blob, add structured append' / 'Skip questions'). cyril's PermissionResponse enum is KIND-based (AllowOnce/AllowAlways/Reject/RejectAlways/Cancel), and to_acp_permission_response uses find_option_id(args, kind) which returns the FIRST option matching that kind (convert/mod.rs ~345). With all options kind=allow_once, cyril ALWAYS returns option-0's id regardless of which the user picked -> the agent silently receives the wrong answer to a design-decision question. The overlay knows state.selected (the index) but PermissionResponse can't carry it. Correct wire reply is {outcome:{outcome:'selected', optionId:'...-option-N'}} for the SPECIFIC chosen option. Evidence: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl (3 user_input questions, ids 3/4/5, each 3x allow_once). Only bites on KAS/v3 + spec/quick-spec/user_input flows; silent (wrong answer, no error).
design: .cyril-qo13/design.md (falsifiable-design, 2026-07-02; cheapest falsifier passed)
acceptance_criteria: PermissionResponse can carry the selected optionId (e.g. a Selected(PermissionOptionId) variant or index); overlay passes through the chosen option's id; same-kind multi-option requests (user_input) return the exact choice; standard tool approvals (distinct kinds) unchanged. Verify against the trace's 3 questions.

notes.content:
SCOPE WIDENED (2026-07-02, from the KAS trace's fs_write tool_approval, id=6): the permission-response fix is bigger than 'carry optionId'. KAS tool_approvals carry _meta.kiro.consent on BOTH request and response. Request: {capability:'fs_write', resource, askType:'implicit', workspaceRoot} + consentRound. The reference client's response ECHOES the full outcome shape: {_meta:{kiro:{consent:{capability, scope, workspaceRoot}}}, outcome:{outcome:'selected', optionId:'accept', _meta:{kiro:{consent:{capability, scope, workspaceRoot}}}}} where scope='invocation' for allow_once (presumably session/always for allow_always). cyril's to_acp_permission_response sends NO _meta at all — so an 'Always allow' grant may not record its scope (ties to trust-persistence [reference_kiro_trust_persistence] — the wire consent scope may be the KAS-native mechanism vs cyril writing the agent store file). => The new PermissionResponse must carry: (a) the selected optionId (the original bug), AND (b) an optional _meta.kiro.consent{capability, scope} passthrough for tool_approvals. CAVEAT: whether KAS REQUIRES the consent _meta vs derives scope from the option kind is UNVERIFIED (schema-present ≠ required, feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime) — needs a control probe: respond 'accept' WITHOUT consent _meta, check grant/scope still registers. Standard tool approvals (distinct kinds) already answer correctly today; this widening is about grant-SCOPE fidelity + the user_input optionId bug.

TRUST-MODEL DIVERGENCE (2026-07-02, from the tool-lifecycle KAS-vs-v2 diff): the permission-response outcome shape is ENGINE-CONDITIONAL — the two engines' trust wire has ZERO field overlap. v2: permission carries _meta.trustOptions[].{patterns[], setting_key, label, display}; response echoes outcome._meta.trustOption.{patterns[], setting_key} (command-pattern trust the client persists to a setting_key — the allowedCommands mechanism, reference_kiro_trust_persistence). cyril already handles v2 trustOptions (trust_options in PermissionRequest, 7 files). KAS: permission carries _meta.kiro.consent{capability, resource, askType} + consentRound; response echoes outcome._meta.kiro.consent{capability, scope('invocation'|session|always), workspaceRoot} (Cedar capability+scope grant, NOT a command pattern). => the new PermissionResponse can't be a single shape: it needs to carry EITHER a v2 trustOption passthrough OR a KAS consent{capability,scope}, selected by engine. This widens the fix again: (a) selected optionId [orig bug], (b) KAS consent{capability,scope} passthrough for tool_approvals, (c) keep the v2 trustOption path. The converter split (convert/kiro.rs v2 trustOptions vs convert/kas.rs KAS consent) is the right seam.

PROBE COMPLETE (2026-07-02, prove-it-prototype): probe = crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/convert/probe_qo13.rs (cargo test -p cyril-core probe_qo13 -- --nocapture) replays all 10 trace permission requests through the REAL parse+convert pipeline; oracle = .cyril-qo13/oracle.py (raw-text extraction of reference-client replies, no cyril code). AGREE item-by-item on all 10 requests x every option: correct reply = options[k].optionId; cyril-current emits option-0 for EVERY pick on all-allow_once requests (11/16 pick-cases wrong on ids 1-5,10) while all 16 distinct-kind fs_write cases are correct. CAVEAT RESOLVED for allow_once: the reference client itself omitted consent _meta on requests 8/9 (present on 6/7, all consentRound=1) and all four fs_writes completed -> consent echo OPTIONAL for invocation-scope grants; no control probe needed. Also: user_input replies are BARE selected outcomes (no _meta at either level), and outcome:'cancelled' is legal (req 1 cancelled -> KAS re-asked as req 2), so Esc->Cancel already wire-valid. RESIDUAL UNKNOWN: whether allow_always grants need the consent _meta scope echo to persist (trace has no always-accept reply) - live control probe needed only for the consent-passthrough half. Full findings: .cyril-qo13/probe-findings.md

DESIGN READY (2026-07-02, falsifiable-design): .cyril-qo13/design.md. Core fix: PermissionResponse -> Selected{option_id: PermissionOptionId, trust_option} | Cancel; ApprovalPhase::SelectTrust carries the phase-1 chosen_option_id (selected re-indexes trust_options in phase 2 -- the hidden hazard); find_option_id + fallbacks deleted. 8 claims, cheapest falsifier PASSED (reply encoding byte-equal to reference client's non-first-option reply -- probe_qo13_reply_shape_matches_reference_bytes). Unknown option kinds proven UNREACHABLE (acp 0.10.2 parse rejects; sentinel test + watch item cyril-p7kp). SCOPE SPLIT per design: KAS allow_always consent-scope -> cyril-gn07; v2 trustOption echo shape -> cyril-sive; this issue = exact-choice fidelity only. Next: budgeted-plan.

PLAN READY (2026-07-02, budgeted-plan): .cyril-qo13/plan.md — 6 slices, expand/contract (workspace green after every slice): 1 PermissionOptionId newtype (mechanical) -> 2 expand Selected variant + converter arm + load-bearing membership warn -> 3 replay probe upgraded to asserting C1/C3 fence (both traces + synthetic single-option) -> 4 UI phase-1 exact pick + oob/empty->Cancel -> 5 SelectTrust{chosen_option_id} provenance (+staleness fixture for back-then-repick) -> 6 contract: delete kind variants/From impl/find_option_id, fix bridge harness. Post-slice: one-time live KAS validation of C8 (user-approved manual fence). Next: checkpointed-build.

BUILD COMPLETE (2026-07-02, checkpointed-build): 6/6 slices landed on main (88988f2, 2ba2fde, 5bcca62, 758f411, ac30697, be95aef). All fences green: exact-choice replay over BOTH 2.11.0 traces + synthetic single-option (C1/C3), reply-shape byte-equality vs reference (C2), trust-provenance + staleness fixtures (C4), cancel/oob/empty (C5/C6), unknown-kind sentinel (C7). Mutation checks proved fences non-vacuous (forced option-0 fails 4 tests; options[selected]-at-trust-confirm fails provenance). 798 tests default / 872 --features kas, clippy --all-targets clean both. C8 MANUAL FENCE: cyril-side = deterministic (C1+C2); server-side LIVE: KAS 2.11.0 accepted cyril's exact bytes for a NON-FIRST option ('always-accept') and honored it (probe experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-user-input-choice-2.11.0.py, after auth workaround — see cyril-dcc6). The user_input-question live re-run (non-first pick on the mode question) still PENDING a fresh token window: the empty-tempdir session explored instead of entering the spec flow, and the IDC token expired before a retry; user_input semantic honoring stands proven by the committed reference trace (ids 2/3/10, non-first picks steering the spec). Rerun when logged in fresh: python3 experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-user-input-choice-2.11.0.py <acp-server.js path>.

Closed: Build complete on main: 6/6 slices (88988f2..be95aef) + review commit 0878f2c (independent C3 oracle wired into replay fence). Acceptance criteria verified: exact-choice replay over both 2.11.0 traces + synthetic single-option (C1/C3), reply-shape byte-equality vs reference client (C2), trust-provenance/staleness (C4), cancel/oob/empty (C5/C6), unknown-kind sentinel (C7); mutation checks proved fences non-vacuous. C8 live: KAS 2.11.0 accepted+honored a non-first-option reply (tool_approval always-accept); user_input semantic honoring proven by committed reference trace (ids 2/3/10). RESIDUAL (optional, non-blocking): live user_input non-first-pick re-run pending fresh IDC token — probe-kas-user-input-choice-2.11.0.py. Scope splits live on: cyril-gn07 (KAS allow_always consent scope), cyril-sive (v2 trustOption echo).

C8 LIVE COMPLETE (2026-07-03, fresh IDC token window): the pending user_input live re-run PASSED. Probe v2 (rewritten in place: probe-kas-user-input-choice-2.11.0.py) reproduces the reference trace's recipe — throwaway local clone of ~/repos/rivets as workspace, set_config_option autopilot=on + mode=spec + model=claude-haiku-4.5, then the trace's spec prompt. A genuine user_input question fired ('Is this a new feature or a bugfix?', 3 options all allow_once, optionIds <toolCallId>-option-N). cyril's exact reply bytes for options[1] ('Fix a Bug') were accepted AND semantically honored: the agent continued 'Got it—this is a bugfix' and branched into the bug-detail flow instead of option-0's feature path. v1 lesson encoded in the probe: user_input never fires from a bare prompt in an empty dir — it is a spec-mode behavior, and permission classification must distinguish standard tool approvals (accept/always-accept/... optionIds) from question sets (all kind=allow_once, non-standard optionIds). Auth via the cyril-dcc6 workaround, refined: file seeded from the sqlite IDC token WITHOUT refreshToken sufficed for the whole session; original file restored after. NO RESIDUAL REMAINS on this issue.

title: KAS hooks host hardening: verify executeHook command echo against the served registry
description: From the cyril-jiyn two-axis PR review (standards R7). respond_execute spawns the wire-supplied command verbatim; the covenant makes executeHook an echo of what cyril served via _kiro/hooks/list ({hookId, hookName, command, ...}), and the covenant even says the client 'handles approval'. Hardening: cross-check hookId/command against the loaded registry and warn or deny on mismatch, so a misbehaving agent cannot run arbitrary commands through the hooks channel — this is the org-gate integrity property. Needs a probe first: confirm KAS always echoes list-served ids/commands unchanged (incl. namespaced ids) before making mismatch a denial, else legit flows break.

title: Ingest kiro-cli chat --list-models --format json as the model catalog (context windows + credit multipliers, zero ACP round-trips)
description:
kiro-cli ships a complete authoritative model catalog behind a subcommand cyril has never used (it appears in cyril only inside archived changelog JSON):

  {"models":[{"model_name":"auto","model_id":"auto",
              "description":"Models chosen by task for optimal usage and consistent quality",
              "context_window_tokens":1000000,"rate_multiplier":1.0}],
   "default_model":"auto"}

Row shape: {model_name, model_id?, display_name?, description?, context_window_tokens?, rate_multiplier?}. KiroCrew /api/models is a verbatim passthrough of this (agents.py:1424-1448).

This closes ROADMAP KAS-4 by the side door: the picker never has to wait for a late configOptionUpdate, and the 2.17.0 transiently-absent-configOption case stops mattering.

Context-window precedence to adopt (model_registry.py:21-29, first-party):
  usage_update.size > --list-models cache > static registry > [1m] heuristic > None
with REFERENCE_WINDOW_TOKENS = 1_000_000 for unknown — explicitly NOT a 200k default, "so an unknown model is never wrongly shrunk". (Their own TS adapter defaults to 200k and is wrong; understating truncates the user context, overstating only mis-scales a meter.)

Traps: dotted vs dashed ids are DIFFERENT models with different windows (claude-opus-4.8 = 1M, claude-opus-4-8 = 200K). Never default rate_multiplier to 1.0 — the served spread is 0.01x-4.4x and kiro re-prices mid-life.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md sections 5.1-5.3.
acceptance_criteria: The model picker and the context meter can populate from --list-models before any configOption arrives. Unknown window resolves to 1M or None, never 200k. Dotted/dashed ids are not folded together.

title: KAS-5b: drain terminal pipes at create (reader task) if KAS ever delays wait_for_exit
description: KAS-5b (cyril-ufie) uses the 'wait does the draining' lifecycle: create spawns the child with piped stdout/stderr and returns the id; wait_for_exit moves the child out and calls child.wait_with_output().await, which drains both pipes concurrently with waiting. Safe because the 2.10.0 capture shows KAS calls wait_for_exit IMMEDIATELY after create (consecutive), so the undrained-pipe window is sub-millisecond. RISK: if a future KAS release delays wait_for_exit while the command is chatty (>64KB before wait arrives), the OS pipe buffer fills and the command blocks on write -> stall. Trigger to act: a capture showing KAS create-then-not-immediately-wait, OR a >64KB-output command stalling. Fix: drain-at-create reader task (spawn_local) that streams stdout+stderr into the entry buffer and reaps on exit (also enables true output-so-far + helps cyril-3lh8 reaping). Re-probe before assuming Option B is permanent.

notes.content: 2026-07-01 issue-set review — the gate is WRONG-BY-OMISSION: 'trigger to act: a future KAS release delaying wait' ignores that cyril-3lh8's cancel path already produces create-without-wait TODAY. A session/cancel landing between create and wait_for_exit means wait never comes; a command that has already written >64KB blocks forever on the full OS pipe (terminal_io.rs:85-104 pipes both streams with no reader until wait, :139) — a PERMANENT orphan plus a registry entry that never evicts. The two issues are mutually invalidating: 3lh8's 'orphan runs until it exits naturally' assumes drained pipes; this issue's 'sub-ms undrained window' assumes wait always arrives. Fix jointly with cyril-3lh8 (session-keyed registry + kill-on-cancel + drain-at-create reader); .kill_on_drop(true) at create is a cheap backstop either way. Keep P4 only if 3lh8's fix kills pre-wait children; otherwise this is effectively P3.
Closed: Fixed in PR #80 (ce0ea4f): shared create-time pipe with a drain reader started before wait arrives; follow-up cyril-ho7o tracks the daemonized-holder stall

title: KAS companion ledger has near-zero behavioural coverage (absorb and drop are observationally identical)
description:
The KAS half of the bridge companion ledger has almost no behavioural coverage,
and the reason is structural rather than an oversight.

Measured during the cyril-upjh sweep fix (PR #76) by mutation: rewriting the new
`ActiveTurn::owes_wire_companion()` gate to a blanket `false` — which disables
companion registration ENTIRELY, including the KAS path it exists to serve —
still passes all 59 other bridge tests, every existing KAS companion fixture
included. Only the new `wire_companion_is_owed_only_under_kas` matrix test fails.

Root cause: absorbing a companion and dropping an unowned terminal both `continue`
with nothing forwarded, so the two outcomes are observationally IDENTICAL on the
notification channel. No black-box test driving the bridge from outside can tell
them apart, which is why the fixture count overstates the real protection.

This is cyril-a71q's own signed blindness B14/B16, not a new regression. Filing it
because the fixture count reads as healthy coverage and it is not: anyone touching
companion registration has far thinner protection than `cargo nextest` suggests.

Possible directions (needs a design decision, hence not swept):
  a. Expose the ledger state through a test-only observation seam so absorb vs
     drop become distinguishable (the upjh fence added a narrow cfg(test) inbound
     injection seam; an observation counterpart would be the mirror of it).
  b. Emit a distinguishing trace/metric on absorb, and assert on it.
  c. Accept the blindness explicitly and document the invariant as reasoning-only.

Evidence: crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/bridge.rs (companion ledger ~line 971,
registration ~2108, absorb paths ~2092 and ~2136). Discovered 2026-08-01 during
the sweep-bugs batch cyril-imjx/cyril-upjh/cyril-tglp.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped with PR #81 (cyril-b4y4, decef9e45) via its option (a): TurnMediator::observe returns Disposition — Absorb/DropStale/DropUnowned are distinct variants with the Absorb evidence payload, so absorb vs drop are directly assertable without the async harness. Proof: mutation M2 (companion gate/clear disabled) now fails mediator_matrix_all_dispositions at f3 + turn_mediation_probe_scenario, where it previously passed all 59 bridge tests.

title: Poisoned-conversation escape hatch: kiro-cli replays full history every turn, so rejected content re-fails forever
description:
A wire invariant with no workaround inside a session: kiro-cli replays the FULL history every turn from a fixed index. Any content the backend rejects is therefore re-sent on every subsequent turn, forever. KiroCrew live log shows one oversized image failing 19 consecutive times (commits a858b6e7e, 1289fbd2d).

This generalizes past attachments. Commit 533323e37 documents the same shape for a whole poisoned native conversation: a persisted conversation the backend deterministically rejects fails every prompt PRE-STREAM with a transient-classified error, so the retry ladder re-prompts the same poison indefinitely.

Their two-part answer:
1. Validate before sending anything into a prompt (they cap images at 2000px longest edge AND 5MiB on the ENCODED payload — Bedrock cap is half Anthropic direct-API allowance).
2. An escape hatch: after 2 consecutive zero-output ladder exhaustions, discard the native conversation (clear the resume sid, cold start) and re-queue once.

For cyril the question is narrower — cyril does not yet resume by default — but the failure mode is real for any /resume path and for attachments. Related: cyril-rtrh (session/load meta).

Also relevant, from the same family (their issue #6022): "Refuse to re-send a payload that was just structurally rejected. A structural rejection is deterministic; retrying it cannot succeed." That guard alone would have turned 17 identical failures into 1.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: A decision on where cyril validates prompt content pre-send, and whether a repeated structural rejection clears the resume sid instead of retrying.

title: Session resume: send _kiro.dev/session_file meta on session/load and verify the modes resume signal
description: Kiro Crew (AWS official open-source ACP client) proves v2 session resume WORKS, contradicting docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md which marks the resume family unstable/unavailable on v1/v2. Crew resume contract: (1) issue session/load DIRECTLY with the ORIGINAL sessionId — never after session/new for the same resume; the fresh-context-replayed-over-loaded-transcript double-session footgun produces stopReason=refusal. (2) params carry cwd, mcpServers:[] and _meta:{"_kiro.dev/session_file": <sidecar path>} — the ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<uuid>.json sidecar already catalogued for metering. (3) A genuine resume echoes modes in the response; anything else means state was NOT restored. (4) Gated on the backend advertising loadSession capability. Cyril today: bridge.rs ~1352 sends LoadSessionRequest::new(session_id, cwd) only — no session_file meta, no modes verification.
acceptance_criteria: BridgeCommand::LoadSession sends session/load with _meta {"_kiro.dev/session_file": path} when a sidecar path is available; load issued directly (no preceding session/new for the resume); response validated — modes present means resumed, absent means an honest error notification back to the App (bridge must notify on every command including failures); gated on advertised loadSession capability with a clear notification fallback; docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md corrected (v2 resume works via this contract); live-verified against a real kiro-cli acp session showing retained transcript context.

notes.content: Source: github.com/kirodotdev/kirocrew @ e44259ce, src/kiro_crew/acp/runtime.py (resume_session) + acp/client.py (_initialize_session). Diffed against docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md 2026-08-04; see memory reference_kirocrew_platform.

Deep-dive addendum (docs/kirocrew-deep-dive.md, critic-VERIFIED at client.py:2199-2250,2553): (1) the ENTIRE transcript replays as notifications BEFORE the session/load response — response deadline must be activity-based (reset per received frame, 600s absolute cap), not fixed; (2) stale session lock after unclean kiro-cli death → transient "active in another process" refusal; bounded backoff ladder (~4 tries) recovers losslessly, then fall back to session/new; drain active turns before SIGTERM at shutdown so the lock releases; (3) CAVEAT: "silently ignored without the _meta session_file" is a KiroCrew DOC assertion, not code-exercised — probe it live; (4) MCP init notifications re-fire during load; set_mode/set_model may get no JSON-RPC response (fire-and-forget, tolerate late replies).

title: Track KAS native persistent memory (AB_MEMORY_EXTERNAL, dark) vs cyril-memory: hidden extraction cost + positioning
description:
KAS 0.52.1 ships a complete persistent-memory subsystem behind the dark experiment flag AB_MEMORY_EXTERNAL (clientConfig memory_external_enabled, default false; internal ramp AB_MEMORY_INTERNAL wins when set; env override KIRO_FEATURE_MEMORY_EXTERNAL_ENABLED=true; user veto via initialize._meta.kiro.settings.userMemoryOptIn=false, mapped from a memory.enabled kiro-cli setting the 2.19.2 registry does not know yet).

Live-verified 2026-08-25 (docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 11): with the env override the model tool roster gains `memory` (list/get/add/update/delete; title-addressed; USER_PREFERENCE|SEMANTIC; scope global|workspace|repo with repo tag from the git remote), the store is ~/.kiro/memories/memories.jsonl (user-editable JSONL), and every new session gets a "# Memory" index block in msg0 (Global + current repo/workspace scopes in full, other scopes as a manifest) that the model applies. NEW in 0.52.1: a turn-end extraction subagent (agentName memory-extraction, parent history + rubric, memory-tool-only, 90 s timeout) that fired after EVERY turn with >=4 new messages — one hidden model call per turn, completely invisible on the ACP wire (no frames, no turn_completion/credit attribution).

Why track: (1) credit attribution gap — once this ramps to external users, per-turn cost rises and cyril cannot see or explain it; (2) product overlap — same surface as cyril-memory (scoped, title-addressed lessons injected at session start + capture), agent-owned and model-driven vs cyril-memory explicit/trust-policed; the vendor-neutral argument strengthens as each agent grows a silo; (3) possible interop later (import/export between ~/.kiro/memories/memories.jsonl and cyril-memory, or suppressing the KAS block when cyril injects its own first-prompt context to avoid double injection).

No wire vocabulary to consume today (no _kiro/memory/* methods, nothing in session/new _meta). Re-check the flag defaults each release audit (clientConfig memory_external_enabled) and the userMemoryOptIn registry key.

Evidence: experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-memory-external-2.19.2.py, kas-memory-external-{on,off}-2.19.2.jsonl, reqdump-kas-memory-extraction-000{2,5}-2.19.2.json.

notes.content: 2026-08-25: CLIENT VETO LEVER verified in KAS 0.52.1 — initialize._meta.kiro.settings.userMemoryOptIn {enabled:false} makes isMemoryEnabled() return false regardless of the AB experiment or the KIRO_FEATURE_MEMORY_EXTERNAL_ENABLED env override (resolveMemoryEnabled reads it only when the key is present; object form {enabled} required). The 2.19.2 TUI maps kiro-cli setting memory.enabled → userMemoryOptIn; cyril's kas/settings.rs BOOL_MAP is the 2.8.1 table and lacks that row, so cyril cannot veto today. title: M2: Teach, forget, and promote memory through MCP and TUI
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Complete the user-controlled memory lifecycle across MCP and TUI. A bound agent can teach an explicit fact or lesson in its current session/project scope and invalidate an editable memory through namespaced tools. The user can inspect the change, forget it, or approve a pending promotion in Cyril. A global write requested by an agent never writes globally; it becomes a pending human decision. Updated state affects subsequent recall and first-prompt context without resurrecting superseded rows.

The demo proves governance rather than raw CRUD: teach a project fact through MCP, recall it, request global promotion, observe the pending TUI item, approve it explicitly, and then recall it from another project. Repeat with refusal and forgetting. An inferred high-confidence value remains narrow and cannot bypass the same policy.

## Placement / boundaries

The memory runtime owns memory types, editability, validation, trust/provenance, conflict resolution, supersession, forgetting semantics, promotion state, audit events, and scope authorization. The MCP adapter exposes namespaced teach and forget operations by translating tool inputs/results only. The TUI owns inspection and explicit approve/refuse interactions but does not re-evaluate scope or conflict rules. The bridge continues to consume the runtime's bounded context result without understanding mutations.

Automatic/model-derived writes remain in the narrowest originating scope. Confidence may affect candidate retention, same-scope conflict resolution, and ranking only; it never authorizes scope widening. Session-to-project promotion requires explicit user action in this slice, and global promotion always does. Fact rows and extracted read-only facts must be distinguishable from editable user memory. Never hard-delete audit history when forgetting; invalidate or tombstone according to the memory type. Do not add knowledge documents, folder ingestion, consolidation, or embeddings here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A bound agent can teach an explicit project fact or lesson through namespaced MCP tools.
- [ ] The same validated write path is used by MCP and TUI teaching actions.
- [ ] New explicit memory is immediately visible to recall and TUI inspection with provenance and audit detail.
- [ ] An agent request for broader or global scope creates a pending promotion instead of widening the write.
- [ ] The TUI can approve or refuse pending promotion; approval changes subsequent scoped recall and refusal does not.
- [ ] Model-reported confidence cannot widen session memory to project or global scope.
- [ ] Forgetting invalidates editable memory, removes it from recall/context, and preserves an audit event.
- [ ] Read-only extracted facts cannot be mutated through the edit tool and return a typed denial.
- [ ] Superseded or out-of-scope rows cannot reappear through fallback behavior.
- [ ] MCP/TUI behavioral tests cover teach, conflict, approve, refuse, forget, read-only denial, and non-widening.

## Blocked by

- cyril-3dqf
design:
## Mechanism contract established by this slice

Memory has three read scopes: current session, current project, and global user. Recall reads them together but preserves origin. For the same structured fact key, the narrowest applicable scope wins (`session` over `project` over `global`); within one scope, user-explicit data wins over derived data. An inferred value can never supersede a user-explicit value. Explicit lessons remain a separate instruction tier and are never resolved as ordinary fact-key conflicts.

A structured fact stores memory ID, validated key, bounded JSON value, scope ID, provenance/trust, optional confidence, active/superseded/invalidated status, evidence references, timestamps, and audit lineage. Confidence has no role in scope authorization. When derived facts arrive later, the write floor is confidence 0.8; within the same scope and trust tier, higher confidence wins, and values within 0.1 are treated as equal so the newer evidenced value wins. This rule does not apply to user-explicit overwrite, which is always an explicit supersession.

MCP teach is treated as user-explicit only within the capability's bound session/project scope. A requested broader scope creates a pending-promotion record containing the source memory ID, target scope, reason, requesting session, and timestamp. It creates no target memory. TUI approval performs one audited superseding write; refusal closes the pending record with no data change. Global promotion is always TUI-approved.

Forgetting invalidates editable lessons/facts and removes them from recall immediately while retaining lineage and audit. Extracted fact projections designated read-only reject update/forget through agent tools; the TUI may invalidate them through its explicit human path. Recall never falls back to superseded or invalidated rows when the winning row is removed or out of scope.

### Semantic facts in first-prompt context

Prompt preparation resolves active facts by key before ranking: current-session beats project beats global, user-explicit beats derived within one scope, and superseded/invalidated rows are removed before any fallback or scoring. The resolved winners render after `CYRIL_LESSONS` and before `CYRIL_EPISODES` in a `CYRIL_FACTS trust="memory-data"` section. Facts are data, never instructions. Each item renders a stable one-line key plus canonical JSON value and a compact scope/provenance label.

Before embeddings land, user-explicit winners rank first; derived winners then rank by literal FTS relevance to the original first user text, confidence, update time, and stable memory ID. With an empty query, recency replaces FTS relevance. The facts section defaults to 4,000 characters and 50 facts, truncates only between facts, and reports omitted count. Combined first-prompt memory defaults to a 12,000-character ceiling: lessons up to 4,000, facts up to 4,000, episodes up to 3,600, with the remainder reserved for framing. Configuration may lower caps but cannot make a section unbounded.

The runtime composes the complete block and returns it through the one prompt-preparation operation. The bridge does not merge sections or re-resolve conflicts.

### Memory mutation tool schemas

`cyril_memory_teach` accepts a strict discriminated object. Common optional fields are `target_scope` (`session`, `project`, or `global`, default `project`) and `reason` (maximum 500 characters). For `kind: lesson`, required `content` is 1-2,000 characters and no fact fields are accepted. For `kind: fact`, required `key` is 1-100 characters matching `^[a-z](?:[a-z0-9_.]{0,98}[a-z0-9])?$`, required `value` is any JSON value whose canonical serialization is at most 4,096 bytes, and no lesson content is accepted. Unknown fields are rejected. Global target never writes directly; it returns a pending promotion.

`cyril_memory_forget` accepts exactly `memory_id` plus optional reason up to 500 characters. It can invalidate only editable memory visible through the bound capability. Unknown, out-of-scope, read-only, already-invalidated, and superseded IDs return typed outcomes without revealing foreign-memory existence.

`cyril_memory_request_promotion` accepts `memory_id`, `target_scope` (`project` or `global`), and optional reason up to 500 characters. It creates or idempotently returns one pending promotion; it never approves it. Only the admin/TUI operations `approve_promotion` and `refuse_promotion` accept a pending promotion ID. Approval rechecks source status and target validity inside the write transaction.

Success results are structured and carry `status` (`stored`, `unchanged`, `pending_promotion`, `invalidated`, `already_invalidated`, `promotion_approved`, or `promotion_refused`), affected opaque IDs, effective scope kind, and safe audit summary. Tool errors reuse the recall errors and add `not_editable`, `conflict_rejected`, `invalid_target_scope`, and `promotion_stale`; all include safe message and retryability. The MCP adapter performs schema translation only; runtime policy remains authoritative.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Teach explicit project facts/lessons through namespaced MCP tools.
- [ ] MCP and TUI share one validated write path.
- [ ] Writes are immediately visible with provenance and audit detail.
- [ ] Broader/global requests create pending promotion rather than widening.
- [ ] TUI approve/refuse changes or preserves subsequent recall correctly.
- [ ] Confidence never widens scope.
- [ ] Forgetting removes editable memory from recall while preserving audit.
- [ ] Read-only extracted facts reject mutation with typed errors.
- [ ] Superseded/out-of-scope rows never resurrect through fallback.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover the full teach/promote/forget lifecycle.
- [ ] First-prompt order and default caps are lessons 4,000 → facts 4,000 → episodes 3,600 under a 12,000-character total, with item-boundary truncation and omitted counts.
- [ ] Fact conflict resolution happens before ranking/rendering; the bridge never merges sections.
- [ ] Teach enforces the discriminated lesson/fact schema, key/value/content/reason bounds, strict unknown-field rejection, and pending global promotion.
- [ ] Forget and promotion-request schemas, structured statuses, and stable typed errors match the Design contract.
