title: KAS RPC sweep: 28 live response shapes captured; 8 methods need param discovery
description:
Live client-callable RPC sweep of the KAS surface (probe-kas-rpc-sweep-2.16.0.py,
capture kas-rpc-sweep-2.16.0.jsonl, kiro-cli 2.16.0 / KAS 0.27.8, 2026-07-31).

Motivation: of 106 KAS method literals, a scan of every committed capture showed
only ~21 had ever been on the wire. This calls every client-callable one and
records the real response, treating typed errors as results.

HEADLINE: **ZERO -32601 across the entire sweep.** Every method dispatches,
including the ~99 NOT listed in `extensionMethods` (which advertises only 7).
Advertisement is not availability on KAS; a client cannot feature-detect by
probing for method-not-found. (Consistent with the sourceProviders finding, now
shown to be the rule rather than a special case.)

28 methods returned a real result. High-value shapes captured:

- _kiro/account/getUsage -> {success, message, data:{planName, billingCycleReset,
  overagesEnabled, isEnterprise, usageBreakdowns[{resourceType, displayName, used,
  limit, percentage, currentOverages, overageRate, overageCharges, currency,
  hasLimit}], bonusCredits[{name, used, total, daysUntilExpiry}], addOnCredits,
  overageCapable}}. This is the KAS equivalent of v2's /usage and is richer than
  what cyril renders today.
- _kiro/permissions/list -> {rules:[{capability, match[], effect, scope, source}]}
  — the actual governance rule set (deny rules over ~/.kiro/settings, .git/**,
  .kiro/agents, .kiro/hooks, ...). This is the permission MODEL, not a prompt.
- _kiro/config/template -> {modes:{availableModes[...]}}
- _kiro/session/export -> {success, filePath} and it WRITES A ZIP as a side
  effect (~/.kiro/exports/kiro-session-<id>.zip). Not read-only; treat with care.
- _kiro/session/{list,rename,compact,delete} all work; compact returns
  {success:true} only when there is history to compact (false on an empty session).
- _session/steer/clear -> {cleared, messageIds[]}
- Full WORKFLOW CONTROL surface works, each with a distinct shape:
    inspect   -> {workflowId, state:<WorkflowState>}
    pause     -> {paused:true}
    resume    -> {workflowId, status}
    cancel    -> {ok:true, previousStatus}
    retry     -> {workflowId, status, retriedNodeIds[]}
    delete    -> {ok:true}
    resumeAll -> {resumed[], skipped[], errors[]}

CONTRACTS DISCOVERED FROM TYPED ERRORS:
- _kiro/spec/{getTaskStatuses,resolveSession} -> -32602 "workspacePaths must be a
  non-empty array" (like _kiro/workflow/list, these need explicit workspace roots).
- _kiro/hooks/setEnabled -> {success:false, code:"invalid_params",
  error:"not available when v2Hooks is disabled"} — a `v2Hooks` gate, previously
  unknown.
- _kiro/sourceProviders/list -> -32000 catalog error (already known).

STILL ERRORING WITH OUR PARAMS (-32603 "Internal error", 8): permissions/explain,
hooks/list, sandbox/status, secret/get, tool/get_diagnostics, _session/steer,
powers/refresh, mcp/toggle. These are NOT auth fallout — the first sweep ran into
token expiry (getAccessToken called 19x, turn failed) and was re-run with a fresh
token (called 1x, turn end_turn, getUsage real); the SAME 11 errors reproduced
identically. So the methods are wired and rejecting our arguments. -32603 is
generic, so the param shapes must come from the bundle, not from guessing.

TWO OTHER OBSERVATIONS:
- fs dialect: advertising kiroFsReadFile/kiroFsWriteFile/kiroFsStat did NOT switch
  KAS off the ACP form — it still called fs/read_text_file. So `_kiro/fs/*` has
  some other trigger, still unknown.
- _kiro/session/history returns {updates:[], hasMore:false} even AFTER a
  successful turn. Either it needs params we did not send, or it is not the
  transcript accessor its name implies. Worth resolving before cyril builds on it.

notes.content:
FOLLOW-UP RESOLVED (probe-kas-rpc-corrections-2.16.0.py, capture
kas-rpc-corrections-2.16.0.jsonl, free — no model turn). Of the 8 methods left on
-32603, only ONE was a genuine param bug. The sweep was wrong about them in three
different ways, and the bundle's dispatch tables settle it.

THE DIRECTION MAP (authoritative, extracted from the bundle):
  47 methods registered client -> agent in src/acp/ext-method-routing.ts
  22 methods the agent sends TO the client (sendClientExtMethod / extNotification):
     _kiro/auth/getAccessToken, governance/state, hooks/{cancel,didChange,
     executeHook,list,sessionStart}, knowledge/indexingStarted, mcp/{elicitation,
     status}, openExternalUrl, policy/{changed,error}, safety/propertiesChanged,
     sandbox/status, secret/{get,store,delete}, sessions/changed,
     spec/taskStatusChanged, system/notify, userInput

1. FIXED — param name. _session/steer wants `message`, not `text`
   (handleSessionSteer). Correct call returns:
       {"queued": true, "messageId": "steer-<uuid>"}
   messageId is prefixed `steer-`, or `notify-` when the message matches
   NOTIFICATION_PREFIX_RE; a caller-supplied messageId is honoured and prefixed.
   Directly useful for the steering work (cyril-vgcm).

2. FIXED — envelope. _kiro/powers/refresh and _kiro/mcp/toggle are handled on the
   NOTIFICATION path (their branch ends `return Promise.resolve()` with no result),
   so sending them as REQUESTS with an id is what produced -32603. Sent as
   notifications they succeed silently AND produce observable pushes:
       _kiro/mcp/status, _kiro/powers/items_changed
   Also sent _kiro/policy/ignore_files_changed as a notification -> the agent
   pushed _kiro/policy/changed. That is a first live observation of policy/changed.

3. CONFIRMED — direction. These four are agent->client and have no agent-side
   handler; calling them as client RPCs is meaningless and -32603 is the honest
   answer. Not defects:
       _kiro/secret/get           (agent asks client for a stored secret)
       _kiro/tool/get_diagnostics (a CLIENT tool, metaKey clientToolGetDiagnostics)
       _kiro/sandbox/status       (push)
       _kiro/hooks/list           (agent asks client: {trigger, sessionId, toolId?,
                                   toolTags?} -> {hooks[]})
   NOTE hooks/list appears in BOTH tables — registered client->agent AND sent
   agent->client. Treat as bidirectional; cyril must be able to ANSWER it.

4. STILL OPEN — _kiro/permissions/explain. handlePermissionsExplain wants
   sessionId plus `capability` OR `toolId`; both forms were tried
   (toolId "fs_read", capability "fs_write" — the latter appears verbatim in
   permissions/list output) and both still return -32603. So the remaining
   failure is deeper than argument naming: the handler dereferences
   session.policySession, which may be unset on a fresh session with no turn.
   Next attempt should run it AFTER a turn, or after a tool call has forced the
   policy engine to initialise.

title: Workflow {{id.output}} can capture a closing pleasantry — silent inter-stage data corruption under a completed run
description:
LIVE on kiro-cli 2.20.1 / KAS 0.54.3, reproduced on a 0.52.1 pin the same hour (so: model/turn-shape, not engine). See docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 6; probe experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-workflow-channels-2.20.1.py.

THE FAILURE MODE CHANGED CHARACTER AND IS NOW WORSE.

2.19.0 failed EMPTY: capturedOutput '' -> the consuming step saw the hole, asked via send_message need_input, and PAUSED the run. Loud and detectable.

2.20.1 fails WRONG: a step told to do its work and stop without a closing message captured 'Done.' — the model's sign-off — and handed THAT to the next step as the payload. The consumer accepted it and the run finished status:'completed' with no error, no warning, no pause. A plausible-looking wrong value propagated through the DAG under a green status.

Measured (2 steps; s1 writes token to a file AND is asked for it in text; s2 receives both channels and writes what it actually saw):
  prompt style 'restate' (asks for a trailing one-word reply): 4/4 live + 1/1 pinned -> capture CORRECT ('ALPHA')
  prompt style 'terse'   (work then signal completion, no restatement): 4 runs -> 'Done.' x3, empty x1 -> capture WRONG
  artifacts file channel: CORRECT in 8/8 runs, both bundles, both styles

So capture correctness is CONTROLLED BY PROMPT SHAPE, not luck — the extractor takes the last assistant message's text entries, so whether the payload is present is a direct consequence of how the step is told to finish.

Impact on cyril:
1. Any workflow rendering that surfaces capturedOutputs must NOT present them as authoritative step results — they may be a sign-off string.
2. 'capture is non-empty => capture worked' is an unsafe check. This audit's own verdict heuristic scored the corrupted run as a pass before it was tightened to compare against the expected value. Do not ship that heuristic.
3. Relevant to the cyril-zd8u renderer work: capturedOutput still has no load-bearing UI, and this is a reason to keep it that way, or to render it explicitly as 'last step message' rather than 'step output'.

Guidance: load-bearing data flow goes through artifacts + files. If {{id.output}} is used, the producing step's prompt MUST demand a trailing restatement of exactly the payload, and the consumer should validate rather than trust.

title: Sharpen the probe-isolation rule: say 'seed under the fake HOME what the probe must observe' (audit found no bad findings)
description:
ORIGINAL PREMISE WAS FALSIFIED — verified 2026-08-30, see docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 9 item 5.

The concern (from KiroCrew AGENTS.md:381-390) was that cyril blanket HOME=<tmp> also relocates ~/.kiro, so a spawned kiro-cli finds an empty ~/.kiro/agents/ and any probe of --agent / set_mode / mode advertisement measures an artificial world. KIRO_HOME is confirmed a real kiro-cli var (it is in kiro own embedded doc index under commands/chat.md keywords, beside KIRO_DATA_DIR).

Audited all ~140 probes in experiments/conductor-spike/. NO past finding is affected:
- Exactly ONE isolated probe spawns `--agent <name>`: probe-v2-tar-allowlist-ab-2.18.1.py, and it SEEDS $HOME/.kiro/agents/tartest.json itself before spawning (lines 32-48). Hermetic — arguably better than the KIRO_HOME split.
- All other probes exercising set_mode/customAgents (plan-handoff, plan-handoff2, plan-to-custom, client-agent) ran with the REAL HOME.
- Every other --agent-looking hit is --agent-engine (engine selection), which does not read the agents dir.
- KAS custom agents ride the wire as _meta.kiro.customAgents, never ~/.kiro/agents/.
- Same class in other ~/.kiro subtrees is handled correctly: probe-kas-powers-2.20.1.py seeds the throwaway HOME with the real powers tree; probe-kas-v2hooks-2.16.0.py creates <workspace>/.kiro/hooks (workspace-relative); probe-kas-nested-agentsmd-2.18.0.py WANTS an empty home-steering dir to isolate workspace steering.

RESIDUAL WORK (all that is left, hence P3): the house rule in feedback_isolate_kiro_probes_with_home says only "HOME=<tmp> + real XDG_DATA_HOME". Every probe author has seeded correctly anyway, but the rule does not SAY to. Add the seeding clause, and note KIRO_HOME as an alternative axis for a probe that wants the real ~/.kiro alongside an isolated home.
acceptance_criteria: The probe-isolation rule states that a probe must seed under the fake HOME whatever it needs to observe, and names KIRO_HOME as the alternative axis. No probe changes required.

title: KAS inlineAgents: probe + expose per-subagent model/effort spawning (dormant _meta.kiro.settings flag)
description:
Discovery (2026-07-17, 2.13.0 KAS bundle static analysis): KAS's invoke_sub_agent tool has a dormant 'inlineAgent' parameter — INLINE_AGENT_SCHEMA {systemPrompt, model?, effort?} — letting the supervising LLM spawn an ephemeral one-off agent with a per-spawn model and reasoning-effort level ('second-opinion reviewer on a different model — without authoring an agent file'). Effort is clamped to the chosen model's catalog-advertised effortLevels; unsupported/omitted falls back one tier below max (belowMax); inline agents inherit parent tools/permissions, never widened. Gated by the 'inlineAgents' AgentSettings key (isSettingEnabled(settings,'inlineAgents'), acp-workspace-connection.ts), default OFF ('Enabled for evals first; flip the default later'). Present + dormant since >=2.11.0 (KAS 0.8.0) with the effort field from the start — release audits never flagged it because the flag never flipped. Sibling gate: 'subagentOrchestration' enables the OrchestrateSubAgent DAG tool the same way.

Why cyril: no on-disk agent config on EITHER engine can express per-agent effort (v2 Agent struct: deny_unknown_fields, no effort field; KAS agent files: no effort field, z.object silently strips strays). This flag is the only per-subagent effort mechanism in Kiro, and it is wire-drivable: cyril can flip it via session/new _meta.kiro.settings on the KAS engine — a capability Kiro's own frontends don't enable yet.

Plan: (1) live A/B probe once auth is available — session/new with settings.inlineAgents enabled vs control; confirm invoke_sub_agent schema gains inlineAgent (visible in tool listing / covenant), have supervisor spawn low-effort + xhigh-effort inline agents, verify effort lands (metadata/effortLevel on subtask, thinking-chunk presence as proxy) and the belowMax clamp. Per feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime: schema-accepted != functional — the flag may be additionally server-gated for evals. (2) If functional, decide cyril exposure: enable-by-default on KAS sessions vs /settings toggle; document in KAS wire audit. Full static evidence recorded in memory reference_kiro_effort_schema_negotiation (KAS inline-agent section).
acceptance_criteria: Live A/B capture proving whether settings.inlineAgents=on changes the invoke_sub_agent schema and whether inline effort levels take effect on the wire (or documented negative result); decision recorded on whether/how cyril enables the flag; KAS wire-audit doc updated.

title: KAS-1 follow-up: auto-refresh kiro token file on stale before getAccessToken reply (wrapper mode)
description:
KAS-1 Part B (cyril-evwh) ships the wrapper auth responder reading ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json -> {accessToken,expiresAt,profileArn}. In WRAPPER mode KAS injects --auth=acp-callback and stops self-refreshing the file, so a STALE token (expiresAt <= now+180s) would be a known-bad reply. KAS-1 returns an actionable Err on stale (user re-runs kiro-cli login). THIS = automate it: on stale, trigger kiro-cli's own refresh (PROBE candidates: kiro-cli whoami/profile/user; OR the file-auth refresh path KAS itself uses) so the reply stays valid >now+3min WITHOUT reimplementing OIDC. Falsifier C9 (.cyril-evwh/design.md): force/await stale file, run candidate refresh, assert expiresAt advances >now+3min. DEFERRED from KAS-1: token was fresh during the build (staleness needs ~1h). is_stale() unit logic already lands in kas::auth; only the refresh trigger + live verification deferred here.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-03 (convergent live evidence from cyril-cb93, PR #84): NOT wrapper-only. The FREE-PATH sqlite responder + the C14a spawn gate hit the same wall: a live run failed at session-create with 'kiro token expired; run kiro-cli login' -> BridgeDisconnected; running ANY kiro-cli command (user whoami) refreshed the sqlite store and cyril then worked. Social-login tokens expire in ~1h (post-y14u both rows are read), so this now bites routinely. Refresh probe confirmed live: 'kiro-cli user whoami' advances the store. Scope should cover both spawn modes + the spawn gate, not just the wrapper callback path.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review — four robustness requirements the implementation must state explicitly (the shell-out is inherently fragile: it relies on an undocumented side effect kiro could remove any release; probe-gating via falsifier C9 is the right mitigation and stays):
(1) tokio::process only, never std::process — the responder runs on the single-threaded bridge (auth.rs:52-54 non-blocking rationale applies doubly to spawning a process).
(2) A timeout — kiro-cli can hang on network.
(3) A single-flight guard so concurrent getAccessToken requests don't spawn N refresh processes.
(4) NEVER trust the exit code — re-read and re-validate via the existing read_token_file + is_stale after the refresh attempt; treat the shell-out purely as a best-effort trigger.
The safe fallback (actionable -32000 Err on stale, auth.rs:159-164) stays load-bearing: refresh failure degrades to today's behavior, never a known-bad reply.

REFRAMED BY cyril-dcc6 DESIGN (2026-07-04): once dcc6 lands, the getAccessToken responder reads the CLI sqlite store (auth_kv token + state profileArn), not ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json — so this issue's 'auto-refresh the token FILE' premise is obsolete. What remains in scope here: the STALE-SQLITE-TOKEN policy. The responder keeps its is_stale() 3-min-buffer gate and errors actionably ('run kiro-cli login'); cyril cannot auto-refresh without consuming the CLI's single-use refresh token (see reference_kiro_kas_launch_contract — refresh-less relay is the safe contract). Likely resolution: early stale detection + a re-login affordance in the UI, not refresh.

PARTIALLY ABSORBED BY PR-39 REVIEW FIXES (2026-07-04): the 'early stale detection' half is now implemented — the free-path spawn gate (store_unservable_reason, auth.rs) applies the same is_stale check as the responder, so a known-expired login fails the spawn actionably instead of dying on the first callback (review finding F3; decision log .cyril-dcc6/review-decisions.md). REMAINING SCOPE: the mid-session case — a UI re-login affordance when a callback returns the -32000 stale error (pairs with cyril-l7tw's App-notification work).

2026-07-26 (measured during PR #68 review) — A THIRD REFRESH CANDIDATE, simpler than the shell-out: the fresh token is directly readable from kiro-cli's own SQLite store. `~/.local/share/kiro-cli/data.sqlite3`, table `auth_kv`, row key `kirocli:social:token` (also `kirocli:odic:token` / `kirocli:external-idp:token` depending on auth method) holds PLAINTEXT JSON {access_token, expires_at, profile_arn, provider, refresh_token} — snake_case, and profile_arn is already in the row. This is the store kiro-cli refreshes INTO, which is exactly why the ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token*.json this issue reads goes stale. Reading auth_kv would avoid reimplementing OIDC *and* avoid the undocumented-side-effect fragility the notes above flag for the whoami/profile shell-out. It trades one fragility for another (another program's DB schema + file locking), so it needs the same C9-style falsifier — but it belongs on the candidate list, which currently does not mention it. Evidence: docs/kiro-2.14.1-wire-audit.md fresh-token recipe.

CORRECTION (same day, after learning the measurement was taken under GitHub SOCIAL auth): the above is n=1 and does NOT generalize — which matters here because cyril's users will not all use the same login. Binary evidence: 'social token has no profile ARN, treating as invalid' (social MUST carry profile_arn in the row) vs 'Lazily resolved profileArn from list_available_profiles' (other methods resolve it via an API call, so it is NOT in the row), plus 'Error getting builder id token from keychain' (Builder ID has an OS-keychain path distinct from the DB row). So under IdC/Builder ID the row key is kirocli:odic:token, profileArn must still come from elsewhere, and the token may not be in auth_kv at all. => Any auto-refresh implementation must branch on auth method and cannot assume a single store shape; the C9-style falsifier needs an arm per login type (social / IdC / external-IdP), not one arm. Treat auth_kv as a candidate for social only until the others are measured.

title: KAS auth: --auth=machine / KIRO_API_KEY bypass _kiro/auth/getAccessToken — simpler fallback path
description: Static analysis of @kiro/agent (present in 0.3.299 AND 0.8.0, i.e. not new but previously undocumented for us): acp-server.js selectAuthProvider priority = (1) KIRO_API_KEY env -> EnvAuthProvider, (2) --auth=acp-callback -> AcpCallbackAuthProvider (current cyril path, host-mediated refresh, profileArn gotcha), (3) --auth=machine -> FileAuthProvider plain-text token at tokenPath or /tmp/access_token, (4) explicit tokenPath JSON, (5) default ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json. Modes 1/3/4/5 never call _kiro/auth/getAccessToken. Option value: degraded-mode fallback when the callback path breaks (e.g. profileArn rotation bugs), and a simpler harness for probes. Note kiro-cli's own spawn of KAS may pin --auth=acp-callback; direct-spawn is where this pays off.
acceptance_criteria: Documented in KAS integration notes; optionally a bridge config knob to direct-spawn KAS with --auth=machine for diagnostics

notes.content: Closed: Already covered: launch-contract memory (2026-06-21 server-side ground truth) documents selectAuthProvider priority incl. --auth=machine/KIRO_API_KEY, and the no-callback free path was empirically confirmed on 2.8.1; cyril-taba tracks the practical token-staleness gap. 2.11.0 audit confirmed the auth layer is byte-identical in 0.8.0 — no new work item.

title: Scoped notification arriving before any main session falls through to the main pipeline
description: Discovered during cyril-fh06 (PR #54): app.rs routing diverts scoped frames only when session.id().is_some() (app.rs:291 at time of finding) — a RoutedNotification::scoped frame arriving before the main session exists is applied to the main SessionController/UiState instead of being dropped or buffered. Shared by both scoped producers (ToolCallChunk and MetadataUpdated). Not reachable in practice today (both frame kinds follow session creation), so P4/backlog — but it is a latent ordering assumption; decide drop vs buffer and fence it.
acceptance_criteria: A scoped notification delivered before SessionCreated does not mutate main-session state; decision (drop vs buffer) documented in the routing code; regression test covers the pre-session scoped frame.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #74 (aab5bcda7). Repro: pre_session_scoped_frame_spares_main - a scoped notification delivered before SessionCreated no longer mutates main SessionController/UiState. classify_notification_route gained a Drop route and the caller became a condition-free match; drop chosen over buffer (rationale in the routing code).

title: KAS-4 — Model the 4 new initialize capability keys: executionTargets/sessionSources/sessionListScopes/sourceProviders (2.12.3)
description: KAS 0.17.2 (kiro-cli 2.12.3) adds four _meta.kiro capability keys on the initialize response: executionTargets (["local"] | +"cloud-sandbox"), sessionSources (["local"] | +"remote"), sessionListScopes (["workspace"] | +"user"), sourceProviders (bool; gates _kiro/sourceProviders/list + listResources). Standalone CLI reports the dormant local-only values. Per the model-full-wire-surface rule, cyril's KAS handshake types (KAS-1/KAS-2 lane) must model or explicit-ignore these. They are the advertisement surface for Kiro cloud/remote agents (remote session store, cloud-sandbox relay, GITHUB/GITLAB/MIDWAY source-provider catalog). Reference: docs/kiro-2.12.3-wire-audit.md; capture experiments/conductor-spike/logs/kas-host-init-2.12.3-20260715.json.

notes.content:
2.16.0 status (docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md, 'Cloud / remote-agent stack'): the four capability keys are UNCHANGED and still dormant (sourceProviders:false, executionTargets:[local], sessionSources:[local], sessionListScopes:[workspace]), and both _kiro/sourceProviders/* methods are present and unmodified in the 109-literal set.

NEW and relevant to this issue: the cloud stack's per-session fields reached the wire on a purely LOCAL run for the first time. _kiro/sessions/changed now carries upserted[].source ('local') and upserted[].executionTarget.kind ('local') — live-verified A/B 2.15.0 vs 2.16.0. These are the same fields that carry 'remote' / 'cloud-sandbox' once KIRO_REMOTE_SESSIONS_ENDPOINT is set, so whatever models the four caps should model these two alongside them.

Also note for any future probing: sourceProviders dispatch is UNCONDITIONAL — an unadvertised call returns typed -32000 'no source provider catalog is configured', NOT -32601. Feature-detecting the cloud stack by probing for method-not-found does not work.

Underneath, the cloud-config transport moved to a generated Smithy client (http-cloud-config-transport.ts + inert-cloud-config-source.ts removed, smithy-cloud-config-transport.ts added) and most src/session/bff-*.ts changed. Wire-neutral; recorded as churn, not a launch signal.

2.17.0 status change: the dormant cloud stack these capability keys belong to went LIVE ('V3 cloud sessions preview to all users', kiro-cli --cloud). KAS acp-server.js unchanged (byte-identical 0.35.11) — the remote side runs the same bundle; new Rust-side control-plane types visible in kiro-cli-chat strings (ListSessionsRequest, SessionSteerRequest, SettingsSet/ListRequest, ProcessHealthPayload, executionTarget). Modeling these initialize keys is now against a SHIPPING feature, not a dormant one.

title: KAS hooks host: execute SessionStart hooks + inject precomputed context (needs AcpPrecomputedHookResult shape)
description: DEFERRED FROM cyril-jiyn (pause decision was 'execute sessionStart hooks'). cyril acknowledges _kiro/hooks/sessionStart with {results:[]} (wire-safe, matches the 2.7.1 host probe). Full execution means running the SessionStart command hooks AND packaging stdout into AcpPrecomputedHookResult[] the agent injects as context — but that element shape is NOT verifiable from the standalone bundle (it consumes response.results opaquely) and the @kiro/acp-type-covenant .d.ts is not installed locally. Blocked on: obtain the covenant hooks types.d.ts (AcpPrecomputedHookResult fields), then execute + package. Do NOT guess the shape (reference_feedback: schema-vs-runtime; verify covenant .d.ts FIRST). Probe: extend .cyril-jiyn/probe-hooks-ab-2.13.0.py to capture a live sessionStart callback payload/response under an authenticated turn.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #63 merged to main (a0f34d0). SessionStart hooks execute in the hooks host, output packaged as the carved+live-verified AcpPrecomputedHookResult shape and injected as HOOK_INSTRUCTION context; typed HookRunOutcome core with executeHook wire pinned unchanged; per-hook file timeout (seconds, default 60); 21 fences incl. Windows + non-blocking. Fixed in-branch: fence-probe profileArn bug (poisoned every KAS probe turn since ~2.13.0; jiyn A/B prompt_completed caveat recorded). Filed: cyril-4rc1 (round-2 review). Deferred: askAgent packaging cyril-n03f, hot-reload cyril-2adk.

title: Probe kiro-cli XDG_DATA_HOME handling — cyril hardcodes ~/.local/share/kiro-cli (KAS root + credential store)
description: PR-39 review finding (failure-hunter #10, code-reviewer S5): discovery.rs derives both the KAS extraction root and data.sqlite3 from the hardcoded KIRO_DATA_DIR_REL='.local/share/kiro-cli'. The 2.11.0 kiro-cli binary contains the XDG_DATA_HOME string (3 hits — dirs-crate pattern), so it plausibly honors it; if a user sets XDG_DATA_HOME, kiro-cli would extract/login elsewhere and cyril would emit loud-but-WRONG 'not found'/'not servable' errors while kiro-cli itself works. Probe: XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/x kiro-cli login + self-extract, check where data.sqlite3 and kas/<ver>-<sha>/ land. If honored: read the env var (absolute paths only) with ~/.local/share fallback — one-line change now that KIRO_DATA_DIR_REL is the single spelling. Related: cyril-lwpm (Windows-host store path).

title: KAS host-io Windows: auto-detect the default WSL distro when none is configured
description: cyril-8tq6 ships explicit distro resolution only (CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO env override, else derived from a \\wsl$\<distro>\... process cwd). When neither source is set on a Windows host, WSL-internal paths still pass through untranslated (honest NotFound). A zero-config fallback would query the host's default distro: wsl.exe -l -q / wsl.exe --status (CAUTION: wsl.exe output is UTF-16LE and --status wording is localized) or registry HKCU\...\Lxss DefaultDistribution -> DistributionName. Needs a real Windows host to validate; deliberately excluded from cyril-8tq6 to keep that PR pure-logic testable on Linux CI.

title: Ctrl+M mouse-capture path is untested end-to-end (no injectable terminal-command seam)
description:
Raised in review of PR #70 (cyril-nd4h).

state::tests::mouse_capture_toggles_from_either_starting_state fences UiState::toggle_mouse_capture directly. It never drives App::handle_key and never observes the crossterm command actually emitted, so it would still pass if Ctrl+M emitted the wrong command, failed to invoke the helper at all, or mishandled the rollback-on-error path (app.rs ~518-530).

The same blind spot now covers startup: main.rs emits EnableMouseCapture and App::set_mouse_captured rolls the flag back on failure, and no test observes either. cyril-nd4h's source-scan fence proves the guard is STRUCTURALLY correct (that the call guards the branch) but cannot prove the emitted command is right.

Fix needs an injectable boundary for terminal commands (a trait or fn pointer App writes through, instead of calling crossterm::execute! inline) so a test can assert the exact command sequence from both starting states. That is an architectural change to App's terminal I/O and was judged disproportionate to cyril-nd4h, whose scope is the config surface.

Would also unlock testing DisableMouseCapture on the exit path and bracketed-paste sequencing.

title: Consolidate center-scroll window helpers and test buffer-flattening duplicated across widgets
description: Addendum (PR #58 gemini review, 7 comments, all one finding — verified valid): the shared buffer-flattening helper should use direct indexing buffer[(x,y)].symbol() rather than defensive .cell().map_or(...) — in-bounds is guaranteed by fixture geometry and direct indexing is the existing house test idiom (input.rs buffer_rows). Deferred here rather than patched 7 times pre-merge.

title: Re-run the KAS OrchestrateSubAgent live capture to confirm the {task, stages, repeat} wire shape
description:
Confirm the KAS OrchestrateSubAgent {task, stages[], repeat} wire shape.

FULLY RESOLVED 2026-08-01 on kiro-cli 2.16.0 / KAS 0.27.8. All three parts captured
live. Probes: probe-kas-inconclusive-rerun-2.16.0.py (task+stages) and
probe-kas-orchestrate-repeat-2.16.0.py (repeat). Captures:
kas-inconclusive-2.16.0.jsonl, kas-repeat-shape-2.16.0.jsonl.

THE UNLOCK: `subagentOrchestration` must be sent in **initialize._meta.kiro.settings**.
The session/new form does NOT work; only the initialize form runs through
bridgeFeatureFlags() and overrides the backend model-config flag that prompts.ts reads
via getDelegationToolId(). The earlier "backend-gated / unreachable" conclusion was wrong.

MEASURED rawInput:
  { "task": "produce a one-word colour name",
    "stages": [ { "name": "pick", "role": "inline",
                  "prompt_template": "...",
                  "inlineAgent": { "systemPrompt": "..." } } ],
    "repeat": { "maxIterations": 2,
                "stopCondition": { "containsText": "ZZUNREACHABLEZZ" },
                "onMaxIterations": "continue" } }

  stage keys : name, role, prompt_template, depends_on?, inlineAgent?
  repeat keys: maxIterations (1-20), stopCondition{containsText}, onMaxIterations
               ("continue"|"abort", nullish, default continue)

DO NOT CONFLATE with the workflow DAG's `repeat` NODE — they are different types:
  OrchestrateSubAgent repeat: maxIterations 1-20, stopCondition containsText ONLY,
                              onMaxIterations continue|abort
  workflow repeat node:       maxIterations 1-1000, stopCondition containsText|fileCheck
                              (or stopWhen), onMaxIterations abort|continue|PAUSE

RENDER CONTRACT — the tool_call carries _meta.kiro.pipeline:
  { "groupId": "pipeline-<first-30-chars-of-task-slugged>",
    "stages": [ { "name", "role", "status", "dependsOn": [], "agentSubtaskId": "<uuid>" } ] }

** RENDERING TRAP (measured across a 2-iteration loop): the pipeline meta has NO
iteration counter. groupId is constant and stages[] keeps ONE entry per stage, whose
status cycles pending -> running -> completed -> running -> completed. A client
rendering from pipeline meta alone cannot distinguish iteration 1 from 2 — the stage
appears to "un-complete". The discriminator is agentSubtaskId: 6 agent-subtask frames
carried 2 DISTINCT agentSubtaskIds, one per iteration. Key iteration identity on
agentSubtaskId, never on stage name or pipeline status. **

This is the same class of bug as the workflow nodePath/iteration finding: the obvious
grouping key silently collapses iterations.

Acceptance criteria satisfied: capture completed with stopReason end_turn and non-zero
tool frames; rawInput captured showing stages[] AND repeat on the wire; CLAUDE.md's
static-evidence caveat replaced with the measured result; redacted captures committed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A capture completes with stopReason set and non-zero tool frames.
2. An OrchestrateSubAgent tool_call rawInput is captured showing whether stages[]/repeat appear on the wire as the schema predicts.
3. The audit doc and CLAUDE.md static-evidence caveat are replaced with the measured result (or the claim is corrected if the wire disagrees).
4. The redacted capture is committed and the attempt summary superseded.

title: Usage log: persist provider request IDs, not just their count
description:
crates/cyril-core/src/usage.rs:263 consumes TurnMeteringUpdate.request_ids() only to derive provider_requests:

    if let Some(request_ids) = update.request_ids() {
        pending.provider_requests = match u64::try_from(request_ids.len()) { ... }

The cardinality is kept and the identity is discarded. The IDs already arrive on the wire — KAS session_info_update kind 'turn_completion' carries requestIds[] (see docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 8) — and TurnMeteringUpdate already models them.

WHY IT MATTERS: the request ID is the only handle that correlates a cyril turn with an AWS-side request. It is the primary column in v2's own hidden /stats panel (reference_kiro_v2_stats_command). Without it, a user reporting 'this turn failed' cannot be matched to a backend request for support or log-chasing, and cyril cannot cross-reference its own usage log against anything server-side. Also note the stall error carries its own requestId in the -32000 data (section 2) — being able to join those is the point.

SCOPE: store the IDs alongside the turn record (a usage_turn_request_ids child table, or a JSON column on usage_turns — pick per the existing schema style in usage.rs), keep provider_requests as the derived count, expose them via the snapshot/record accessors, and cover with a test that a multi-request turn round-trips every ID. One captured turn carried 4 IDs, so plural is the normal case, not an edge case.

NOT in scope: per-request timings — see the non-goal in the usage.rs module docs (cyril cannot observe individual provider requests from the ACP layer).

title: KAS-5b — terminal host-callback responders (terminal/* + shell_type)
description:
KAS-5b: the terminal half of host I/O, split from cyril-7bdu (KAS-5a = fs read/write). Implement the typed acp::Client terminal methods cyril must answer when it advertises the terminal capability: create_terminal {sessionId, command, args, cwd}, terminal_output {sessionId, terminalId}, wait_for_terminal_exit {sessionId, terminalId}, release_terminal, kill_terminal (+ _kiro/terminal/shell_type {sessionId}). Wire shapes captured @ 2.10.0 in .cyril-7bdu/host_callbacks_2.10.0.json (bare ACP methods, every call carries sessionId, cwd absolute).

REUSES the KAS-5a seam (.cyril-7bdu/falsifiable-design.md): cap advertisement via Engine::client_capabilities() (add terminal:true), the ADR-0004 loop host-io mediation arm, the non-blocking-resolver invariant, and platform::path translation. Terminal STRESSES the non-blocking invariant hardest: a shell command can run up to 60s, so create_terminal must return a terminalId immediately and wait_for_terminal_exit must await via tokio::process (NOT a thread-pinning std::process wait) or it starves the single-threaded bridge runtime (rpc.rs spawns each request, but the runtime is current_thread+LocalSet). terminalIds must be unique across concurrent terminals; output/wait/release/kill on an unknown id must error, not panic. create with a nonexistent command must error, not panic the bridge.

DEPENDS ON KAS-5a (cyril-7bdu) for the seam. Run its own falsifiable-design pass before build.

notes.content: Closed: Merged in PR #36 (feat/kas-5-host-io -> main, c89a1f0). fs (5a) + terminal (5b) host-callback responders shipped; review fixes (stdin=null, logged reaps, wedge-on-error, cross-platform test gating) in a128633. CI green on Linux/macOS/Windows. Follow-ups remain as separate issues (3lh8, 0v42, 8tq6, g9vt, r3t6, 1rpv, ihj1).

title: Foreign-session AllowAlways can persist into the main agent config
description: Design review for cyril-z4eo found that UiState::approval_confirm returns only TrustOption, while App::persist_trust_grant selects SessionController::current_mode_id from the main session. A permission originating in a non-main/subagent/peer session can therefore send the correct wire response but persist its patterns into the main agent's on-disk config. cyril-z4eo will preserve the origin through trust confirmation and must not write a foreign grant into the main config; this issue owns durable persistence for foreign grants once session-to-agent-config ownership is available.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A foreign-session AllowAlways grant is never written to the main session's agent config. 2. The originating session is retained through trust confirmation. 3. If the foreign session's owning agent config is known, persist to that config; otherwise report that the grant is session-scoped only. 4. Main-session persistence remains unchanged and regression tests cover both origins.

title: clippy expect_used is deny-in-practice for tests despite the warn-level intent; add clippy.toml allow-expect-in-tests
description:
`clippy::expect_used` is set to "warn" at the workspace level with the comment
"tests legitimately use `.expect()`", but CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets
-D warnings`, which promotes every warning to an error. So the stated intent —
that tests may use `.expect()` — does not actually hold.

Worse, it fires ASYMMETRICALLY: `Option::expect` trips the lint inside a `#[test]`
fn while `Result::expect` does not. Existing integration tests happen to use only
the `Result` form, which is why this stayed invisible until a new test file used
the `Option` form.

Hit during the cyril-imjx sweep fix (PR #75) in
crates/cyril-ui/tests/picker_active_marker.rs. Worked around with
`let ... else { panic!(...) }` rather than an `#[allow]`, since CLAUDE.md forbids
`#[allow(...)]` directives outright. The workaround is noisier than the `.expect()`
it replaces and does not generalize.

Fix: add a `clippy.toml` at the workspace root with

    allow-expect-in-tests = true

(and consider `allow-unwrap-in-tests` alongside it, matching the same stated
intent for `unwrap_used`, which is "deny" at workspace level). That makes the
declared policy real instead of aspirational, and removes the incentive to write
`let ... else { panic!() }` boilerplate in tests.

Verify after: a test using `Option::expect` compiles under
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the non-test `unwrap_used`/
`expect_used` discipline is unchanged.

Discovered 2026-08-01 during the sweep-bugs batch.

title: ActiveTurn omits engine, so the wire-companion expectation registers for v2 too
description:
cyril-a71q's design specifies the active-turn record as {owner, engine, session} and the mediation policy as: on release, "register the wire companion expectation (KAS ONLY)".

The shipped `ActiveTurn` omits `engine`, so the registration is unconditional. Every release — v1/v2 included — leaves a session-keyed `Wire` expectation dangling in the companion ledger.

Benign today, verified: only `convert/kas.rs` produces an identity-free (unstamped) TurnCompleted, so under v2 the dangling Wire expectation can never be matched and is simply replaced by the next release. The ledger stays bounded at one entry either way.

It is a latent trap rather than a live defect. If any future v2/v1 path ever emitted an unstamped completion — a converter arm, a synthesized recovery frame — it would be absorbed as a phantom companion for a turn that had already released, and the real turn would lose its release. The guard the design specified is what prevents that, and it is absent.

Fix: carry the engine on ActiveTurn (the value is already known at dispatch — run_loop holds `engine: Rc<dyn Engine>`) and gate the Wire-expectation registration on it. Add a fence asserting a v2 release leaves the ledger empty.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ActiveTurn carries the engine captured at dispatch.
2. The Wire companion expectation is registered only under KAS.
3. A fence asserts a v2 turn's release leaves the companion ledger empty.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #76 (c413d9bcf). Repro: v2_release_leaves_companion_ledger_empty - before the fix a dangling Wire expectation from turn 1 absorbed turn 2's completion, leaving turn 2 stuck busy. ActiveTurn now carries the engine and owes_wire_companion() gates the Wire registration to KAS. Second fence wire_companion_is_owed_only_under_kas pins the engine x companion matrix.

title: host_io write_atomic root-CI fixture: root writes into 0o555 read-only parent
description: Discovered during the cyril-jwi5 sweep fix (PR #86): protocol::kas::host_io::tests::write_atomic_unwritable_parent_errs_target_intact (host_io.rs:494) fails under euid 0 — verified failing under 'unshare -r cargo nextest'. Root bypasses permission bits, so the 0o555 unwritable-parent fixture happily writes and the expected error never occurs. Same bug class as cyril-jwi5; same remedy: a geteuid().is_root() skip guard with a logged reason, mirroring the one PR #86 added to host_shell.rs system_host_checks_effective_execute_permission.

title: NON-GOAL: per-provider-request usage granularity (unobtainable from the ACP layer)
description:
Filed as a documented non-goal so it is not re-litigated. Recorded in the crates/cyril-core/src/usage.rs module docs, which is where an implementer would look.

THE ASK THAT WILL RECUR: 'cyril's usage log should show per-request rows like kiro-cli's hidden /stats does' — one row per backend request with its own duration and time-to-first-chunk.

WHY IT CANNOT BE DONE: a single turn fans out into several backend requests (one captured turn_completion carried 4 requestIds). kiro-cli can show per-request rows because IT issues those calls and instruments them in-process — chat_cli_v2::agent::acp::request_stats, a Mutex<VecDeque<RequestRecord>> ring buffer (see memory reference_kiro_v2_stats_command).

Cyril sits one layer above, on ACP. It observes the turn boundary and, at turn end, an aggregate requestIds[] — never the individual requests, their start times, or their first bytes. The information is not on the wire cyril reads, so no amount of observer work recovers it. provider_requests is therefore a COUNT, and turn-level duration_ms / ttft_ms cannot be decomposed per request.

WHAT IS IN SCOPE INSTEAD:
- cyril-uefh — persist the request IDs themselves (enables correlating a turn with backend-side records; does NOT yield per-request timings)
- cyril-9kyk — p90 percentiles on the turn-level latencies

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS: only kiro emitting per-request timing on the wire. It does not today; /stats keeps that data process-local and does not expose it over ACP (stats is absent from every v2 commands/available capture). Re-open only if a wire audit shows per-request timing frames.

Evidence: docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 8.

title: Make the hooks panel responsive
description:
## What to build

Render hooks through a responsive table that keeps all hook meaning accessible on narrow terminals. Wide views retain Trigger, Command, and Matcher columns; narrow views stack matcher information beneath the command instead of dropping it.

## Blocked by

- cyril-cc5e
- cyril-nrnq
- cyril-a14l
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Wide terminals render the three-column hooks table with correct Unicode cell alignment.

title: _kiro/powers/*: render installed powers; refresh is declared-but-unimplemented
description:
kiro-cli 2.20.1 added a /powers TUI command. The WIRE surface is older — present in KAS 0.52.1 and 0.54.3 — and cyril has never rendered it. See docs/kiro-2.20.1-wire-audit.md section 3.

A power = an installable MCP-server bundle at ~/.kiro/powers/installed/<name>/mcp.json, registry-tracked via installed.json, mentionable as @powers.

Live findings:
- _kiro/powers/list takes NO params, returns {powers:[], errors:[]}. NOT advertised in agentCapabilities._meta.kiro.extensionMethods (still 23 entries) but dispatches fine.
- _kiro/powers/items_changed is SESSION-SCOPED and pushed UNPROMPTED at session creation with the full list — cyril never needs to call list() to populate. Shape: {sessionId, status:'success', powers:[...]}.
- _kiro/powers/refresh is DECLARED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED: -32603 Internal error, data.details 'Unknown ext method: _kiro/powers/refresh'. Do not call it. Trap for any client assuming declared => callable.

Item schema (live):
  {name, description, displayName, keywords[], mcpServerNames[], hasSteeringFiles, isAgentPlugin,
   _meta:{kiro:{resource:{resourceType:'power', source:{origin:'user'}}}}}

Scope: consume items_changed to populate a powers view; do NOT wire a refresh affordance to the unimplemented method.

title: KAS 0.38.7: run-level workflow 'paused' now arrives pre-run_complete — tolerate both orderings, key immediacy off node_paused
description:
kiro-cli 2.18.0 ships @kiro/agent 0.38.7, which consolidates run-level 'paused' emission on _kiro/workflow/* from 5 sites to 3: the park sites (executeNode pauseRequested, parkPausedWatch, repeat onMaxIterations:pause) no longer emit run-level paused inline or flip run status at park time. A single new run-loop site emits paused {workflowId, pauseReason, ...attribution} immediately before the NON-TERMINAL run_complete, AFTER the executor unwinds. Two consequences: (1) paused always carries attribution now (the repeat path previously sent it bare); (2) it arrives LATE — node_paused (unchanged, 12=12 sites, node-first ordering) is the only immediate pause signal.

Impact: cyril-6beh's WorkflowTracker was TDD'd against three committed 2.16.0 captures that predate this — the state machine must tolerate BOTH orderings (park-time paused AND pre-run_complete paused). cyril-zd8u's renderer and cyril-0qe6's /workflow commands must key pause chips / approvals prompts off node_paused, treating run-level paused as a summary frame.

Evidence: static diff of acp-server.js 0.35.11 vs 0.38.7 (2.18.0 audit, 2026-08-13); markParkSnapshotConsistent 3→0, markAncestorsPausedAlongPath 2→0 (pre-marking machinery removed). See memory reference_kiro_2_18_0_diff + experiments/conductor-spike captures.

notes.content: Closed: PR #96 merged — pause-ordering compatibility fenced; both orderings + attribution tolerated, node_paused stays the immediate signal

title: Bridge hang: kiro security-filter interrupt emits marker chunk then NEVER sends session/prompt response — is_busy wedges forever
description: When the kiro-cli built-in, non-overridable security filter cancels every tool use in an assistant turn (e.g. shell commands containing sensitive keywords), it emits a plain agent_message_chunk with the EXACT text "Tool uses were interrupted, waiting for the next user prompt" and returns to idle WITHOUT ever sending the session/prompt response. The cyril bridge derives TurnCompleted from that response, so this wedges toolbar.is_busy true forever — the event loop never recovers and every subsequent Enter is swallowed. KiroCrew (a sibling ACP client hardened by 39k users) ships a workaround: exact-after-strip match on the chunk text (exact, not substring, so a model merely QUOTING the marker in prose cannot end a turn), synthesize turn completion, keep the chunk visible to the user, and audit-log the event since it is a permission decision made outside client control.
acceptance_criteria: Live repro captured first via KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH confirming no session/prompt response follows the marker (per the schema-vs-runtime rule — the KiroCrew claim is code-documented, not capture-proven); marker detected with exact-after-strip comparison and TurnCompleted synthesized so is_busy clears; the chunk text still reaches the chat as a visible message; detection does NOT fire on a substring or mid-prose quote (regression test with the marker embedded in a longer chunk); the quirk recorded in docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md with the capture as provenance.

notes.content: Source: kirocrew @ e44259ce src/kiro_crew/acp/client.py:553-565 (_TOOL_INTERRUPTED_MARKER, exact-match rationale), applied at all 3 prompt-dispatch paths (3070/3203/3701). Critic-VERIFIED in code; NOT yet a committed cyril capture — verify live first with KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH + a bash prompt containing a sensitive keyword (e.g. credentials). See docs/kirocrew-deep-dive.md top adoption #1.

2.19.0 reprobe note: the new v2 stream-idle watchdog (api.streamIdleSoftTimeout/HardTimeout, audit docs/kiro-2.19.0-wire-audit.md) does NOT cover this scenario — it guards an OPEN response stream for silence, while w0vy is the engine ending the stream normally and then never emitting the session/prompt response (no stream in flight for the watchdog to time out). Workaround still required. Related new vocab: stream_stall_notice/retry_warning rendering is cyril-svi2.

If it does not, the only escape today is quitting cyril. Until then cancel-under-stall stays UNVERIFIED: the healthy-streaming cancel (cyril-14ou probe, turn_end{cancelled} in 4.3s) is explicitly NOT proof for the blocked-stream case. cyril-14ou ships the indicator with this limitation recorded.

title: M3: Register and synchronize a folder source safely
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Extend the cited knowledge path with a human-confirmed folder source that stays synchronized safely. `/library` previews the canonical root, eligible file count, estimated chunks, configured limits, and exclusions before any content is read into the library. After confirmation, Cyril scans supported documents, indexes them through the existing document path, reports progress, updates changed files, removes vanished documents, and preserves searchable citations.

The demo covers lifecycle and safety: confirm a small folder, search a cited result, change one file and see only that document refresh, delete it and see the result disappear, and add an identical copy under another source and see one stored document retain both source locations. Sensitive roots, unreadable entries, and links escaping the confirmed root are refused or reported without silently indexing them.

## Placement / boundaries

The knowledge module owns source configuration, canonical containment, supported-document filtering, ignore rules, bounded walking, per-document state, change detection, deletion, incremental jobs, document-level deduplication, and alternate source locations. It must reuse the existing validated document ingestion/search interface rather than creating a second chunk/index path. The runtime owns scheduling, cancellation, checkpoints, and progress events. The TUI owns preview, explicit confirmation, pause/resume/remove actions, and progress projection only.

Canonicalize and validate at each filesystem boundary, including again immediately before opening a file. Refuse sensitive paths and symlink/junction escapes. Distinguish missing, unreadable, unsupported, skipped, failed, and deleted outcomes. Cap files, bytes, chunks, and work per sweep; zero or invalid configuration must not accidentally mean unbounded. Deduplication is per document, not per aggregate source, and deleting one source must not remove a document still owned by another location. Do not add automatic project scanning, URL sources, embeddings, or graph extraction in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/library` previews canonical root, eligible/capped files, estimated chunks, limits, and exclusions before ingestion.
- [ ] No folder content is indexed until the user explicitly confirms the preview.
- [ ] Confirmed scans ingest supported documents through the existing single-document path and expose checkpointed progress.
- [ ] Changed files refresh only their own document; vanished files remove their searchable chunks.
- [ ] Sensitive roots, unreadable entries, and link/junction escapes are refused or reported with distinct outcomes.
- [ ] Path containment is revalidated immediately before each file open to close replacement races.
- [ ] File, byte, chunk, and per-sweep limits are enforced without silently treating invalid values as unbounded.
- [ ] Identical documents collapse to one stored copy while preserving every source location and citation.
- [ ] Removing one source preserves documents still referenced by another source location.
- [ ] Behavioral tests use temporary trees and cover preview/confirm, incremental change/delete, limits, escape refusal, dedup, progress, cancellation, and restart.

## Blocked by

- cyril-39xn
design:
### Initial reader and chunker contract

The first confirmed-folder reader guarantees text documents only: `.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.org`, `.rst`, and `.adoc`, matched case-insensitively. It accepts UTF-8 (with or without BOM) and BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE, normalizes line endings for indexing while preserving one-indexed original line mapping, and rejects undecodable content. PDF, DOCX, HTML, source-code, JSON/YAML, logs, and archives are not silently treated as text; they are Unsupported until a dedicated reader slice defines extraction and citation behavior. An agent may still submit already-extracted text through the single-document MCP path.

Default limits are 20 MiB per file, 5,000 eligible files per source, and the source's configured per-sweep chunk budget. Hidden files/directories and `.git`, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, `.venv`, and `venv` trees are excluded before descent. Source-specific include/ignore globs are compiled and shown in preview; invalid patterns reject confirmation rather than degrading to no exclusions. A zero/negative limit is invalid, never unbounded.

The deterministic heading-aware chunker targets 800 words with 160 words of overlap and a 1,200-word hard maximum. Markdown/MDX ATX and setext headings, Org headings, reStructuredText/adoc section headings, blank paragraphs, lists, and fenced code blocks are preferred boundaries. The current heading path is copied into each chunk. A single block above the hard maximum is split at sentence/line boundaries and then words as a final fallback. Overlap never crosses document boundaries and is not duplicated in the displayed citation range. Empty/whitespace documents are Skipped, not successfully indexed.

Each chunk records normalized content, document content hash, zero-based chunk ordinal, heading path, and one-indexed inclusive source line range. Stable chunk identity derives from document identity plus ordinal and chunker-contract version; a chunker version change schedules the document for rebuild. Search returns the exact stored chunk text plus its source mapping.

Folder state records discovery fingerprint, content hash, reader/chunker versions, status, active chunk IDs, and alternate source locations. Change replacement and deletion update that document atomically through the existing single-document ingestion seam.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Preview root, eligible/capped files, estimated chunks, limits, and exclusions before ingestion.
- [ ] Require explicit human confirmation before indexing.
- [ ] Reuse the validated single-document path and expose checkpointed progress.
- [ ] Incrementally refresh changed files and remove vanished documents.
- [ ] Distinguish sensitive, unreadable, escaped, unsupported, failed, and deleted outcomes.
- [ ] Revalidate containment immediately before file open.
- [ ] Enforce file/byte/chunk/sweep limits safely.
- [ ] Deduplicate per document while preserving alternate source locations.
- [ ] Preserve documents still owned by another source when one source is removed.
- [ ] Temporary-tree tests cover lifecycle, safety, progress, cancellation, and restart.
- [ ] Initial folder formats/decoding are exactly the Design allowlist; unsupported binary/structured formats never fall through as text.
- [ ] Default 20 MiB/file, 5,000 files/source, exclusions, strict glob validation, and positive bounded sweep configuration are enforced.
- [ ] Chunking deterministically targets 800 words, overlaps 160, hard-caps 1,200, preserves heading path, and records one-indexed source lines.
- [ ] Reader/chunker version changes rebuild affected documents through the single ingestion seam.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M3. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.
Mechanism contract added: initial supported formats/decoding, scan exclusions/limits, deterministic 800/160 heading-aware chunking, citation line mapping, and versioned rebuild identity.

title: Re-probe session/set_model and v1/v2 configOptions — CLAUDE.md may be stale on both
description:
Two CLAUDE.md protocol claims are contradicted by first-party evidence and need a live probe against 2.20.1.

1. "session/set_model - behind unstable feature flag, not advertised in capabilities."
   MEASURED on kiro-cli 2.15.1 by a raw JSON-RPC probe with no client code in the path (KiroCrew commit 5790395c1): acked synchronously in 12.5ms; conversation carried across the switch INCLUDING ACROSS VENDORS; sticks over subsequent turns; fired mid-turn the in-flight turn is undisturbed and completes with end_turn, new model takes effect next turn. On 2.15.2, `auto` is advertised in availableModels and set_model("auto") returns OK {}.
   KiroCrew calls it unconditionally in production and builds its entire model-entitlement layer on it. Cyril routes model changes through kiro.dev/commands/execute instead — a more expensive path if set_model works.

2. "config_options - always null on the v1/v2 engine."
   KiroCrew parses configOptions from the session/new AND session/load response on BOTH backends and derives valid /effort levels from it (client.py:2578-2702). Their supports_config_option docstring frames an absent effort option as a claude-adapter-version issue, not a kiro one.
   (Partially overlaps cyril-cxwb, which covers lifting config_options for KAS; this is the v1/v2 half.)

Cheap probe: capture session/new on current kiro-cli and check whether configOptions carries an effort entry; then attempt session/set_model with a served id and observe.

Whichever way it lands, correct CLAUDE.md — a stale "not implemented" note is the kind that quietly costs a feature.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 9.

---
## VERIFIED 2026-08-30 against kiro-cli 2.20.1 — both claims settled

Probe: experiments/conductor-spike/probe-v2-set-model-2.20.1.py
Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/v2-set-model-2.20.1.jsonl

1. session/set_model WORKS. Served id claude-opus-5 acked in 1.4ms with an empty {} result; the session
   sidecar confirms the paid turn actually billed claude-opus-5. Cyril's doc was HALF wrong: "not
   advertised in capabilities" is TRUE (agentCapabilities.sessionCapabilities is {}), but it inferred
   UNUSABLE from UNADVERTISED. KiroCrew's 2.15.1 finding holds at 2.20.1.
2. configOptions: cyril was RIGHT, and more precise than KiroCrew — the key is ABSENT ENTIRELY from the
   v2 session/new result (top-level keys only ['models','modes','sessionId']), not null.
   session/set_config_option -> -32601 Method not found, data "session/set_config_option". KiroCrew's
   both-backends parsing is a claude-adapter path. cyril-cxwb (KAS half) unaffected.
3. set_model does NOT validate — bogus id accepted in 0.4ms; next prompt dies in 0.4s with -32603 and
   zero session/update frames. Upgrades cyril-fj6j to MEASURED.

CLAUDE.md corrected. Nothing left to probe — close after review.
acceptance_criteria: Both claims re-probed against current kiro-cli with a control, and CLAUDE.md updated to match the observed behavior.

title: Theme-source scanner breaks on CRLF checkouts — main's Windows CI red since 2026-07-12
description:
conversation_theme_sources.rs audit_source computes token offsets with 'source_offset += line.len() + 1', which under-counts CRLF files by one byte per line (lines() strips 
). signed_ranges come from source.find() (true byte offsets), so on Windows runners (no .gitattributes, Git-for-Windows autocrlf) every token deep in a file drifts below its signed exemption range: production_highlight_is_clean false-flags the four Color::* arms INSIDE color_to_rgb (highlight.rs:198-201). Reproduced deterministically by CRLF-converting the source and re-running the algorithm (LF: clean; CRLF: exactly CI's four findings). Main red since the theme-work push 2026-07-12 (run 29182785122); first surfaced on PR #51 which inherited it via merge. Fix: normalize 
 -> 
 in production_source before auditing + a CRLF regression test on audit_source.
