title: KAS free-path auth responder cannot serve SocialGitHub logins (kirocli:social:token row unread)
description: kas/auth.rs TOKEN_ROW_SQL reads only kirocli:odic:token (Builder-ID/OIDC). A SocialGitHub login (kiro-cli user whoami accountType=SocialGitHub) stores its token at kirocli:social:token, so the pre-spawn servability check reports 'kiro token row absent — logged out; run kiro-cli login' even though kiro-cli IS logged in and the v2 engine works. Free-path AND wrapper KAS spawns (both --auth=acp-callback) are unusable for social-login users. Found live during cyril-dn91 slice 7 (2026-08-02, kiro-cli 2.16.0). Fix direction: probe the store per the auth-methods playbook (accountType FIRST, then the matching row family odic vs social), add the social row shape to the parser + expiry/refresh handling (interacts with cyril-taba's refresh work).

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #82 merged to main (05ffd29), absorbed into cyril-dn91 by user decision. Both per-login-method token rows read (odic + social); freshest-expiry tiebreak; state-arn preferred with inline fallback; 3 fences (social_login_row_is_served, social_inline_arn_is_the_fallback, freshest_token_row_wins_when_both_present). Live-verified: KAS session creation succeeded from a SocialGitHub login.

title: M4: Add shared local embeddings and retrieval-quality gates
description:
## Parent

cyril-ct0y

## What to build

Add one runtime-owned local embedding backend shared by memory and knowledge, then prove that it improves retrieval without becoming an availability dependency. The runtime embeds eligible semantic/episodic memories and knowledge chunks, stores vectors and an embedding signature in their existing SQLite rows, embeds each query once, computes bounded cosine candidates, and fuses vector and FTS5 rankings. `/memory` and `/library` show model readiness, lexical fallback, re-embedding progress, completion, and failure.

The demo covers normal and degraded operation: a paraphrased query finds a relevant memory and cited document that lexical search misses; disabling or failing the model immediately returns to FTS5 without losing data; changing the model/signature schedules restart-safe re-embedding while lexical results remain available. A frozen retrieval corpus reports recall, reciprocal rank, abstention, and citation fidelity so ranking changes are judged against evidence.

## Placement / boundaries

The memory runtime is the sole owner of model loading, embedding concurrency, vector width/signature, backfill/re-embedding jobs, and model health. Memory and knowledge retrieval modules own their candidate construction, scope/trust filters, cosine scoring, fusion, and budgets. SQLite owns vector persistence; the embedding backend is not described or implemented as a vector index. The TUI owns status/progress projection only. MCP tools consume the same retrieval interfaces and do not embed independently.

Model absence, download/load failure, unsupported hardware, and dimension/signature mismatch degrade to lexical retrieval with structured status. Never load one model copy in the TUI and another in the MCP adapter. Store no vector whose signature or dimension differs from the active embedding space. Re-embedding is checkpointed, bounded, cancellable, and restart-safe. Begin with bounded brute-force cosine over SQLite candidates; do not add FAISS, a vector database, ANN service, or entity graph unless a separate benchmark-backed decision demonstrates need.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One local embedding backend in the runtime serves both memory and knowledge; TUI and MCP processes load no duplicate model.
- [ ] Eligible memory and knowledge rows store vectors with model/signature/dimension metadata in SQLite.
- [ ] Each query is embedded once and vector ranking preserves every existing scope, trust, validity, and source filter.
- [ ] Vector and FTS5 rankings are deterministically fused under bounded candidate/result budgets.
- [ ] Model unavailable, loading, failed, or unsupported states fall back to lexical retrieval without breaking recall/search.
- [ ] Model/signature/dimension changes never compare incompatible vectors and schedule checkpointed re-embedding.
- [ ] Re-embedding is cancellable and resumes after restart without losing lexical availability or duplicating work.
- [ ] `/memory` and `/library` expose model and re-embedding state with actionable errors.
- [ ] A frozen corpus reports recall at fixed K, reciprocal rank, abstention, and citation fidelity for lexical and hybrid modes.
- [ ] Tests prove paraphrase lift, lexical fallback, scope equivalence, signature mismatch handling, restart, deterministic fusion, and absence of ANN/graph dependencies.

## Blocked by

- cyril-39xn
- cyril-nxq5
design:
## Mechanism contract established by this slice

Every stored vector is nullable and carries an embedding signature derived from model identity, vector dimension, and preprocessing-contract version. Vector bytes include an encoding version. A row is vector-comparable only when signature, dimension, and encoding all match the active backend. Changed or missing signatures remain FTS-searchable and enter the checkpointed re-embedding queue.

A query is redacted and embedded once. Scope, trust, validity, and source filters run before either retrieval leg. FTS5 and cosine each produce an ordered candidate list; they are fused by reciprocal-rank fusion with initial equal weights and `k = 60`, then deterministically tie-broken by the existing domain score/timestamp and stable memory ID. Weight changes require the frozen-corpus gate rather than ad hoc tuning.

Episodic vector candidates rank before fusion by `cosine × (0.7 + 0.3 × importance) × exp(-0.03 × age_days)`. Semantic facts do not decay; scope/conflict selection happens before ranking. Knowledge chunks do not decay and retain source-scoped citation metadata. Admission thresholds are selected and pinned from the frozen corpus to balance relevant recall with abstention; they are not guessed independently in callers.

The runtime owns one embedding backend and serializes native-model access. MCP and TUI request retrieval from the runtime and never instantiate an embedder. Model load/download failure, unsupported hardware, or query-embedding failure removes the vector leg and returns the lexical result with degraded status.

Initial vector search is bounded brute-force cosine over eligible SQLite rows. Re-embedding persists progress by stable row ID and signature, is idempotent, and can resume after restart. FAISS, vector databases, ANN services, and entity graphs remain prohibited until a separate measured decision demonstrates that this implementation misses a stated quality or scale target.

### Entity-graph admission gate

The initial implementation creates no entity, relation, mention, or graph-index tables and runs no latent entity extraction. FTS5 plus vectors is the measured baseline. The frozen retrieval corpus must include a separately reported multi-hop partition with supporting-chunk and citation judgments.

Graph work requires a new design/issue only when the baseline multi-hop recall@5 is below 0.85 and a disposable graph prototype improves recall@5 by at least 0.10 absolute while keeping citation fidelity at or above 0.95 and worsening abstention accuracy by no more than 0.02 absolute. The comparison uses identical chunks, scope filters, result budget, and queries. If the baseline already meets the target or the prototype misses any guardrail, no graph schema/extractor lands.

A future admitted design must also specify canonical entity identity, relation provenance/evidence, trust, transactional chunk-update/delete repair, source-scoped traversal, injection resistance, and rebuild/version behavior. No current caller or schema reserves speculative graph fields.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One runtime-owned local backend serves memory and knowledge with no duplicate TUI/MCP model.
- [ ] Store vectors with signature/dimension metadata in SQLite.
- [ ] Embed each query once and preserve all scope/trust/validity/source filters.
- [ ] Deterministically fuse vector and FTS5 rankings under bounded budgets.
- [ ] Degrade every unavailable/failure state to lexical retrieval.
- [ ] Never compare incompatible vector spaces; schedule checkpointed re-embedding.
- [ ] Cancel/restart re-embedding without losing lexical availability or duplicating work.
- [ ] Show model/re-embedding status in /memory and /library.
- [ ] Report fixed-corpus recall, reciprocal rank, abstention, and citation fidelity.
- [ ] Prove paraphrase lift, fallback, scope equivalence, mismatch handling, restart, and no ANN/graph dependency.
- [ ] No graph schema or latent entity extraction lands in this issue.
- [ ] A future graph issue is admitted only when the frozen multi-hop baseline is below 0.85 recall@5 and a prototype adds at least 0.10 recall@5 while preserving ≥0.95 citation fidelity and ≤0.02 abstention regression.

notes.content: Roadmap reference: ROADMAP:Phase-5+; memory milestone M4. The installed Rivets CLI has no --external-ref option.
Divergence decision: no latent graph data. A separate graph design is admitted only by the pinned multi-hop recall lift, citation-fidelity, and abstention gates.

title: Tool purpose is blank on ~half of tool calls — kiro-cli emits both __tool_use_purpose and __toolUsePurpose
description:
kiro-cli echoes the reserved purpose argument under BOTH spellings. MEASURED by KiroCrew in a single real session: 160 __toolUsePurpose vs 184 __tool_use_purpose, across the same tools (commit 174a10a86). Reading one spelling blanks the purpose on roughly half of cyril tool pills.

Models also paraphrase the name — __purpose, __thinking_purpose and __woohoo_purpose all occur in real transcripts (_dispatch.py:471-491) — so KiroCrew matches by SHAPE rather than an allowlist: dunder prefix, normalized name ending in "purpose". An exact allowlist "silently drops every one of them".

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 4.2.
acceptance_criteria: Both canonical spellings are read through one extractor, matched by shape (dunder prefix + normalized suffix "purpose"). Unit test covers snake_case, camelCase, and one paraphrase.

title: Local gate never compiles kas-gated code — document/mandate --features kas in the standard verification loop
description: Surfaced by the 2026-07-04 bug sweep (cyril-lw67/cyril-0gke fixers): the CLAUDE.md-documented local gate (cargo test / cargo nextest run / cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings) never compiles feature-gated kas code (e.g. protocol/kas/terminal_io.rs), so kas modules are locally unlinted and untested unless the developer remembers --features kas. CI covers it via the dedicated KAS Feature job, but both sweep subagents had to independently discover and add 'cargo nextest run -p cyril-core --features kas' + matching clippy to their gates. Cheap fix: add the two --features kas commands to CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section (and any agent-facing gate checklists) so the local loop matches CI. Pre-existing; not introduced by the sweep PRs (#41/#42).

title: PowerShell family has zero behavioral terminal fixtures (spec cyril-6bol SC3)
description: spec.md SC3 requires 5/5 behavioral fixtures per runnable supported shell family (spaced argument, pipe, redirection, variable expansion, profile-defined environment). posix and fish have all five; PowerShell has none — installed_shells_preserve_external_exit_42 only checks exit 42 and only when /usr/bin/pwsh exists. Notably PowerShell is the one family whose launch line omits -NoProfile, so the profile-load behavior (spec B6) is entirely unverified for it. windows_powershell_lifecycle_smoke (added on the PR branch) covers create/wait/output/exit-code on Windows CI; the remaining fixtures (pipe, redirect, $env: expansion, profile capture) still need pwsh-on-Linux and/or Windows-gated tests.

title: KAS layer idiomatic cleanup batch (2026-07-01 implementation review)
description:
Small idiomatic/silent-failure items from the 2026-07-01 implementation review, batched. Each is independently landable; none changes behavior on the happy path.

1. thiserror migration: version.rs returns Result<_, String> (:10,34,47,72); discovery.rs KasMissing has structured variants but implements neither Display nor Error (hand-rolled reason(), flattened at bridge.rs:303 via .map_err(|m| m.reason())); auth.rs internal plumbing is Result<_, String> (:51,137). CLAUDE.md mandates thiserror with structured metadata; string errors cannot be pattern-matched — this bites when cyril-taba must distinguish stale/missing/corrupt token programmatically. KasMissing is 90% there: #[error(...)] attributes would delete reason() outright.
2. auth.rs:152-166 — log (debug!/warn!) before returning Err to KAS on every error path (missing home, unreadable token, missing profileArn, stale). Sibling modules log per the surface-do-not-swallow rule (host_io.rs:94, terminal_io.rs:304-320); auth failures present as opaque dead turns with nothing in cyril.log.
3. convert/kas.rs:43-45 — log before returning None when a context_usage frame lacks usagePercentage; the same function already warns for present-but-unparseable breakdown (:56). Wire drift here would silently freeze the context % display.
4. discovery.rs:111 — NoHome reason is misleading when KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH is set (the bundle WAS located via the override; the reason says to set the var that is already set). Add token-path context to that arm; the test matrix (:266) covers no-home only without overrides.
5. client.rs:280 — debug!-log the method name of unhandled _kiro/* ext requests before returning the null default; @kiro/agent adds host callbacks nearly every release and a new required callback currently degrades invisibly.
6. Named constants for the JSON-RPC codes -32602/-32603/-32000 (raw literals in ~12 places across auth.rs, host_io.rs, terminal_io.rs, client.rs).
7. settings.rs:103-172 — rename the minified-JS identifiers (e, n, c, k, ts) carried over from the zme() transcription; replicate semantics, not names.
8. terminal_io.rs:287 — one-line comment on the `code as u32` sign-loss cast (Windows negative NTSTATUS wraps to the conventional unsigned form — the reasoning is sound but appears nowhere).
9. version.rs:19-22 — drop the dead .unwrap_or("") on the infallible first split().next(); the .filter(!is_empty) does the real work.
10. bridge.rs:825-838 — QueryCommandOptions RPC failure collapses to CommandOptionsReceived { options: [] }, indistinguishable from a command with genuinely no options (a PARSE error correctly emits BridgeError). Emit BridgeError for the RPC-failure case too.
11. client.rs:130-140 (pre-existing) — on ext-notification params parse failure, early-return after the error! instead of substituting Value::Null and double-logging through the engine path.
12. settings.rs:63-66 — debug! on the no-home empty-settings fallback (the module's only unlogged fallback; its own doc warns this is exactly the bare-fallback-flags failure shape). Also fix the doc: initialize is once per BRIDGE, not once per session.
13. Document (or make async) the two remaining sync call sites — settings.rs:26 std::fs via KasEngine::client_capabilities (engine.rs:107) and version.rs:48-51 std::process — both provably startup-only, but the layer's own invariant (host_io.rs:15-17) says never call sync fs/process on this runtime, and neither site documents why blocking is acceptable there.

title: Concurrent permission requests silently clobber each other; approvals carry no session attribution
description:
UiState.approval (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs:87) is a single Option<ApprovalState>
and show_approval() (state.rs:1344) assigns it unconditionally. A second permission
request arriving while one is open OVERWRITES the first and drops its `responder`
oneshot -- the user never sees it, and the agent's session/request_permission is
answered by a dropped channel rather than by a human. There is no queue and no test
for a second concurrent request.

Separately, PermissionRequest (crates/cyril-core/src/types/event.rs:416) carries
{tool_call, message, options, trust_options, responder} and NO session id.
client.rs:218 builds it from args that DO contain sessionId and drops the field, so
the overlay cannot say which session is asking.

WHY THIS IS NOW LOAD-BEARING (W1)
Both defects are pre-existing -- CLAUDE.md already documents that the agent "may
initiate multiple tool calls in parallel before waiting for permission responses",
so the clobber has been reachable on v2 all along. It needs two approvals in flight
at once to bite, which is occasional today.

Workflows make it structural. A workflow run executes steps as PEER SESSIONS, and
`parallel` is one of only three node types the seven bundled recipes use. Two
branches doing real work will request permission concurrently, from sessions the
user cannot see. With reattach-on-demand (ROADMAP W1) a user can also attach to a
run whose step is ALREADY blocked on a permission that was never displayed.

SCOPE (decided in the 2026-08-08 grilling: "queue + attribute, in scope")
  1. Replace the single slot with a queue (VecDeque), draining on resolve.
  2. Thread session_id through PermissionRequest from the ACP args.
  3. Label the overlay with the originating session, and -- once the workflow
     registry exists (cyril-jxfu) -- with the run/node it belongs to.

Ordering note: (1) and (2) are independent of the workflow work and fix a shipped
silent failure on their own. (3) needs cyril-jxfu for the run/node half; the plain
session-id label does not.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two permission requests in flight: both are presented in order; neither responder is dropped. Regression test drives two show_approval calls and asserts the second does not displace the first.
2. PermissionRequest carries the originating SessionId, threaded from the ACP request args (not reconstructed).
3. The approval overlay names the originating session when it is not the main session.
4. cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass, including --features kas.

notes.content: Closed: Merged in PR #91

title: Reach KAS via the kiro-cli relay (--agent-engine v3 --auth-method cli) — retires the _kiro/auth/getAccessToken work item
description:
Cyril KAS launch research concluded standalone KAS needs `node acp-server.js`, file-based auth, and a profileArn-bearing _kiro/auth/getAccessToken callback. AWS abandoned that route.

KiroCrew spawns:  kiro-cli acp --agent-engine v3 --auth-method cli

kas_transport.py:58-63: "cli keeps token resolution inside the kiro-cli process, which already holds the OIDC refresh token. Without it the engine would expect its host to answer _kiro/auth/getAccessToken." The relay consumes the callback internally — the frame never reaches the ACP client.

They abandoned the direct-spawn route because it "made Crew depend on kiro-cli internal on-disk layout" ({data_dir}/kas/{version}-{hash}/...). Measured frame parity: the relay forwards complete NDJSON frames byte-for-byte and advertises TWO extension methods the direct route did not (_kiro/sourceProviders/list, _kiro/sourceProviders/listResources) — a superset.

They pass the engine flag explicitly rather than relying on the default "because the default is kiro-cli to change and a silent fall back to v2 would look like KAS working while serving a different agent entirely". Note cyril is AHEAD here: protocol/kas/version.rs:32 already resolves kas vs v3 from the installed version; KiroCrew hardcodes v3 and would break on 2.7.1.

Depends on cyril-hg2x (KAS needs protocolVersion = integer 1).

Security note for whoever picks this up: KAS runs tool execution UNSANDBOXED either way — the relay spawns it without --sandbox and KAS sandbox factory resolves an absent config to its no-op backend. See findings section 6.3.

Source: docs/kirocrew-acp-seam-findings.md section 6.1.
acceptance_criteria: Cyril can drive KAS through the relay with no auth-callback implementation. The engine flag is passed explicitly, never left to the kiro-cli default.

title: Render workflow step streams: run panel + step drill-in over the cyril-jxfu route
description:
cyril-jxfu lands routing + attribution for KAS workflow step peer sessions: WorkflowUiState holds per-step-session streams (message history, activity), populated via NotificationRoute::Workflow, with late-claim re-parenting from the optimistic subagent store. Nothing renders those streams yet — the App comment on the Notification::Workflow arm ('The changed flag is deliberately unwired: nothing renders workflow state yet') still holds after cyril-jxfu.

SCOPE
- A run panel (WorkflowTracker read model: runs, nodes, statuses, loop iterations) and step drill-in (WorkflowUiState streams), following the crew_panel/subagent drill-in pattern but reading workflow state — workflow steps deliberately do NOT ride SubagentTracker/crew_panel.
- Wire workflow-state changed flags into redraw_needed.
- TuiState additions for the renderer seam.

Explicitly out of scope of BOTH cyril-jxfu (routing only) and cyril-0qe6 ('Out of scope: rendering the run (panel/drill-in)'). cyril-0qe6's /workflow attach is the natural entry point for the panel.

notes.content: 2.19.0 audit live-workflow finding (docs/kiro-2.19.0-wire-audit.md § 14): node_complete.capturedOutput is EMPTY in every observed run (0.46.1 live, 0.38.7 pinned, and the committed 2.16.0/2.16.2 captures) — the KAS extractor never matches the speak-then-send_message turn shape and the 0.46.1 transcript fallback reads a mismatched schema. Do not spend renderer UI on capturedOutput; treat it as reserved until kiro fixes capture. Also: step-session titles are now `<workflow> · <nodeId>` (live-confirmed) — useful for stream headers. See cyril-f7tm for the retry-wait node_paused discriminator.

2026-08-25 (2.19.2 audit, docs/kiro-2.19.2-wire-audit.md § 1): node_complete.capturedOutput is now NON-EMPTY ("ALPHA" / "ALPHA-BETA", {{s1.output}} interpolated) — but the same-day KAS 0.48.0 pin captured too, and the extractor / transcript fallback / wf-coder are byte-identical across builds: the MODEL now restates its answer as a second assistant message after the send_message completion tool (distinct -say replayId, ~2.4 s later). Model/backend behavior, not an engine fix → capturedOutput is usable-but-roulette; still do not spend load-bearing UI on it. Renderer consequence: step streams show the answer TWICE (say → Send Message tool → say); both chunks are real messages with different replayIds — do NOT dedup, just expect a post-tool restatement.

title: Cache completed Write diff derivations
description: Review finding #13: completed Write tool calls recompute the same Myers diff twice per frame, including off-screen history. Derive summary and lines once or use a bounded coherent cache.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One diff derivation supplies both summary and rendered lines.
- [ ] Historical rendering does not recompute unchanged diffs each frame.
- [ ] Coherence tests and a repeated-render benchmark pass.

title: tethys callers returns false negatives — unsafe as the blast-radius step in /sweep-bugs and /ship
description:
`tethys callers` returns confident FALSE NEGATIVES in this workspace, which makes
it unsafe as the impact-analysis step it is used for (the /sweep-bugs and /ship
skills both instruct agents to bound a blast radius with it).

Measured 2026-08-01 after a fresh `tethys index` (2309 symbols, 97 files):

  ActiveTurn                    type                  resolves, correct (1 caller)
  EffortLevel                   type                  resolves
  classify_notification_route   free fn, same file    resolves, correct (1 caller)
  parse_options_response        free fn, cross-module "No callers found"  <-- WRONG
  show_picker                   inherent method       error: not found: symbol
  split_active_label_suffix     private free fn       error: not found: symbol

`parse_options_response` has one PRODUCTION caller and seven test callers. The
production one is `crate::commands::parse_options_response(&value)` at
crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/bridge.rs:1402 — a path-qualified call inside a
nested closure. tethys reports "No callers found", which to a blast-radius
question reads as "nothing calls this, safe to change".

Two failure modes, unequal in danger:
  1. "No callers found" — symbol IS indexed, call edge missed. Silent and
     confident. This is the dangerous one.
  2. "error: not found: symbol" — inherent methods and private free fns are not
     in the symbol table at all. At least this fails honestly.

`--lsp` does not rescue it. It fails with
`LSP error -32603: file not found: .../crates/cyril-core/src/commands/mod.rs`
then logs "returning DB-only callers" and prints the same wrong answer. Silent
degradation to a weaker method while still printing a confident result is the
worst failure mode for an analysis tool.

Also: the flag the skills tell agents to pass, `--exclude-speculative`, DOES NOT
EXIST in the installed build (/home/dwalleck/.local/bin/tethys) and errors out.
Real usage is `tethys callers [-t|--transitive] [--lsp] <SYMBOL>`.

Side effect: `tethys index` writes an untracked `.rivets/index/` directory.
`.rivets/.gitignore` did not cover it (fixed 2026-08-01 by adding `index/`), so
before that a `git add -A` could have swept the index into a commit, and
`gh pr create` warned about an uncommitted change on every agent that ran the
impact-analysis step.

Action: either fix/upgrade tethys, or demote it in the skills to a hint with
rg/grep as the authority for caller enumeration. All three agents in the
2026-08-01 sweep batch found their real callers via rg, not tethys.

notes.content: Closed: INVALID - filed on a wrong premise. --exclude-speculative DOES exist (tethys 2425521, 2026-07-23); the binary at ~/.local/bin/tethys was built 2026-06-30, 363 commits stale, so the flag postdated it. Rebuilt from source and re-ran every probe: show_picker needs a QUALIFIED name (UiState::show_picker resolves fine - my query was malformed); split_active_label_suffix resolves; parse_options_response resolves. One narrow real limitation remains and is not a defect: the default DB-only resolver misses path-qualified cross-module calls (super::convert::kiro::parse_options_response at bridge.rs:1430) - default finds 11 callers/1 file, --lsp finds 12/2 files including bridge.rs. --lsp is the documented remedy and works. The /sweep-bugs and /ship instructions were CORRECT as written. Real action if any: reinstall tethys from ~/repos/tethys (cargo build --release), and note tethys --version is a frozen 0.1.0 so it cannot signal staleness.
